# Bugs

Known compiler defects: incorrect output, crashes, miscompiles, rejection of valid code, missing diagnostics for unsafe code.

For missing features and language design gaps see `TODO.md`.

Each entry's first line is a **[priority size]** tag plus a one-sentence summary; the full description follows on the next lines. Priority is one of:

- `IMM` -- users hit this in their first non-trivial program (or basic Python idioms);
- `HIGH` -- users hit this regularly in non-trivial programs / stdlib work;
- `MED` -- specific patterns or advanced features;
- `LOW` -- latent / quality / hardening, no current user impact.

Size is one of `small` (hours-1d), `medium` (1-3d), `large` (~week), `xlarge` (bigger).

Entries may carry an immutable **slug** in brackets right after the headline (e.g. ``[`union-nocopy-field-store`]``) -- a stable anchor for pointing at one entry out of hundreds. Add one when an entry is first referenced (from source, a test, or another entry); new entries get one up front. Every reference, in code comments and inside this file alike, is spelled ``BUGS.md#<slug>`` -- an anchor-style token that cannot collide with ordinary prose, so one grep finds every reference. A slug never changes once assigned, even if the headline is later reworded, and `tpyc/test_bugs_slugs.py` fails on a reference whose entry is gone -- so a fixed entry cannot be deleted while a stale pointer to it survives. **What that check does NOT cover:** it validates `BUGS.md#<slug>` citations only. Around 150 source and test files still mention `BUGS.md` as a bare file reference, which cannot dangle but also cannot be resolved to an entry, and nothing counts them down. The backlog this convention has to work through is therefore the REFERENCE side, not the entry side -- an un-slugged entry costs nothing, an un-slugged reference is the thing that sends a reader to an 829-entry file.

Entries tagged `deferred: MIR` are gated on the THIR/MIR migration (see `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Open Questions 9/11/13) and must NOT be patched in the current AST/sema model -- the clean fix lands in the IR. Do not select them for `/tpy-next` or `/tpy-fix-bug`.

## Compiler bugs

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A ternary over two plain RECORD names declared into a pointer-repr `Optional` slot is emitted as a pointer initialised from an object.** [`optional-slot-record-ternary-emits-pointer-init`] `xs: P | None = a if c else b` with `a, b: P` emits `P* xs = ((c) ? (a) : (b));`, which the C++ compiler refuses (`cannot convert 'P' to 'P*'`). The ifexpr OPTIONAL_TO_PTR re-tag in `_borrow_local_binding` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) assumes the lowered ternary already IS the slot's `T*` -- true when the arms are Optional-typed or `optional_to_ptr` lifts, false for two bare record lvalues, which the ifexpr lowering binds as the `T&` select. The fix is either an address-of over the select (`&((c) ? (a) : (b))`, both arms lvalues) or declining the re-tag when the arms are not pointer-form. The container twin `xs: list[int32] | None = a if c else b` rejects at `decl.slot_type`. Found by the route-merge survey.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) An `Own`-returning PROPERTY read passed to a mutable static-method slot renders bare and cannot bind the `T&`.** [`own-property-rvalue-bare-at-mutable-static-slot`] `class H: @property def p(self) -> Own[R]: ...`, `class K: @staticmethod def take(r: R) -> int32: r.n += 1 ...`, then `K.take(h.p)` emits `K::take(h.p())` and the C++ compiler refuses to bind the prvalue to `R&`; the CALL form `K.take(mk())` hoists `R __tmp_1 = mk();` correctly. The qualified-call (marker) family's `native_record_call` row (`_native_record_call_arg`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) admits any rvalue record source at any non-Own/Optional/Union slot and never asks whether the slot is a mutated `T&`; the row is documented for `const T&` and template slots, where a prvalue binds. The container twin rejects at `method.qualcall.arg.call_rvalue`. The fix is the slot-mutability fact threaded to the marker family (the argument-table family collapse in TODO.md), after which the property source hoists like the call. Found by the route-merge survey.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A `@dispatch` record method's parameters are never const-inferred, so an rvalue argument the signature-const verdict admits bare cannot bind the emitted `T&`.** [`dispatch-method-params-never-const-inferred`] `class K: @dispatch def take(self, r: R): self.n = r.n; @dispatch def take(self, s: str): ...` emits `void take(R& r)` although the body only reads `r`, because the codegen signature pass skips mutation facts for every function whose `overload_form` is set (`_get_method_mutated_params` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, meant for the bodyless `@overload` stubs) -- while sema's `const_borrow_params` for the same variant says the slot IS const. The argument rows that bind a prvalue in place trust the sema verdict, so `k.take(mk())` (record) and `k.fill(mks())` (container, `k.fill(xs: list[str])`) render bare into the mutable reference and the C++ compiler refuses (the container face was a located reject, `call.ret_type.container`, until the rvalue-call result gate stopped being record-only). The same skip also picks `overloads[-1]`'s facts for every variant of a set. The fix is codegen's: read the variant's own mutation facts (a bodied `@dispatch` variant has them) and spell the non-mutated params `const T&` like any other method's; every `@dispatch` record method signature over a reference-typed param changes with it. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small] (spurious diagnostic on valid code) A borrow-returning callee's result bound to a local from a HOISTED temporary argument is warned as dangling.** [`lend-back-of-hoisted-temp-warned-as-dangling`] `r = head(mk())` with `def head(xs: list[Rec]) -> Rec: return xs[0]` prints `warning: Result borrows from temporary argument 'xs'; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement`, but the emit hoists the argument into a named local at the binding's own scope (`std::vector<Rec> __tmp_1 = mk(); Rec& r = head(__tmp_1);`), so nothing dangles and the program runs correctly. Sema's lend-back check models the argument as a statement-scoped temporary; the hoist rows made it a block-scoped local. Same text for a record and a container argument. The fix is sema's: a lent-back argument the lowering hoists is not destroyed at end-of-statement. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small] (wrong signature consulted) The user-method argument gate reads the FIRST overload's signature facts, not the resolved overload's.** [`record-method-arg-gate-reads-first-overload`] `_lower_method_arg_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) passes `overloads[0]` to `_record_method_arg_ok`, so every row that reads `const_borrow_params` or `mutated_params` off `req.overload` (the const-slot rows, the rvalue-in-place rows) judges an overload SET by its first member; a set whose variants differ in which parameter they mutate gets the wrong verdict for the later variants. Masked today by `dispatch-method-params-never-const-inferred` (the signatures are all mutable anyway). The fix threads the resolved `FunctionInfo` the call carries. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A BORROW-returning `__add__` whose payload is a CONTAINER has no render at an `Own` return slot, in either spelling.** [`dunder-borrow-container-own-return`] `def __add__(self, o: Pool) -> list[int32]` then `def f(p: Pool, q: Pool) -> Own[list[int32]]: return p + q` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.+.record`, and so does the explicit `return copy(p + q)` -- the binop's own lowering declines a RECORD operand at the borrow-bind read the copy-construct tail takes. The RECORD payload of the same shape lowers (`tests/cases/returns/warn_return_record_borrow_dunder`), so the two families disagree on one operator spelling; sema warns the copy at both. Pinned by `tests/cases/returns/error_return_container_borrow_dunder`. The binop result gate keeps the record slice for this reason: widened, the borrow-dunder result binds a const alias and a write through it is a C++ error instead (`binop-borrow-result-alias-bound-const`). Found while downgrading the Own-return borrowed-source error to the owning-slot warning 2026-09-06.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `list([...])` over a str-element literal has no lowering arm.** [`list-ctor-over-str-literal-unlowered`] `a = list(["x", "y"])` rejects at `expr.call:call.special.call_type.builtin_generic` (`tests/cases/list/error_list_ctor_str_element_literal`); the bare literal `["x", "y"]` and `list(xs)` over a named list compile. The builtin-generic call form (`list(<literal>)`) is one of the special-builtin callee kinds the call lowering has no arm for when the element target the call derives is a str literal's. Found while pinning the reject tag during the route merges.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `if xs:` on a pointer-repr `Optional[container]` name has no render: the truthiness mode sema attaches is the None test alone.** [`optional-container-truthiness-drops-emptiness`] `def probe(xs: list[int32] | None) -> bool: if xs: ...` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.name` (`tests/cases/none_safety/error_truthy_optional_container`). The pointer-repr Optional NAME row in the truthiness lowering renders the bare pointer test, which is the whole truth for a record pointee (a record without `__bool__` / `__len__` is truthy whenever it is not None) and half of it for a container's: CPython's `if xs:` is `xs is not None and len(xs) > 0`. Sema attaches no truthiness mode to the Optional name, so the row cannot tell the two apart and keeps the container rejecting rather than emit `(xs)` and print True for an empty list. The fix is sema's: a pointer-repr Optional over a type whose own truthiness is an emptiness or dunder test gets a mode that says so, and the row renders `xs != nullptr && <pointee test>` (the value-repr Optional already renders `::tpy::is_truthy` over the whole optional). Found by the route-merge sweep when the Optional-ptr binding stopped being record-only.
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A nested def that returns a borrow inside a function returning a VALUE is validated against the ENCLOSING function's return type.** [`nested-def-return-validated-against-enclosing`] `def outer() -> int32: def inner() -> R: return GR; ...` stops with `Internal error: outer: THIRReturn at ...: BORROW return value for value-typed return int32` -- the THIR validator checks the nested def's `THIRReturn` against `outer`'s return type. The record spelling crashes on master; the container spelling (`def inner() -> list[int32]: return GL`) crashed the same way from 2026-09-22, where it had been the located reject `return.record_source.ptrlocal.borrow`, so the crash is the only diagnostic the shape gets. Fix shape: the validator's return check reads the function whose body the `THIRReturn` sits in (the nested def), not the enclosing frame's. Probes `/tmp/agents/unify/review/safety/p18/main.py` (record), `p19/main.py` (container). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the gate unification.
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A `match` arm spelled `case _ as v:` over a RECORD subject crashes the lowering.** [`match-bound-wildcard-record-arm-ice`] `match r: case _ as v: v.x += 1` raises `AttributeError: 'TpyWildcardPattern' object has no attribute 'patterns'` in `_match_record_arm_always` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`): its docstring says a wildcard arrives as `test is None`, but an `as`-BOUND wildcard arrives as a `TpyWildcardPattern`, and the tail assumes an or-pattern (`for a in test.patterns`). `case v:` over the same subject lowers. Fix shape: treat a `TpyWildcardPattern` test as the always-arm before the or-pattern walk. Surfaced building the reference-sink sweep 2026-09-22 (its `match_capture` sink is spelled `case v:` because of it).
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A tuple literal over a CAPTURED unannotated list local inside a nested def crashes sema.** [`nested-def-tuple-of-captured-pending-list-ice`] `s0 = [1, 2]` in a function, then `def inner() -> None: t = (s0, 1)` raises `AssertionError: Internal error: composite expr type tuple[PendingList[...]#N, IntLiteral(1)] still has a Pending* leaf after finalization` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`, via `_analyze_nested_def` -> `resolve_all`): the captured literal is finalized in the enclosing body after the nested def was analyzed, so the tuple built inside it still holds the pending leaf. An annotated `s0: list[int32]` compiles, and so does the same tuple in the enclosing body. Hits list, record-element list and Array sources in a function, a method and a constructor (9 cells of the reference-sink sweep, 2026-09-22).
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) Passing a recursive-alias-typed parameter to a parameter of the same alias reports `Type mismatch in argument: expected Json, got Json`.** [`recursive-alias-param-identity-mismatch`] `type Json = None | bool | int32 | str | list[Json]`, `def take(p: Json)`, `def f(pv: Json): take(pv)`: the check compares alias INSTANCES rather than the alias, so the same spelled type on both sides is reported as a mismatch a reader cannot act on. Surfaced by the reference-sink sweep 2026-09-22 (`ru_wrap__nested__param__*` rows).
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud, internal-sounding message) The `protocol_slot` argument cell admits a FIELD read when the gate is told there is no flush position, and lowering then rejects it from inside with a prose message instead of a tag.** [`protocol-slot-field-arg-no-flush-tag`] At a flush-less argument position -- the nested constructor one is the reachable spelling -- `_protocol_slot_arg(..., temps_ok=False)` returns True for a field read at a structural-protocol slot, and the render then raises `protocol arg-temp outside a flush position`, which reaches the user as *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (protocol arg-temp outside a flush position)*. Every other reject at that position spells a `call.ctor_arg.<family>` tag, so this one reads like an internal assertion and cannot be histogrammed with the rest. The gate and the render disagree about which faces are temp-free: the predicate's `temps_ok=False` leg excludes the structural-RVALUE temp but not the field read's. Reproducer: a `@dynamic` protocol `DynP`, a record `K` whose `__init__` takes a structural-protocol parameter `p: P`, a fixture `class B` with a field of a conforming record type, then `Rc.new(Box(K(b.field)))` -- `tests/cases/calls/ctor_nested_tempfree_args` is the same chain with the shapes that do work. Tripwire: the cells `proto_p__ro__obj_field__nested` and `proto_p__ro__nested_field__nested` of `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.expected.json` hold that message as their verdict. Workaround: bind the field to a local first (`p = b.field; Rc.new(Box(K(p)))`), which the bare-NAME face admits. Fix shape: the predicate's no-flush leg excludes every face whose render hoists, so the gate's answer and the render's agree -- the field read then falls through to the family tail and gets its tag. Found sharing the temp-free rows into the nested ctor family, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (compiler crash, no located message) A generator that ASSIGNS a local inside a `finally` body stops with `Internal error: 't'`.** [`gen-finally-local-assign-internal-error`] The whole program is
  ```python
  def gen_finally() -> Iterator[str]:
      try:
          yield "f start"
      finally:
          t = 0
          t += 1
          print("finally " + str(t))
  ```
  and `tpy` prints `Internal error: 't'` with no file, line or construct -- a bare `KeyError` escaping as the CLI's catch-all. CPython runs it (`f start` / `finally 1`). Reading a local in the `finally` is fine; it is the first WRITE inside the finally body that trips it, so the resumable finally's scope does not know the name the frame layout was built for. Loud but useless: a user gets no way to locate the line. Repro `/tmp/agents/review_loopsrc/testcov/p2b.py`. Surfaced by the test-coverage review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence) REBINDING the name a `for` iterates, inside the loop body, changes what the rest of the loop iterates.** [`foreach-rebound-name-reiterated`] `xs = [1, 2, 3]` then `for v in xs: t += v; xs = [100, 200, 300]` sums `501` where CPython sums `6`: CPython binds the iterator to the ORIGINAL list object at the head and a rebind of the name cannot reach it, while the emitted loop keeps `begin`/`end` over the NAME and the rebind reseats the storage they walk. The generator spelling diverges the same way (`[1, 200, 300]` where CPython yields `[1, 2, 3]`), so it is not about frames -- the plain function is the everyday face. No diagnostic; the rebind is ordinary Python. Repros `/tmp/agents/review_loopsrc/parity/p7c_rebind_sync.py` (plain) and `p7b_rebind.py` (generator). Fix shape: a loop over a NAME has to name the object the head evaluated -- the same one-evaluation capture a call source already takes -- or the rebind has to be refused while the iteration's loan is live, which is the loan a plain `for` and a genexpr for-head already file. Surfaced by the cpython-parity review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A frame re-renders an ITERATOR-OBJECT `for` source rooted at a frame LOCAL, or reached through a free function, at every advance, so an impure accessor handing one back runs once per element.** [`frame-iter-next-source-reevaluated`] Inside a generator or `async def` the `next` / `iter_next` strategies spell the advance off the source expression itself -- `__for_r_0.emplace(h.get().__next__());` -- so a source that names existing storage is EVALUATED once per step. With
  ```python
  class Holder:
      calls: int32
      def get(self) -> SimpleIter: self.calls += 1; return self.it
  def rows(h: Holder) -> Iterator[str]:
      for v in h.get():
          yield "x " + str(v)
  ```
  TPy reports `calls 4` over three elements where CPython reports `calls 1`; the values are right, the side effects are not. NARROWED 2026-09-22: a method-call source whose receiver chain is rooted at a param, a capture or `self` is now held by reference in the frame (`frame_slot<T&>` of the source's own `decltype`; `iter_object` in `tests/cases/generators/frame_for_source_once` counts one call), so the shape above is fixed. What still re-renders: a chain rooted at storage the frame holds BY VALUE -- a frame local (`h = Holder(); for v in h.get():`) or a by-value param (`h: Own[Holder]`, a value type, an owned `str` copy, a deduced `Fn` / static-protocol slot; `own_param_iter` in the same case pins the shape) -- because the reference would point into the frame's own storage and a frame move would invalidate it; a chain with a hop that returns BY VALUE (`self.make().get()`), which would point into a temporary; and a FREE-function call returning a reference (`for v in pick(h):`), whose root the receiver walk does not see. Both keep `__for_r_0.emplace(<call>.__next__())` per advance. Repro `/tmp/agents/review_loopsrc/testcov/p4_iternext_lvalue.py` (rewrite `h` as a local). Surfaced by the test-coverage review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21.

- **[MED small] A script filename containing a hyphen produces an invalid C++ namespace.** [`hyphenated-script-name-cpp-namespace`] Running a valid Python script named `m317-parity-independent.py` emits `namespace tpyapp::m317-parity-independent`, which the C++ compiler rejects. Renaming the same script to `m317_parity_independent.py` builds and runs successfully; CPython accepts either filename. `module_to_cpp_namespace` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py` replaces dots with namespace separators but does not escape the script basename. Found by an independent parity probe during the MIR tuple-storage review; unrelated to MIR admission or tuple storage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught, pre-existing) A comprehension whose ELEMENT is a borrow-returning method call spells an array of references.** [`comprehension-elem-borrow-call-array`] `ys = [b.rec_m() for _ in range(2)]`, with `def rec_m(self) -> R` returning a field by reference, emits `std::array<R&, 2>` and the C++ compiler rejects it ("forming pointer to reference type"). Verified on master and on the property-read-normalization branch alike, so it is not the normalization's. The comprehension's element slot takes the call's BORROW return form as the element type instead of deciding between an owning copy and a container that cannot hold a reference -- the same question the accessor spelling of the same comprehension is refused for (`container_elem.accessor_lends_storage`, `tests/cases/records/error_property_elem_lends_storage`), which is why only the method spelling reaches the emitter. The TUPLE-element sink of the same source renders an owning copy instead, so the fix is the comprehension sink's, not the whole element family's. Loud, never silent. Fix shape: give the comprehension element slot the same verdict the tuple element slot takes (copy, warned) or the reject the accessor spelling takes; the choice is the element-slot rule, so it belongs with `container_elem.accessor_lends_storage` rather than beside it. Tripwire: the cells `comp_elem__rec__meth__{named,temp}` of `scripts/thir_migration/review/property_position_sweep.expected.json` are `ok` at the comp phase and fail the script's `--exec` half. Found by building and running the sweep's new rows, 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent missing null check, WARNED as present) A `@property` read through an UNPROVEN `Optional[record]` receiver emits the bare member call with no null check, while the line warns that one was added.** [`property-read-unproven-optional-receiver`] `def via_prop(h: H | None) -> int32: return h.val` with `@property def val(self) -> int32` emits `return h->val();` and warns *Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check* -- the check is NOT there, so a None receiver dereferences a null pointer where CPython raises. The METHOD twin on the next line gets it: `h.val_m()` emits `return ::tpy::deref_check(h).val_m();` under the identical warning. Probe `/tmp/agents/t1safety/p10_opt_recv.py`; identical on master, so the property-read normalization neither caused nor fixed it. The warning is the aggravating half: a reader who sees it has been told the program is safe. Cause, and the fix's home: sema stamps `needs_optional_runtime_check` on the ACCESS node when the receiver's type is an unproven Optional, and the property path never renders it -- on master because the synthesized getter call was built before the stamp and carried `deref_depth == 0`, and on this branch because `become_method_call` (`tpyc/parse/nodes.py`) deliberately does NOT transfer the receiver-shape markers (`needs_optional_runtime_check`, `deref_depth`, `deref_narrowed_to`, `ptr_non_null`): they were stamped for a FIELD lookup, and transferring them made three cases spell hops the getter render does not take (`method.marker.deref.ptr`). So the fix is not to transfer the marker but to ask the RECEIVER's category where the getter call is lowered, the way the method-call arm already does -- one question at the dispatch, not a marker copied across a node-kind change. Surfaced by the property-read normalization review (safety-model), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) A `@property` read in both arms of a TERNARY off a read-only receiver has no render, because the binding's const-ness is not taken from the receiver.** [`getter-source-const-not-tracked`] `v = s.r if c else s.r` with `@property def r(self) -> Rec` in a body that only reads `s` is a located reject, `expr.ifexpr`, on master and on the property-read normalization alike -- the arm stays closed precisely because the render it would take is ill-formed: the body emits `void prop_ternary(const Src& s, bool c)`, the const receiver selects the `@auto_readonly` const twin whose return is `const Rec&`, and the binding form spelled off the getter's DECLARED return is `Rec& v = ((c) ? (s.r()) : (s.r()));` -- *binding reference of type 'Rec&' to 'const Rec' discards qualifiers*. The container flavour is the same (`v = s.xs if c else s.xs` -> `std::vector<int32_t>& v = ...`). The spelled-method twin COMPILES: `s.r_m()` is not `@readonly`, so the call marks the receiver mutated, the parameter stays `Src&` and the non-const overload runs -- `void meth_ternary(Src& s, bool c)`. So the cost today is a reject where the method spelling renders, not wrong code. Probe `/tmp/agents/task1/impl/const_getter_pair.py`. Cause: the local's binding FORM is computed from the getter's DECLARED return (`Rec`, a borrow -> `T&`) while its CONST-ness is not taken from the receiver at a composite init. The bare decl `v = s.r` escapes it only by accident -- `_is_borrowing_auto_readonly_accessor` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) credits that init as a mutation of `s`, so the parameter is `Src&` and the non-const twin runs; a ternary init is not a method call, so no credit fires and the two halves disagree. Both halves are one decision: the TODO entry *"A borrow DECLARATION is credited as a mutation of its source"* proposes rooting that credit on the WRITE instead, which removes the accidental escape and makes the const-ness question unavoidable -- so fix them together. This entry BLOCKS the storage-ref lift arms queued in TODO.md (a ternary arm lifting `optional_to_ptr(s.o())` spells `const T*` off a const receiver and hits the identical mismatch). Surfaced by the property-read normalization review (codegen-correctness), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output / wild pointer) The literal-bound-local proof that a loop runs does not see a mutation that empties the container.** [`literal-bound-local-proof-ignores-mutation`]
  `NarrowingTracker._name_bound_to_nonempty_literal` (`tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`)
  proves a `for` head runs at least once when the name it iterates has exactly
  one write in the write history and that write is a non-empty container
  literal. Mutation is not a write, so the proof survives everything that can
  empty the container in between:

  ```python
  boxes = [Box(1), Box(2)]
  boxes.clear()
  for b in boxes:
      last = b
  last.n = 99          # accepted; `Box* last;` is read uninitialized
  ```

  TPy writes through a wild pointer (no diagnostic; the run above survives only
  by luck); CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`. Same with `boxes.pop()` twice,
  with `del boxes[0]`, and with the container passed to a callee that drains it
  -- the interprocedural spelling being the one no local check can see.
  Reproducer `/tmp/agents/review_zt/safety/pW_wildptr.py`. Loud alternatives
  (`items: list[Box] = []` then `append`, a parameter, a call result) do not
  prove and are unaffected.
  **Fix shape:** the container-non-empty flow-fact family TODO.md's emptiness-guard
  entry describes -- a fact keyed on the container place, seeded by a non-empty
  literal binding and by `len(c) > 0` / a truthiness test, KILLED by a rebinding
  and by any mutation that can empty it (`clear`, `pop`, `remove`, `del`, a pass
  to a mutating parameter), merged at joins like `ValueRange`. One family closes
  this defect and that feature gap together; neither should be built without the
  other, since the kill set is what makes the seed sound.
  **Interim bounds**, each independent of the family: null-initialize the
  hoisted pointer predecl and keep the promoted local out of the proven
  non-null set after the loop, so the unsound slice is a checked null
  dereference instead of a wild pointer; or drop the proof when the name has
  any method call, `del` or pass-as-argument between its binding and the loop.

- **[LOW small] (lost check elision + duplicated decoder, no diagnostic) A literal `range()` bound is recognized by the loop-runs proof but not by the range-facts recorder.** [`range-literal-bound-arm-unreached`] Two decoders read the same `range()` arguments and disagree. `NarrowingTracker._range_arg_range` peels `TpyCoerce` and so proves `for i in range(int32(3))` runs; `_track_for_range_facts` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) does not, so the same head leaves the loop variable the generic `ValueRange.for_range_index()` (lo=0, no upper bound) instead of `[0, N-1]`. Verified 2026-09-18 by wrapping the method and recording its argument node kinds: `range(4)` arrives as `('TpyCoerce', 'TpyIntLiteral')` while `range(len(a))` arrives as `('TpyCall', None)` and takes its own arm. Consequence: `a = [1, 2, 3, 4]` + `for i in range(4): total += a[i]` emits the checked `::tpy::__getitem__(a, i)` where the symbolic `range(len(a))` spelling emits the bare `a[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]`. The asymmetry runs the other way for the `while` spelling: `i = 0; while i < int32(3):` does NOT prove the loop runs, because `condition_provably_true` reaches the operand through `_operand_range` rather than through the literal peel. **Fix shape:** one decoder for a `range()` bound and one for an integer operand, both peeling coercions, with `_track_for_range_facts` and the two proofs calling them -- not a second copy of the peel. Filed rather than applied because widening the loop variable's range changes bounds- and div-check elision across the corpus. The same literal-recognition narrowness sits on the `while` side: `liveness.while_head_always_true` matches the literal `True` node alone, so `while 1:` and `while not False:` take the opposite verdict from `while True:` for one program -- a name bound on every `break` path out of them is reported unassigned (verified 2026-09-18, `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/c3_while1.py` and `c4_whilenotfalse.py`).

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A `for` over a set, dict or bytes LITERAL at the head is not lowered.** [`hoisted-local-over-set-dict-literal-head-unlowered`]
  `for x in {1, 2, 3}: y = x` then `print(y)` reports `this construct is not yet
  supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.branch_decls)`; with
  `y` given a value before the loop the same head reports
  `iter.set_literal_shape` (`iter.dict_literal_shape`,
  `iter.bytes_literal_shape` for the sibling spellings). So the literal head is
  unlowered on its own, and a body-first local read after the loop just takes
  the earlier of the two rejects. Binding the same literal to a name first
  (`s = {1, 2, 3}` then `for x in s:`) compiles and runs, which is the
  workaround and also what shows the gap is the head form alone. Sema proves
  these heads run (`for_head_provably_runs`) because whether a loop RUNS is a
  language truth and must not encode a lowering gap -- so the program reaches
  the honest lowering reject instead of a definite-assignment message that
  would be wrong. **Fix shape:** give the literal-head routes in
  `tpyc/thir/lower/` the `hoist_decls` the container / range / enum routes
  already take, and materialize the literal as the iteration source the way the
  name-bound spelling does.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong value / missing safety check) A `while True:` loop's `else` clause never runs, but its narrowing facts reach the code after the loop.** [`whiletrue-else-facts-escape`]
  The `else` clause of a `while True:` is dead code -- nothing falls out of the
  head -- yet what it proves is merged into the post-loop state:

  ```python
  def f(flag: bool) -> int:
      x: int | None = None
      while True:
          if flag:
              break
      else:
          x = 5                  # never runs
      return x + 1               # TPy prints 1; CPython raises TypeError
  ```

  TPy emits an unchecked dereference of the `int | None` (the `else` clause's
  `x = 5` narrowed it to `int`) and prints `1`; CPython raises
  `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'`.
  Pre-existing and identical at `a8c56ce958`. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/h1_whiletrue_else_narrow.py`. **Fix shape:**
  the same predicate that already tells the body join there is no fall-through
  edge (`liveness.while_head_always_true`) should keep the `else` clause's
  facts out of the post-loop state entirely -- the clause is unreachable, so it
  contributes nothing, neither bindings nor narrowing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code) A `break` or `continue` inside a `try` whose `finally` binds a name does not count that binding.** [`break-join-ignores-finally-binding`]
  The post-loop assignment join snapshots the assigned set AT the `break`, so a
  name bound by a `finally` the break unwinds through is missing from it, and a
  read after the loop is rejected with `variable 'w' may not be assigned at
  this point`. Repro: `for i in range(3):` / `try:` / `if flag: break` /
  `finally: w = 9`, then `return w` -- CPython runs the `finally` on the break
  path and prints `9`. The `continue` edge is the same snapshot and the same
  gap: `for i in range(1):` / `try: continue` / `finally: v = 1`, then
  `return v` is rejected where CPython prints `1` (verified 2026-09-18,
  `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/b1_try_finally_continue.py`). The conservatism
  is on the safe side (it rejects, never miscompiles) and no corpus case has
  either shape. **Fix shape:** take the snapshot after the `finally` bodies the
  edge unwinds through rather than at the `break` / `continue` statement
  itself -- one fix for both edges, since they file into one record.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) After a bare `raise` in an `except E as e` handler of a return-tier `try`, a `finally` nested INSIDE that handler reads `e` moved-from.** [`reraise-moves-bound-error-before-finally`]
  `except Bad as e: try: raise / finally: print("finally sees:", e.message)` inside an `@error_return(Bad)` function prints `finally sees: ` under TPy and `finally sees: boom` under CPython. `e` is `auto& e = *__err_opt_N`, and the bare `raise` parks `__tpy_ret = ::tpy::make_unexpected(std::move(*__err_opt_N))` BEFORE the finally body runs, so the body reads the moved-from object (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`, unchanged by the return-exception value work). Only the nested form reaches it: in a `finally` of the OUTER try CPython has already unbound `e`. A data-carrying return exception (a `str` or container field) is what makes it observable. Fix shape: materialize the parked value after the finally chain, or copy instead of move when a finally frame is active. Found by /tpy-review (safety-model) 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, loud) The `ReturnException` marker as a type-parameter bound renders a struct where C++ expects a concept.** [`return-exception-marker-as-type-param-bound`]
  `def show[E: ReturnException](e: E) -> None` emits `template<::tpy::ReturnException E>`; `::tpy::ReturnException` is the empty value BASE of user return exceptions, so C++ reads a class-type non-type template parameter and g++ fails at the first call ("expected a constant of type 'tpy::ReturnException', got 'E1'"). The declaration alone compiles. Before the value base existed the same bound failed for lack of any such symbol, so this never worked. The marker has no methods to bound a generic over, so the cheap fix is a sema reject of the marker as a bound; the structural one is TODO.md "Return exceptions: follow-ups" item 3 (a base-spelling entry separate from `ProtocolInfo.cpp_concept`). Found by /tpy-ready's second opinion 2026-09-18.

- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence) `str(e)` of a return exception is its declared `message` field and nothing else, so it differs from CPython's `args` rendering, and `print(e)` disagrees with `str(e)`.** [`return-exception-str-reads-message-only`]
  Four faces, probed 2026-09-18. (1) A class with `def __init__(self, code: int32, detail: str)` and no `message`: `str(e)` is `""` under TPy and `(1, 'x')` under CPython. (2) A class that declares `message`, stores it, and calls a bare `super().__init__()` (legal; it clears `args` in CPython): TPy prints the message, CPython prints `""`. (3) For a class that declares `message`, `str(e)` and an f-string print the message while `print(e)` prints `<Missing object at 0x...>`: the `__str__` codegen emits for the field is invisible to `_record_has_str_repr`, which picks the `operator<<` body (the thrown tier's same `print(e)` symptom is the `print(e)` / `str(e)` entries below). (4) A class-level default (`message: str = "x"` with an argless `__init__`): TPy's `str(e)` is `x`, CPython's is `""`. No diagnostic on any of them; the rule is documented in docs/ERROR_RETURN_DESIGN.md "Exception Type", which is not a warning. (1) predates the return-exception value work on both tiers; (2) and (3) are its consequences. Root and fix are one design question -- no implicit `__str__`, the class writes its own, which CPython runs identically -- in TODO.md "Return exceptions: follow-ups", item 4. Found by /tpy-ready's second opinion.

- **[HIGH small] (SILENT miscompile) Inside an `@error_return(E)` function, `try: return <@error_return(E) call>` never runs its `except E` handler: the callee's result is returned as-is, unchecked.** [`try-return-error-call-skips-handler`]
  `@error_return(Bad) def outer(k): try: return inner(k) / except Bad as e: print("handler ran"); raise` with `inner` raising `Bad`: CPython prints `handler ran` and then the caller's `outer caught`; TPy prints only `outer caught`. With a mutation in the handler (`e.line = 99` before the bare `raise`) the caller sees the unmodified error. Not an ordering divergence -- the handler body never executes. The `return` operand is a call whose `std::expected<T, E>` already is the enclosing function's return type, so the statement renders `return ::inner(k);` with NO unwrap; the `has_value()` check that would `goto __except_N` (`_er_check_stmt` / `_er_check_inline`, `tpyc/thir/emit.py`, both of which do consult `try_except_label`) is never emitted, and the handler label is dead code. The pass-through is right outside a `try` and wrong under a return-tier `try` whose handler catches `E`. The ASSIGNMENT form (`v = inner(k)` then `return v`) checks and dispatches correctly, which is why no case reaches it. Distinct from the all-return-tier entry below (a non-`@error_return` outer whose `goto` tier lacks a trailing return under `-Werror`; its handler runs) and from the expression-level unwrap skipping `finally` bodies (there the call IS unwrapped). Unchanged by the return-exception value work (identical at its branch point); found by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH medium] (rejects-valid, loud) A caught exception cannot be passed where its base class is expected: `except ValueError as e: log(e)` with `def log(e: Exception)` is a type mismatch.** [`exception-value-upcast-rejects`]
  `Type mismatch in argument 'e': expected Exception, got ValueError`, for every builtin exception and for a user `class MyErr(Exception)` alike -- the everyday "hand the error to a logging helper" shape. The child-to-parent value upcast in `sema/compatibility.py` admits only `is_user_record` nominals on BOTH sides, and the builtin exception stubs are `@native` records, so the hierarchy the C++ side really has (`::tpy::ValueError : ::tpy::Exception`, bindable to `const ::tpy::Exception&`) is never consulted. `isinstance(e, KeyError)` on an `Exception`-typed binding is refused by the same blindness, with a message that is false as worded: "isinstance() check type(s) 'KeyError' are not subclasses of 'Exception'" (see also the two `isinstance()`-on-an-exception entries below). Out of scope for the fix: a `ReturnException` class, which is a plain value outside the Throwable hierarchy and has its own pointed diagnostic. Found 2026-09-18.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Passing a caught exception to a `Throwable` parameter fails the C++ build.** [`exception-as-throwable-arg-ill-formed`]
  `def takes(t: Throwable) -> None` called as `takes(e)` under `except ValueError as e` passes sema and emits `::tpy::RefAdapter<::tpy::Throwable, ::tpy::ValueError> __tmp_1{e};` -- g++: "variable ... has initializer but incomplete type". `Throwable` is a `@dynamic` protocol the exception classes INHERIT (`BaseException : ::tpy::Throwable`), so the argument should bind the base reference directly; the call site instead takes the structural-conformer path and wraps it in an adapter that is never defined for a nominal implementer. Found 2026-09-18.

- **[LOW small] (parity) `repr()` of an exception value does not render CPython's `Name(args)` form.** [`exception-repr-form`]
  `repr(e)` prints `<__main__.NF object at 0x...>` for a user exception class (host-dependent text, so it cannot be snapshotted) and an empty string for a bound `StopIteration`; CPython prints `NF()` / `NF('msg')` and `StopIteration()`. Sibling of the two `print(e)` / `str(e)` entries below, which cover the message form. Found 2026-09-18.

- **[LOW medium] Cyclic enum imports can leave a stale reference wrapper in a function signature.** [`cycle-enum-stale-reference-signature`]
  With `a` importing enum `Color` from `b` and `b` importing `a.lookup`,
  `a.lookup() -> Color` can retain `Ref[Color]` in its registered FunctionInfo
  after its finalized AST return becomes value-type `Color`. Declaration
  registration saw the cycle placeholder before enum classification; the
  later normalization preserves the existing Ref wrapper. The existing
  `imports/mutual_cycle_with_enum` case still builds and runs correctly, so
  no runtime defect is established. The inconsistency prevents a faithful
  semantic signature join; THIR callee metadata stays absent for this shape.
  Fix requires checking declaration finalization across cycle peers and
  sibling parameter/aggregate signatures, separately from metadata carriage.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong value) A `Callable`-typed local LAMBDA copies the enclosing local it reads, with no diagnostic, where the identical `def` spelling warns.** [`callable-local-lambda-copies-capture-silently`] `read: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: len(data)` renders `[data]` -- a full copy taken at creation -- so a later `data.append(...)` is invisible to it: TPy prints `2` where CPython prints `3`. Writing the same body as a nested `def` produces the `copies local ... preventing move` warning; the lambda spelling produces nothing, although the divergence is the same one that warning exists to announce. Probe `/tmp/agents/review3/p16_lambda_copy.py`; pinned as the `lambda`/`lambda_sibling` lines of `tests/cases/nested_def/escaping_local_copy`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) Two nested `def`s with the SAME name in one scope reach the C++ compiler as a redeclaration.** [`duplicate-nested-def-name-in-one-scope`] Two `def h()` at the same level of one body is legal Python (the second rebinds the name); tpyc emits two `auto h = [...]` in one block and g++ reports `conflicting declaration 'auto h'`, naming generated code rather than the source. The block-scoped spelling (one per `if` arm) is fine -- each arm is its own C++ block. **Fix shape:** either reject at the second `def` with a located diagnostic, or emit the rebind as an assignment to the first slot. Probe `/tmp/agents/r3/dupname.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A nested `def` does not capture a name only its own LAMBDA reads.** [`nested-def-lambda-only-capture-missing`] `def sib(): f = lambda: len(xs); return f()` inside a function that owns `xs` builds a lambda with no capture-default over a name the enclosing def never captured: g++ reports `'xs' is not captured`. A nested def's capture set comes from the name references its body's statements make, and a lambda withholds its body from that walk because it is its own scope -- so the name reaches neither capture list. Probe `/tmp/agents/task2/siblam.py`; reproduces at `21dcef707b` (the capture formula is unchanged there). Found 2026-09-17 checking whether `TpyNestedDef.captured_names` needs a lambda-aware fallback -- it does not, because this shape does not compile either way. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (valid source rejected) Importing one module under multiple names loses earlier bindings.** [`duplicate-module-import-alias`]
  With a module `store` defining `count`, `import store` followed by
  `import store as alias` rejects a function returning `store.count` with
  `Undefined variable: 'store'`. CPython keeps both names bound to the same
  module. The parser's module-keyed alias map retains only one local name,
  and its top-level import list deduplicates by module. These paths are
  unchanged by M2.10. Fixing import registration is separate from MIR's
  qualified global identities and needs `/tpy-fix-bug` analysis of aliases,
  repeated imports, dotted modules and import initialization.

- **[MED medium] (silent wrong result) Imported scalar bindings track later rebinding in the defining module.** [`imported-scalar-binding-tracks-foreign-rebind`]
  With `store.count = 1`, `from store import count as saved`, followed by
  `store.reset()` setting count to 9, CPython retains saved=1 while TPy reads
  9. Bool bindings have the same divergence. The emitted imported-name read
  and `store.count` both name the defining C++ global; Python's import binds
  the current value independently. Reexported attributes have the same risk.
  Reproduced with native execution and CPython during M2.10; the relevant
  emission paths are unchanged from master. Distinct from the view-lifetime
  defect `BUGS.md#imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`.
  M2.10 excludes from-import bindings and reexported module attributes.
  Fixing import storage and initialization needs a separate `/tpy-fix-bug`
  analysis across scalar, reference, tuple, view and reexport bindings.

- **[MED small] (valid source rejected) A record-union local cannot be initialized directly from self.** [`self-record-union-initializer`]
  In an ordinary `Cell` method, `saved: Cell | Other = self` fails THIR lowering
  at `decl.ptr_union_source`, even for eligible plain records. The equivalent
  typed union initialized from a record parameter is supported; an Optional
  local initialized from self also compiles. The union declaration source
  selector in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` does not admit the receiver form.
  Reseating a union to self similarly fails `decl.union_reseat_source`; an
  Optional initialized to None then assigned self fails `decl.opt_reseat_source`.
  Audit receiver identity, value-versus-pointer form and readonly propagation
  across declarations, assignments, methods and constructors before extending
  the shared selector. M2.8 pins this existing source gate and excludes the
  shape; fixing source admission is outside its analysis-only scope.
  Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Copying a readonly record-union parameter into a local drops pointee constness.** [`readonly-record-union-local-copy`]
  With ordinary `Cell` and `Other` records holding `value: int32` and an
  `__init__` that assigns it, this function passes frontend analysis:

  ```python
  def observe(current: readonly[Cell | Other], other: Cell) -> int32:
      saved = current
      other.value = 12
      if isinstance(saved, Cell):
          return saved.value
      return 0
  ```

  Import `int32` and `readonly` from `tpy`. The parameter emits
  `::tpy::Union<const Cell*, const Other*>`, but `saved` emits
  `::tpy::Union<Cell*, Other*> saved = current;`, which cannot convert
  without dropping constness. The narrowed local also selects `Cell*`.
  Spelling the parameter `readonly[Cell] | readonly[Other]` has the same
  failure. CPython returns 12 for `observe(cell, cell)`; directly narrowing
  `current` without copying it also works in TPy and observes the shared
  mutation. Preserve the selected source capability through local union
  binding and extraction; audit inferred constness and sibling transfer
  sites rather than adding a cast. Distinct from the call-admission gap
  `BUGS.md#readonly-union-arg-at-inferred-const-slot`.
  Confirmed by generated C++ and `g++ -fsyntax-only` during M2.5 design
  probes on M2.4's merged tree (`f22952127f`). Deferred with user approval;
  this source shape remains outside proposed M2.5 coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Reassigning a scalar-union parameter writes through its const-reference parameter slot.** [`scalar-union-parameter-reassign-const`]
  With `int32` imported from `tpy`:

  ```python
  def scalar(current: bool | int32) -> int32:
      saved = current
      current = True
      if isinstance(saved, int32):
          return saved
      return 0
  ```

  The signature emits `const ::tpy::Union<bool, int32_t>& current`, then
  the body emits `current = true;`. C++ rejects assignment through the
  const reference. CPython's `scalar(int32(7))` returns 7: `saved` retains
  its value while the local parameter binding changes. Copying `current`
  into a separate local and reassigning that local works in TPy.
  Reconcile the union parameter convention with parameter-rebinding
  storage; simply removing const would incorrectly mutate caller storage.
  Audit value-union parameter reassignment alongside other wrapper and
  callable positions. Confirmed by generated C++ and `g++ -fsyntax-only`
  during M2.5 design probes on M2.4's merged tree (`f22952127f`). Deferred
  with user approval; parameter reseats remain outside proposed M2.5
  coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A tuple literal combining a mutable record local and a readonly record parameter is rejected.** [`readonly-record-tuple-literal-rejected`]
  With a `Cell` class whose constructor assigns its `int32` field `value`:

  ```python
  def example(source: readonly[Cell]) -> int32:
      local = Cell(1)
      pair = (local, source)
      local.value = 9
      return pair[0].value
  ```

  THIR lowering rejects the tuple declaration at
  `stmt.var_decl:decl.tuple_literal_shape`; the scalar bindings work.
  CPython, using the TPy annotation stubs, returns 9. A tuple containing
  only the mutable local, `(local,)`, lowers; mutation after capture must
  remain visible through that tuple. Preserve each element's access and
  alias semantics when extending tuple-literal admission, and audit the
  declaration, hoist, parameter and return siblings. This fails before MIR
  construction and is distinct from the auto-copy metadata defect
  `BUGS.md#readonly-auto-tuple-copy-fact`.
  Confirmed during M3.11 probes on 2026-09-21; deferred for a separate fix
  with user approval. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW medium] (latent THIR metadata) Auto copies of readonly borrowed tuples can claim mutable payloads.** [`readonly-auto-tuple-copy-fact`]
  For `def inspect(pair: tuple[Cell, int32], writer: Cell): saved = pair; writer.value = 7; return saved[0].value`, inferred deep constness can emit `const std::tuple<const Cell*, int32_t>& pair`; the `auto saved = pair` copy preserves those const pointers, but `THIRVarDecl.tuple_layout` claims a mutable Cell payload. Explicit whole-tuple readonly and alias chains have the same mismatch in free functions, methods and constructors. The `decl.btuple_alias` producer in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` consults `const_borrow_tuple_locals`, whose `ensure_borrow_tuple_const` deliberately records only reassigned/hoisted bindings. Mutable parameter copies and mixed-access annotated elements remain correct. M2.7 MIR rejects the mismatched copy (`payload copy type or access mismatch`), so this neither changes emitted C++ nor admits unsafe analysis. Do not fix only the first parameter hop or broaden the existing const set without auditing its rendering/admission consumers; preserve the selected per-element source capabilities through all auto-copy chains. Related to, but distinct from, the tuple-unpack fact below. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (latent THIR metadata) Optional record tuple-unpack reads lose the selected readonly capability.** [`optional-tuple-unpack-readonly-fact`]
  Unpacking an Optional record from a const tuple emits `const Cell*`, but
  subsequent `THIRName.optional_read` facts describe a mutable
  `THIRBorrowedRecord` (`readonly=False`). Minimal source:

  ```python
  from tpy import int32

  class Cell:
      value: int32

      def __init__(self, value: int32):
          self.value = value

  def read(pair: tuple[int32, Cell | None]) -> int32:
      n, item = pair
      if item is not None:
          return item.value
      return n
  ```

  The tuple parameter is inferred const; both the presence-test read and
  the narrowed field-receiver read of `item` carry the wrong capability.
  A chained source also reproduces it: `n, item = holders[0].pair` with
  `holders: readonly[list[Holder]]` and
  `Holder.pair: tuple[int32, Cell | None]`.
  Tuple-unpack lowering in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` records the target
  in `lc.pointers` and selects `const Cell*` in `target_cpps`, without
  recording that constness in `lc.const_locals`. Optional read-fact
  production in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` consequently loses it.
  Generated C++ remains correct, and MIR currently rejects tuple unpack
  for the whole body, so these facts do not admit an unsafe MIR body.
  Fix and test capability propagation before admitting this shape to MIR;
  audit sibling unpack paths and existing consumers of `lc.const_locals`
  before changing the shared context. Confirmed before and after the
  master merge (`3d041b21d8`, `b4f5d1e8a9`); recorded for a separate fix
  with user approval. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, toolchain-caught) Immediate field access through a walrus tuple uses value access on a pointer.** [`walrus-tuple-immediate-field-access`]
  With a record `Cell` holding `value: int32`,
  `print((saved := (current,))[0].value)` emits `.value` on the `Cell*`
  returned by `std::get<0>`, and the C++ compiler rejects it. CPython prints
  the field normally. Reading a scalar member of a mixed walrus tuple and
  accessing its record member later through `saved` avoids this immediate
  projection path. Fix the tuple-element receiver access classification;
  this is separate from tuple capture loan registration. Found during the
  M2.3 prerequisite audit; deferred with user approval.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) Forwarding an `Fn` parameter to a non-storing named helper is rejected by THIR's callable argument gate.** [`fn-parameter-named-forwarding-rejected`]
  `def relay(f: Fn[[], int32]) -> int32: return f()` and
  `def use(f: Fn[[], int32]) -> int32: return relay(f)` pass semantic analysis,
  but `use(lambda: 3)` rejects at the forwarding call with
  `expr.call:call.arg_shape.other_callabletype`. CPython prints `3`; neither
  helper stores or returns the callable, so this is not the designed restriction
  on escaping `Fn` values. Replacing both parameter annotations with `Callable`
  admits the corresponding forwarding shape. The rejection comes from the
  argument-admission fallback in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`; fixing it must check
  templated callable argument lowering and forwarding lifetime/ownership, not
  simply remove the gate. Reproducer: the two definitions above, imported
  `Fn`/`int32` from `tpy`, followed by `print(use(lambda: 3))`. Confirmed at
  `d9c5173358` during the callable-contract feasibility pass, independently of
  any proposed admission rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) A generic method calling a `Callable` with an open-type argument can force that argument const.** [`generic-method-callable-param-forced-const`] `def invoke(self, cb: Callable[[T], None], x: T): cb(x)` inside `Runner[T]`, instantiated at a mutable reference type such as `Cell`, emits `readonly_form_t<T>` for `x` although the callback needs `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` (`const Cell&` versus `Cell&`); C++ compilation fails while CPython runs. Direct callable fields and indexed callable fields have the same failure; the free-function twin works. Callable argument mutation tracking deliberately skips open `T` (`sema/calls.py`), then an inferred-readonly method forces parameter constness (`sema/functions.py`, `param_const.py`). These paths predate indexed callable-field support. Fixing this requires reconciling generic callable mutation and method const inference, including the existing generic combinator corpus, rather than changing field dispatch. Related to `BUGS.md#generic-ref-param-drops-const` and the `Wrap[T]`/`cmp_to_key` readonly-receiver entry, but this failure involves an independent method argument. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/p03_safety/{named_method,direct_generic,named_generic}.py`, measured 2026-09-16. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) A lambda body cannot materialize a temporary for a mutable-reference call argument.** [`lambda-body-reference-argument-temp`] `f: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: cb([1])`, where `cb: Callable[[list[int32]], int32]`, rejects at `expr.lambda:lambda.body:expr.call:call.arg_shape.container`; the same call in an ordinary function body works. Lambda expression lowering has no argument-temporary flush point. Named, direct-field and indexed callable spellings now share that existing gate, rather than some reaching C++ with an invalid rvalue-to-reference binding. General lambda-body temporary storage and its lifetime need a separate lowering change, not a per-callee exception. Pinned by `tpyc/thir/test_computed_callable_args.py`.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) Indexing a container field directly from a record-returning call hits the shared receiver gate.** [`call-rooted-container-field-index`] `def get(a: App) -> App: return a` followed by `get(a).values[0]`, where `values: list[int32]`, rejects at `subscript.recv.field_chain`; binding `b = get(a)` first permits `b.values[0]`. This also limits `get(a).callbacks[0](x)` after indexed callable-field disambiguation is fixed. Semantic analysis accepts the receiver and must analyze it only once; the remaining gap is the common THIR container-field receiver admission, shared by reads and writes, rather than callable invocation. Expanding that family requires checking borrowed versus owning call results and temporary lifetimes across its consumers. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/p03_call_rooted_container.py`, measured 2026-09-16. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A ternary whose arms are record-valued rvalues cannot be the body of a lambda or nested `def`.** [`closure-body-record-ternary-rejected`] `direct(lambda k: Node(0) if flag else Node(1), n)` at an `f: Fn[[Node], Own[Node]]` slot stops with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.lambda)*, and the same body spelled as a nested `def` (`return Node(0) if flag else Node(1)`) stops with `stmt.return:return.record_source.TpyIfExpr.storage` -- so both closure spellings refuse it and there is no way to write the shape. CPython runs it and prints `0`. The neighbours compile: a scalar ternary lambda body (`lambda n: n if n > 0 else 0`) runs, and so does a record ternary of LVALUE arms (`lambda k: ns[0] if flag else k` at a borrow contract), so the gap is a record-typed ternary with a non-lvalue arm (a constructor call, or `copy(k)`) rather than ternaries in closures generally. A `copy()` call alone in a lambda body is fine (`lambda k: copy(k)` at an `Own` contract runs), so the two lower independently and only their composition rejects. Also blocks the natural remedy for a closure with mixed borrow/fresh return paths ("copy on the borrow path"), which is exactly this shape. Probes `/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/tern/{t1,t4,t5,t6,t7}.py`, measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (accepts invalid, silent) `sorted` / `min` / `max` take `key` POSITIONALLY, where CPython makes it keyword-only -- so a program that compiles and runs under TPy is not valid Python.** [`key-arg-accepted-positionally`] `sorted(xs, negate)` prints `[3, 2, 1]`, `min(3, 1, negate)` prints `3` and `max(3, 1, negate)` prints `1` under TPy; CPython over the same source raises `TypeError: sorted expected 1 argument, got 2` (and reads the extra argument of `min`/`max` as one more value to compare). The stubs declare `key` as an ordinary positional parameter (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_funcs.py:525` for `sorted`, `:125`/`:131`/`:174`/`:180` for `min`/`max`), and nothing marks it keyword-only. The over-accept is not even self-consistent: the positional form takes a named function but rejects a lambda (`sorted(xs, lambda n: -n)` -> *Lambda parameter types cannot be inferred without context*), while `key=` accepts both. Fix shape: a keyword-only marker on those stub params, so the positional spelling gets a located error naming `key=`. Probes `/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/p_key2.py` (accepted) and `p_key3.py` (the `key=` spelling, parity-clean), measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) An `Fn` contract whose result is a REFERENCE-typed Optional is unsatisfiable: the contract states the STORAGE form (`std::optional<Node>`) while the callee and the contract body's own call-result local both render the BORROW form (`Node*`).** [`fn-contract-reference-optional-result`] `def find(f: Fn[[Node], Node | None], a: Node) -> int32:` with a body `r = f(a)` / `if r is not None: return r.v` emits, and both ways of feeding it fail the C++ build. A `def` callee (`def pick(n: Node) -> Node | None`) fails the `requires` clause, with no TPy source location -- the diagnostic names only the generated `.hpp`/`.cpp`:

  ```
  error: no matching function for call to 'find(Node* (&)(Node&), Node&)'
  note: constraints not satisfied
  note: '__fn(__a0)' does not satisfy return-type-requirement
     17 |       { __fn(__a0) } -> std::convertible_to<std::optional<Node>>;
  ```

  A lambda (`find(lambda n: n, a)`) passes the clause, because the lambda's own return is rendered in the contract's storage form -- `[](Node& n) -> std::optional<Node> { return n; }`, itself a silent COPY of a node CPython would alias -- and then the contract's BODY rejects the same mismatch from the other side:

  ```
  error: cannot convert 'std::optional<Node>' to 'Node*' in initialization
     41 |     Node* r = f(a);
  ```

  So no callee spelling satisfies the contract. Cause: `_gen_fn_template_parts` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:357`) spells the constraint from `fn_type.return_type.to_cpp()`, the bare storage form, while a `def` returning `Node | None` and the call-result local inside the `Fn` body both take the pointer borrow form -- the two halves of one contract disagree on the form. VALUE-typed Optionals are unaffected: the same shape at `Fn[[int32], int32 | None]` compiles and runs, since storage and borrow form coincide there, so the trigger is a reference-typed inner (class / `list` / `dict` / `set`). The wrapper spelled to PROPAGATE the result (`def find(f: Fn[[Node], Node | None], a: Node) -> Node | None: return f(a)`) never reaches C++ at all -- it stops at `error: in function 'find': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return)`. The designed resolution is already sliced: `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md` carries a located reject row for the reference-typed `Optional` / union callable result (no callee can satisfy `Fn[[Node], Node | None]`, and the spelling reaches C++ ill-formed today); this entry is the measured shape behind it. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fn_file_bugs/{b1b_fn_optional_local,b1d_fn_optional_lambda,b1c_fn_optional_value,b1_fn_optional_result}.py`, measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0 with `uv run tpy` (g++-14). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `Own[Callable[...]]` at a RETURN slot rejects at `return.slot_type` for every callee spelling, while the bare `Callable[...]` return it is supposed to resolve to works.** [`own-callable-return-rejected`] `def make() -> Own[Callable[[int32], int32]]` stops with `error: in function 'make': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:return.slot_type)` whether the returned value is an annotated closure local (`f: Callable[[int32], int32] = lambda i: i + 1` / `return f`), a module-level function reference (`return inc`), or a nested `def`. Dropping the `Own` wrapper makes all four spellings -- including the direct `return lambda i: i + 1` -- compile and run, printing `2`. `Own[T]` at a return is defined to resolve to plain `T` (CLAUDE.md, "at a return it resolves to plain `T`"), so the two spellings name the same slot and only one of them lowers. Cause: `ret_callable` (`tpyc/thir/lower/context.py:791`) is `isinstance(rt, CallableType) and not rt.is_template`, and the `Own` peel sitting right beside it (`own_value_scalar`, `:797`) covers only scalars, `char` and protocol-`auto` slots -- so an `OwnType` over a `CallableType` matches no `ret_supported` row and the return arm is never entered. The contextual-inference half is fixed: a direct lambda now receives its parameter types through `Own[Callable[...]]`, including at argument and container bindings. The return still reaches the existing THIR return-slot rejection; the remaining defect is lowering, not inference. Returning a `Callable` is documented as the supported shape -- `docs/CLOSURES_CALLABLE_DESIGN.md:155` rejects `-> Fn[...]` with "cannot return Fn (use Callable)" -- and the bare form honours that; it is the owning respelling of the same return that has no lowering. Distinct from BUGS.md#move-only-closure-in-callable-slot, which is a bare `Callable` return whose closure MOVE-captures a non-copyable value (a C++-level `std::function` copyability failure, not a lowering gate). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fn_file_bugs/{b2_return_callable_own,b2b_local_then_return,b2g_own_funcref,b2h_own_nested_def}.py` (rejecting) and `{b2c_bare_callable,b2f_bare_lambda_direct,b2d_funcref,b2e_nested_def,b2j_own_param_funcref}.py` (working), measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Inside a generator or `async def`, `except StopIteration` over an `@error_return` call is refused whenever the `try` needs frame states of its own.** [`frame-try-next-error-return-miscompiles`] `def my_zip2[A, B](ia: Iterator[A], ib: Iterator[B]) -> Iterator[tuple[A, B]]` driving two iterators with `try: x = next(ia)` / `except StopIteration: break` errors at the `try` line instead of miscompiling. **The silent miscompile is CLOSED** (2026-09-15, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py` `_build_try`): it used to emit `x.emplace((*({ auto __er_1 = ::tpy::next(ia); if (!__er_1.has_value()) ::tpy::tpy_panic("unhandled error return"); &::tpy::unwrap_ref(*__er_1); })));` under a `catch (const ::tpy::StopIteration&)` that nothing throws -- exhaustion PANICKED instead of breaking, and the slot was filled from a pointer into a statement-expression local dead at the semicolon. **What remains is the feature.** Sema classifies a `ReturnException` handler as the return tier (`TpyTry.tier`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py:_classify_try_tier`); the sync emit honours it with `auto __try_tmp_2 = ::tpy::next(ia); if (!__try_tmp_2.has_value()) goto __except_1;` (the form `math.sumprod` relies on), but the resumable CFG carries `TryRegion.tier` without an edge for the failing unwrap, so it would wrap the region in a C++ `try`/`catch` that never fires -- `StopIteration` is never THROWN in TPy (`raise StopIteration` auto-promotes to an error return, and in a non-`@error_return` frame it is rejected outright), and every unwrap inside it would fall back to the unhandled (panic) disposition because `_EmitState.try_except_label` is only set by the sync `_emit_try_return`. **Exactly which shapes reject:** a DECOMPOSED try (one holding an `await`/`yield`, or a `break`/`continue` leaving it) whose body holds a call the handler catches -- sema decides that at the call-admission check (`sema/calls.py:_check_error_return_handled`) and records it on `TpyTry.handled_error_return`, which `_build_try` reads. Across generator and `async def`; `next(it)`, a user `@error_return` callee, and the discarded-call form; a frame-slot, frame-field or value target; with and without a `finally`; inside a `with` body; `yield` inside the `try` body. All of those were wrong before the reject. Unaffected (correct before and after, pinned by `tests/cases/generators/frame_try_return_exception`): a LEAF try in a frame (no suspension inside it, no transfer leaving it), a whole suspension-free loop in a frame, a DECOMPOSED try whose handler no call in the body can enter (`try: yield x / except StopIteration: pass|break|return` -- the dead catch is harmless), module level, and every sync position. **Fix shape** (the precedent is `AsyncForAdvance`, which already spells exactly this edge): give the CFG a terminator for a handled `@error_return` call -- `ok_bb` / `failed_bb`, the latter the handler entry -- splitting the try body at each such call; skip the C++ `try`/`catch` for a return-tier `TryRegion` in `_emit_case`; render the check as `if (!__try_tmp_N.has_value()) { __state = S_...; continue; }` with the bind shapes `_for_advance_parts` already enumerates. An `as`-binding handler additionally needs its `__err_opt_N` capture as a frame field. Pinned rejecting by `tests/cases/generators/error_frame_try_return_exception` (the tripwire: it fails the day the shape lowers); the `async def` twin goes through the same `_build_try` arm and is covered by the compiling `async def` sections of `tests/cases/generators/frame_try_return_exception`. Blocks writing `zip` in TPy source (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found 2026-09-13 by the combinator feasibility probe; miscompile closed 2026-09-15, reject narrowed to the handled shape the same day. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.

- **[MED small] (compiler crash on valid code) A `@dispatch` pair of GENERATOR bodies crashes sema with a bare `AssertionError`.** [`dispatch-generator-pair-sema-crash`] Two same-named `@dispatch` defs that both return `Iterator[T]` and both have a `yield` body abort the compile with `Internal error:` and no message -- `assert elem_type is not None` in `_analyze_yield` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py:3895`): the function whose body is being analyzed has no `generator_yield_type`. Reproduces both for a pair differing in a PARAM TYPE (`pred: Fn[[T], bool]` vs `pred: None`, `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/px_dispatch.py`) and for one differing in ARITY (`.../px_dispatch2.py`), so it is generator bodies under `@dispatch` generally, not the `None` param. `typing.overload` is the other spelling of an overload set (`docs/OVERLOAD_DESIGN.md`) and was not probed for this shape; either way an unlocated crash is the wrong answer. Blocks the `filter(None, it)` variant of a TPy-source `filter` (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found 2026-09-13 by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A comprehension unpacking a POINTER-TUPLE yield skips the `tuple_elem_ref` deref the `for` statement applies.** [`comp-unpack-pointer-tuple-skips-deref`] `[n.v for i, n in my_enumerate(nodes)]`, where `my_enumerate` is a TPy generator yielding `tuple[int32, T]` (rendered `std::tuple<int32_t, ::tpy::val_or_ptr_t<T>>`, hence `std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>` at `T = Node`), emits `auto& n = std::get<1>(__tup_1);` and g++ rejects `n.v` with *request for member 'v' in 'n', which is of pointer type 'Node*'*. The `for`-STATEMENT over the same generator is correct in the same TU -- `auto&& n = ::tpy::unwrap_ref(::tpy::tuple_elem_ref(std::get<1>(__tup_1)));` -- so it is the comprehension's unpack head that misses the normalization, not the yield form. Sibling of BUGS.md#comp-dict-items-ref-value, which is the same unpack head over `d.items()`; a fix should cover both faces. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/nest_comp.py` (built with `tpyc -b`, error confirmed 2026-09-13). Blocks consuming a TPy-source `enumerate`/`zip` from a comprehension (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) `list(gen)` over a generator yielding a POINTER TUPLE pushes the borrow form into a storage-form vector.** [`collect-pointer-tuple-into-storage-vector`] `list(my_enumerate(nodes))` renders `::tpy::construct<std::vector<std::tuple<int32_t, Node>>>(my_enumerate<Node>(nodes))` over a generator whose yield type is `std::tuple<int32_t, ::tpy::val_or_ptr_t<T>>`, and `collect`'s `result.push_back(unwrap_ref_move(*__r))` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/ranges.hpp:188`) is handed a `std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>`: *no matching function for call to `std::vector<std::tuple<int, Node> >::push_back(std::tuple<int, Node*>)`*. `unwrap_ref_move` normalizes a whole ref-wrapped element, but nothing lifts a tuple ELEMENT from the borrow form to the storage form at this seam; the precedent that does is `tuple_to_storage` / `tuple_to_storage_move` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/format.hpp:886` / `:905`), already used where a borrow-form tuple reaches an owning slot. `construct`'s other arm, `from_range`, assigns straight from the range's iterators with no element conversion either, so the lift belongs at the `construct` seam rather than in one arm. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/nest_listctor.py` (built with `tpyc -b`, error confirmed 2026-09-13). Found by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) `float32` arithmetic with an `int` (BigInt) VARIABLE operand emits `static_cast<float>(BigInt)`, which does not compile.** [`float32-bigint-operand-static-cast`] `a = float32(1.5); n: int = 2; a + n` renders `(a) + static_cast<float>(n)` and g++ rejects the cast from `tpy::BigInt`; every float32 operator overload taking `other: int` (`+ - * / // % **` and the reflected forms) spells the same `static_cast<float>({0})`, so all of them fail with an int VARIABLE, while an int LITERAL operand takes a different path and works. The `float32.__add__(self, other: int) -> float32` stub overload admits the operand, so the fix is the operand render: route a BigInt through its explicit conversion (`static_cast<float>(n.to_double())` or the BigInt-to-float helper the `float` operators use). Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the scalar-rename followups.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) The synthesized async-factory wrapper lambda `std::move`s every non-value param, so an `async def` with a plain reference-type param (no `Own`) passed as a callable value fails the C++ build.** [`async-factory-wrapper-moves-borrow-param`] `async def runit(xs: list[int32], n: int32) -> int32` (an ordinary borrow param plus a scalar) passed as the `f` argument of `async def drive(f: Callable[[list[int32], int32], Own[Cancellable[int32]]], xs: list[int32])`, whose body spawns it with `asyncio.create_task(f(xs, 4))`: the function ref is coerced to the `Callable` slot, `_async_factory_wrap_cpp_facts` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) synthesizes the coroutine-factory wrapper lambda, and g++-13 rejects it --

  ```
  error: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'std::vector<int>&' to an rvalue
         of type 'std::remove_reference<std::vector<int>&>::type' {aka 'std::vector<int>'}
     63 | __sub_0.emplace([](std::vector<int32_t>& __a0, int32_t __a1) -> std::unique_ptr<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>> { return ::tpy::make_adapter<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>>(::tpyapp::factory_listparam::runit(std::move(__a0), __a1)); }, (*data));
  note: initializing argument 1 of '__coro_runit runit(std::vector<int>&, int32_t)'
  ```

  Cause: the forward loop spells `std::move(__aN)` whenever `isinstance(ptype, OwnType) or not ptype.is_value_type()`, and the second disjunct is wrong for a borrow. `CallableType._callable_param_cpp` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) renders a non-`Own` reference-type hint param as a MUTABLE lvalue ref `T&`, and the frame factory the lambda calls takes `T&` as well, so the move turns the lambda's own lvalue parameter into an rvalue that cannot bind. Every non-`Own` reference-type param is affected (`list`/`dict`/`set`/class); `Own[T]` params and value-typed params are correct. Fix shape: move only for `OwnType` params -- the owned form the callee consumes -- and forward a borrow by bare name so it stays an lvalue. Toolchain-caught, never silent. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/review_adl/factory_listparam.py`, built with `uv run tpy --cxx gcc-13` on 2026-09-14 (0.6.0.dev0). Pre-existing and independent of the ADL free-callee fix: that fix changed only the wrapper's callee SPELLING, while the forward loop and the `T&` lambda parameter it cannot bind are byte-identical before it, so the shape fails the same way on master. Adjacent with a DISTINCT trigger: BUGS.md#async-fn-borrow-param-own-hint is the mirror case -- there the callable HINT says `Own[T]` while the async fn's param is a borrow, and the fix is a sema rejection of the coercion; here hint and callee AGREE on the borrow and it is the wrapper's own render that is wrong, so neither fix covers the other. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the ADL free-callee fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A literal-specialized overload set mangles its callee at the CALL site but not at the DEFINITION site, so a `@dispatch` set over `Literal` params never builds, and an `@overload` one never builds across modules.** [`literal-dispatch-overload-unmangled-definition`] Two faces of one gap between `literal_mangled_name` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:171`) and the emitters that spell a definition.
  - **(a) `@dispatch`, any module.** Two bodied same-named variants with `Literal` params (`/tmp/agents/review_adl2/lit_main.py`: `pick(m: Literal["a"])` / `pick(m: Literal["b"])`) emit `int32_t pick(std::string_view m)` TWICE -- g++ reports `redefinition of 'int32_t tpyapp::lit_main::pick(std::string_view)'` -- while every call site spells `pick__lit_a` / `pick__lit_b` (`free_literal_mangled_name`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:3807`), which then do not exist. A `@dispatch` variant is self-contained (no stub/impl pair), so it never reaches `_gen_literal_specialized_function` (`functions.py:1172`), the one emitter that renames a definition; it takes the ordinary per-function path and keeps the plain name. The declarations in the header collide the same way.
  - **(b) `@overload`, cross-module only.** The stub/impl form DOES mangle both definition and declaration (`litmod2.hpp` declares only `mode__lit_r` / `mode__lit_w`), but the importing module's re-export line is spelled from the SOURCE name: `using ::tpyapp::litmod2::mode;` -> `'mode' has not been declared in 'tpyapp::litmod2'` (`/tmp/agents/review_adl2/lit_main2.py`). Same-module `@overload` is fine (`tests/cases/calls/overload_literal_bool`), and the call-site spelling is right in both cases -- only the `using` is wrong; it should name every mangled specialization (or the re-export should be dropped for a literal-only set, since callers spell the qualified mangled name anyway).

  Both verified 2026-09-14 on 0.6.0.dev0 with `uv run tpy`.
