- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) A container-element union name at a MUTABLE union parameter slot does not compile.** [`storage-union-element-at-mutable-borrow-slot`]
  `for e in xs: bump(e)` over `xs: list[A | B]`, with `def bump(u: A | B)` mutating through `u`, emits the bare `bump(e)` while `e` is bound as the STORAGE union (`const ::tpy::Union<A, B>&`, the element form) and the slot is the mutable borrow: g++ reports `could not convert 'e' ... to 'tpy::Union<A*, B*>'`. No lowering arm wires `to_ptr_variant()` onto a storage-bound container-element name reaching a pointer-variant slot -- the CONST half of the same shape works, because the const wrap asks how the source is bound and answers `to_const_ptr_variant`. Two things are wrong at once and a fix has to settle both: the missing mutable lift, and the element binding itself -- mutation through a loop element is not credited to the container, so `xs` binds `const std::vector<...>&` and no mutable borrow of `e` exists to take. CPython runs it. Pre-existing: `231114b18e` renders the same signature and the same bare argument. No case in the corpus reaches it. Repro `/tmp/agents/constptr/storage_src.py`. Found probing the mutable-slot residual of the union const-pointee flip 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `readonly[A | B]` argument is refused at a plain non-mutating `A | B` parameter, although the two render the same type.** [`readonly-union-arg-at-inferred-const-slot`]
  `def peek(u: readonly[A | B])` calling `def total(v: A | B)` (which only discriminates `v`) rejects with `Cannot pass readonly[A | B] as mutable A | B in argument 'v'`. Since a non-mutating union parameter borrows const pointees, BOTH signatures are `::tpy::Union<const A*, const B*>` -- the call would compile and mutate nothing. The readonly rule reads the ANNOTATION, not the rendered form, so it cannot see that the callee's inferred verdict already gives the guarantee the annotation asks for. CPython runs it. `tests/cases/union/error_union_readonly_param_pass` and `error_union_readonly_method_param_pass` pin today's rejection, so lifting it changes two committed diagnostics and is a DESIGN decision, not a cleanup: the rule would have to consult the callee's const verdict (available only after Phase-2) at an argument check that runs earlier. `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` records it as a limitation. Found closing the union const-pointee flip 2026-09-10.

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) A const-bound source at a pointer-repr TUPLE ELEMENT slot does not compile.** [`const-source-at-mutable-tuple-element-slot`]
  `def inner(t: tuple[Box2 | None, int32])` emits the deep-const element form in its signature (`const std::tuple<const Box2*, int32_t>&` -- a tuple element has always borrowed const, `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`), but a caller building the tuple renders the MUTABLE element: `def outer(obj: Box2): return inner((obj, 5))` emits `inner(std::tuple<Box2*, int32_t>{&(obj), 5});` out of a `const Box2& obj`, and g++ refuses with `no matching function for call to 'std::tuple<Box2*, int>::tuple(<brace-enclosed initializer list>)'`. The signature reads the slot's const-ness and the tuple-LITERAL argument render does not, so the two disagree about one ABI. Same class as the union-parameter const-pointee defect fixed in 2026-09-10's borrow-form work, at the tuple-element position, and NOT fixed by it: that fix puts the const on a union's pointees, while this render never asks the slot at all. Reproduces identically on `231114b18e` and after the union flip (rendered in a detached base worktree, byte-identical). CPython runs it. Fix shape: the tuple-literal arg render must take its element spelling from the slot, the way the union arg lift takes `deep_const_borrow_params` -- the same *one call-arg position does not thread a verdict every other position threads* family as `BUGS.md#union-ret-decl-blocks-arg-temp`. Repro `/tmp/agents/ptrunion/tuple_elem.py`. Found probing the tuple-element position for the union const-pointee flip 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An argument that needs a hoisted temp is refused when the call's result initializes a pointer-variant UNION local.** [`union-ret-decl-blocks-arg-temp`] `r = uret(A(2))` with `def uret(u: A | B) -> A | B` rejects at `expr.call:call.arg_shape.union`, while the identical argument at the identical slot lowers when the callee returns a scalar (`s = scalar(A(1))` with `def scalar(u: A | B) -> int32` hoists its `__tmp_N` and runs). The difference is the declaration, not the argument: a union-returning call's result declares a ptr-variant local through its own statement lowering, which does not thread the flush position into the argument gate, so the ctor-temp row is unreachable there. Binding the argument first (`a = A(2); r = uret(a)`) compiles. Sibling of `BUGS.md#resumable-arg-temp-no-flush` -- same shape, a different position that offers no flush point. Repro `/tmp/agents/unionarg/verify/q04_ctorarg_unionret.py`. Found while fixing the narrowed-union-arg lift 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) The pointer-variant union RETURN arm takes the address of a const-bound name without the const-pointee spelling, so a `readonly` source at a union return does not build.** [`union-return-addr-of-const-blind`]
  `member_lvalue_ret` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) picks the returned variant's spelling from the declared return type alone and never asks how the returned NAME is bound: returning a `readonly[Dog]` (or `readonly[Pet]`) parameter at `-> Pet | Cat` emits `::tpy::Union<Cat*, Pet*> give_union(const Dog& d) { return &(d); }`, and g++ rejects with `could not convert 'const Dog*' to 'tpy::Union<Cat*, Pet*>'`. Pre-existing on the exact-member path -- a `readonly[Pet]` source at `-> Pet | Cat` failed the same way before -- and the subclass-or-equal widening of that arm added the subclass-under-readonly spelling as a second way to reach it. This entry is the direct NAME-source RETURN path; the argument-position and field-source faces of the same const union are filed on their own (`BUGS.md#storage-union-element-at-mutable-borrow-slot` for the element-name-at-a-mutable-slot face, and the const-blind member lift is face (4) of the un-slugged "storage-form union value at a borrow position" entry below). CPython runs it. Reproducer:
  ```python
  class Pet: pass
  class Cat(Pet): pass
  class Dog(Pet): pass
  def give_union(d: readonly[Dog]) -> Pet | Cat: return d
  ```
  Fix shape: the return arm must decide the variant spelling from the callee's const-borrow verdict the way the argument lift does (`::tpy::Union<const Cat*, const Pet*>` as the return type when the source is const-bound), or reject with a located diagnostic instead of emitting a type the toolchain refuses. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (loud C++ error, or a SILENT wrong value when the global's slot dereferences) A nested `def`'s fresh local -- or its PARAMETER -- named like a MODULE GLOBAL is emitted against the global's slot.** [`nested-local-shadows-module-global`] `def outer(): def inner(): a = 1.5; print(a)` with a module-level `a = "..."` renders the closure body as `a = 1.5;` against the global's `std::string` slot -- no local decl, so g++ rejects the print (`print_float(std::string&)`), and with a same-typed global the closure would silently overwrite it. The PARAMETER spelling needs no assignment at all: `def ident(n: int32) -> int32: return n` nested in a function, with a module-level `n = Holder(5)`, emits `return (*n);` -- the global's pointer slot deref applied to the parameter -- and g++ rejects it (*invalid type argument of unary '*'*). EVERY read of such a parameter takes the deref, a bare `return n` included, and a parameter whose name matches no global renders correctly. When the parameter's type HAS a `__deref__` the deref is well-formed and the program is SILENTLY wrong: `def show(n: Box[int32])` with a module-level `n = Box(7)` prints `7` where CPython prints `Box(7)`. CPython makes both the local and the parameter bindings of the nested function (no `global` declaration). The unpack form `a, b = r` inside the nested def takes the same wrong turn (bare `a = std::get<0>(__tup_1);`). The module-global twin of [`nested-local-shadow-requires-nonlocal`]: there the enclosing-local collision rejects, here the module-global one miscompiles. Repros `/tmp/agents/nested_global_shadow/assign.py` (plain assign), `unpack.py` (unpack), `/tmp/agents/safety/free_shadow.py` (parameter, loud), `/tmp/agents/safety/box_shadow.py` (parameter, silent; both parameter repros reproduce at `21dcef707b`). One spelling of the parameter form was masked until 2026-09-17 inside a constructor, by the `super().__init__()` false reject the tracking-state node-identity fix closed. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong value) A nested `def`'s fresh local named like a FRAME FIELD of the enclosing generator or `async def` reads and writes that field.** [`nested-local-shadows-frame-field`] `def gen(): for i in range(2): w = i * 100; yield w` then `def helper(): for j in range(2): w = j; ...` nested in `gen` and called after the loop: `helper`'s `w` gets no C++ declaration of its own, so its loop writes the enclosing frame's `w` (the implicit `this->w`) and the outer read after `helper()` comes back `4` where CPython prints `200` (verified 2026-09-14 with `uv run tpy`; a plain pre-loop local crossing a `yield` collides the same way, so the defect predates the loop-hoist work, which only widened the set of names that become frame fields). The frame-field twin of `BUGS.md#nested-local-shadows-module-global`: the nested def's lowering resolves an unqualified name against the enclosing frame before its own locals. **Fix shape:** a nested def's own bindings shadow the frame's in its lowering scope, as they shadow the enclosing function's locals in sema. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A nested function's local assignment is mistaken for an outer write requiring `nonlocal`.** [`nested-local-shadow-requires-nonlocal`]
  Inside `for b in range(3)`, define `def local() -> int: b = 10; return b` and accumulate `b + local()` in the enclosing function. CPython prints `33`; TPy rejects the inner assignment with `Cannot assign to 'b' in nested function without 'nonlocal' declaration`. The declaration and assignment guards in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` check membership in `outer_scope_locals` without allowing a fresh shadowing local; these guards are unchanged at session base `2bd8dec8b6`. Adding `nonlocal` would change the program's meaning and is not a repair. A same-named nested parameter can exercise the scope inverse without this assignment. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_closure_shadow.py`, logs `range-closure-shadow-cpy.log` and `range-closure-shadow-frontend.log`. Separate from range induction and escaping-closure capture semantics. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A suspension-free range loop in an async or generator body rejects a writable target.** [`async-no-await-range-target-write-rejected`]
  An `async def` containing `for i in range(5): i = 0` without an `await` rejects at `foreach.var_shadow`; adding a suspension inside the loop takes the existing frame-counter path and compiles. CPython accepts both and runs five iterations. This is the no-suspension resumable admission path, separate from ordinary THIR range induction. Observed during `/tmp/agents/analysis-loops/` triage and rechecked after the range fix in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_noawait.py` (`range-noawait-frontend.log`, `range-noawait-cpy.log`); the accepted suspending form is retained as an inverse in range regression coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
  A generator with the writable loop before its only `yield count` hits the same `foreach.var_shadow` rejection; CPython yields `3`. The loop has no suspension even though the enclosing function is a generator. Exact witness `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_generator_leaf.py`, logs `range-generator-leaf-frontend.log` and `range-generator-leaf-cpy.log`. A yield inside the loop uses the independent frame counter and remains covered by the passing regression.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A nonlocal closure defined before the first later loop binding cannot capture that name.** [`nonlocal-before-first-loop-binding-rejected`]
  `def change(): nonlocal i; i = 10` declared before `for i in range(3): change()` inside the enclosing function rejects with `No binding for nonlocal 'i' found in enclosing scope`. CPython recognizes the loop target as an enclosing local and accepts the program. An already bound target uses existing hoisted storage; this forward declaration instead needs scope discovery before closure analysis. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/analysis-loops/closure_before.py`, frontend diagnostic `closure_before.err`. This is distinct from escaping-closure late binding and does not require changing accepted range induction. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH medium] (silent divergence) A generator without cleanup can resume after an exception escapes its body.** [`generator-resumes-after-escaping-exception`]
  In `def stream() -> Iterator[int]: yield 1; yield fail(); print("continued"); yield 3`, where `fail()` raises `ValueError`, retain the iterator and catch that error around the second `next()`. CPython leaves it exhausted: the next pull raises `StopIteration`. TPy instead executes `print("continued")` and yields `3`. The generated frame stores the post-yield resume state before evaluating the throwing expression; `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` only emits the enclosing catch that marks `S_DONE` when `_dtor_cleanup_cases(cfg)` is nonempty. This emitter behavior is unchanged from session base `2bd8dec8b6`; the standalone witness imports no math and uses no nested records. Confirmed with native g++-14 execution and CPython in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/generator_exception_reuse.py` (logs `generator-reuse-native.log` and `generator-reuse-cpy.log`). Found during math propagation review; cleanup-bearing generators and coroutine siblings require their own audit. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Passing a scalar member into a value-union parameter inside an assertion rejects.** [`assert-value-union-argument-temp`]
  With `def echo(value: float | str) -> float`, `assert echo(9.0) == 9.0` fails at `expr.call:call.arg_shape.union`; the same program passes CPython without importing math. Binding a typed `float | str` local before the assertion uses the existing union pass-through and compiles. The scalar-to-value-union argument row requires an argument temporary, but `TpyAssert` calls `_lower_truthy` without temporary-flush rights; the logical truthiness recursion also drops those rights rather than forwarding them. Both members here are value types, so this is distinct from the pointer-union literal defects. Reproduced by `/tmp/agents/session-triage/value_union_assert.py` while authoring math coverage. The unprobed logical-condition siblings need an audit with the shared condition-lowering fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An integer-literal `match` subject is rejected instead of matching integer patterns.** [`match-int-literal-subject-rejected`]
  `match 10:` with `case 10:` fails with `match subject must be a union, enum, primitive, record, or Optional type, got 'IntLiteral(10)'`; CPython accepts it. Binding the literal to a local before the match compiles. The same rejection surfaces when matching a target from a literal iterable: `for selector in [0, 1, 2]: match selector:` reports `IntLiteral(0)` during the math exception-policy case, before code generation or execution. The match admission check needs to handle the literal's primitive type consistently; changing loop induction or math exception adapters cannot repair it. Original evidence: `/tmp/agents/analysis-loops/`; re-observed in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/math-case-targeted-2.log`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (invalid generated C++, loud) Distinct free functions and flat-record methods can receive the same resumable frame name.** [`flat-resumable-frame-name-collision`]
  `async def A_c()` and `class A: async def c(self)` both emit a complete `struct __coro_A_c` in one module; `A_B.c` and `A.B_c` both emit `__coro_A_B_c`. Named synchronous generators have the same collisions under `__gen_` (two yields suffice). Baseline probes pass CPython and the TPy frontend but emit duplicate complete struct definitions; no native build was run for these witnesses. The flat branch of `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py::resumable_struct_name` concatenates owner and method with underscores and omits a free-versus-method discriminator. Nested owners have a separate unambiguous encoding; fixing the legacy flat namespace requires coordinated declaration/reference naming and snapshot changes. Renaming a colliding function or method avoids the collision. Evidence: `/tmp/agents/flat-frame-collisions/`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A concrete BYTES-FAMILY member cannot be passed to a union parameter that contains it.** [`bytes-member-arg-not-lifted-into-union`] `def f(u: bytes | bytearray)` called as `f(ba)` with a `bytearray` local rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.union`, and so does a `str | String` slot fed a `str` literal. The member lift is not missing in general -- measured 2026-09-09, `int32 | A` lifts BOTH member names, and `list[int32] | A` lifts the container one -- so the gap is specific to a union with a bytes/str-family member, whose slot the arg ladder's `_union_member_lift_arg` / `_arg_ptr_union_slot` pair does not admit. The gap itself is older than the type split -- `bytearray | Rec` over a record rejects identically, and did before the split -- so what the split changed is only that the SAME-SPELLING `bytes | bytearray` sub-shape now gets far enough to reach it, the duplicate-spelling guard having refused the union outright before. The union's own machinery is fine: the isinstance arm and the `Own[union]` return both lower, and the variant discriminates correctly at runtime -- `tests/cases/bytes/distinct_spelling_union` pins that and carries the two declared-only functions this entry explains. Fix shape: widen the member-lift slot test to the bytes/str family the way it already admits records and containers. Filed with the distinct-C++-types unit 2026-09-09.


- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught; PRE-EXISTING) A bytes LITERAL at a generic record constructor's `T` slot renders the static span, which the `const T&` slot cannot bind.** [`generic-ctor-bytes-literal-span`] `class Cell[T]` with `def __init__(self, value: T)` plus `Cell[bytes](b"p")` emits `Cell<::tpy::Bytes>(::tpy::bytes_literal("p", 1))` against `explicit Cell(const T& value)` and g++ rejects (`no matching function ... Cell(tpy::BytesView)`). A bytes literal's render is target-dependent -- the owning `bytes_literal_owned` at a storage sink, the static `bytes_literal` at a view-shaped param -- and `_bytes_literal_view_slot` answers off the SUBSTITUTED param type (`bytes`, which is view-shaped at a parameter) without seeing that this particular slot spells `const T&`. Verified pre-existing on master 9577f40476 (identical error with the shared `std::vector<uint8_t>` spelling), so it is not a consequence of the type split; it became visible when a bytes rvalue started being admitted at a generic slot. `bytes(b"p")` is not a workaround (it rejects at the gate); a bytes NAME is. Fix shape: thread the const-ness of the resolved slot into the literal's form verdict, or hoist the owned temp there as the readonly slot does. Found probing the generic body positions 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid) `repr()` of a `bytes` value is rejected: `No matching overload for repr(bytes)`.** [`repr-bytes-not-representable`] `builtins.bytes` (and `bytearray`) declare no `__repr__` in `lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_bytes.py`, so neither satisfies the `Representable` protocol `repr` requires, though `print(b)` works and the runtime has had `::tpy::__repr__` overloads for both buffers all along. CPython's `repr(b"ab")` is `"b'ab'"`, which is exactly what the runtime already produces. Fix: declare `__repr__` on both stubs (`@cpp_template("::tpy::repr_of({self})")`, the shape `__hash__` already uses). Pre-existing; found probing the bytes surface 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An argument that needs a hoisted temp is refused at a RESUMABLE body's `return <call>` and `yield <call>`.** [`resumable-arg-temp-no-flush`] With `def take[T](v: T) -> bool` and `def make() -> Own[Rec]` over a record `Rec`, `yield take(make())` in a generator and `return take(make())` in an async body both reject at `expr.call:call.generic_arg_shape`, while the same `return take(make())` in a PLAIN function lowers and the two-step form (`r = take(make())` then `return r` / `yield r`) lowers in both resumable bodies. The reject is honest -- neither the frame's return nor its yield offers a statement to flush a `__tmp_N` decl into -- but both are plain positions, so the workaround is arbitrary from the user's side. The witness is a REFERENCE-typed instantiation whose call rvalue has to be bound: the str-parameter and scalar shapes this entry used to name both lower now that an instantiated body takes the instantiation's own forms, so neither is a witness any more. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/stringtype_impl/probe_move/ratref.py`. Found while covering the positions for the view-at-a-generic-slot fix 2026-09-08; re-witnessed 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (silent generated-code change from an unrelated fact) Reach analysis walks every `__dict__` a statement can reach, so a new `FunctionInfo` field holding types changes the emitted includes.** [`reach-walk-picks-up-any-functioninfo-type-field`] `_iter_typed_children` (`tpyc/sema/reach_analysis.py`) recurses into any object with a `__dict__` reachable from a statement node -- including a call's `resolved_function_info` -- and treats every `TpyType` it finds as a module the generated code references. Adding the owning-slot copy obligations to `FunctionInfo` (types of the SLOTS a callee's body stores into, a diagnostics-only fact) therefore added four transitive includes to `tests/cases/generics/generic_arg_temp_instantiated_slot`'s header until the two field names were listed in the walk's skip set beside `enum_member_of`. The skip list is a denylist: the next field to hold a type is picked up silently, and only a snapshot diff says so. Fix direction: walk an explicit allowlist of the fields whose types the generated code actually names, so a new field is invisible until it opts in. Found while landing the per-instantiation owning-slot copy verdict 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container FIELD read at a generic callee's composite `list[T]` slot rejects.** [`generic-composite-slot-field-arg`] `has_item(self.labels, k)` with `self.labels: list[str]` and `def has_item[T](xs: list[T], v: T)` rejects at `call.generic_arg_shape`, while the same read bound to a local first (`xs = self.labels; has_item(xs, k)`) lowers and renders the member read bare. The generic family's pass-through rows for a substituted composite slot (`_container_pass_through_arg`) are NAME-only; the still-OPEN composite slot already has its field twin (`call.generic_open_slot_field_composite`), so only the substituted side is missing the row. `tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_view_form_positions` binds the local for exactly this reason. Found while covering the positions for the view-at-a-generic-slot fix 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) An `Own[T]` CONSTRUCTOR parameter whose payload is `@nomove` does not compile.** [`own-nomove-ctor-param-cpp-error`] `def __init__(self, v: Own[Pinned])` storing `self.val = v` emits the member init `val(std::move(v))`, which needs the move constructor `@nomove` deletes; the toolchain reports it at the generated line, with no TPy location. This is a `@nomove` gap, not a generic one: the same program fails identically at `Holder[Pinned]` (`explicit Holder(::tpy::own_param_t<T> v) : val(std::move(v)) {}`) and at a hand-written `TwinHolder` whose field is a plain `Pinned` (`inline TwinHolder::TwinHolder(Pinned&& v) : val(std::move(v)) {}`). Fix: sema rejects `Own[@nomove]` at a constructor parameter that initializes a field (or the field init itself) with a located message, or the member init constructs in place rather than moving. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/generic/p4_own_ctor.py`. Found while auditing the generic-form class 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A VIEW or an ENUM value at a generic slot is refused by the lowering.** [`generic-slot-view-enum-arg-rejects`] `echo(bv)` with `def echo[T](v: T) -> T` and `bv: BytesView` rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot`, and `Cell(bv)` at `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`; an enum member at the same free-function slot (`has_item(xs, k)` with `k = Color.RED`) rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot` too, though the enum reaches a generic RECORD's slot fine. The generic argument rows admit scalars, `str`, records, containers, tuples and `None`; the other value-type families -- the views (`BytesView`, `Span`, the dict views), `Range`, the slices, and enums at a free-function slot -- match no row and fall through to the reject. Distinct from the str/bytes view at a generic slot, which the lowering does admit and now materializes an owned temp for (`tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_view_form_positions`): here nothing is emitted at all. Both the C++ obstacle (the runtime's value-type trait was made to match the registry, 2026-09-08) and the str/bytes admission are gone, so what is left for THESE families -- the borrowing views with no owned counterpart, `Range`, the slices, and enums at a free-function slot -- is admission rows: they need no materialize, only a bare pass-through row. `tests/cases/generics/generic_value_form_instantiation` pins the shapes that do lower and names this entry for the one that does not. Found while pinning the value-form instantiation 2026-09-08.


- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A BORROW-returning call at a generic FREE function's `T` slot is refused, where the same argument at a generic RECORD METHOD's `T` slot binds bare.** [`generic-free-call-borrow-return-arg-rejects`] `f(h.borrow())` with `def f[T](v: T) -> None` and `Holder.borrow() -> Cell` (a `T&`-returning getter) fails at `expr.call:call.generic_arg_slot`, reported on the call line; `b.m(h.borrow())` with `class Box[T]` and `def m(self, v: T)` compiles and renders the bare bind `b.m(h.borrow());`, which aliases the holder's field exactly as CPython does. So this is not a temp-versus-no-temp difference between the seams -- neither builds a temp -- but a missing ADMISSION row at the free-call seam: its prologue (`_pre_generic_slot_family`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) admits a CALL at a substituted non-value `TypeParamRef` slot only when `is_rvalue_source` holds, and a borrow-returning getter is not one. The method and marker ladders carry the row this needs (`borrow_ret_record_marker` -- a `T&`-returning F1-record call at a plain record ref slot binds in place, no temp, no copy); the generic free-call ladder has no analogue. Fix direction: mirror that row in the generic-plain family, and pin it with a case that MUTATES the holder and prints through both handles, so the bare bind is proved to alias rather than copy. The reject itself is bound-independent -- the shapes above use an unbounded `Box[T]` / `f[T]` -- but a mutation-OBSERVING pin needs a bounded `T` (an unbounded one cannot touch a member), which is why the happy case spells `Bumper[T: Bump]`. Neighbouring entry for the other source shapes refused at the same slot: `generic-slot-view-enum-arg-rejects`. Pre-existing (identical on `4346504539`); found by review probes while folding the three generic seams into one verdict 2026-09-09. Pinned by `tests/cases/generics/error_generic_free_call_borrow_arg`, whose happy twin `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` runs the method seam's accepted form.

- **[LOW small] (spurious diagnostic) A generic method returning its own `T` PARAMETER warns about a temporary when the argument is a borrow.** [`generic-return-through-param-spurious-temporary-warning`] `def bump_it(self, v: T) -> T: v.bump(); return v` on `class Bumper[T: Bump]`, called as `got = b.bump_it(h.borrow())` where `Holder.borrow() -> Cell` returns a `T&` alias of a live field, warns *Result borrows from temporary argument 'v'; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement* on the binding line. The argument is not a temporary: it aliases the holder's own cell, which outlives the statement, so the borrow the result carries is sound and the warning is noise on valid code. The same call at STATEMENT position (result discarded) warns nothing, so the verdict is taken at the binding. Fix direction: the temporary-argument check should ask whether the argument expression is a temporary (a borrow-returning call is not) rather than treating every call-shaped argument as one. Pre-existing; re-probed 2026-09-09 (`/tmp/agents/sdb2/t3.py`). This is why `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` keeps its method `-> None` and observes the alias through the mutation instead of through the returned handle.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reassigning a `T`-typed parameter inside a generic body is rejected where the monomorphic twin is accepted.** [`generic-param-reassign-rejected`] `def bump[T](v: T) -> T: v = v` (any reassignment of the parameter) fails with *Cannot reassign parameter 'v' of type 'T'; assign to a new local variable instead*, while `def bump_concrete(v: float32)` reassigning its parameter compiles and runs; CPython accepts both. The guard stands in for the parameter's C++ form: `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` is a mutable `T&` at a reference-type instantiation, where a reassignment would write through the caller's object rather than rebind a local. It fires on every instantiation, including the value-typed ones whose slot is `const T&` and where a local copy is exactly what a concrete parameter already gets. Fix: decide it per instantiation (or emit the same local-copy the concrete path emits for a `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` type) instead of refusing on the open parameter. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/generic/p5_float32_mutate.py` and `_twin.py`. Found while auditing the generic-form class 2026-09-08. The same `_check_nonvalue_rebinding` guard rejects a range target of open type `T`: `def count[T: AnyFixedInt](stop: T)` with `for i in range(stop): i = 10` fails with `Cannot reassign loop variable 'i' of type 'T'`; CPython runs all three iterations at `stop=3`. An attempted `int32(stop)` bound also rejects, at `call.type_ctor.scalar_arg`; its separate witness is `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_generic_cast.py` and the full-fixture diagnostic is `range-case-frontend-9.log`. The passing range regression instead takes `values: list[T]` and uses the concrete integer bound `len(values)`, with parameter mutation observed by the caller; this does not admit an open-`T` counter. Verified in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_generic_rebind.py` (`range-generic-rebind-frontend.log`, `range-generic-rebind-cpy.log`); the shared sema guard is unchanged at session base.


- **[LOW small] (test-harness parity gap) `isinstance(x, int32)` answers differently under the CPython stubs.** [`isinstance-int32-cpy-stub-subclass`] `lib/cpy/tpy`'s `int32` is an `int` SUBCLASS, so a plain literal reaching an `int32 | str` slot is not an `int32` instance under CPython (`isinstance(3, int32)` is False) while TPy, whose default int IS `int32`, answers True. A four-line probe with no other construct shows it. Any case that branches on `isinstance(x, int32)` with a literal source therefore prints differently on the cpy phase; the `tpy.dispatch` runtime in `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py` sidesteps it for the common shape (a plain `int` argument matches any fixed-int annotation it fits), leaving user-written `isinstance` checks and one residual dispatcher shape -- two same-arity fixed-int variants that both fit a literal go to the first declared under CPython where the compiler picks the narrowest; the shape became reachable when the value-union arg temp in an `and` right operand started lowering (2026-09-07). Fix in the stub layer: make the stub's `int` the default fixed-int type for `isinstance` (or map `isinstance(x, int32)` to an `int` test when the case's default_int is int32), not in the compiler. Found while fixing the conditional-operand argument copy.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `@nomove` rvalue at the FIRST comparator of a chained comparison rejects.** [`nomove-first-comparator-chained-compare`] `a < take(Pinned(11)) < 99` with `take(p: Pinned) -> int32` and `Pinned` `@nomove` rejects at `call.arg_shape.optional`: pair 0 of a chained compare lowers with no flush right, so the optional-pointer constructor face has nowhere to hoist its temp, while the same call as an `and` operand or at the second comparator lowers (those positions carry a conditional region). Pinned as the reason the `@nomove` warn case's inverse uses an `and` left operand. Fix: give the first comparator of a chain the same flush right the later comparators have (their region machinery), keyed on the position, not the operator. Found while fixing the conditional-operand argument copy.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An UNSPELLED argument temporary in a conditionally evaluated operand is refused instead of deferred.** [`cond-operand-unspelled-arg-temp-rejects`] `return b or use(Src(7))` with `use(r: Reader)` a structural-protocol slot rejects at `argtemp.cond_defer`; so do the sibling rows that declare their temporary `auto` on purpose -- the container-literal / record-rvalue / range marker-protocol arms, the coroutine-factory, str-literal, iterator-rvalue and generator-expression protocol temps, and the generator-factory reference slot (eight rows in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`; two further rows there spell a type but record no movability -- a protocol-argument spec and a `@dynamic` adapter spelling, neither a type whose movability can be asked -- and reject the same way). The temporary has to be un-spelled so the protocol's concept deduces the concrete type, and the deferred form needs a spelling (`std::optional<T>` cannot name `auto`), so the conditional-operand gate refuses rather than hoist the build ahead of the guard -- which is what it did before 2026-09-07, running the constructor in a branch CPython skips. Binding the value to a local ahead of the expression compiles. Closing it needs the deduced type reachable at lowering for those rows (the concrete init type rather than the protocol slot), not a change to the gate. Pinned by `tests/cases/operators/error_cond_operand_protocol_arg`. Filed while fixing the eager owned-argument copy 2026-09-07.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code) Binding the result of a generic method whose readonly-ness was INFERRED emits a non-const local against a const-qualified return.** [`generic-method-inferred-readonly-return-binding`] `class Box[T]` with `def keep(self, v: T) -> T: return v` -- no `@readonly` annotation, so Phase 2 infers it -- called at a reference-typed instantiation and bound to a caller local (`got = b.keep(c)`) emits `Cell& got = b.keep(c);` against the emitted `::tpy::val_or_cref_t<T> keep(const T& v) const`, and g++ rejects it: *binding reference of type 'Cell&' to 'const Cell' discards qualifiers*. The front end accepts the program; the failure names a generated line. Cause: at the CALLER's lowering the call node's `resolved_function_info.is_readonly` is still the pre-Phase-2 value (False), so the local is spelled mutable. `_sync_inferred_const` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) copies the inferred verdict back onto the callee's own `TpyFunction` -- which is what makes the SIGNATURE const -- but nothing re-syncs a call site's cached `FunctionInfo` for a generic instantiation; the non-generic twin (`def keep(self, v: Cell) -> Cell`) reads True and binds a const local. **Second shape, same seam:** with an explicit `@readonly` the local binds const correctly, and then a MUTATION through it (`got.n = 42`) is not diagnosed by TPy at all -- it surfaces as *assignment of member 'Cell::n' in read-only object* from the C++ compiler, in the non-generic twin too, so the readonly enforcement gap at a readonly-bound local is independent of genericity. Fix direction: re-ask (or re-sync) the readonly verdict where the call site spells the binding, and give the bound local's mutation a located TPy diagnostic. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/sdtail/probe1.py` (generic, inferred), `probe6.py` (non-generic control), `probe5.py` (explicit `@readonly`); pre-existing on `4346504539`. Found by the tail review of the generic-seam fold 2026-09-09, while pinning why `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` cannot bind the method's return.

- **[MED small] (silent copy, no diagnostic) A borrow-returning call at a GENERIC generator's YIELD slot is not diagnosed, and the monomorphic twin does not compile at all.** [`generic-own-slot-borrow-call-unwarned`] `def stream[T](h: GHolder[T]) -> Iterator[T]: yield h.borrow()` copies the payload into the yield slot with no diagnostic -- mutating the source while the yielded value is live prints the pre-mutation value, where CPython prints the mutation. Root: `yield_uses_borrow_slot` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) excludes a `TypeParamRef` element from the borrow slot, so the yield is a copying slot that the owning-slot borrowed-source check (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, the `isinstance(expected, OwnType)` arm) never sees; the exclusion is justified in its docstring on RENDERING grounds (avoiding a double `val_or_ref` wrap), not on ownership. The concrete twin `def stream_twin(h: Twin) -> Iterator[Cell]: yield h.borrow()` cannot be used to compare: it rejects at lowering with `res.yield_type`, so this shape is a generic-equals-twin divergence in BOTH directions. **Second witness of the same asymmetry** (2026-09-08): a borrow-returning getter feeding an owning CONSTRUCTOR slot compiles when the payload is an open `T` (the shape `tests/cases/generics/warn_generic_own_slot_borrow_call`'s `GBox.dup` pins) and is refused at lowering with `method.ret_type` when the same body spells `Cell` directly -- which is why that section has no twin beside it. The four concrete spellings measured (`sink(t.borrow())` at an `Own[Cell]` param, the same bound to a local, `Twin(t.borrow())` at a ctor slot, `CBox(self.get())` with an `@auto_readonly` getter) all reject; a free borrow-returning call rejects as `call.ret_type.record_borrow`. The sibling owning slots -- container insert, `Own[T]` parameter, `Own[T]` return -- were closed 2026-09-08 (the entry originally covered all four); pinned by `tests/cases/generics/warn_generic_own_slot_borrow_call`, which omits a yield section for exactly this reason. Re-measured 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, unlocated) Awaiting a GENERIC method of a GENERIC class spells the sub-coroutine frame with only ONE of its two template arguments.** [`generic-class-generic-async-method-template-args`] `class Box[T]` with `async def with_label[U](self, u: U) -> int32` emits `template <typename T, typename U> struct __coro_Box_with_label`, but the awaiting frame declares its slot as `std::optional<__coro_Box_with_label<int32_t>>` -- the class parameter's argument only -- and g++ rejects it with `wrong number of template arguments (1, should be 2)`, followed by cascading `'<expression error>' in namespace 'std'` and undeclared-slot errors in the .cpp. Unlocated: the front end accepts the program and the failure names a generated line. **The local-bind framing this was first reported under is refuted**: both spellings fail identically and neither is rejected at sema -- binding the coroutine to a local first (`c = b.with_label[int32](7); await c`) emits the bad slot as `c`, and the inline `await b.with_label[int32](7)` emits the same bad slot as `__sub_0` (measured 2026-09-08, probes `/tmp/agents/generic4/async_method_probe.py` and `async_method_inline.py`). Site: the sub-struct spelling in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` builds the frame type from the OWNER's type args and drops the method's own. Distinct from the inherited generic-async entry above (that one is about an ancestor's args being unbound and rejects cleanly at sema; this one is a method's own params being dropped and does not reject at all). Found by the tail review of the unit-4 closing fix 2026-09-08.

- **[HIGH small] (silent copy, no diagnostic) A call through an `Fn`/`Callable` VALUE bound to a BORROW-returning function copies at every owning slot with no diagnostic.** [`callable-value-borrow-return-copies-unwarned`] With `def identity(c: Cell) -> Cell: return c` and `f: Fn[[Cell], Cell]`, both `out.append(f(c))` and `return f(c)` at an `Own[Cell]` copy the payload: TPy prints `1` where CPython prints `99` after the source is mutated past the boundary, and no warning fires at either slot (probes `/tmp/agents/tail/fn_alias_probe.py` and `fn_alias_return_probe.py`, measured 2026-09-08 against master `2bd8dec8b6` as well as the fix branch -- pre-existing, unchanged). The same call spelled directly (`out.append(identity(c))`) DOES warn, so the divergence is the callable-value indirection, not the callee. Cause: the synthetic `FunctionInfo` that `analyze_callable_value_call` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) builds carries the `Fn` type's declared return, but every reader treats the callee as opaque -- `is_rvalue_source` (`tpyc/value_category.py`) has no registry entry to consult and falls through to its rvalue default, so `returns_borrow` says no and the owning-slot check never runs. Fix direction: the declared return on that synthetic FI carries the borrow fact as faithfully as a declared function's does, so `returns_borrow` should read it the same way -- but an `Fn` whose declared return is a reference type then borrows at EVERY owning slot in the corpus, so the radius must be measured (`rpytest --no-exec`) before the arm lands; it is its own unit. Note the interaction with the twin rule: the GENERIC leg `Fn[[T], K]` must reach the same verdict as its monomorphic twin, which is why the opposite classification is currently spelled as an explicit `is_callable_value` exclusion rather than left to fall out. Found by the tail review of the unit-4 fix round 2026-09-08. **Second face, the rebinding LOCAL** (2026-09-15): `def use(f: Fn[[Node], Node], a: Node, b: Node) -> None: q = f(a); q.v += 1; q = f(b); q.v += 1` called with `f = same` (`def same(c: Node) -> Node: return c`) prints `1 10` for the caller's `a.v b.v` where CPython prints `2 11`. The render is a VALUE slot that copies the borrow AND turns the rebind into an assign-through: `Node __slot_1 = f(a); Node* q = &__slot_1; ...; (*q) = f(b);`, so both mutations land in the copy. The generic twin (`def gen[T](f: Fn[[T], T], ...)`) renders the same shape with `T` for `Node`, so the divergence is not confined to owning slots -- any local bound from a callable result loses the alias. Probe `/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/p_rebind.py`; render read with `tpyc --dump-code`. Designed resolution: `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A generic body cannot return its own `T | None` parameter, because the RETURN position is still committed to `T*`.** [`generic-optional-return-committed-to-pointer`] `def echo[T](o: T | None) -> T | None: return o` compiles the template but fails at a value-typed instantiation: the parameter is `::tpy::opt_param_t<T>` (`std::optional<int32_t>` at `int32`) while the return is `T*`, so g++ reports *cannot convert `std::optional<int>` to `int*` in return* inside the instantiation, with no TPy source location. The monomorphic twin `def echo(o: int32 | None) -> int32 | None` compiles and runs. The parameter form is now decided per instantiation (`opt_param_t<T>`), but the return keeps `force_pointer_repr` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) so a `T | None` return can alias the field it reads (`return self._val` renders `optional_to_ptr(this->_val)`, a pointer INTO the record) -- an optional return would copy there. Closing it means the return taking a trait of its own (`std::optional<T>` at a value T, `T*` at a reference one, with a matching lift at the field read) and the receiver local taking the natural substituted form, which retires `force_pointer_repr` entirely -- the flag's own docstring names conditional-ABI templates as the exit. The same shape was already ill-formed before the parameter changed (the call site built the value form against a `T*` slot), so this is the residue of that fix, not a regression. Found while making the `T | None` parameter a runtime trait 2026-09-08.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) A return-type mismatch on a coroutine value prints the same type on both sides.** [`coro-return-mismatch-prints-same-type`] `def make(c: Cell) -> asyncio.Cancellable[bool]: return probe_async(c)` reports `Type mismatch in return value: expected Cancellable[bool], got Cancellable[bool]`, which tells the reader nothing -- the two types differ in something the `__str__` does not render (the coroutine struct's identity behind the `Cancellable[T]` wrap). Dropping the annotation reports `expected None, got Cancellable[bool]`, so the check itself fires correctly; only the rendering collapses. Whatever the real distinction is, the message has to name it (or the check has to accept the return). Found 2026-09-08 probing whether an async frame holding a borrowed param can escape its caller -- this reject is one of the two things that stop it, so it is load-bearing for the resumable-frame borrow family above. Repro `/tmp/agents/gu3/c9_escape3.py`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A value-repr `int32 | None` local passed to a generic `T | None` slot rejects.** [`optional-value-local-at-generic-slot`] `none_int: int32 | None = None` then `probe_gen(none_int)` on `def probe_gen[T](val: T | None) -> bool` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.generic_arg_shape`, where the reference-typed twin (a `Cell | None` local into the same slot) lowers. A bare int LITERAL at the same slot (`probe_gen(2)`) rejects the same way, where a binop of the same type (`probe_gen(n + 1)`) and an explicit `int32(2)` both lower. The generic call's argument gate (`_generic_plain_arg_ok`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) enumerates argument shapes against a bare `TypeParamRef` slot and has no row for an `Optional[TypeParamRef]` one, so the shape that would now render as a bare pass-through (both sides are `std::optional<int32>` after the parameter-form fix) is refused before it gets there. Pre-existing: reproduces unchanged on the branch base with the old pointer parameter form. Repros `/tmp/agents/gu3/b6_optlocal.py` (the local) and the `probe_gen(2)` line of `tests/cases/generics/optional_param_trait_form` (the literal, which the case spells `int32(2)` for that reason). Found while making the `T | None` parameter a runtime trait 2026-09-08.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Every body shape over a `ValueType`-bounded `T | None` PARAMETER is unlowered.** [`bounded-optional-param-unrouted`] On `class BoundedBox[T: ValueType]`, `def probe(self, val: T | None) -> bool: return val is not None` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.is not.tparam`, `def echo(self, val: T | None) -> T | None: return val` at `stmt.return:name.optval_read`, and `def __init__(self, val: T | None): self._val = val` at `ctor.mil_field.optional.name`. The bounded RETURN position lowers (`tests/cases/generics/generic_optional_value_bound`); only the parameter is blocked. Pre-existing: reproduces unchanged on the branch base. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `Any` against a CONCRETE operand, and `k in dict[Any, V]`, are accepted by sema and rejected by THIR.** [`any-vs-concrete-compare-rejects`] `a: Any = 1; a == 1` / `1.0 == a` / `a == f` with `f: float64` reject at `stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.==` (so does `!=`), and `k in d` on a `dict[Any, str]` at `binop.shape.in`; CPython answers all of them. - **[MED small] (sema accepts against its own rule, then loud reject) `Any < Any` passes sema and rejects at THIR.** [`any-ordering-accepted-by-sema`] `a: Any = 1; b: Any = 2; a < b` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.<`. `tpyc/sema/protocols.py` states `Comparable` is non-conforming for `Any` ("the user must narrow first"), yet the comparison type-checks, so the rejection lands in the wrong phase with the wrong message. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `isinstance(a, T)` on an `Any` as a VALUE expression rejects.** [`isinstance-any-value-expression-rejects`] `print(isinstance(a, str))` with `a: Any` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.special_form.isinstance`; only the `if isinstance(a, T):` narrowing form lowers. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Any` FIELD cannot be read, and a `str` field cannot be stored into `Any`.** [`any-field-read-rejects`] With `slot: Any` on a record, every read of `h.slot` -- `cast(str, h.slot)`, `print(h.slot)`, `x: Any = h.slot`, `take(h.slot)`, `f"{h.slot}"`, `return self.slot` from a method -- rejects at `field.result_type`; `isinstance(h.slot, str)` is a sema error ("first argument must be a variable name"). - **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) Printing an isinstance-narrowed `bytes` out of an `Any` emits a bare `std::cout << __a`.** [`narrowed-bytes-print-ill-formed`] `a: Any = b"by"; if isinstance(a, bytes): print(a)` renders the narrowed `const tpy::Bytes&` with the raw stream operator rather than the bytes printer a plain `bytes` local gets, and `tpy::Bytes` has no `operator<<`. - **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence) A MONOMORPHIC integer compared against a float is compared as a double, so a value beyond 2**53 compares equal to a float it differs from -- `int` and every FIXED width alike.** [`int-float-compare-rounds-bigint`] `big: int = 9007199254740993` against `f: float64 = 9007199254740992.0` prints True for `big == f` and `big <= f` where CPython prints False: the compare renders `(static_cast<double>(big) == f)` (`_binop_operand_casts`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), which rounds the arbitrary-precision side to the nearest double before comparing. The fixed widths reach the same wrong answer by the C++ usual arithmetic conversions instead of an explicit cast, with no lowering row involved at all: `a: int64 = 9007199254740993` prints `a == f` True and `a < f` False (CPython: False, False), and `u: uint64 = 2**64 - 1` equals `1.8446744073709552e19`. No diagnostic anywhere. Equality, inequality and all four ordering operators; ordinary program shapes (`x <= 1.5`, `big == f`) get a silently wrong answer, which is why this is HIGH rather than a 2**53 curiosity. The value-union leaf (`tpy::detail::py_eq` / `py_ne` / `py_cmp`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/value_compare.hpp`) and `Any` compare EXACTLY since 2026-09-14 -- for BigInt and for every fixed width -- through the allocation-free `vc_i64_cmp_float` / `vc_u64_cmp_float` cores, with `vc_bigint_*_float` falling back to decomposing the float only beyond int64 range. The fix is therefore not a per-side cast: `_binop_operand_casts` wraps ONE operand and cannot emit a two-operand helper, so it needs a whole-expression binop arm that routes an `int op float` pair through `vc_*_cmp_float` (both orders, all six operators). When it lands, drop the three "twin still rounds" caveats: the header comment in `value_compare.hpp`, the union bullet in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, and the `u_int_*` section comment in `tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq`. Probes `/tmp/agents/any_fix/mono/main.py` (BigInt) and `/tmp/agents/any_fix/mono_fixed/main.py` (int64/uint64). A `match` arm reaches the same compare since 2026-09-15: `case 1.0:` over an `int64` subject renders the bare `subject == 1.0` (`tests/cases/match/numeric_literal_kinds`), so the fix has to cover the match-literal spelling too -- and BOTH directions at BOTH float widths: `case 16777217:` over a `float32` subject hits under TPy where CPython misses (the `float32` threshold is 2**24, not 2**53; probe `/tmp/agents/review_b2/r2/prec.py`), and an int literal over a `float` subject rounds the same way as the float-literal-over-int direction. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09; widened to the fixed widths 2026-09-14.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) An `int` compared against a `uint32` does not compile.** [`bigint-vs-uint32-compare-ill-formed`] `def eq(a: int, b: uint32) -> bool: return a == b` renders `(a == ::tpy::BigInt(b))`, and `BigInt(uint32_t)` is ambiguous: `BigInt(int32_t)`, `BigInt(int64_t)` and `BigInt(uint64_t)` are all integral conversions of equal rank, so the toolchain reports the error at the generated line with no TPy location. The sibling widths are fine (`uint8`/`uint16` promote to `int32_t`, `uint64` matches exactly), so only the 32-bit unsigned spelling is affected -- on either side, and for the ordering operators too. Fix: the BigInt wrap spells the widened form (`::tpy::BigInt(static_cast<uint64_t>(b))`), which is what the value-union leaf already does for the same pair (`tpy::detail::vc_to_bigint`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/value_compare.hpp`). Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/twins.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A container or recursive-alias compare over a record that defines no `__eq__` fails in the C++ toolchain with no TPy diagnostic.** [`container-compare-record-without-eq`] `def eqd(a: dict[str, Plain], b: dict[str, Plain]) -> bool: return a == b` with `Plain` defining no `__eq__`, and `def cmp(a: list[Expr], b: list[Expr])` over `type Expr = Lit | BinOp` with neither record defining one, both fail at the generated line: sema admits the container pair (the element's equality is never required) and the emit reaches a comparison the element type does not have. CPython runs both -- `dict.__eq__` and `list.__eq__` fall back to identity, so `eqd(a, a)` is True and `cmp(xs, ys)` is False for distinct objects -- so this is a rejects-valid divergence, just a loud one. The message depends on the shape: a union alternative pair reaches a named `static_assert` inside the leaf ("comparing two values of one TPy type that defines no equality") -- a REFERENCE union's container element too, since its storage form is `::tpy::Union` as well -- while a plain record element reaches `no match for operator==` at the container's own line. Both are unlocated toolchain errors. Fix: sema requires the element type to conform to `Equatable` at a container/wrapper compare and says so with a TPy location, or the identity fallback is emitted. Probes `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/vu_dict2.py` and `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/probe3/main.py`. Cannot be pinned as a case (an `error_` case needs a front-end diagnostic; this one is a C++ error). Found by the review of the value-union equality fix 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A NON-generic recursive alias with a fixed-width numeric member renders the TPy type name into C++.** [`nongeneric-alias-member-spelling`] `type V = int32 | float64 | list[V]` emits `using variant_type = std::variant<float64, int32_t, std::vector<V>>;` -- `float64` is a TPy name with no C++ declaration, so the header does not compile ("'float64' was not declared in this scope"), unlocated. The same alias spelled with `int | float` builds, and the signature of a function taking `list[V]` spells the members correctly AND in a different order (`std::variant<int32_t, double, std::vector<V>>`), so the wrapper struct's member rendering and the signature's have drifted apart -- two renders of one type that must agree. Independent of the equality work: `git show master:tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` differs from the current `_gen_recursive_union_struct` only in the `operator==` lines. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/nongen_alias.py` with the `int32 | float64` leaf. Found by the review of the value-union equality fix 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A value union has no equality at the TYPE level, so every consumer that asks for one rejects.** [`value-union-no-equatable-conformance`] Sema resolves no `__eq__` for a `UnionType` (`resolve_binop`, `tpyc/sema/operators.py`) and gives it neither `Equatable` nor `Hashable` conformance (`classify_protocol_conformance`, `tpyc/sema/protocols.py`), so six ordinary Python shapes are refused although the same-type union compare itself works: a union against one of its own members (`u == 1`, `binop.shape.==`), a direct `tuple[union, ...]` compare (`binop.shape.==`), `needle in xs` / `xs.count` / `xs.index` over `list[union]` ("requires element type ... to conform to 'Equatable'"), a union as a dict KEY or set element ("not hashable"), and `sorted` / `min` / `max` over `list[union]` ("does not satisfy 'Comparable'"). Every one of them runs in CPython. The runtime answers already exist -- `::tpy::Union`'s own operators (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/union_type.hpp`) and `::tpy::Union`'s (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/ptr_union.hpp`) are what the same-type compare reaches at a storage and a borrow position respectively -- so this is conformance plumbing plus a hash that agrees with the new equality, i.e. a feature (`/tpy-add-feature`), not a fix. A union of RECORDS used to be listed here too; it compares now that the borrow form is its own type (`tests/cases/union/reference_union_borrow_eq`), and the conformance is still what the six shapes above wait on. The missing conformance also makes the union path LOOSER than its twin in one direction: ordering two members that define no ordering (`a < b` on `Fixed | Zone`, both `@dataclass(frozen=True)` ValueType records) compiles and raises `TypeError` at runtime, which is CPython's answer, while the monomorphic `Fixed < Fixed` is a located sema error ("Comparison '<' on 'Fixed': no '__lt__' method defined"). A `Comparable` check at the union compare is where both would agree; `tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq` pins the runtime raise as the current behaviour. Probes `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s04,s07,s08,s09,s41`, `p04`, `p05`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (message divergence) The runtime `TypeError` for an unorderable pair names the TPy type where CPython names the Python one.** [`union-order-typeerror-names-tpy-type`] `a < b` on an `int32 | str` holding an int against a str raises `'<' not supported between instances of 'int32' and 'str'`, where CPython for the same source says `'int' and 'str'`; on a user record it is `'__main__.Fixed'` against CPython's `'Fixed'`. The message comes from `tpy::type_name<T>()` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/type_name.hpp`), which deliberately spells TPy names so diagnostics never leak C++ ones -- the same convention every other runtime message follows, and `int32` IS the type the user wrote. So this is a house-convention divergence, not a defect in the message: recorded because a program that prints `str(e)` sees different text under TPy and CPython, and `docs/PITFALLS.md` requires a test to print a stable token rather than the message for exactly that reason (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq` does). Fix only if TPy decides runtime exception TEXT should match CPython's, which is a wider decision than unions. Found by the review of the `::tpy::Union` redesign 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[]`-wrapped value union at a compare does not lower.** [`own-union-compare-rejects`] `def eq(a: Own[int32 | float64], b: Own[int32 | float64]) -> bool: return a == b` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.==`, where the same parameters spelled bare or `readonly[]` lower and render `(a == b)` (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq`). `Own[T]` on a value type transfers nothing, so reading one to compare it is the same value read; the compare gate's own `Own` leg (`_tparam_value(_unwrap_own(...))`) admits only a type parameter, and the value-union pair is checked after it on the unwrapped type only for the RENDER. Fix: unwrap `Own` before the union pair's admission too. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/own_readonly.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) A `match` subject diagnostic spells an internal type name.** [`match-diagnostic-spells-intliteral`] `match 1:` reports `match subject must be a union, enum, primitive, record, or Optional type, got 'IntLiteral(1)'` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`, interpolating `effective_type`). `IntLiteral` is not a type a user can write, so this is a `docs/PITFALLS.md#no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` hit; the leak is `IntLiteralType.__str__`, so any other message interpolating a type that may still be literal-seeded carries it too. - **[MED small] (spurious warning on valid code) A comprehension's `if` clause does not narrow the element it tests, so a filtered optional access warns.** [`comp-filter-none-test-not-narrowing`] `[item.x for item in items if item is not None]` over `list[Foo | None]` warns `Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check` at `item.x`, although the filter retains only non-None elements; the same test written as an `if` STATEMENT around the access narrows and stays silent. Loud (a warning plus a runtime check), never wrong output. Pinned as the current behaviour by `tests/cases/optional/comp_filter_unproven_optional_access`. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07.

- **[MED small] (hidden allocation) An already-owned `str` at an `Own[str]` slot is copy-constructed into a temp and the temp moved, where the record twin moves the source itself.** [`own-str-slot-temp-copies-owned-source`] `xs.append(t)` with `t` an owned `std::string` local (a concat result), and `self.kept.append(v)` with `v: Own[str]`, both render `std::string __tmp_1{t};` followed by `xs.push_back(std::move(__tmp_1));` -- a full copy-construct plus a move of the copy -- while the same shape over a record renders `xs.push_back(std::move(v));` with no temp at all. Two separable parts: the temp itself is pure noise (`push_back(t)` costs the same one copy and is what the slot wants), whereas ELIDING the copy needs a last-use fact the lowering does not have at that slot. Root: `_own_lvalue_temp_slot` / `_own_move_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) exclude value types from the temp-free move row, and the str-family carve-out in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` forces the temp path at every `Own[str]` slot regardless of whether the source already owns its buffer. Invisible to every test: the temp and the direct copy print alike. A third source reaches the same render now that a `str` FIELD is admitted at the slot: `ns.append(r.name)` over `name: Own[str]` emits `std::string __tmp_1{r.name}; ns.push_back(std::move(__tmp_1));` per iteration, while the `bytes` twin in the same loop (`ts.append(r.tag)`) binds bare through `arg.bytes_owned_lvalue` -- so the two view-family halves disagree at one slot, which makes the str-family carve-out the thing to remove rather than a per-source exception. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch6_review/review/codegen/p10.py`. Pinned as the current render by `tests/cases/list/append_owned_str_local` and `tests/cases/str/own_str_arg_temp_in_while_condition`. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07; the field source added by the batch-6 codegen review.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) Every THIR reject message ends in its internal reject tag, and one arm spells a THIR node class name into it.** [`reject-tag-reaches-the-user`] The message reads `... not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:binop.shape.+)`, and `_record_source_reject_detail` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the fall-through `f"return.record_source.{type(v).__name__}.{slot}"`) puts a node class name inside it: `tests/cases/pointers/error_readonly_ptr_at_mutable_return`'s committed `diag.txt` reads `return.record_source.TpyCoerce.borrow`. The `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` entry in `docs/PITFALLS.md` counts reject-reason codes as internal names, so the whole tag is in scope, not only the node name. Another instance a user meets on valid-looking code: aliasing a whole owning tuple frame local (`u = t`) reports only `(res.btuple_source)` (`BUGS.md#frame-tuple-reassigned-owning-alias`). Dropping the tag is not the fix: it is what the reject queue in `scripts/thir_migration/review/` and about 370 `error_` cases key on. Fix shape: a user-facing sentence per tag family naming the Python construct, with the tag kept in a trailing bracket (or behind a verbose flag) for the queue and the case annotations. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07.

- **[LOW small] (silent resource leak) A consuming method on a type with `__del__` that RAISES before its transfer completes never runs the receiver's destructor.** [`consuming-method-raise-skips-del`] Codegen sets `this->__tpy_owned_ = false` unconditionally at the ENTRY of every consuming method (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, the `__del__` suppression that prevents a double free of the moved-from receiver), so if the body raises before the move (a `finally` that raises after `return self`, or any raise ahead of the return) no object ever takes ownership and the one-time cleanup is skipped -- not a double destruction, a dropped one. Reproduces on master without any `finally`: any consuming method on a `__del__` type that raises before its `return`. Fix shape: clear the flag at the MOVE (the `THIRMove` of the receiver, `ret.self_move` / the finally-deferred capture), not at method entry, so an aborted transfer leaves the receiver owned. Found by the safety review of the consuming `return self` move 2026-09-07.

- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, perf) A last-use write of a reference-typed local into an `Any` field copies the payload once.** [`any-field-write-copies-source`] `h.payload = n` with `n: Node` at its last use renders `h.payload = std::move(::tpy::make_any(n));` (`tpyc/thir/lower/field_write.py`, `_lower_any_field`): `make_any(T value)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/any.hpp`) takes its argument BY VALUE, so `n` is copy-constructed into the parameter and the outer `std::move` acts on a prvalue, which is inert. `_is_move_source` already proves `n` is dead after the write, so the fix is to move the source into `make_any` (`make_any(std::move(n))`) -- one render change, no semantic change (the source is never read again). Invisible to every test: the copy and the move print alike. Pinned as the current render by `tests/cases/dynamic_attrs/any_field_write_last_use_moves`. Found by /tpy-review 2026-09-06.
- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, perf) A `str` element of a tuple unpack is COPY-assigned out of the dead unpack temp, where an owned element at the same site is moved.** [`unpack-str-element-copied-from-dead-temp`] `s, k = pair()` (with `pair() -> tuple[str, int]`) renders `auto __tup_1 = pair(); s = std::get<0>(__tup_1); k = std::get<1>(__tup_1);` -- `__tup_1` is a temporary nothing reads again, so the `std::string` copy is pure overhead, while an `Own[list[int]]` element at the identical site renders `xs.emplace(std::move(std::get<0>(__tup_1)));`. Both renders are visible side by side in `tests/cases/generators/frame_clause_hoist_binders/expected/include/main_inl.hpp`. Present at the top-level (non-clause) position too, so it is the unpack element render rather than anything about the hoist. Invisible to every test: the copy and the move print alike. **Fix shape:** the per-element assign reads the unpack temp at its last use, so each element can take `std::move(std::get<N>(__tup))` uniformly instead of only the owned ones. Found by /tpy-review 2026-09-20.
- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, perf) A `for` head unpacking an OWNED yield copies the whole element before moving its `Own` member out.** [`for-head-owned-yield-copies-before-move`] `for i, b in g(3)` over `Iterator[tuple[int, Own[Box]]]` renders `const auto& __for_tup_0 = *__r_1; auto __tup_1 = __for_tup_0; Box b = std::move(std::get<1>(__tup_1));` -- the per-iteration result `__r_1` is the loop's own value, yet the head binds it const and so has to copy it to have something to move from. Output is right (each `b` is a distinct object, pinned by `iterators/gen_tuple_yield_own`); the cost is one copy of the tuple per iteration, a `Box` copy included. Sema is right to tag the member owned (the head's source is fresh each iteration), the lowering's `NAME_COPY` head bind (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the `for` head arm) is the one that pays. **Fix shape:** bind the head holder mutably (`auto&& __for_tup_0`) when a member is owned, so the move comes off the iteration value itself; `TupleSourceBind.NAME_COPY` then has no consumer and goes. Surfaced while closing the live-source unpack copy (2026-09-22).
- **[LOW small] (hidden allocation, perf) Unpacking a tuple read off a FIELD or a CONTAINER ELEMENT copies the whole tuple, where a local or param source binds it by const reference.** [`field-tuple-unpack-copies-whole-tuple`] `x, k = h.f` for `f: tuple[bytes, int32]` renders `auto __tup_1 = h.f; ::tpy::BytesView x = std::get<0>(__tup_1);` -- a copy of the owning `::tpy::Bytes` (an allocation plus a byte copy) that the view `x` then points INTO. The same unpack off a local (`x, k = t`) or a param renders `const auto& __tup_1 = t;` and allocates nothing. `str` elements take the same split, and so does a container-element source: `x, k = xs[0]` on `list[tuple[bytes, int32]]` renders `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::__getitem__(xs, 0);`. Output is identical, so no test sees it. The source lives at least as long as the statement in all three cases, so the field has no lifetime reason to differ; it is the receiver kind reaching the unpack-temp decision. A field tuple with a REFERENCE element is not affected: it takes the `tuple_to_pointer` lift and aliases. Measured 2026-09-21 on `04a797ddf2` by the tuple element matrix (cells `bytes__field__T_unpack`, `str__field__T_unpack` and `bytes__collection__T_unpack` against `bytes__local__T_unpack` / `str__param__T_unpack`, form column). **Fix shape:** the unpack temp's bind-by-reference verdict keys on the source being an lvalue the statement cannot invalidate, which a stored field read and a container element read both are, not on the source being a bare name; same family as `BUGS.md#unpack-str-element-copied-from-dead-temp`. `docs/PITFALLS.md` hidden-allocation class.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) Returning a module-global `Record | None` at an `Optional[record]` return emits the dereferenced global.** [`global-optional-record-borrow-return`] `_r: Rec | None = None` plus `def find() -> Rec | None: return _r` emits `Rec* find() { return (*_r); }` -- the global slot's read is dereferenced where the pointer-repr optional return wants the pointer -- and g++ rejects it (`cannot convert 'Rec' to 'Rec*' in return`). A PARAM or a LOCAL of the same type returns fine (`return x` renders the pointer), so it is the module-global slot specifically; the same global compares fine against `None` at a call site, so only the return position is affected. A module-level optional record with a lookup function that returns it is ordinary Python. Related to the value-Optional global narrowing entry below (same "the global slot's read is not recognized by the optional rows" family) but a different consumer -- there the reject is loud and front-end, here the front end accepts and the C++ does not build. Repro `/tmp/agents/i1/p/bug1.py` (20 lines). Found 2026-09-06 while converting the THIR resumable unit pins to cases -- the unit test string-matched the emitted `(find() == nullptr)` and never compiled the program. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) Awaiting a `Task[T]` whose payload is a VIEW assigns the view into an owning frame field.** [`await-task-view-payload-frame-field`] `async def sub() -> BytesView` plus `t = asyncio.create_task(sub()); r = await t` gives the frame field `r` the OWNED type (`std::vector<unsigned char>`) while the await's result stays the view (`tpy::own_return_t<std::span<const unsigned char>>`), so the resume assignment `r = std::move(__r0).value();` has no matching `operator=`. Awaiting the coroutine directly (`r = await sub()`) is not affected -- it is the `Task[T]` hop that loses the view spelling on the way to the frame slot. `print(len(await t))`, which never binds a local, compiles and runs. Loud, not silent. Repro `/tmp/agents/i1/p/bug4.py` (18 lines). Found 2026-09-06 while converting the THIR resumable unit pins to cases -- the unit pin asserted a face witness on the lowered THIR and never built the C++. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) A read of a module global BEFORE the same body's local assignment to that name resolves to the global instead of raising.** [`read-before-local-shadow-resolves-global`] Python makes a name assigned anywhere in a function a local for the WHOLE body, so `y = gate.x` ahead of `gate = Gate(1)` raises `UnboundLocalError`; TPy resolves the early read to the module variable and prints a value. Same family as the `match`-capture and post-handler `except`-capture entries: TPy's local model is block-scoped where Python's is function-scoped, so closing it means the same bind-then-mark-dead change, not a local patch. Scoped 2026-09-15 to the ATTRIBUTE-receiver spelling: `y = gate.x` ahead of `gate = Gate(1)` compiles and prints the global's field, while the bare-NAME alias `y = gate` and every scalar spelling are rejected instead -- see [`global-shadow-shapes-rejected-not-diverging`] for the rejected siblings and [`unbound-local-read-reported-as-global-read`] for their wording. Pinned (as the compiler's current behaviour, with `no_cpython.txt`) by `tests/cases/globals/global_record_read_before_shadow`, which is the only remaining shape reaching the dedicated global-record-receiver lowering arm. Surfaced while converting the THIR unit pins to cases. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `copy()` over a CALL source at a ctor MEMBER-INIT field write rejects at `ctor.mil_field.{record,container}.call`.** [`copy-call-source-ctor-mil`] `def __init__(self, h: Holder): self.q = copy(h.brec())` rejects, while the same write in an ordinary method (`s.q = copy(h.brec())`) lowers, and so do the setitem, container-literal-element, `Own[T]`-arg and return sinks -- every one of them classifies its `copy()` source through `copy_construct_source` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`), which keys on the source's value form. The ctor member-init driver is a separate gate that still keys on the source being a bare NAME, so the two-step (`p = h.brec()` then `self.q = copy(p)`) is the only spelling there (`tests/cases/records/copy_call_source_sinks` pins it). Route that gate to the same classifier. Found while widening the `copy()` source shape 2026-09-06.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A TUPLE element at a reference BORROW return slot rejects, where the same element off a list/dict returns bare.** [`tuple-elem-at-ref-borrow-return`] `def first(self) -> list[int32]: return self.pair[0]` on `pair: tuple[list[int32], list[int32]]` rejects at `return.record_source.subscript.borrow` (`tests/cases/returns/error_return_tuple_elem_borrow`), while `return self.rows[i]` over `list[list[int32]]` routes. The reject is SOUND as the gate stands: a borrow-form tuple stores element POINTERS, so `std::get<N>` hands back a `T*` that no `T&` slot can bind -- and `_container_elem_lvalue_subscript` excludes every tuple receiver because the binding's form is walk state it cannot see. The storage-form tuple (a field, as in this repro) does yield the referent and could return bare, so what is missing is the form split, not the render. Whoever adds it must keep the borrow-form leg rejecting: the return ladder's `elem_sub_ok` guard exists precisely because the prechecked subscript lowering below it would otherwise emit the pointer into the reference slot. Found 2026-09-05 while merging the record and container return arms.

- **[LOW small] (wrong value-category answer, latent) `call_returns_cpp_ref` answers True for a VOID-returning method, so a builtin container's constructor call reads as a borrow-returning lvalue.** [`void-method-reads-as-borrow-returning`] `bytearray(b"z")` resolves to `bytearray.__init__` -- a native METHOD whose `fi.return_type` is `VoidType()` and whose `fi.is_constructor` is False -- and `call_returns_cpp_ref` (`tpyc/value_category.py`) only excludes a value type / `TypeParamRef` / `Own` / `Optional` / `Union` / protocol return. `VoidType.is_value_type()` is False, so the predicate reports "returns `T&`" for every `__init__` spelled this way. A user record's ctor is unaffected (`fi.is_constructor` short-circuits above the return check), so the hole is the builtin `__init__` shape. The shared classifier `is_rvalue_source` answers correctly for the same expression (a call whose callee names a registered record is an rvalue), which is why nothing miscompiles today: every consumer that pairs the two is safe. The reference if-expr arm pairs them deliberately -- admitting `bytearray(b"z")` as an lvalue ARM renders a prvalue `?:` that silently COPIES the other arm (probed: TPy prints 97 where CPython prints 90). - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; pre-existing in sema) A NESTED def's container param never gets the const-borrow verdict, and its non-const `T&` propagates to the ENCLOSING function's param and to the enclosing method's inferred `@readonly`.** [`nested-def-container-param-drops-const`] `def outer(xs: list[int32]) -> int32: def inner(v: list[int32]) -> int32: return len(v); return inner(xs)` emits `int32_t outer(std::vector<int32_t>& xs)` where the same body without the nested def infers `const std::vector<int32_t>&`; the lambda param renders `std::vector<int32_t>& v` unconditionally (`_lower_nested_def`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`; the top-level path goes through the const-borrow verdict). Identical on the pre-deletion AST emitter, so sema-side (mutation inference never seeds a lambda param), but user-reachable only since 2026-09-03 when the nested-def container-param arm landed (master hard-rejected the shape). Fix shape: run nested-def params through the same const-borrow verdict as top-level params and let the verdict feed the enclosing function's inference. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `case x as y` -- a whole-subject `as` over a plain capture -- rejects on the record, union and optional-record `match` tiers.** [`match-as-capture-composite-tiers`] `match r: case x as y:` on a record subject, `match u:` on a `Cat | Dog` subject and `match o:` on an `Optional[Box]` subject all die at `stmt.match`; the scalar, chain, str-switch and poly tiers bind both names since 2026-09-03 (`THIRMatchArmEntry.pre_bindings`, case `tests/cases/match/scalar_arm_shapes`), and the inner-scalar face of the optional tier (`Optional[int32]`) routes through the scalar switch.
