- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; was ill-formed C++ on both paths) An `or` / `and` select over `bytes` operands whose runtime spellings differ rejects.** [`bytes-select-mixed-runtime-spelling`] With `a: bytes` a PARAM (a `::tpy::BytesView` at runtime): `v = a or f()`, `f() or a`, `a and f()`, `a or b"zz"`, `b"" or a` all reject at `binop.shape.||` / `binop.shape.&&` (detail `valuesel.bytes_mixed`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`), the same shape the if-expression row already rejects as `ifexpr.bytes_mixed`. The pre-deletion AST rendered every one ill-formed (`std::vector<uint8_t>` initialized from a span, or a span bound over an owned temporary -- dangling as well as ill-formed), so there is no render to mirror; the bytes family has no one-argument conversion in either direction, unlike the str arm's `std::string(sv)`. Measured against the oracle's own output with g++: param vs owned local is a hard compile error in either order (`vector` from `span`); `a or b"zz"` compiles but the literal arm DANGLES (a span over `bytes_literal_owned`'s temporary); `b"zz" or a` is valid (the literal is hoisted). An owned LVALUE against a view has a valid render the oracle never emitted (`(cond ? ::tpy::BytesView(c) : a)` -- spanning a live local), so closing that pair is a new mixed-pair cast rule, a decision. Same-spelling operands route, including two params at an OWNED sink (return, `Own[bytes]` return, record field -- materialized with `view_to_owned_conv`, i.e. `::tpy::bytes_copy(...)`, since the closing review of 2026-09-03; before that the select took its form from the result type and dropped the copy) and a still-view param against a REBOUND param (`b = bytes([113]); v = a or b` composes a span over the live owned local, safe). A rebound param against an owned local or a literal (`b = bytes([113]); c = bytes([1, 2]); v = b or c`, `v = b or b"xy"`) REJECTS: `_view_at_runtime` keeps answering "view" for a reassigned param on purpose -- an arm that answered "owned" from the reassignment facts was tried on 2026-09-03 and made `b or b"xy"` a same-spelling pair whose view result dangled over the vector temporary (ASan use-after-free, no diagnostic), so the reject stays until the mixed cast takes its direction from the sink (TODO "view-family mixed-operand cast direction"). One more face of the name-keyed answer: inside an `async def` a `bytes` param lives in the coroutine frame as an OWNED field (`is_owned_in_coro_frame`, no reassign prologue), so `a or c` against an owned local rejects as a mixed pair there although both operands are vectors at runtime. Found 2026-09-03 by the batch-1 review's bytes spelling matrix.

The gate mirrors sema exactly, so `c == True` against an `int32` slot now also rejects (the explicit `c.__eq__(True)` is a sema type error) although the old bare render happened to agree with CPython; a value-preserving bool-to-int admission is sema's call, not the row's. - **[LOW small] (misattributed diagnostic) A user `__setitem__` call whose value parameter is a plain record warns "copies X into container" at the CALL SITE, although the parameter binds `const X&` and nothing is copied there.** [`setitem-copy-warning-at-call-site`] `s[0] = z` with `def __setitem__(self, index: int32, value: Data)` emits `::tpy::__setitem__(s, 0, z)` -- a by-reference pass -- yet sema reports `copies Data into container; use copy() to make this explicit` on that line. The copy, if any, is the callee's own field write (`self.a = value`), which sema already warns about on ITS line (`copies Data into field`), so the call-site warning double-reports and points at the wrong line; a user following it adds a `copy()` at a site that copies nothing. The warning is right for a BUILTIN container store (`xs[0] = z` on a `list[Data]`), which is where the wording comes from; the user-`__setitem__` path should not reuse it. Witness: `tests/cases/records/setitem_record_value_slot` pins the warning as emitted. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `readonly[ArrayList[T, N]]` parameter cannot read its own elements -- the element type comes back `readonly[Ref[Point]]` and every member access is refused.** [`readonly-not-projected-through-ref`] `def show(lst: readonly[ArrayList[Point, 8]]): p = lst[0]; print(p.x)` fails with `Cannot access field 'x' on type readonly[Ref[Point]]`. The `auto_readonly` `__getitem__` returns a reference, and on a readonly receiver the readonly wrapper lands OUTSIDE the `Ref[T]` instead of being projected onto the pointee, so the field lookup sees a wrapper it has no rule for rather than a `readonly[Point]`. Dropping `readonly` from the annotation and changing nothing else compiles, which isolates the projection rather than the element read. Taking a container read-only and then reading it is ordinary code, and there is no spelling of the access that gets through. **PRE-EXISTING** -- reproduces byte-for-byte on the pre-cutover checkout, so it is not fallout from deleting the AST body emitters. Loud, not silent. Fix shape: project `readonly` through the `Ref[T]` wrapper when unwrapping an element read, so the binding resolves `readonly[Point]`. Repro `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/ro_arraylist.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A NUL `char` is falsy in a boolean context, where CPython -- and this project's own documented rule -- make every `char` truthy.** [`char-nul-truthiness-diverges`] `nul = char("\0")` followed by `if nul:` takes the ELSE branch under TPy and the THEN branch under CPython. `char` lowers to C++ `char`, and the condition renders as the bare `if (nul)`, which is C++'s `!= 0` test -- so the one code point whose integer value is zero flips. `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` puts `char` in the str-like family (`len(c)` returns 1) and states the truthiness rule for that family as `__len__() != 0`, which is constant-true for a `char`; CPython agrees, since a length-1 `str` is always truthy. So the C++ side is the wrong one, not the stub. Silent: no diagnostic fires, and the divergence is invisible to a test that never uses NUL. Reachable wherever a `char` comes from parsed or binary input -- a NUL terminator, a padding byte, a `chr(0)` sentinel -- which is exactly where a scanner would test it for emptiness. Both paths render identically, so this is not a lowering artifact. Fix shape: render a `char` condition as the constant-true form the str-like family already uses (evaluating the operand for its side effects), rather than falling through to the scalar `!= 0` test. Repro `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/char_truthy.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) `functools.reduce` COPIES its accumulator, so a function that mutates the accumulator in place loses the mutation.** [`reduce-accumulator-copied`] `reduce(add, [1, 2, 3], seed)` where `add(a: Acc, b: int32)` does `a.total += b; return a` prints `6 0` under TPy and `6 6` under CPython -- the reduction's own result is right, but the caller's `seed` was never touched. `lib/tpy/functools.py:20` opens with `acc: U = copy(initial)` (and the no-initial overload with `copy(a[0])`), where CPython's `reduce` aliases the seed and hands the same object to every call. Silent: no warning fires, because the copy is written explicitly in the stdlib body. **PRE-EXISTING.** Fix shape is a decision, not a patch -- the `copy()` is what gives the loop an owned local to rebind, so aliasing the seed means the accumulator has to be a borrow of the caller's value and the `Own[U]` return has to go, which changes `reduce`'s signature. In-place accumulation is a normal use of `reduce`, so the divergence is reachable without doing anything unusual. Re-confirmed 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0 (`/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/p_reduce.py`: `6 0` vs CPython's `6 6`). Designed resolution: `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`, later slice **D2** -- the seed's fate is a parameter-position question, not a result-form one, so slice 1 leaves `functools.reduce` untouched and this entry open. D2 makes the consuming fold explicit (`Fn[[Own[U], T], Own[U]]` with `initial: Own[U]`, the accumulator round-tripping by move, which is also the only shape that works for a `@nocopy` accumulator) and designs a Python-compatible `reduce` SEPARATELY: CPython's borrows the seed initially, may own later results, and returns the seed itself for empty input, so respelling the seed `Own[U]` alone would consume it in the functional form too (`reduce(lambda a, x: a + [x], xs, seed); print(seed)`), trading this divergence for a use-after-move on a correct program. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `import math` does not compile at `--default-int BigInt`.** [`math-hypot-bigint-slice`] A program whose only import is `math` fails with `lib/tpy/math.py:144: error: in function 'hypot': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:subscript.slice_shape)`. The blocking line is `for c in coords[1:]:` over a varargs `*coords: float` param -- the slice-source shape has no lowering arm at that iteration position when the default int is BigInt. `int32` and `int64` both compile the same module, so the reject is keyed on how the slice bound renders, not on `hypot` itself. A whole stdlib module being unreachable at one `--default-int` setting is worse than the single missing arm suggests: nothing in `math` is usable, whether or not the program calls `hypot`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) `[r] * n` over a reference-type element COPIES each element and, unlike the sibling spellings, warns about nothing.** [`list-repeat-reference-elem-copy`] `rows = [r] * 3` then `rows[0].n = 99` leaves `rows[1].n` and `r.n` unchanged under TPy; CPython puts the SAME object in every slot, so all three see the write. The neighbouring spellings diverge identically -- `[r, r]` and `append(r)` also copy -- but both emit `copies Row into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit`, so a reader is told. The repeat form emits no diagnostic at all, which makes it the one spelling where the value-vs-reference decision is invisible. **PRE-EXISTING.** The CONSTRUCTOR position is the same row one sink over: `self.rows = [r] * 3` in `__init__` lands the identical `from_range(repeat_range(..))` render in the member-init list and is likewise unwarned, so the family now has a silent face inside the ctor as well as at a local and a field write -- name all three when the warning is added. Minimum fix is that missing warning at the repeat row, so every spelling says the same thing; whether the repeat should instead ALIAS is the same question the sibling spellings raise and should be settled once for the family, not per row. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Fourth sink (2026-09-04): the list-repeat admitted as a COMPREHENSION element (`[([c] * 2) for _ in range(2)]` prints `99 1 1 1` where CPython prints `99 99 99 99`, unwarned; `tests/cases/list/comp_element_list_repeat` covers value elements only). Still to be settled once for the family, not per row.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud today; was silent wrong output) A ternary method receiver mixing an lvalue and a temporary operand would lose the mutation, and is refused instead.** [`ternary-receiver-mixed-category-copies`] `(a if c else make()).bump()` where `a` is a record local and `make()` returns `Own[C]`: the C++ conditional over an lvalue and a prvalue is a prvalue, so the call would mutate a COPY of `a` where CPython mutates `a` (the AST emitter rendered the bare `(c ? a : make()).bump()` and printed 1 where CPython prints 2). Re-measured 2026-09-05, per spelling: the record RECEIVER form rejects at `expr.ifexpr` and the container receiver form at `method.recv.other` (`tests/cases/operators/error_ternary_mixed_category_receiver`); the record DECLARATION form `x = a if c else make()` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`, the tag the element-lvalue spelling `rs[0] if c else R(9)` also takes (`tests/cases/control_flow/error_ternary_mixed_category_arms`); the CONTAINER declaration form `x = xs if c else mk()` compiles and carries the documented copy warning. So no silent copy is reachable: the receiver spellings reject, the value-position spellings warn. The reject is a fence, not the fix: valid code is still refused, and the fix is a materialization that keeps the lvalue arm an lvalue (e.g. a pointer select over `&a` and a hoisted temp). Both-lvalue arms alias correctly. Retagged HIGH -> MED on 2026-09-05 because no spelling is a SILENT wrong-output any more -- every reachable copy is warned and every unwarned one is a located reject. Found by the crash-fix review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
