- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A polymorphic `match` inside a method whose readonly-ness is INFERRED casts away const: the emitted signature takes `const`, the `dynamic_cast` target does not.** The `auto& __match_subject_1 = this;` bind and the `dynamic_cast` of a `Pet**` this entry recorded are FIXED -- the subject now binds `(*this)`. What survives is BROADER than the `match self:` headline it was filed under: for any method sema infers `@readonly` for (no decorator), the emitted `std::string Animal::describe() const` pairs with `if (Dog* __mpoly_0 = dynamic_cast<Dog*>(&__match_subject_1))` off a `const Animal*`, and g++ reports `conversion casts away constness`. The SAME method with an EXPLICIT `@readonly` emits `dynamic_cast<const Dog*>` and compiles, which is what isolates the gap: `_poly_subject_const` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:7757`) decides from the subject expression's ReadonlyType / const-borrow-name facts and never consults the enclosing method's inferred `is_readonly`. It bites `match self:` and `match self.<field>:` alike (both verified as build failures), and the corpus witnesses (`tests/cases/match/poly_expr_*`) all spell `@readonly` explicitly, which is why nothing fails today. Loud and toolchain-caught. Repro: a `@dynamic` `Tag` protocol, `class Animal(Tag)` / `class Dog(Animal)`, then an UNDECORATED `def describe(self) -> str:` holding `match self: / case Dog(): return "dog" / case _: return "?"`. The record-ternary composition (`c = self if flag else other` then `match c:`) now compiles and prints correctly, so that half of the entry is closed. Fix shape: seed the poly-cast const from the receiver's EMITTED const-ness, not from the subject expression alone. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

The comprehension one was re-verified as still-divergent AFTER that fix landed (`repro2.py`, ctor still runs per element). The match one could NOT be re-verified: `repro3.py` as written is rejected by sema (`class pattern 'Dog' does not match subject type 'Animal'`) both before and after the fix, so the original "exec-verified" claim for that position rests on a repro that does not compile today -- re-establish a compiling repro before treating the match guard as confirmed. An adjacent agent also proposed `elif` / `while` / `assert` / single-filter comprehensions / non-OR match guards as already-correct -- NOT independently verified, so do not treat that as a closed list either. Surfaced while scoping the short-circuit arg-temp fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence; residue of the conditional-region fix) An `auto`-typed arg temp in a conditionally-evaluated operand is still evaluated UNCONDITIONALLY.** `TempState.conditional_region` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) defers a conditional-operand temp by declaring it as an uninitialized `std::optional<T>` slot and banking `__tmp_N.emplace(init)` into the operand -- but `std::optional<auto>` is not a spelling, so `_slot_spellable` leaves any `auto`-typed temp eager. One site is a real divergence: `expressions.py:276`, the nullable-protocol-union arg path, which falls back to `create_typed("auto", gen)` when the analyzer has no type for the argument (`arg_expr_type is None`) and the argument is a genuine temporary -- so a ctor there still runs in a skipped branch. The two sibling `auto` sites (`expressions.py:1312`, `1325`) copy an LVALUE into an `Own[T]` slot; that copy runs no user code, so it is a wasted copy in a skipped branch (potentially of a large container) rather than a parity divergence. **Not witnessed live:** the `arg_expr_type is None` fallback is hard to reach and no repro was constructed -- confirm the shape is reachable before spending on it. Fix shape: give the site an explicit type so the slot can be spelled (the `Own[T]` str arm just above it already does exactly this, using `type_to_cpp(own.wrapped)` instead of `auto`), rather than teaching the region to handle `auto`. Surfaced while landing the conditional-region fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence; residue of the conditional-region fix) A NON-MOVABLE arg temp in a conditionally-evaluated operand is still evaluated UNCONDITIONALLY.** Sibling of the `auto`-typed residue above, different cause: `TempState._register` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) defers by emplacing into a `std::optional<T>` slot, and `emplace(T(...))` requires `T` move-constructible where the eager `T t = T(...);` form compiles via guaranteed C++17 elision even with the move deleted. So a temp whose type is non-movable (`@nomove`, or a record transitively owning a `UninitArrayStorage` of a non-trivially-relocatable element without `__move__`) MUST stay eager or the program stops compiling -- the `movable` gate on `_register` does exactly that, and `tests/cases/operators/short_circuit_nomove_arg` pins it. The cost is that `flag and take(Pinned(7))` builds the `Pinned` even when `flag` is false, so a ctor with side effects diverges from CPython for this one type class. Verified live: without the gate, `emplace(Pinned(7))` is a hard g++ error (`no type named 'type' in 'struct std::enable_if<false, Pinned&>'`), so the fix without the gate would have been rejects-valid; with the gate the shape compiles and runs eagerly. **Also over-conservative in the safe direction:** `is_movable()` is False for any `@nomove` record, but codegen only emits the deleted C++ move when the record also has a `__del__` (`records.py` `nonmovable` branch, which early-returns on `del_method is None`) -- a `@nomove` record without `__del__` keeps an implicit move and could have deferred. Fix shape: emplace via an in-place factory whose `operator T()` returns a prvalue (direct-init through a conversion function is elided, so no move ctor is needed), which would close both this entry and let the gate be dropped -- a runtime-helper addition, so it needs a design pass, not a patch. `create_typed` also defaults `movable=False` (a C++ spelling alone cannot answer movability); measured as costing zero snapshot churn across the corpus, so no `create_typed` deferral is witnessed today, but a caller that knows its type moves can opt back in. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness) of the conditional-region fix. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` for the factory, or leave as-is.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A walrus target typed pointer-repr `Optional` has no lowering arm for a CALL source.** `if (x := maybe_get(i)) is not None:` for `def maybe_get(i: int32) -> Own[Item | None]` dies with `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.walrus)` (verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03; the earlier symptom, `x = maybe_get(i)` against an `Item* x` and a g++ `cannot convert 'std::optional<Item>' to 'Item*'`, is gone with the AST emitter). The `opt_ptr` arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:6967`) delegates to `_walrus_opt_ptr_source`, which admits only a storage-Optional FIELD source, `None`, or an already-pointer NAME; a bare call rejects with detail `walrus.opt_ptr_src`. Closing it is not just adding the arm: the owning `std::optional<T>` rvalue must first materialize into stable storage before its address is taken, which is exactly the rebind-slot / resumable-ptr-slot machinery the sibling `TpyVarDecl` / `TpyAssign` pointer-rebind path already runs -- so a naive form fix would trade the compile error for a frame pointer into a destroyed temporary. Loud and reproducible in sync and resumable-frame bodies alike. Workaround: bind in a separate statement (the VarDecl path handles it). Everyday shape -- worth queueing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A borrow-tuple walrus bound from a tuple LITERAL over a `readonly` container spells a non-const element pointer -- ill-formed C++.** `(t := (i, nodes[i]))` for `nodes: readonly[list[Node]]` emits `t = std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>{i, &(nodes[...])}` where the address-of yields `const Node*`, and g++ reports `no matching function for call to 'std::tuple<int, Node*>::tuple(...)'` (verified directly, sync and resumable-frame bodies alike). The explicit tuple-type prefix comes from the walrus decl's borrow spelling, whose const-ness is read off `const_borrow_form_tuple_locals`, while the element render derives its own const from the SOURCE -- so a const-rooted literal element and the non-const tuple type disagree. A CALL source is unaffected (it renders its own borrow tuple). Loud and toolchain-caught, no corpus witness. Workaround: bind in a separate statement, or drop `readonly`. Pre-existing and independent of the resumable-frame walrus fix, which reproduced it unchanged on both paths. Repros `/tmp/agents/walrus-fix/r3_consttuple.py` (frame) and `r3b_sync.py` (sync). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of that fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Independent of the per-element capture fork that fixed the six sibling shapes (the slot is identical on both sides here; only the move differs), and structurally invisible to `move_audit`, whose join is empty at a copy/alias-position arm. Which render is right is now an open question with no second author to defer to: the element IS an owned last-use param, so the move is arguably correct and the deleted emitter's bare pass a missed move. The THIR fork now DEFERS the shape (`_proto_tuple_elem_borrow` returns None for any `Own` element; the unit that pinned the defer went with the THIR unit suite), so nothing miscompiles today -- what remains is deciding the oracle render and then admitting the shape on both paths. - **[MED small] (silent wrong output) Rebinding a BORROW-form tuple-unpack target writes THROUGH the alias instead of rebinding the name.** [`borrow-unpack-target-rebind-writes-through`] `x, y = both(p, q)` (for `def both(p: Point, q: Point) -> tuple[Point, Point]`, and the mixed `ref, owned = split(p)` flavour off `-> tuple[Point, Own[Point]]`) binds the borrowed element as `auto&& x = ::tpy::unwrap_ref(::tpy::tuple_elem_ref(std::get<0>(__tup_1)));`, and a later `x = q` emits a bare `x = q;` -- a copy-assign into the referent, so `p` silently becomes `q`. The `is_ref` leg of `_standalone_unpack_target_binds` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:2181`) picks bind mode `"ref"` at `:2239` off `_f1_record` alone and never consults `lc.prescan.reassigned`; `tpyc/thir/emit.py:4454` then spells the `auto&&` alias. So it misses the pointer-local promotion the sibling target classes at the same site already do for a reassigned name. Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. - **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `self: auto_own[Self]` combined with `@overload` emits every specialization TWICE with identical signatures.** `class W: @overload def m(self: auto_own[Self], x: int32) -> auto_own[int32]: ...` plus a `str` stub and an impl emits four member functions -- `int32_t m(int32_t)` and `int32_t m(std::string_view)` each declared twice -- and g++ rejects ("cannot be overloaded with"). Method expansion clones both the stubs and the impl into borrowing + consuming halves, so each stub appears twice; `_gen_overload_specialized_method` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) then takes `is_readonly=stub.is_readonly` but `is_consuming=impl.is_consuming` -- so the consuming axis comes from whichever clone `_collect_method_overload_groups` registered first and never varies per stub, leaving the two clones of each stub spelling one signature. Note the ownership consequence even if the duplication were suppressed: one polarity of the pair would be unreachable for the whole overload set, selected by clone-registration order rather than per-stub intent. The non-composed `auto_own` pair (no `@overload`) is unaffected -- it emits a borrowing and a consuming body correctly. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR: the emission is the AST path, and `codegen_cpp/functions.py` is untouched by the branch that found it. Loud, no corpus witness. Fix shape: derive the consuming polarity per STUB the way const-ness already is, and suppress the duplicate where both clones of a stub would spell one signature. Repro `/tmp/agents/ovl/aown.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR overload-clone skip; the reviewer reported it as a silent polarity collapse, and building the repro showed it is actually a hard compile error. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A record inheriting a builtin container with NO explicit `__init__` emits `using std::vector<int32_t>::list;` -- the inherited-constructor `using` spells the TPy type name instead of the C++ base's constructor.** `class Plain(list[int32]): pass` then `Plain([1, 2, 3])` fails with `'list' has not been declared in 'class std::vector<int>'`; a second error rides along (the ctor arg renders `std::array<int32_t, 3>` where the base wants `std::vector<int>`). The inherited-ctor `using` is emitted from the record's TPy base NAME, but the base's C++ spelling comes from the container formatter, so the two never agree for a formatter-carrying builtin -- the injected-class-name is `vector`, not `list`. Declaring any `__init__` avoids it (the record then has its own constructor). Loud, no corpus witness. Pre-existing -- reproduces unchanged at `5af9b227b`. Fix shape: emit the inherited-ctor `using` against the base's rendered C++ type (its injected-class-name), or suppress it for formatter-carrying builtin bases and synthesize a forwarding ctor. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh3/noinit.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR inherited-container row and confirmed independently. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid) `x in t` is rejected when `t` is a record inheriting `set` -- "Cannot use 'in' with non-iterable type Tags".** `class Tags(set[StrView]): ...` then `"x" in t` errors, though the record inherits `__contains__` from the set stub and CPython accepts it. The membership dispatch resolves `__contains__` / iterability against the receiver's own record, not its inherited builtin base, so every container-inherited operator-protocol dunder is suspect here (`in`, and by the same shape iteration and comparison dunders) -- ordinary inherited METHOD calls (`t.add(...)`, `t.discard(...)`) resolve correctly, so the gap is specific to the operator paths. Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: call the method form. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR (the reject is in sema). Witness: the shape was cut from `tests/cases/inheritance/inheritance_builtin_dict_set` for exactly this reason. Fix shape: let the membership / iterability resolution walk the record's parents to a builtin container base, as the method-call path already does. Surfaced writing that case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `super().<method>()` on a builtin-container base spells the TPy method name against the C++ base type, ignoring the stub's `@native` rename.** In `class Overrider(list[int32])`, an overriding `append` calling `super().append(value)` emits `this->std::vector<int32_t>::append(value)` -- `std::vector` has no `append`, g++ rejects. The qualified-super render composes `NominalType(parent).to_cpp()` with `escape_cpp_name(method)`, so it never consults `fi.native_name` (`push_back`) the way the ordinary inherited call does (`ml.append(10)` -> `ml->push_back(10)`, correct); a `@native(function=True)` stub like `pop` would need the free-function form instead, which that render cannot spell at all. Loud, no corpus witness -- overriding an inherited builtin method is already warned about ("Method 'Overrider.append' hides 'list.append'"), and no case does it. THIR keeps this on the AST path (the super-marked call is outside the plain-member slice), so no mirror to unwind. Fix shape: route the super/unbound-self dispatch through the same fi-driven native-name / free-function selection the plain member call uses, keeping only the base qualification. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh/ovr.py`. Surfaced probing the THIR inherited-container receiver row's override boundary. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `return <void call>` at a `-> None` slot rejects at `call.ret_type.void`, in a sync def and an `async def` alike.** [`async-void-return-drops-call`] `def outer() -> None: return noisy()` and `async def outer() -> None: await asyncio.sleep(0); return noisy()` (`noisy() -> None`, prints) both fail with `(expr.call:call.ret_type.void)`: the return lowering sees a non-None operand and lowers it as a value, and the call lowering refuses a void result, where CPython evaluates the call and returns its None. Before the `return None` canonicalization (2026-09-13) the async form was WORSE -- the resumable ReturnT arm keyed the whole render on the slot being void and never evaluated the operand, so the call was silently dropped; the one `_return_carries_value` verdict now routes any non-None operand at a void slot down the value arms, so both positions reject loudly and the silent drop is gone. Fix shape: a non-None operand at a void return slot is evaluated as a discarded statement before the bare `return;`, in the sync arm and the resumable ReturnT arm alike (one rule, both positions). Probes `/tmp/agents/review_retnone2/p_sync_void_call.py`, `/tmp/agents/review_retnone2/p_async_void_call.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, async-sink cells 4-7 round); re-verified after the canonicalization 2026-09-13. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A pointer-repr container NAME in a REF vararg pack takes `&name` over the un-deref'd pointer.** A module-global `list[T]` (a `T*` pointer slot) passed by name into a `*args: T`-style REF pack renders `&xs` -- `T**` where the `std::array<const T*, N>` element needs the deref'd `&(*xs)` -- a hard g++ error on BOTH codegen paths (reviewer-probed with the AST alone). No corpus witness (the committed vararg cases pass locals/elements). THIR mirrors the render; the BORROW_BIND threading in `_lower_vararg_pack` documents that its "renders identically" claim holds only for the currently-reachable record slice. Fix shape: the pack element render should read pointer names through the same deref the value positions apply. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, cells 15 round). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A `match` capture passed as a VARARG takes the address of an already-pointer local.** [`vararg-of-pointer-capture-takes-address`] `def bump_all(*counters: Counter)` called as `case Bag(c=q): bump_all(q)` emits `std::array<Counter*, 1> __tmp{&q}` where `q` is already a `Counter*`, so g++ reports `cannot convert 'Counter**' to 'Counter*' in initialization`. The capture binds to the pointer form (it aliases the subject's field), and the pack element render does not deref a pointer-repr NAME before taking its address. Same mechanism as the module-global `list[T]` REF pack entry above -- the pack element render is pointer-blind for every pointer-repr source, not just globals -- so fix them together. Pre-existing: identical on master, where the const-inference miss adds a second error ahead of it. This is why `tests/cases/match/match_capture_mutation_credited` has no vararg section, although the vararg arm of the call-edge attribution it covers does handle captures. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_vararg_simple.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++) A raw-lowered `@error_return` call with a nested `@error_return` call in its argument subtree renders ill-formed C++.** `self.p = make(inner(n))` (both callees `@error_return`, inside a try or auto-propagate body) emits the outer `__try_tmp_N` block with the inner call's expression-level unwrap misplaced -- g++/clang reject (`cannot convert std::expected<int,E> to int32_t`; `deduced type 'void' for '__try_tmp' is incomplete`). Any raw statement-level er sink reaches it (name bind, field target, discard); no corpus witness exists because sema/codegen never gated it -- the THIR side rejects the shape via `_reject_nested_error_return_arg` at all four statement sinks, keeping both paths in fallback lockstep without blessing the broken render. Fix shape: the AST's raw-call statement handlers must pre-hoist nested er unwraps (or reject with a diagnostic). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, long-tail cells 11 round) with a direct g++ compile of the AST-only output. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small, latent UB] A top-level global-slot write inside a FOR-loop body leaves the global pointing at a BLOCK-scoped slot; the WHILE-body twin freezes the first iteration.** At module init, a first rvalue write to a non-value global inside a for-each body emits the backing slot WITHOUT `static` (`Point __global_slot_1 = Point(i);`) and then `p = &__global_slot_1;`, so any read after the loop exits derefs a dead stack slot -- latent UAF that happens to pass exec (the frame memory is typically intact within `__tpy_init`; the repro below builds, runs and prints `2`). The `static` is dropped by `branch_scope=in_branch` on the `GLOBAL_RVALUE` `THIRPtrLocalDecl` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:4503`, gated to for-bodies at statements.py:7609) and consumed at `tpyc/thir/emit.py:3843` (`_gs_static = "" if stmt.branch_scope else state.slot_static`). The sibling scopes do NOT share the defect and must not be conflated with it: the same write inside an `if`/`while`/`with`/`try` body is a hard reject (`stmt.var_decl:top_level.global_slot_branch`, statements.py:7606), so until 2026-09-04 the for-body arm was the only one that emitted; the `if` / `with` / `try` bodies now emit too, correctly with `static` (`tests/cases/globals/global_slot_branch_and_hoist` for `if`, `tests/cases/control_flow/with_target_reuse_read_after_global` for `with`; `try` probe-verified); the `while` body still rejects (`tests/cases/globals/error_global_slot_while_write`), so the for-body arm is the one outlier still emitting the unsafe form. The `while`-body twin (2026-09-04, oracle-verified) is worse than latent: a module-level `while` whose body writes a non-value global prints `0 0 0` where CPython prints `0 1 2`, because the slot's first-iteration value is re-read on every pass; it still rejects on THIR. Witness: `inference/reassign_none_loop_narrowing` (post-loop `if x is not None: print(x.x)`). Repro: `class Point` with an `int32` field, `p: Point | None = None`, `for i in range(3): p = Point(i)`, then `if p is not None: print(p.x)`. Fix shape: NOT a bare static-ize -- `static T slot = init;` initializes once, which would freeze the first iteration's value. Route the for-body write through the existing hoisted flavor instead (`GLOBAL_HOIST_RVALUE`: a `static std::optional<T>` slot declared outside the loop, re-emplaced per iteration), which gives both a stable address and per-iteration assignment. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] Sema stamps concrete narrow facts on statically-dead branches of exhaustively-folded isinstance or-chains, emitting dead extractions.** `if isinstance(v, A) or isinstance(v, B):` on `v: A | B` folds the second leaf to `true` (the chain is tautological), yet the implicit-else path carries a concrete `{v: A}` fact -- the AST emits an unreachable `auto& __v = *std::get<A*>(v);` past the early-return if (and, for the negated flavor, inside the dead branch). Semantically harmless (unreachable code) but wrong facts on dead paths; both paths emit it identically (THIR mirrors the oracle per the byte-diff discipline -- see the or-chain wave ledger entry, 2026-08-12; witness `tests/cases/union/union_isinstance_or_chain`'s `two_member`/`negated_or`). Fix belongs in sema's fold-aware fact stamping, not in either emit path.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NARROWED-Optional field as a borrow-tuple element has no lowering arm.** In a method returning `tuple[Inner, int32]` (a `std::tuple<const Inner*, ...>` borrow tuple), `return (self.maybe, 1)` under `if self.maybe is not None:` dies with `error: in function 'get': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.tuple_literal)`, while the plain-field flavour `return (self.inner, 0)` compiles (both verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03). The earlier symptom was the un-deref'd `&(this->maybe)` -- an `std::optional<Inner>*` into the `const Inner*` slot, rejected by g++ -- and it is gone with the AST emitter. The field-element leg (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:11596`, rejecting at `:11612` with detail `btuple.elem_source`) excludes an Optional-DECLARED field deliberately, but its comment's rationale -- that the AST emitted the broken render there so the shape must defer until the AST is fixed -- is stale: that emitter is gone and this leg is the only author, so it simply owes the narrowed deref. Fix shape: render `&((*this->maybe))` for a proven-narrowed Optional field element instead of rejecting. No corpus witness (the committed borrow-tuple cases use plain fields/names). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Bytes ternary mixing a plain view-param arm and a bytes literal emits uncompilable C++.** `def f(c: bool, b: bytes) -> bytes: return b if c else b"x"` renders `return ((c) ? (b) : (::tpy::bytes_literal_owned("x", 1)));` -- the span param and the owned-vector literal have no common type, so the emit fails at the C++ step (clang: no conversion from `std::span<const unsigned char>`). Hidden because no exec witness exercises the shape (the narrowed `Optional[bytes]`-param flavor takes the whole-ternary `bytes_copy` wrap and compiles). Surfaced 2026-08-07 by the THIR wave-39 widening: THIR's arm is narrowed to the value-opt-param flavor and the plain-param flavor keeps deferring (the fence pin that documented it went with the THIR unit suite) until this emit is fixed -- the likely fix is applying the same owned materialization the str-mixed arms get.
- **[HIGH small] (silent UAF, certain) A `StrView` FIELD member-initialized from an owned-str-returning CALL dangles immediately.** `self.view_field: StrView = make_greeting(name)` in a ctor emits `Holder(...) : view_field(make_greeting(name)) {}` -- the `std::string` temporary dies at the end of the mem-initializer, so the `std::string_view` field points at freed storage from construction onward. - **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, `__del__`-observable) A value moved into an `Optional[Own[R]]` PARAMETER is destroyed at the callee's return, while CPython keeps it alive to the caller's frame end.** [`opt-own-by-value-param-early-del`] `def take(p: Own[Pic] | None) -> int32` called as `take(other)` with `other: Pic | None` at its last use (or a plain local moved into the same slot, `auto_move/auto_move_own_optional_narrowed`): the parameter is a by-value `std::optional<Pic>`, so the moved-in payload dies when the callee returns, where the caller's `other` still names the object in CPython. The plain `Own[Pic | None]` spelling binds `&&` and matches; `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` states the `T&&` contract for `Own` parameters and now names this exception. Fix shape: give the `Optional[Own[T]]` parameter the same `&&` form. Pre-existing at the constructor slot; reachable from free functions and methods since 2026-09-11. Found 2026-09-11 in review.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[R] | None` PARAMETER forwarded into an `Own[R | None]` element slot rejects at `method.arg_shape`.** [`opt-own-param-forward-into-own-opt-slot`] `def f(p: Own[Pic] | None, sink: list[Pic | None]) -> None: sink.append(p)`; the `Own[Pic | None]`-spelled parameter forwards fine, and a pointer-repr `Pic | None` LOCAL at the same slot rebuilds and moves since 2026-09-11 -- the parameter's `Optional[Own[R]]` spelling has no row at the slot, and inside the callee `return p` rejects at `return.storage_opt_source` and a narrowed write `p.n += 2` at `stmt.aug_assign` -- the spelling is admitted at the signature and usable only for reads. Found 2026-09-11. Pre-existing on master `331fbc2948`.
- **[LOW small] (spurious warning; an unneeded copy) Storing an `Own[R | None]` PARAMETER into an `R | None` field copies and warns instead of moving.** [`own-optional-param-field-store-copies`] `def __init__(self, p: Own[Pic | None]) -> None: self.p = p` warns `copies Pic | None into field; use copy() to make this explicit` and, when the field store is the only use, also `Own[Pic | None] param 'p' is never consumed`; the plain `Own[Pic]` twin moves silently. The parameter is the caller's transfer, so the store is the consumption and should render the null-safe move the argument slot already renders for the same shape. Found 2026-09-11. Pre-existing on master `331fbc2948`.

Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the scope-leak fix.

No repro constructed -- a targeted probe (leftover `readonly[A | B]` const-ref param colliding with a ctor's Own-union param) rendered correctly because the MIL move arm consults none of them, and ctor params are never const-ref by design (a ctor's params carry no const verdict). The failure class is the fixed bug's: a same-named collision flipping a silently-different-but-compiling render. If a repro appears, extend the scoped seeder's clear with a purpose-named field tuple ("names read during the pre-setup window") rather than overloading PARAM_LOCAL_SET_FIELDS further. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + codegen-correctness).
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A WALRUS inside a PLAIN LAMBDA argument binds the ENCLOSING function's slot while the lambda captures nothing -- g++ rejects.** [`lambda-arg-walrus-not-captured`] `def app(f: Fn[[int32], int32], x: int32) -> int32: return f(x)` called as `app(lambda v: (w := v + 1) + w, n)` emits `int32_t w;` at FUNCTION scope plus a capture-less lambda `[](int32_t v) -> int32_t { ... (w = ::tpy::add_check<int32_t>(v, 1)) ... }`, so g++ answers `error: 'w' is not captured` / `note: the lambda has no capture-default`; CPython runs the same program and prints `r 4`, the walrus being a local of the lambda there. Not overload-specific -- identical emission through a plain non-generic `Fn` param and through a `@dispatch` pair (probes `/tmp/agents/restore_fix/r1b_control.py` and `/tmp/agents/v_live/p16_plain_fn.py`, byte-identical at and before the live-handle restore fix, verified 2026-09-17). The genexpr-filter sibling (a walrus in a genexpr filter) has the opposite scoping question, BUGS.md#genexpr-walrus-target-stays-in-frame: there the target genuinely belongs to the enclosing function, whereas a lambda is its own scope in Python -- the sema half of this one is BUGS.md#lambda-body-walrus-binds-enclosing-scope, which says the binding must BECOME the lambda's own local. Fix shape: bind a lambda-body walrus target in the lambda's own scope and emit it as a body-local (no function-scope hoist, no capture), landing it with that entry -- adding `&w` to the capture list instead would compile but keep the CPython divergence that entry records. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the live-handle restore fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) An `assert isinstance(...)` narrowing inside one branch of a RESUMABLE body (generator/async) leaks its C++ extraction alias into sibling branches of the flat CFG -- g++ rejects.** `def gen(a: int | str, flag): if flag: assert isinstance(a, int); yield str(a + 1) / else: print(a)` emits `const auto& __a = std::get<...>(a);` scoped inside the if-block and then references `__a` again in the else-block, where it is out of C++ scope -- `'__a' was not declared in this scope`. The non-resumable equivalent compiles fine (the persistent alias and its readers share a scope there); only the flat-CFG resumable driver splits them. Same flat-CFG-scoping family as the `await`-in-`except ... as e:` entry below, different root: the U4 persistent assert-narrow alias is emitted block-scoped while its narrowing fact stays live for the rest of the function. Fix shape: hoist the persistent extraction alias to frame/function scope in resumable bodies (or re-extract per BB). THIR fences the shape rather than mirror it (the union STR print row rejects in resumable bodies; the unit that pinned both the fence and the leak's mutation-detection went with the THIR unit suite); fixing the AST unfences it. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + docs-sync, the dynret/union-returns round; both compiled independent repros). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A reassigned borrow-tuple local with ONE const binding source and a later ELEMENT WRITE emits ill-formed C++.** `_compute_borrow_tuple_const` ORs const over ALL binding sources, so `t = h.pair; t = h2.pair; t[1].val = 9` (h const-inferred, h2 not) declares `std::tuple<int32, const Box*> t` and then writes through the const pointer -- g++ rejects (`assignment of member ... in read-only object`) though the write targets h2's mutable storage and CPython accepts. The const-OR is right for declarations (mutable->const lift compiles) but the ELEMENT-WRITE fact must feed back: a written name needs its const sources rejected in sema (a located diagnostic) or the write must re-anchor. Loud, toolchain-caught, no corpus case (the existing cases never write through a const-flipped name). - **[HIGH small] (compiler crash on valid code, contract violation) A `THIRValidationError` escapes as an internal error instead of a located reject and kills the compile: a temp-needing call ARGUMENT at a tuple-unpack source.** [`thir-validator-escapes-unpack-temp`] `a, b = f(M())` -- the unpack-source call's ctor arg needs an arg temp, the unpack position does not thread `allow_temps`, and the gate admits the shape anyway; lowering builds a `THIRArgTemp` under the non-flushable statement and the post-lowering validator raises, so plain `tpyc --dump-code` exits 1 with `Internal error: main: THIRArgTemp at SourceLocation(...): THIRArgTemp under a non-flushable statement position` (re-reproduced 2026-09-02; originally probe-found while widening the tuple-return source gate, 2026-08-03, and verified pre-existing on `4b4983395`). This violates the stated lowering contract -- a shape lowering cannot handle must raise `ThirUnsupported`, which the fold point turns into a located `ThirRejectError`, never escape as an internal error. The general claim rides here: a too-strict validator RULE is a compiler crash on valid code, not a diagnostic. This entry is the only live holder of that claim -- its former sibling was withdrawn. **A SECOND node type reaches the same escape at the same position:** `a, b = send(b"hi")` where `send` takes a `bytes | dict[str, str] | None` -- the bytes literal needs a union-lift temp, and lowering builds a `THIRUnionArgLift` under the non-flushable unpack, dying with `Internal error: main: THIRUnionArgLift at SourceLocation(...): temp-bearing THIRUnionArgLift under a non-flushable statement position`. So the over-admission is not specific to `THIRArgTemp`: the unpack source's flushability is not threaded into ANY temp-bearing arg gate. Fix shape: thread the unpack source's flushability into the call-arg gate, so the gate refuses the temp-needing arg and the reject is reported at the blocking line. Routing the raise somewhere gentler is not an option -- with a single author a validator raise has nowhere to go, so per-RULE correctness is the only fix and every structural rule must be exactly as strict as the render actually requires. No corpus case holds either shape, and the unit that asserted the CURRENT raise went with the THIR unit suite; the two spellings above are the reproduction. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `@overload` impl whose isinstance dispatch sits BEHIND a live dynamic branch is a hard compile error for the statically-True stub.** `@overload def judge(a: Dog, n: int)` + `(a: Cat, n: int)` over `def judge(a: Dog | Cat, n: int): if n > 3: return 'big'; elif isinstance(a, Dog): return a.name; else: return str(a.lives)` -- the Dog stub resolves the isinstance True BEHIND the live `n > 3` branch, and lowering declines the fold rather than emit a body that silently drops the dynamic branch: `error: in function 'judge': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.if:if.overload_true_after_dynamic)`. `_lower_overload_folded_if` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:7166`, the `if.overload_true_after_dynamic` detail at `:7200`) admits a chain only when the True-resolved node has no live predecessor; the fix is to emit the live prefix and fold the True node into its else tail. Not exotic -- an early-out guard ahead of the isinstance dispatch is an ordinary way to write an overload impl -- so worth queueing. The unit fixture that pinned the reject went with the THIR unit suite. Surfaced designing the THIR live-chain mirror. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) BODIED `@overload` variants (mode b) with `Literal` params emit unmangled duplicate definitions while the CALL site references the mangled name -- the C++ never compiles.** Two bodied stubs `def k(a: int32, m: Literal["fast"]) -> int32: <body>` / `Literal["slow"]` emit as two identical `int32_t k(int32_t, std::string_view)` definitions (duplicate symbol), while the call `k(1, "fast")` emits `k__lit_fast(1, "fast")` -- a symbol nothing defines. The bodied-stub fall-through in `gen_function_def` never applies `literal_mangled_name`, but the call-site `is_literal_mangled` predicate keys only on "multi-overload + resolved fi has a Literal param" and fires regardless. Loud (duplicate definition + undefined reference), no corpus case (the shape cannot pass exec). Both paths emit identically -- THIR routes the call with the same mangled spelling via the shared helper, so this is AST-side, not a divergence. Fix shape: mangle bodied literal-stub DEFINITIONS with the same `literal_mangled_name` (definition + forward decl + cross-module attr spelling), or reject the bodied-Literal combination in sema. Repro: the two bodied `Literal` stubs above plus the `k(1, "fast")` call, through `--dump-code` (the unit that carried the source went with the THIR unit suite). Surfaced re-pinning the callee-reject units for the THIR literal-overload round. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) An augmented assignment through a CALL receiver (`o.get().v += 1`) double-evaluates the receiver call in generated C++ where CPython evaluates it once.** [`augassign-call-receiver-double-eval`] The aug-assign arm of `_lower_stmt` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` lowers `stmt.target` TWICE -- once as the assign lvalue, once as the binop's left operand (the `else` leg beside the class-constant `_lower_class_const_write_target` split) -- so `target OP= value` becomes `target = (target OP value)` with the receiver call spelled on both sides. Verified 2026-09-03: `uv run tpyc --dump-code` emits `o.get().v = (o.get().v) + (::tpy::BigInt(1));`, and `uv run tpy` reports 2 receiver calls where CPython reports 1. The only exercised receivers are pure accessors (Box.get), so the cpy phase stays green. **The `@property` spelling is HELD at a reject**: a read is a method call from sema on, so `b.rec.x += 1` would otherwise emit `b.rec().x = ::tpy::add_check<int32_t>(b.rec().x, 1);` and run an IMPURE getter twice -- the shape that makes this observable rather than merely wasteful. Because evaluation order is a postponed language decision, fixing that one site would settle the class by accident and leave the spelled-method twin disagreeing, so a getter anywhere on the target's receiver chain rejects with `augassign.recv.accessor_double_eval` (`_augassign_recv_is_accessor`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`), pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_property_augassign_receiver`. The reject goes when this entry is fixed, not before. The `<call>.field += ...` spelling (`borrow_out(b).x += 1`) is untouched and still double-evaluates; it is pinned as a render by `tests/cases/records/property_read_positions`' `return_pos` section, whose comment names it. Same family as the temp-hoisted argument ordering entry below: one expression, spelled more than once in the render, where CPython spells it once. Fix: evaluate the receiver once into a local and aug through the alias; the class-constant leg already splits its receiver eval off exactly once via `recv_eval`/`recv_wrap`, so extend that split to a general call receiver. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) Copying a non-copyable recursive-union member out of an accessor (`w = box.get()`) passes sema and fails only at g++.** A recursive-union wrapper (`type Value = int | str | Neg` where `Neg` owns a `@nocopy` `Box[Value]`) holds `Neg` by value in its `std::variant`, so `Neg`'s deleted copy ctor deletes `Value::Value(const Value&)` -- and a plain decl `w = n.inner.get()` (a borrow-returning accessor result copied into an owned local) emits `Value w = n.inner.get();`, which g++ rejects with `use of deleted function`. CPython runs the same line fine (it aliases). No front-end diagnostic points at the copy; contrast `error_union_box_field_copy`, which catches the structurally identical copy at a FIELD-assignment site -- the local-decl sink is missing the same check. Both codegen paths emit the identical (uncompilable) C++, so this is an AST-side sema gap, not a THIR divergence. Repro: the wrapper-accessor decl above run through the toolchain (probe left at `/tmp/agents/probe_wrapper_copy3.py`); the unit fixture that carried it went with the THIR unit suite. Fix shape: extend the union-member copy check that guards field assigns to owned-local decl (and likely return/arg storage) sinks. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the THIR receiver-row wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) `is_type_non_copyable` has no `UnionType` arm, so a store into a field/container typed as a union of `@nocopy` members is never rejected.** [`union-nocopy-field-store`] With `A` and `B` both `@nocopy` and a field `u: A | B`, `self.u = tmp` emits `::tpy::to_value_variant<std::variant<A, B>>(tmp)` and dies in raw libstdc++ spew (`no matching function for call to 'std::variant<A, B>::variant(...)'` -- the variant's copy ctor is deleted because an alternative's is) with no TPy diagnostic. The structurally identical store into a `@nocopy` RECORD field IS rejected (`cannot copy non-copyable type 'Box[Expr]' into field`, pinned by `tests/cases/union/error_union_box_field_copy`), so this is one missing arm, not a policy. Both `tpyc/sema/context.py:1337` (`is_type_non_copyable`, which upgrades the copy WARNING to an error) and its narrower sibling `is_type_nocopy` (`:1296`) walk `Readonly` / `Own` / `Optional` / `Tuple` / `RecursiveAliasInstanceType` / dyn-protocol / record and then fall through to `get_record_for_type(<union>)` -> `None` -> `False`. The recursive-alias arm exists for exactly this reason (its comment: a non-copyable alternative propagates through the wrapper's `std::variant`), and a plain union lowers to a `std::variant` just the same. Sema-layer, so both codegen paths inherit it. Independent of the last-use copy-warning suppression: verified at the local's last use (no warning at all) and at a non-last use (warns `copies B into field` but never upgrades), both spewing. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Fix shape: give both helpers a `UnionType` arm returning True when any member is non-copyable. Repros `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion/main.py` (last use) and `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion2/main.py` (non-last use). Surfaced probing the field-store copy-warning suppression. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `await` inside an `except ... as e:` handler body reads `e` out of scope in the generated coroutine.** The handler binding is a C++ `catch (const MyErr& e)` parameter, but the resumable frame splits the handler body at the suspension, so the post-resume code reads `e` from a later, disjoint `case` block after the catch scope has already exited -- g++ reports `'e' was not declared in this scope`. Idiomatic async retry/logging code (`try: await op() / except TimeoutError as e: await report(e)`) is valid Python and gets raw compiler spew. Root cause is that an except capture is never given frame storage: it lives only in the catch parameter, so it has nowhere to survive a suspension. The `with` member of this family is fixed -- a target is frame-resident unconditionally and the emit binds through that field -- and the remaining siblings are this one, which has no gate at all, and the match capture, whose `needs_frame_field` gate is still narrower than the construct (see the match entry below). Fix shape: give a handler binding read after a suspension a frame slot and copy the caught value into it at catch time, so the resume block reads the slot rather than the dead parameter. Note the capture must take an OWNING frame copy, not the aliasing form the `with` target uses: `_classify_pointer_alias_locals` deliberately excludes handler bindings because the caught object dies at handler end, so a pointer would dangle. Verified on master, independent of the capture-registration work. Three separate review passes converged on this same missing-frame-storage gap, of which this is the sharpest form. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (cpy stub divergence, blocks test coverage) The `lib/cpy` `Span` stub mis-bounds a span minted by `take_ptr(x).span(n)`, so the last element raises where TPy reads it fine.** `a = Array[int32, 3]([10, 11, 12]); s = take_ptr(a[0]).span(3)` then `s[2]` prints `12` under TPy and raises `RuntimeError: span index out of bounds` under `PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`, while `len(s)` reports `3` on both -- so the stub's length and its index bound disagree. Stub-only (`lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py` ~406, seen only by CPython), so it is a test-infrastructure defect rather than a compiler one, but it blocks cpy-comparing any case whose shape needs a pointer-minted Span: `control_flow/with_target_pointer_bearing_value` had to drop its `Span` half for exactly this reason (the shape is still covered by the compiler fix and a scratch probe, just not by an exec+cpy case). Repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/spanchk/main.py`. Surfaced authoring the pointer-bearing-value with-target case.
- **[LOW small] (inconsistent fact, no observable effect today) A `with ... as t` target records `Own[T]` as its frame-local type where an ordinary binding of the same value records `T`.** `def __enter__(self) -> Own[Item]` makes the target's `generator_locals` entry `Own[Item]`, while `t = make()` over the same `-> Own[Item]` function records `Item`. The storage consequence is closed -- the frame-layout plan now looks THROUGH `Own` at the object it names, so both spellings land on the same `frame_slot<Item>` field (before that, the target's `Own` read as a value type and took a bare field, which default-constructed at frame creation and so failed to build outright whenever `Item` held a non-default-constructible member such as a `Box`; pinned now by `control_flow/with_target_own_enter_no_default_ctor`). What remains is the recorded type itself: two different answers for the same value depending on how it was bound, which any future consumer keying on it would read differently. Fix shape: record `T` at the with target, matching the ordinary-binding spelling, and drop the plan's `Own` unwrap if nothing else needs it. Surfaced by the inverse test of the with-target storage fix.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A return-tier `try`/`except` in which EVERY path returns emits an unreachable fallthrough with no return, so `-Werror=return-type` rejects it.** `def outer(k: str) -> int32: try: return inner(k) / except NotFound as e: return e.code` (with `inner` `@error_return`) emits the `goto`-based return tier ending `__after_try_1:; }` -- both real paths return, but the label is still a syntactic fallthrough point, so g++ reports "control reaches end of non-void function". A plain `uv run tpy` builds it (the harness compiles with warnings-as-errors, which is what surfaces it), so it bites the test suite and any `-Werror` build. Pre-existing and independent of name shadowing -- reproduced with a non-colliding binding, `/tmp/agents/scopens/p_rt_plain.py`. Existing return-tier corpus cases miss it because they re-raise or continue after the try rather than returning on every path. Workaround: assign in the handler and return after the try (what `tests/cases/name_shadowing/except_return_tier_shadow` does). Fix shape: emit an unreachable-return (or `__builtin_unreachable`) after the join label when every tier path terminates. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `match` capture that persists past the match and is read by a LATER suspension gets no frame slot.** `needs_frame_field` (`sema/match.py:171-175`) only scans for suspensions inside the match statement's own arms, but a capture is an ordinary function local in Python and stays live afterwards -- so `case 5 as hit: ...` followed later in the body by `yield hit` leaves `hit` as a C++ local scoped to one switch-`case`, read out of scope from a later one. Undiagnosed C++ build failure. The predicate needs to ask whether the capture is read after any suspension anywhere in the body, not just within the match. Reproduced: `case 5 as hit: pass / case _ as hit: pass` then `yield 1` / `yield hit` gives `error: 'hit' was not declared in this scope` where CPython prints `1` then `5` -- repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/v_match_after.py`. Pre-existing (byte-identical on master). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `with ... as NAME` capture that reuses an already-bound name, and any `with` whose `__enter__` returns a tuple, are hard compile errors.** `x = 1` then `with Counter(5) as x:` (a `-> Counter` `__enter__`) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.with)` -- valid Python, since CPython simply rebinds the name. A borrow-form TUPLE target is the second face and needs no reuse at all: `__enter__ -> tuple[Item, int32]` bound by a single `with CM(base) as p:` rejects with the same bare `stmt.with`. `_lower_with` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:15100`) admits a fixed ladder of target rows -- plain non-value hoist, pointer predecl, the frame-resident flavors -- and raises `stmt_reject_reason(stmt)` with no detail for everything else, so the message names no shape. Two things are owed: a located TYPE diagnostic for the incompatible-type reuse (`_analyze_with` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` still calls `current_scope.define` unconditionally, bypassing the reassignment-type-mismatch check that guards a plain `x = ...`), and a tuple-target row. The SAME-type value reuse this entry also covered is FIXED: `case 1 as v:` then `with CM(7) as v:` (a `-> int32` `__enter__`) now emits `auto v = __ctx_1.__enter__();` in its own scope, builds and runs. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the with-target storage branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) A read of a name shadowed by a later-arm `match` capture reports callability, not the shadowing.** `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` where `helper` is also a module function reports `'helper' is not callable` -- correct to reject (CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`, since the capture makes the name a function-local), but the message names neither the `match` capture nor the scoping rule, so a user whose code compiled before this became reachable has no path from the message to the cause. Pinned by `tests/cases/name_shadowing/error_match_capture_shadows_function`. Fix shape: when the shadowing binding is a pattern capture, say so and point at the capture. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) A `match` capture does not make its name a function-local for the arms BEFORE it, so an earlier arm can still reach an outer binding of that name.** Python makes a capture pattern's name a function-local everywhere in the enclosing function, so any arm referencing it raises `UnboundLocalError` unless that arm bound it -- verified: `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` raises in CPython. Arms AFTER the capture behave correctly (the binding is visible and the read is rejected); arms BEFORE it still resolve the name to the module-level function and silently succeed. Same family as the post-handler `except` read entry below: TPy models captures as block-scoped where Python scopes them to the function. Closing both means function-scoped capture locals (bind-then-mark-dead), a variable-model change tracked in TODO.md -- not a local patch, and NOT fixable by resetting the namespace per arm, which would re-break the after-arms case that now works. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic) The unconsumed-`Own` warning is WHOLE-TUPLE granular, so a dropped owned ELEMENT is never reported.** [`unconsumed-own-warning-whole-tuple-granular`] A scalar `Own[T]` param that is never consumed warns (`Own[Box] param 'x' is never consumed`), and a fully-owned tuple param that is never touched warns (`owned tuple param 'p' is never consumed`) -- but the tuple form is an all-or-nothing check on the aggregate. Two shapes slip through, both verified: (1) a fully-owned tuple that IS unpacked but then drops an element (`a, b = p; sink(a)` -- `b` is never consumed, no warning), since an unpack at the source's last use counts as consuming the tuple; and (2) a MIXED `tuple[Own[A], B]` param whose owned element is never consumed, which warns nothing at all because it is not an "owned tuple param" to begin with. Under the elementwise rule (`TODO.md`) element `i` should behave as `Ti` would as a singleton at that position, and a singleton `Own[T]` param warns -- so both should. The remediation is the same one the scalar warning implies: drop the `Own` from that element and take a borrow. Note shape (2) additionally cannot be consumed even if you try (see the mixed-param consume entry above), but the warning is a separate defect: it is missing for shape (1) too, where consumption works fine. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A HOISTED mixed owned+borrow tuple local fails to build when its OWNED element is not C++-default-constructible.** `try: p = make_mixed(c)` / `except: p = make_mixed(c)` for `-> tuple[Own[Guard], Cell]` emits the hoisted decl `std::tuple<Guard, Cell*> p;` and then assigns -- but a class with `__del__` (a user `__del__`, or `Box[T]` / `Rc[T]` / `Arc[T]`) suppresses the C++ default ctor, so g++ reports `no matching function for call to tuple<Guard, Cell*>::tuple()`. The straight bind and the rebind are unaffected (both declare WITH an initializer), and the all-borrow sibling is immune (its elements are pointers, always default-constructible) -- this is specific to the mixed tuple's by-value owned half at the one decl path that must declare before it can assign. Distinct from the nearby tuple entries: no `Own` marker, no rvalue source, and the mismatch is the Optional-WRAPPED tuple param rather than a bare tuple. **Second, separable defect on the same shape:** adding a default (`= None`) emits `= std::nullopt` at the free-function declaration, instantiating `std::optional<std::tuple<Rec, ...>>` over the still-incomplete `Rec` -- the hazard `default_needs_call_site_fill` (`typesys.py`) exists to dodge, which it misses here because it tests the Optional's inner for `NominalType.is_user_record` and that inner is a `TupleType`. Surfaced by the semantic-conflict pass of `/tpy-merge-master` on `fix-positional-defaults`, probing whether master's new tuple-form facts interact with the default-suppression rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence) A MIXED owned+borrow tuple GLOBAL (`G: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(V)`) takes owning storage and COPIES its borrowed element where the local twin aliases it.** [`global-tuple-ref-storage-form`] The all-borrow half of this entry is closed (2026-09-22): a tuple of references at a module global is the tuple of the pointer slots every reference-typed global is (`std::tuple<Box*, Box*> G{}`, bound once at module init, rebind from a function body refused with the scalar's error), so `G: tuple[Box, Box] = (V, V)` then `G[0].n = 43` reaches `V` (TPy 43, CPython 43); a fresh literal element makes the global OWN it (sema marks it `Own` on the binding, storage form, nothing to alias), and an importing module reads the form off the binding type. What remains is the MIXED global: `mixed: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(V)` for `-> tuple[Own[Box], Box]` records `tuple[Own[Box], Box]` on the binding, keeps storage (`std::tuple<Box, Box> mixed`), and `tuple_to_storage` copies the borrowed element, so `mixed[1].n = 44` prints TPy **2** vs CPython **44**, silently -- pinned by the `mixed_write` section of `tests/cases/tuple/element_vs_singleton_global` (which keeps `no_cpython.txt` for exactly this line). The local twin (`p = make_mixed(V)`) takes the mixed render `std::tuple<Box, Box*>` and aliases; the global would take the same render -- the owned element by value in static storage, nothing dangles -- with the declare-then-assign default-constructibility caveat the `Own`-element entry below records. Until then the cheap half is the stopgap warning at this sink (TODO: "Warn at the mixed-tuple module GLOBAL as a stopgap"): the per-element copy warning the field and container sinks already give, so the divergence is acknowledged rather than silent. The same form closes a second cell: a tuple global that OWNS a reference element (`tg = mk(1)` off `-> tuple[Own[Box], int32]`, or `(1, Box(5))`) is its own storage, so a module-level rebind (`tg = mk(7)`) would overwrite the object a pointer-slot target unpacked out of it (`gx, gk = tg` -- `gx` points into `tg`); the scalar global re-points at a fresh static slot and keeps the old object. That rebind is REFUSED at sema once such an unpack has happened (`Cannot reassign global variable ... a module-level unpack borrowed an element of it`, pinned by `globals/error_owning_tuple_global_rebind`; with no alias the rebind stays a plain storage assign, and the function-body form is held by the `global.unseeded` lowering reject rather than by the rule), which is the diagnostic that holds the cell until the owning tuple global is a pointer at per-assignment static backing -- the one mechanism both this and the mixed global need. The same backing is what a LATER module-level literal with a FRESH element needs: `P: tuple[Box, int32] = (V, 1)` then `P = (copy(W), 2)` at module level rejects (`expr.tuple_literal`) where the scalar `S = copy(W)` allocates a fresh static slot and re-points -- the elementwise render is `static Box __global_slot_N = copy(W); P = {&__global_slot_N, 2}` (loud today, a tuple-equals-scalar position gap; the first literal's fresh element is handled by the `Own` marking on the binding, a later one has no slot). Lowered HIGH -> MED with the all-borrow half closed; the mixed global is a narrower shape (a call returning per-element ownership, bound at module level). The old entry's second symptom (an alias into the tuple following a `global g` rebind) is a loud `global.unseeded` reject on both the base and the fixed tree, so it was stale, not closed. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (rejects-valid twice over, where the scalar warns) A borrowed tuple passed to an `Own[T]` CALL-ARG slot gets three verdicts depending only on the source's expression shape, where the scalar arg has one.** [`borrowed-tuple-at-own-call-arg`] `xs: list[Box]` + `xs.append(v)` (borrowed param) WARNS `copies Box into owned storage; use copy()` and copies (TPy 2, CPython 42 -- acknowledged). The tuple spelling `xs: list[tuple[Box, Box]]` gives: a LITERAL source `xs.append((v, v))` -> hard **error** ("Cannot pass borrowed value as argument 'value' tuple element 0 Own[Box] without explicit copy()"); an LVALUE source (`t = make(v); xs.append(t)`, `t = (v, v); xs.append(t)`, or a tuple PARAM) -> a located **reject** (`expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`), at last use or not; a CALL source (`xs.append(make(v))`) -> the per-element copy **warning** (`copies Box into owned storage (tuple element 0)`, one per element) and a copy, which is the scalar's verdict and the only one of the three that matches it. (Re-measured 2026-09-21 on `e43c7a5398`, repros `/tmp/agents/tupprobe/a/`: the lvalue source used to warn and the call source used to copy SILENTLY; the silent cell is gone.) Not a container-vs-user-function issue: a user `def sink(x: Own[Box])` called with a borrowed param emits the IDENTICAL warning to `xs.append(v)`, and a local at last use moves in both while a reused local warns in both (verified) -- `Own[T]` at a param means one thing everywhere and the call site needs only the signature. - **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A subscript read of a `bytes` tuple ELEMENT is rejected at every position, where the identical program over `str` compiles.** [`bytes-tuple-element-subscript-read-rejects`] `def f(t: tuple[bytes, int32]) -> None: print(t[0])` errors `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.expr_stmt:subscript.tuple_shape)`; swap `bytes` for `str` and it compiles and matches CPython. Measured 2026-09-21 on `e43c7a5398`, the same source at both element types: the reject holds for a tuple PARAM, a local bound from a call, a local LITERAL (`t = (b"xy", 1); print(t[0])`), a FIELD (`h.f[0]`), a container element (`xs[0][0]`), a `for` loop variable over `list[tuple[bytes, int32]]` and a module GLOBAL, and for every consumer tried -- `print(t[0])`, `len(t[0])`, `t[0] == b"x"`, `y = t[0]` (`stmt.var_decl:subscript.tuple_shape`), `return t[0]` and a call argument `g(t[0])` (`stmt.return:subscript.tuple_shape`). It keys on the element READ, not on the tuple: `t[0]` on `tuple[int32, bytes]` compiles, `t[1]` rejects. The workaround is the unpack (`x, k = t`), which compiles at every one of those positions but the GLOBAL -- there the unpack rejects too (`stmt.tuple_unpack`, while the `str` twin `x, k = G` compiles) and `print(G)` rejects (`print.arg.tuple_name`), so `G: tuple[bytes, int32] = (b"hello", 1)` can be declared and then not read by any of the five spellings tried. The mechanism is one missing family in the element gate: `_tuple_subscript_value_read` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) admits the element when it is a value scalar, `_owned_str_slot`, a callable value, a value `Optional`, a nested value tuple, an enum or a `Ptr` -- an owned `bytes` slot is the same `std::get<N>(t)` lvalue read as the owned `str` one (`const ::tpy::Bytes&` beside `const std::string&`) and is simply not listed. **Fix shape:** the owned-str arm becomes the owned VIEW-FAMILY arm, keyed on the element's value form rather than on a second type name, and the global-unpack and `print(G)` rejects are re-measured after it, since they may share the gate. Every consumer above needs checking against the `str` render, not only `print` (a `bytes` print goes through `BytesPrinter`). Not measured: a `bytearray` element, which is a reference type and stops earlier on a different tag (`len(t[0])` -> `call.native_arg.record_nonf1`); generator/async bodies; a nested tuple (`t[0][1]`). Surfaced by the tuple-element-vs-singleton matrix re-probe, where it blanked the whole `bytes` row; repros `/tmp/agents/tupmatrix/d6/`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; one undiagnosed build failure) The `Own` element of a MIXED owned+borrow tuple PARAM cannot be consumed, unpacked, aliased or written through.** [`consume-own-element-of-mixed-tuple`] `def f(x: Own[Box])` renders `Box&&` and the callee may move `x`; `def f(p: tuple[Own[Box], Box])` renders `const std::tuple<Box, Box*>&` and every way of reaching element 0 as an owned value stops. Measured 2026-09-21 on `e43c7a5398`, a copyable `Box` and a `@nocopy` twin giving the same verdict in each cell: the unpack `owned, borrowed = p` is a located reject (`stmt.tuple_unpack`), whether or not `p` is used afterwards (a `sink(o)` of the unpacked owned element on the same body also warns `copies ... into owned storage` first, since the target is a borrow of the const param); the subscript consume `sink(p[0])` is a located reject (`expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_record_f1`); the element alias `owned = p[0]` is a located reject (`stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`); the write `p[0].n = 99` passes the front end and fails the C++ build (`assignment of member ... in read-only object`, the by-value slot inheriting the const outer reference -- the write-through half of the return/param asymmetry entry in the Safety section). What works is reading: `return p[0].n + p[1].n` compiles and matches CPython, and a write through the BORROWED element (`p[1].n = 77`) reaches the caller. CPython accepts all of it (`owned, borrowed = p; owned.n = 99; borrowed.n = 77; return p[0].n + p[1].n` prints 176). The rejects are the generic unlowered-shape message, not a diagnostic that names the limitation or the remedy (take the owned element as its own `Own[T]` parameter), and no case pins the PARAM flavour -- `tuple/error_mixed_tuple_name_unpack` pins the unpack of a mixed LOCAL. No `never consumed` warning fires for the element either (the whole-tuple-granular warning entry above), so the one element that cannot be consumed is also the one that never reports going unconsumed. The const-borrow param render is itself correct and deliberate (a mixed tuple's borrow slot aliases the caller, so the whole-tuple `&&` ownership ABI does not fit) -- what is missing is per-element move-out from it, which needs per-place partial-move tracking (see the aggregate-member move-out gap in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`). Lowered HIGH -> MED on the same measurement: the entry was HIGH for a silent lost write (the unpack copied the whole tuple off the const reference and printed 78 against CPython's 176) and a raw deleted-copy build failure for `@nocopy`; neither reproduces, both are located rejects now. Repros `/tmp/agents/tupprobe/m/`. Surfaced by the tuple-element-vs-singleton census. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Correct and located, just pointed at the wrong thing; the equivalent through the class NAME (`P.NOPE`) names the member. Fix shape: resolve the field against the record before falling through to the value read, so the miss reports the member. Surfaced probing `cls` in non-construct contexts on the classmethod branch.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) Binding an `except ... as` capture to a local alias fails the C++ build -- the catch parameter is `const` but the alias decl is a non-const reference.** `except MyError as exc: e = exc` emits `MyError& e = exc;` while the handler catches `const MyError&`, so g++ rejects with "binding reference of type 'MyError&' to 'const MyError' discards qualifiers". Toolchain-caught, not silent. Reading a FIELD off the capture (`exc.code`) is fine -- only binding the whole object to a local trips it. Verified byte-identical with and without the capture-registration fix, so it is independent of name shadowing: reproducer `/tmp/agents/scopens/p_alias.py` (a 3-line handler, no name collision). Fix shape: either the alias decl follows the catch parameter's const-ness, or the handler catches by mutable reference where the binding is later aliased -- the decl and the catch signature must agree. Surfaced while probing the capture-registration fix (the fix moved resolution far enough to reach codegen, exposing this). Note for whoever fixes it: `tests/cases/name_shadowing/except_capture_shadows_class` is read-only because mutating through the capture trips exactly this bug -- once it is fixed, that case wants a mutate-and-observe assertion so the boundary stops being parity-blind if catch ever becomes by-value.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) Reading an `except ... as NAME` capture AFTER its handler resolves to whatever NAME meant outside instead of raising.** CPython makes the capture a function-scoped local and deletes it at handler end, so a later read is `UnboundLocalError`; TPy unbinds the capture from the local namespace, which re-exposes the outer binding (a module-level class of that name, say) and the read silently succeeds. Probe: a class `Reg` with `code = 999` plus `except MyError as Reg: inside = Reg.code` then `return inside + Reg.code` prints 1006 under TPy where CPython raises. Accepts-invalid on pathological input, and the value read inside the handler is correct (that was the shadowing bug, fixed) -- only the post-handler region diverges. Closing it means modelling Python's function-scoped locals for captures (bind-then-mark-dead rather than unbind), which is a variable-model change, not a local patch: TPy's whole local model is block-scoped. Surfaced by the capture-registration fix.

Fix shape: the protocol-typed iterator decl needs the reference-preserving spelling (`auto&&`, or `decltype(auto)`) when the init is a borrow-returning `__iter__`; both paths must change together (byte-identity), and the concealing test wants a mutate-after-bind observation. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) on `thir-decl-slot-track`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent, unverified] `get_resolved_type`'s `var_types` short-circuit now resolves pending CONTAINER types too, and no test exercises that half.** The short-circuit was fixed to route through `resolve_type()` so a tuple-unpack target's `PendingStrType` no longer leaks out unresolved; `resolve_type()` also resolves `PendingListType`/`PendingDictType`/`PendingSetType`. That is the architecturally right chokepoint (the non-`var_types` path has always resolved both), but the container half is a behavior widening nobody has a witness for. The specific worry is one level down, in `_resolve_pending_container`'s BEST-EFFORT fallback (`make_list(elem)` / `make_dict` / `make_set`, taken when sema's resolution never ran). Before this change that path could not be reached from the short-circuit, so an unresolved pending list surfaced as a LOUD `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen` crash; now it can silently become `list[T]` where the truth is `Array[T, N]` -- a reference-vs-value guess, and a copy-vs-alias decision keyed on it would be a SILENT divergence, the project's most serious class. (The resolved answer itself is the truthful one -- returning it is strictly better than returning the raw pending node, which is why the fix is not to narrow the resolution back to views.) A whole-corpus comp run over both variants (view-only vs container-inclusive) produced byte-IDENTICAL output, and a review pass could not construct a reachable case across ~89 `get_resolved_type` call sites, so there is no evidence of a live defect -- this is filed because "unverified across 89 call sites" is exactly what resurfaces later as an aliasing bug, not because a symptom exists. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity, self-tagged low confidence) on `fix-pending-view-unpack`.
- **[MED small] (wrong answer from a type predicate, latent) `Own[T]` reports `is_trivially_destructible() == True` for every `T`, so `Own[bytes]` / `Own[list[int]]` claim to be cheap heap-free value types.** `OwnType.is_value_type()` returns `True` unconditionally (deliberate -- documented as "Own[T] uses T&& at param boundaries; treat as value type for other purposes", `tpyc/typesys.py:1673`), and `is_expensive_copy()` is NOT overridden, so it falls through to the base implementation whose `_nominal_td()` is None for a wrapper type and returns `False`. `is_trivially_destructible()` is `is_value_type() and not is_expensive_copy()` (`tpyc/typesys.py:523`), so it is `True and not False` regardless of the wrapped type -- confirmed directly: `OwnType(NominalType('builtins.bytes')).is_trivially_destructible()` is True where the bare `bytes` answers False. Fix shape: forward `is_expensive_copy()` (and probably `is_trivially_destructible()`) to `self.wrapped` on `OwnType` -- but check each existing consumer first, since `is_value_type()`'s unconditional `True` is load-bearing at param boundaries and the three predicates are entangled. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Fix shape, two independent parts: (1) body type inference needs a fixed point over the loop back-edge before dependent locals are typed (the real fix); (2) regardless, a float->int operand narrowing at a checked-arith emit site should WARN -- the silent `mul_check<int32_t>(double, double)` coercion is never intended. The const half of the shape now agrees (frame field, window seeding, and alias classification all read the deep-const verdict since `fix-yield-escape-verdict`); the remaining fix is the alias-ASSIGNMENT emission arm: a pointer-repr tuple element alias must copy the element pointer (`a = std::get<0>(p);`), not take its address -- the `&`-wrap is correct only for value-storage element sources.
