- **[MED small] A bare non-value borrow yield never climbs a field-path alias to its owning param/receiver -- the yield arm omits the `through_field=True` the return arm uses.** `b = o.f` then `yield b` (non-value elem type): the return branch marks with `through_field=True` (statements.py TpyReturn, comment names exactly this climb `b = o.f; return b -> o`), but the pre-existing non-value yield arm calls plain `mark_param_mutated(root)`, so the `"o.f" -> "o"` climb (context.py, through_field-gated) never runs and the owner stays unmarked -- the enclosing method can be wrongly inferred readonly (const receiver vs mutable `val_or_ref<T>` yield slot), the identical failure class the borrow-tuple yield fix closed. The new tuple arm three lines below DOES pass `through_field=True` -- the asymmetry is now intra-yield. Related when fixing: `mark_param_returned` has no 8a.5/field climb at all (loop-iterable + bp sources only), so `b = items[i]; return b` under-records `return_borrows_from` on BOTH sides -- **and so does the plain field alias**: `tmp = self.item; return tmp` records `return_borrows_from=frozenset()` where the direct `return self.item` records `{-1}` (verified by instrumenting `mark_param_returned`: `addr_taken_roots` yields `['tmp']` and `binding_provenance['tmp'].borrow_source_roots` is empty, so the climb has nothing to follow). Consequence beyond the yield asymmetry: `mutation_propagation` blocks readonly inference on `-1 in return_borrows_from`, so a method handing back a mutable borrow of self through a local hop can be wrongly inferred `@readonly`. The `with`-manager provenance question (`returns_borrow_rooted_at_self`) works around this with its own AST-level root walk; fixing the table would let it read the fact off `return_borrows_from` instead -- a combined "yield marking mirrors return marking" fix (this + the transitive-rule entry below) should sweep it. **No longer latent** (2026-09-15): `class Bag: items: list[Node]` with `def walk(self) -> Iterator[Node]: ... node = self.items[i]; yield node` is inferred readonly, so the frame binds `const Node*` against a `val_or_ref<Node>` yield slot and g++ rejects (`could not convert 'const Node' to 'std::expected<tpy::val_or_ref<Node>, tpy::StopIteration>'`) -- the subscript flavour of the same missing climb. Repro `/tmp/agents/frame_try_next/constyield.py`. Surfaced by the fix-yield-escape-verdict readiness retrospective. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW-MED small, latent] `yield inner(items)` never propagates the callee's borrow contract -- the return branch's transitive rule (8b rule 3) has no yield analog.** `_analyze_yield`'s escape marking walks `addr_taken_roots(stmt.value)`, which returns `[]` for calls, so a yield of a borrowing call result marks nothing: the callee's `return_borrows_from` is consulted at RETURN sites (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` TpyReturn branch, "8b rule 3") but not at yields. Mechanism verified; the free-fn shape compiles and runs correctly (`/tmp/agents/yieldfix/transitive_probe.py`), so the observable break needs a shape where the missing mark flips a verdict -- e.g. a METHOD generator yielding `pick(self.items)` staying wrongly readonly-inferred (const receiver vs mutable yield slot), or a param verdict staying const. Fix shape: mirror rule 3 at `_analyze_yield`'s marking block (same `resolved_function_info.return_borrows_from` walk, same readonly-callee exemption). Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the yield-escape tuple verdict (the non-transitive half is fixed). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A container extended with ITSELF relies on `tpy::list_extend`'s `v.insert(v.end(), other.begin(), other.end())` with `other` aliasing `v` -- standard-UB if the vector reallocates mid-insert.** [`list-self-extend-aliases`] Three spellings reach it, all emitting `::tpy::list_extend(v, v)`: `xs += xs`, the explicit `xs.extend(xs)`, and the FIELD form `self.nums.extend(self.nums)` (the last since 2026-09-05, when the stub arg rows stopped being spelled per receiver kind; the two NAME spellings are pre-existing). Verified working on the current toolchain (g++-14/libstdc++) for both no-realloc and forced-realloc sizes, so latent, not observed; CPython doubles the list. Fix shape, closing all three at once: a one-line self-alias guard in `list_extend` (`if (&other == &v)` reserve first or copy the source) -- the hazard is the runtime helper's, not the lowering's, and fencing the field spelling alone would refuse code the name spelling compiles today. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the pending-list aug-assign fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) An unsupported aug-op on a PENDING container target leaks the internal type repr in the error message.** `xs = [1, 2]; xs *= 2` errors correctly but prints `Operator '*=' is not supported for PendingList[IntLiteral(1), 2]#0` -- the pending type's debug repr, not a user-facing name (the annotated form prints `list[int32]`). Fix shape: render pending container types through their user-facing resolution (or a `list[...]` placeholder) in diagnostics. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the pending-list aug-assign fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid by design, tracked for the real fix) `a += b` falling back to a borrow-returning `__add__` (no `__iadd__`) is REJECTED with a located error -- CPython rebinds `a` to the returned object (aliasing).** The loud reject (sema/statements.py aug-assign fallback) replaced a silent divergence: the emitted in-place update copy-assigned the returned object's fields into `a`'s existing storage, so post-`+=` mutations of the aliased operand were invisible through `a` (TPy 1/1 vs CPython 1/77). The real fix is rebind-as-alias for aug-assign targets: promote the target to a pointer slot (the `aug_assigned` prescan set does not feed the `reassigned` set that drives `T* a` codegen) and register the borrow, mirroring the plain-assignment path. Escape hatches until then (named in the error): define `__iadd__`, or return `Own[...]` from `__add__` (the fresh-value fallback works and matches CPython). Test `error_augassign_borrow_fallback`; inverse in `op_own_return_fresh`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the operator-dunder borrow-return fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) A `__call__` with a concrete `Own[T]` param emits an `operator()` shim that forwards the param by bare name -- no `std::move` -- so the T&& delegation fails the C++ build unconditionally.** The method takes `T&&`; the shim's forward (`return __call__(x);`) passes an lvalue. The property-setter emit already handles this shape (`extension.py` moves Own-typed setter values); `_gen_call_operator` needs the same per-param `std::move` wrap. Loud, pre-existing (identical emit on master; probe `/tmp/agents/opreview/owncall.py`); adjacent to (but not introduced by) the shim-mirroring rework. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic noise) Non-scalar field writes can warn when a call result borrows only the containing record.** [`record-field-borrow-false-invalidation`]
  Numeric/character stored-field writes no longer warn: assigning an integer or
  augmenting it preserves both the record and its field storage. The remaining
  distinction is a borrow of the whole record versus a borrow into a field's
  payload. A call returning the record itself can still leave an ELEMENT loan
  on its root, so replacing a string/container field warns even when the result
  only aliases the record and remains valid. The same replacement can invalidate
  a view into that field, and a property setter can replace arbitrary storage,
  so neither warning may be suppressed by the field's type alone. Resolve the
  projected borrow contract before narrowing these residual warnings.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) An UNIMPORTED tpy type name used as a generic type ARGUMENT silently resolves to `?`; the error surfaces later at a use site as e.g. "Cannot index type ArrayList[?]" instead of the missing-import hint.** `al = ArrayList[int32, 4]()` without `from tpy import int32` compiles the construction with an unresolved type arg and errors only at `al[0]` ("Cannot index type ArrayList[?]") -- no location pointing at the subscript, no `'int32' requires: from tpy import int32` suggestion. Value/annotation positions get the hint (bare `char("x")` -> "'char' requires: from tpy import char"; `Own` in an annotation -> parse-time "requires"), so only the expression-level subscript type-arg slot misses it. Correct rejection, wrong message + location. Fix shape: route unknown names in generic-subscript type-arg position through the same missing-import suggestion machinery instead of yielding an unresolved `?` arg. Repro `/tmp/agents/relcheck` smoke (2 lines). Surfaced by the 0.5.0 wheel-packaging smoke test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A STEPPED slice of a `bytearray` returns `bytes` where CPython returns `bytearray`.** `bytearray(b"abcd")[::2]` is typed (and emitted) as `bytes` per the stub `bytearray.__getitem__(index: slice) -> bytes` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_bytes.py`), so downstream `isinstance`/mutation behavior diverges from CPython's fresh `bytearray`. The basic-slice overload returns `BytesView`, a separate documented view design; only the stepped form's concrete owned type is wrong. Fix shape: a `bytearray_stepped_slice` returning `Own[bytearray]` (mirror of `bytes_stepped_slice`; bytearray is a reference type, so unlike the value-typed `bytes` returns the `Own` spelling is load-bearing there). Surfaced by the operator-dunder borrow-return fix's stub-contract sweep (cpython-parity agent). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) `a is b` between two reference-type records is rejected -- "'is' / 'is not' can only compare Optional/Ptr/union types with None" -- where CPython answers identity.** Reference types have stable addresses in TPy, so `is` is expressible as an address compare; today only None/enum/bool-literal compares are allowed (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py:983`). With borrow-returning dunders/methods now genuinely aliasing, identity is only observable via mutation -- a first-class `is` would let tests and users assert aliasing directly. Value-type operands should stay rejected (no identity). Loud, pre-existing. Surfaced writing the operator-dunder borrow-return aliasing tests. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (semantics decision for mixed value/reference operands).
- **[LOW small] (accepts-invalid) A bound `self.__init__(...)` call from a NON-`__init__` method passes sema and emits `this->__init__(...)` -- a call to a nonexistent C++ member (only the real ctor exists), failing the C++ build.** Only the unbound `Parent.__init__(self, ...)` and `super().__init__()` spellings are sema-gated to inside `__init__` (`methods.py`); the bound form slips through. Loud today (g++ rejects), but note for any future fix: a naive destroy+reconstruct re-init emission would BYPASS the CPython-interop `has_views_into` guard (tp_init's registry scan protects only the boundary path), so a TPy-side re-init must either be rejected like the unbound forms or route through the same live-view check. Probe `/tmp/agents/reinit_probe.py`. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the borrow-view rung.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) A by-value FIELD typed as a DERIVED class emits an incomplete-type C++ error regardless of source order -- derived-class definitions are sorted after all plain records.** `class A: ...; class B(A): pass; class C: b: B` fails `field 'b' has incomplete type 'B'`: `sort_records_by_inheritance` emits every non-derived record's full definition before any derived one's, so a plain record holding a derived-typed field can never see the complete type first (moving `B` earlier in the source does not help). CPython accepts the program. Loud (toolchain-caught). Fix shape: make the record sort field-dependency-aware (a by-value field edge is as hard a dependency as a base-class edge). Probe `/tmp/.../ordprobe/main.py` (10 lines). Surfaced building the borrow-view upcast test (which it blocks -- the classifier's exact-match gate is unit-pinned in `tpyc/interop/test_export_shape_views.py` instead). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) `print(...)` writes each argument as it is evaluated, so an argument whose evaluation itself writes to stdout interleaves ahead of the earlier arguments' output.** [`print-arg-output-interleaves`] `print("prefix:", noisy())` where `noisy()` prints `side effect` and returns 7 emits `prefix: side effect` then `7`; CPython evaluates the whole argument list first and emits `side effect` then `prefix: 7`. The call lowers to a chained `std::cout << "prefix: " << noisy()`, and C++17 sequences an overloaded `<<`'s left operand before its right, so the literal reaches the stream before the callee runs. Silent, output-only, and needs a print argument that itself writes to stdout -- a debug/logging helper nested in a print is the realistic shape. Distinct from the reflected-binop and hoisted-arg ordering entries: those reorder the *evaluations*, this one interleaves the *output* while evaluation order is correct. Fix shape: evaluate every argument into temps before the first stream write (the temp-hoist machinery already exists for other arg shapes). Repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/v_print_order.py`. **Second face, same root:** when the argument RAISES instead of printing, the earlier arguments are already on stdout while CPython emits nothing at all -- `print("prefix", boom(0))` inside a `try` prints `prefix caught` under TPy and `caught` under CPython (`/tmp/agents/match_literal/printord.py`, 2026-09-15). The fix shape above closes both. The raising face includes an `@error_return` argument whose failure leaves through `except E` (`print("tag:", find(k))` prints `tag: ` before the handler's own line); `tests/cases/error_return/return_exception_value_surface` binds each call result before printing to stay clear of it (2026-09-18). Surfaced while re-verifying the with-target optional-copy entry, whose probe made the interleaving visible. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A REFLECTED record-dunder binop (`x // y` resolving `__rfloordiv__`) evaluates the right operand before the left -- CPython evaluates left-to-right.** The `is_reverse` swap (`wl, wr = wr, wl` in `_emit_binop`, `tpyc/thir/emit.py:755`, the swap at `:792`) happens before `expand_cpp_template` embeds the operand renders positionally (`({self}).__rfloordiv__({0})`), and C++ sequences the receiver expression before the argument -- so `make_n() // make_b()` with side-effecting operands prints `make_b, make_n` where CPython prints `make_n, make_b` (reflected dispatch happens AFTER both operands evaluate, left-to-right). Confirmed against CPython over `lib/cpy` on the same source. Silent -- output-only, observable only when both operands carry side effects (no corpus case; `truediv_floordiv_distinct` uses names/literals). Same class as the membership needle/haystack entry below; the fix is an evaluation-order temp for the left operand before the swapped render. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing the record-dunder rvalue admission (2026-07-22 wave). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) Membership with a CALL haystack evaluates the haystack before the needle -- CPython evaluates the needle first.** `needle_expr in f()` emits the haystack call's render first (the receiver of `.contains`/`.find`/`__contains__`), then the needle; CPython's bytecode evaluates the needle expression before the container expression, so when BOTH sides have side effects the observable order differs. Silent -- output-only divergence, only observable when both operand expressions carry side effects (rare; no corpus case). Both codegen paths share the shape (the AST membership arms and THIR's mirrors emit identically), so this is NOT a THIR drift -- fixing it means an evaluation-order temp (`auto&& __in_lhs = <needle>;` before the receiver render, like the tuple-literal membership arm already does) in BOTH paths, or accepting and documenting the divergence. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing the wave-next membership widenings; pre-existing, unchanged by that wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) An auto_readonly accessor whose body returns a reference field via a TERNARY into `T | None` is rejected on the const twin, though the equivalent statement form compiles.** `def __getitem__(self, w: int32) -> Rec | None: return self._v if w > 0 else None` (`_v: Rec`, a reference type) errors `Cannot pass readonly[Rec] as mutable readonly[Rec] | None in ternary branch`; the statement form (`if w > 0: return self._v` / `return None`) compiles and aliases correctly. Root cause: the implicit-auto_readonly const twin (readonly `self` => `self._v` is `readonly[Rec]`) checks the ternary return arm against the UN-projected mutable `Rec | None` return type, where the statement-return path projects const onto the return. Distinct from the mixed-arm ternary silent-copy entry below (that is a local-binding value-category copy with no diagnostic; this is a hard sema reject on a return). Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: use the statement form. Pre-existing (unrelated to the `getitem_function_info` tagging); surfaced writing the accessor-generic-returns temporary-receiver test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (project const onto the const-twin ternary return arm, mirroring the statement-return path).
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A METHOD returning a ptr-variant union (`-> Dog | Cat`) is a hard compile error -- in the body, and again at the call site.** `class Kennel: animal: Dog | Cat` with `def __getitem__(self, i: int32) -> Dog | Cat: return self.animal` prints `error: in function '__getitem__': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return)`; renaming the accessor to a plain `pick` rejects identically, and a method that merely relays a union PARAM compiles its body then rejects at the consumer with `(expr.method_call:method.ret_type)` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:9862`/`:12870`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:9036`). A FREE function with the same signature (`def pick(a: Dog | Cat) -> Dog | Cat: return a`) compiles and runs, so the reject is method-specific. The old analysis still names the shape to fix: `_apply_implicit_auto_readonly` (`tpyc/sema/method_expansion.py`) wraps ANY non-value accessor return in `ReadonlyType`, and `is_ptr_variant_union` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/forms.py`) never unwraps `ReadonlyType`, so the const twin's return slot is a `std::variant<const Cat*, const Dog*>` no return row can fill. Fix mirrors the Optional arm: unwrap `ReadonlyType(UnionType)` (or teach `is_ptr_variant_union` to see through the readonly wrapper) so the ptr-variant lift applies. Not exotic -- a union-returning getter or accessor is an ordinary shape -- so worth queueing. Same accessor-return family as the `@property` pointer-repr `Optional` entry below. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + meta-review reproduction) of the accessor-generic-returns branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A by-value `@property` read bound to a local is admitted only STRAIGHT-LINE and only for a CONTAINER-returning getter.** [`own-property-iterable-materialize`] `q = s.taken` for a `-> Own[Rec]` RECORD getter rejects `decl.slot_type`, and the same container-returning read branch-hoisted -- the two arms of an `if`/`else`, a `with` body, a `try`/`finally` -- rejects `reseat.branch_rvalue_source`, because `_rebind_rvalue_source_ok` admits only a `TpyCall`/`TpyMethodCall` rvalue and the branch-hoisted slot assign does not hand the read the STORAGE result use a call gets (`_rebind_rvalue_use`), so the source lowering rejects `method.ret_type`. The method twin (`q = s.take_m()`, the branch-hoisted `a = s.snap_m()`) compiles at both positions, so this is a property-vs-method gap in the accessor family. **The ITERATION half of this entry is fixed** (2026-09-18): a property read is a method call from sema on, so `for x in c.snapshot:` takes the owning `auto __obj_N =` capture on the sync route and the frame's own `__for_src_N` slot in a generator or `async def`, exactly as the spelled twin already did. The fences that stood in for that (`_by_value_property_iterable`, `foreach.by_value_property_iter`, `res.by_value_property_iter`) are gone, and the value-typed and VIEW-returning getters they also took are admitted with the `Own[...]` one -- pinned by `tests/cases/records/own_property_foreach`, `tests/cases/generators/gen_own_property_foreach`, `tests/cases/generators/gen_value_property_foreach` and `tests/cases/generics/open_t_property_value_foreach`. The frame flavour is re-admitted with the caller-blindness `frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller` describes, which is that entry's decision and not a fence this one can express. The bind-first workaround still applies to the two positions above and is pinned by `tests/cases/records/own_property_value_decl`; `list(c.snapshot)` still rejects at an argument-position row (`call.inst_arg_shape`). Repros `/tmp/agents/thir-tail-0821/impl-rd/smoke/e_prop_mut.py`. Same accessor-return family as the `@property` pointer-repr Optional entry below. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen while widening the THIR property-position rows. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `@property` getter returning a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` (`-> Rec | None`) emits an `std::optional<T>&`-returning accessor whose body returns rvalues/nullptr -- uncompilable C++ for any non-field-backed getter.** [`property-getter-pointer-optional-return`] Reachable from the `@export` boundary too since Optional crosses it (2026-09-22): an exposed-class `@property -> Optional[Cls]` is admitted by the boundary validator and fails in the module half with the same error, one line away from where a non-ext program fails -- the fix is this entry, not a boundary-side reject. A getter whose body is `if self.on: return self._v` / `return None` over a plain `Rec` field emits `inline std::optional<Rec>& Holder::value() { if (this->on) { return &(this->_v); } return nullptr; }` (and the same for the const twin), so g++ reports `invalid initialization of non-const reference of type 'std::optional<Rec>&' from an rvalue of type 'Rec*'` and the `std::nullptr_t` twin. The SIGNATURE convention is the printer layer's: `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:1581` gives a property getter the storage `std::optional<T>&` (or `std::variant<A,B>&`) return instead of the method convention (`T*`), which only holds when the body returns a stored optional FIELD; the body honours it at exactly one return row (`ret.opt_field_ref`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:11629`, a bare `self.f` read) and every other return takes the ordinary pointer-lift arms. Toolchain-caught, not silent. The fix must pick ONE convention for optional-returning property getters (likely the method convention: return `T*`, adjusting the property-read consumption sites symmetrically). Same accessor-optional family as the record-`__getitem__` fix on `fix-accessor-generic-returns` -- there the CONSUMER was wrong, here the EMISSION convention is. Surfaced by the accessor-generic-returns analysis (Phase 4 sibling survey). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A CONTAINER inner has the same two errors from a plain `return self._v` (`-> Optional[list[int32]]` over a `list[int32]` field, both twins, measured 2026-09-22 on master); the METHOD spelling of the same getter compiles.
- **[MED small] (miscompile) A plain record pointer-local reseated from a `readonly[T]` param emits `Point* p = &(q);` off a `const Point&` -- invalid const conversion, uncompilable.** `def f(q: readonly[Point], c: bool): p = Point(1); ...; p = q` renders the address-of without const-propagating the pointer decl (`const_indirect_locals` never sees the reseat-source constness). Identical on BOTH the AST and THIR paths (byte-identical, both broken); no corpus case exercises it. Either propagate const from the reseat source into the decl (making every read `const Point*`) or reject at sema (a mutable-pointer local aliasing a readonly param is arguably a readonly-model violation -- consider the sema-error tier first). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the escape-hoist cell.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Pending-container resolution never runs for a NESTED-function body, so ANY container literal declared inside a closure is unresolved at codegen.** [`nested-def-pending-container-unresolved`] The straight-line everyday shape is enough: `def outer(): def inner(): xs = [1, 2, 3]; xs.append(4); print(len(xs))` fails with `error: in function 'outer': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:container_lit.slot_family)` (the diagnostic names the ENCLOSING function, not the closure the literal is in). The free-function, method and top-level sites each call `LocalTypeDeduction.resolve_all()` immediately after `_prescan_and_analyze_body` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`); `_analyze_nested_def` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) is the one body site that does not, and `nested_def_scope` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) then discards the nested `FunctionTrackingState` via `restore_function_state`, so the nested body's pending stores -- `pending_branch_decl_maps`, `pending_composite_exprs`, `pending_loop_vars` -- are lost unfinalized and the enclosing function's later `resolve_all` never sees them. Second witness, a hard crash rather than a reject: a literal first declared inside an if/try/with/match BRANCH of a nested def reaches codegen as `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen` (`def outer(c): def inner(): if c: xs = [1, 2] else: xs = [3]; return xs[0]; return inner()`). Third witness, from the frame-captured-view hoist: `gen([1, 2, 3])` at a `Span[int32]` generator param inside a closure rejects with `generator/coroutine view argument's backing type is unresolved` -- the hoist spells its backing temp off the RESOLVED container type, and inside a nested def there is none. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/nested/a.py` (reject) and `/tmp/agents/nested/b.py` (view hoist). Fix shape: run the deduction pass for a nested body exactly as the outer one does -- `self.deduction.resolve_all()` inside the `nested_def_scope` block, right after `_prescan_and_analyze_body` -- which covers all three stores at once; that one line compiles both reproducers (corpus impact unmeasured). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + safety-model) of `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`; broadened from the branch-only flavor while closing the frame-captured-view hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) `list(d.values())` / `list(d.keys())` over a dict with REFERENCE-type elements copies where CPython aliases, with NO warning -- the bound-container form of the same copy DOES warn.** `d: dict[str, Node]; vals = list(d.values()); d["a"].v = 999; print(vals[0].v)` prints `1` under TPy and `999` under CPython, and `tpyc` emits nothing; the sibling `c = list(b)` over a still-live `b: list[Node]` emits `warning: copies Node elements; use copy_iter() to make this explicit (or copy() to copy the entire container)`. Both verified at `c95406e26` and at HEAD. The divergence itself is the accepted materialization semantics (`docs` calls this out for container ctors) -- the DEFECT is that the diagnostic that makes it non-silent does not fire for a dict-view source. Suspected site: the warning gate in `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` (~855-900) keys on an lvalue source or on an rvalue whose element type carries a semantic `Ref`, and a dict-view rvalue satisfies neither; NOT runtime-confirmed, so treat the mechanism as a lead rather than a root cause. Codegen-path-independent (the shape falls back to the AST path entirely). Fix shape: extend the warning gate's rvalue arm to dict/container VIEW sources, whose elements are borrows of the parent container. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the THIR instantiation-gate wave; pre-existing, unrelated to that wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (crash) A container instantiation over a literal with NESTED literal elements crashes codegen: `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen`.** `a = list([[1, 2], [3]])` (also the single-element `list([[1, 2]])`) at plain function scope -- no nested def, no branch topology, so this is NOT the nested-def lifecycle entry above. The OUTER literal resolves (it is the call's arg), but the inner literals stay `PendingListType` and reach `to_cpp()` through the ctor's `@cpp_template` substitution (`_resolve_cpp_template_type_params`, `tpyc/sema/calls.py:361` -> `typesys.py:4181`) -- the instantiation path never runs the nested-literal resolution that the equivalent annotated decl (`a: list[list[int32]] = [[1, 2], [3]]`) does. Flat element literals are fine (`list([1, 2])`); the named-local form (`src: list[list[int32]] = [[1, 2]]; a = list(src)`) compiles. Same expected-type-into-nested-literal family as the annotated dict-literal-of-list-literals entry below. Fix shape: resolve the arg literal's nested element types before the ctor template substitution reads them. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen probes around the THIR container-literal instantiation arm; pre-existing on master. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A genexpr yielding the literal's elements into the instantiation reaches the same crash (`list(r for r in grid)`), and handing one to an `Iterable[list[int32]]` parameter is a loud reject instead (`Type <genexpr>[PendingList...] does not conform to protocol Iterable[list[int32]]`): the yield type is still the unsettled literal type when the call is checked. Seen reviewing the genexpr frames 2026-09-21.

Flat literals work; a nested literal in a PLAIN decl also works (different emit arm) -- only the branch predecl slot-assign spelling is wrong. Probe `/tmp/agents/plfix/p_nested1.py`. Fix shape: render the literal through the same nested-container emit the plain decl uses (typed construction, not bare brace-init) at the slot-assign arm. Surfaced by the readiness retrospective's nested-literal probe on `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

The named-local form (`p = Pair[Node](a, b); p.first()`) compiles: a general method call hard-codes `is_consuming_receiver=False` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`), so only the rvalue-receiver syntax reaches the consuming overload. The annotated form (`m: list[list[Point]] = ...`) compiles and runs. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared in a try's ELSE body (with the except-handler declaring the same name) emits assignments to an undeclared predecl slot -- g++ `'xs' was not declared in this scope` / `'__slot_N' was not declared`.** `try: ... except ValueError: xs = [3] else: xs = [1, 2]` then a post-try read: the branch-decl predecl machinery covers the handler's decl but the ELSE body's assignment renders the slot/pointer form (`xs = &*(__slot_2 = {1, 2})`) without the corresponding declarations reaching its scope. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple ternary whose arms carry DIFFERENT C++ tuple forms is a hard compile error.** `t = p if c else h.pair` (a borrow-form `std::tuple<int32, Box*>` param against a storage-form `std::tuple<int32, Box>` field) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type)` -- the decl's slot ladder (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:9978`) has no row for a ternary whose arms disagree on tuple form, so nothing lifts one side to the other's. Loud either way. Fix shape: give the tuple ternary a row that lifts a storage arm via `tuple_to_pointer`, or reject the mixed pair in sema with the message the readonly twin already gets. - **[MED small] (misleading diagnostic) The per-element `Own`-coercion warning and error name the WHOLE tuple where a single element is at stake.** Rebinding a mixed tuple local to an all-borrow storage source (`p = h.pair` for `p: tuple[Own[Box], Box]`) warns `copies tuple[Box, Box] into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit` -- but only element 0 is copied; element 1 still aliases, which the pinned case's own output shows (`elem0: 7`, `elem1: 66`). The `@nocopy` variant is worse: `cannot copy tuple[Guard, Box] into owned storage of type 'Guard'; target is non-copyable` conflates the whole-tuple SOURCE type with one element's TARGET type in a single sentence. Root cause: the tuple-to-tuple element-wise compat recursion (`_check_compat`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` ~1141) passes the whole-tuple `source_expr` unchanged into each per-element check, so the generic Own-coercion message reads `get_expr_type(source_expr)` -- the aggregate -- instead of the element's own type. The sibling `warn_pointer_repr_tuple_copy` path (container append) already gets this right and appends `(tuple element i)`, so it is the fix shape: pass the element's source (or at least the index) into the per-element check. Not silent and not a miscompile, but it weakens the "warned, therefore acknowledged" premise the `tuple/mixed_own_tuple_local_realias` `no_cpython` pin rests on -- a user can reasonably read it as "the whole tuple is deep-copied".
