- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach through a TERNARY call argument, so a param mutated only via a ternary is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def via(b: Box, c: Box, pick: bool) -> int32: return bump(b if pick else c)` (where `bump(b: Box)` writes `b.val`) emits `int32_t via(const Box& b, const Box& c, bool pick)` and then `bump(((pick) ? (b) : (c)))` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Box&' to 'const Box' discards qualifiers`. Passing the same param DIRECTLY (`bump(b)`) infers `Box&` correctly, so the gap is the ternary arg specifically: `mutation_propagation` walks call args but does not descend into a `TpyIfExpr` to attribute the callee's mutation to each arm's name. Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic, pre-existing (reproduces at merge base). Any arg shape that wraps names in an expression is worth checking with it (an `and`/`or` arm is the obvious sibling). Workaround: bind the selected object to a local first, or use an if/else statement. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mixdecl/y2_ternary_const.py`. Surfaced probing decl paths during the mixed-tuple borrow-position work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach a LOOP ELEMENT passed to a mutating callee, so the source param is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def f(*ps: Point): for p in ps: touch(p)` (where `touch(p: Point)` writes `p.x`) emits `void f(::tpy::varargs<const Point> ps)` and then `touch(p)` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Point&' to 'const Point' discards qualifiers`. Mutating the element DIRECTLY in the loop body (`p.x += 1`) infers the mutable slot correctly, so the gap is specifically a mutation that only happens inside a callee: `mutation_propagation` attributes the callee's param mutation to the loop VARIABLE, and neither the vararg flip (`_maybe_flip_vararg_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) nor its sibling `_sync_inferred_const` climbs from a loop var to the container/pack it iterates. Not vararg-specific and not generator-specific -- measured on all four cells: `*args` pack and plain `list[Point]` param, each on a plain function and on a generator (the generator twin emits `touch((*p))` against the same const element). Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic; pre-existing (the vararg flip and the const inference both predate the frame's varargs admission). A generator expression's source is a PARAM of the function sema builds for it, so since genexprs became frames this also reaches a genexpr over a LOCAL list (`sum(len(r) for r in ll if append_one(r))`, which the closure render compiled). Workaround: mutate the element inline in the loop body, or take an explicitly mutable slot. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fixround/p17_flip.py` (pack, plain fn), `p18_flip_gen.py` (pack, generator), `p19_list_sibling.py` (plain `list` param). Fix shape: mutation propagation must map "loop var over X is mutated" back to X (the same climb `_borrow_storage_root`/`loop_var_iterable` already record for borrow tracking), so both const-inference flips see it. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the resumable-frame varargs admission. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared inside a TRY body of a generator/async function types the frame slot from one arm's fixed-size Array while the writes emplace a vector -- g++ "no matching function for call to `emplace`".** `async def f(n): try: xs = [n, n] except ValueError: xs = [0]` + a post-try read emits `::tpy::frame_slot<std::array<int32_t, 1>> xs;` (the size from the HANDLER's literal) against `xs.emplace(std::vector<int32_t>{n, n});` -- the write site reads the sema branch-decl snapshot (forced off the Array optimization by `_force_branch_decl_lists`, so `list[int32]`), but the frame-slot field is spelled from `func.generator_locals`, which keeps the unforced per-decl type. The if/else and match-arm topologies are correct (their frame local carries the merged list), so the gap is the generator-locals collection not consulting the branch-decl snapshot. Loud (toolchain-caught). Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/smoke13/trybody4/main.py` (`tpyc --dump-code` shows the mismatch directly). Fix shape: apply the branch-decl snapshot type when collecting generator locals (the same override `_emit_branch_decls` performs on `var_types`), so the slot and its writes agree. NB THIR mirrors the WRITE side by applying that same override (`lc.frame_local_types` in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`); when the slot spelling is fixed, both paths stay in lockstep. Surfaced by the THIR branch-nested frame-decl cell (wave-next13). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, latent] A MIXED async tuple return (pointer-repr record element + value element) emits uncompilable C++ at BOTH ends -- the surviving sibling of the fixed value-tuple untargeted render.** `async def mixed(r: Rec, n) -> tuple[Rec, int32 | None]: return (r, None)` is sema-accepted and breaks twice: (1) the callee's return render stays untargeted -- `std::tuple<Rec, std::optional<int32_t>> __tpy_async_ret = std::tuple<Rec*, std::monostate>{&(r), nullptr};` -- because the tuple-literal-targeted arm in `_async_return_value_cpp` deliberately gates on `not has_pointer_repr_element()` (the async return slot is the STORAGE tuple even for mixed shapes, so the borrow-form spelling never converts); (2) the CALLER's await-bind declares the frame field in borrow form (`std::tuple<Rec*, std::optional<int32_t>> a;`) and assigns the callee's storage tuple into it (`a = std::move(__r0).value();` -- no operator=). Fixing (1) is not just widening the gate: a param-rooted record element at a storage slot needs the sync arm's deref-COPY discipline (`tuple_to_storage` family), and (2) is a borrow/storage-form decision at the frame boundary -- the recurring duality class (docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md "Borrow Form vs Storage Form"). Both shapes unreached in the corpus; probes `/tmp/agents/fix-async-ret/probe_retro.py` (return site) + `probe_mixed_call.py` (both sites). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the value-tuple render fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (consider sema-rejecting the shape first if the form design is deferred).
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) An `async with` whose `__aexit__` is typed `exc_val: None -> bool` (a suppressing manager) compiles without a diagnostic but does NOT suppress a body exception -- TPy panics with an uncaught exception where CPython suppresses and continues.** The `None`-typed `exc_val` slots past the block that gates the `Optional[BaseException]` suppression form (`BUGS.md` async-with entry / the diagnostic at that path), so this shape silently emits non-suppressing cleanup. Distinct from the documented `exc_val: Optional[BaseException]` async-with-suppression gap (blocked by a diagnostic): this variant compiles clean and miscompiles. Pre-existing -- reproduces on `ffb79ebbef`, unrelated to the cleanup-double-run fix; surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing adjacent shapes. Fix shape: either reject the `exc_val: None` + `bool`-return async-`__aexit__` shape with the same diagnostic the `Optional` form gets, or implement suppression for it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (coordinate with the async-with suppression design).
- **[MED small] (missing diagnostic) The `'raise' in '__del__' cannot propagate` warning skips `try` subtrees, so a `__del__` that raises from inside a `try`/`except`/`finally` compiles silently.** A bare `raise` in `__del__` warns at the raise line; the same raise inside any `try` subtree (handler body, `finally` body, or the `try` body itself) produces NO warning -- the walker that finds raise sites does not descend into `TpyTry`. The user's only signal is the runtime `TurboPython panic: uncaught exception in __del__` abort (`tests/cases/exceptions/panic_del_try_finally_raise` pins it). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/finally-fix/probe_del.py` (silent) vs `probe_del_bare.py` (warns). Fix shape: descend into `try_body`/handler bodies/`finally_body` when collecting `__del__` raise sites. Was previously noted only as an aside inside the finally-fall-through-elision entry (whose other half is now fixed); re-filed standalone so it isn't lost. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A `return` of a TUPLE with reference-type elements under `try`/`finally` captures the elements (copy) before the finally runs, so a finally mutating an element local is invisible in the returned tuple.** [`tuple-return-under-finally-captures-early`] `try: return (b, 5) / finally: b.n += 1` -- TPy prints the pre-mutation value, CPython (whose tuple holds an alias to `b`) the post-mutation one. Residual sibling of the fixed scalar case (finally-deferred return capture): the scalar fix captures a borrow before the inline finally chain and materializes after it, but a tuple literal must still EVALUATE non-name element expressions before the chain (evaluation order/side effects), so deferral needs per-element borrow capture plus an rvalue-hoist for computed elements (the frame-capture rvalue arg hoist is the precedent machinery). Probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_sib45.py` (`f_tup`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A `return <reference-type local>` under a finally that CONTAINS a suspension (`await`/`yield` -- the CFG pending-return lowering) still captures the value eagerly, so the suspending finally's mutation of the local is invisible in the returned object.** The CFG arm parks the value in the frame's `__finally_ret_<n>` slot before transitioning to the finally states; a deferred borrow there would be a frame-self-pointer surviving suspensions (the async-borrow-escape family, BUGS 309/311), and multiple return sites share one slot, so deferral needs a parked discriminant (which return fired) materialized at AsyncFinallyExit -- or frame pinning. Excluded from the finally-deferred-capture fix in `liveness.collect_finally_return_candidates` (suspension check suppresses the WHOLE subtree of a suspending-finally try, so this also covers a return under an inner NON-suspending finally with a suspending-finally ancestor -- probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_cfg_inner.py`, same eager-copy divergence, and the list shape keeps its loud copy() error there). Probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_cfg.py`: TPy 10, CPython 11. For a `@nocopy` payload the eager pending-slot store (`this->__finally_ret_<n> = ...`) is a deleted-copy-assignment C++ BUILD FAILURE, not just a silent divergence. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `nonlocal` REBIND inside a nested def overwrites the outer local's storage IN PLACE (no slot model), observable through any alias of that local.** `scan_reassigned_vars` deliberately does not recurse into nested defs, so a local rebound ONLY via `nonlocal b; b = ...` in a closure never gets the `__slot_N` pointer indirection a direct rebind gets -- the closure's assignment clobbers the same C++ storage, where CPython rebinding leaves the old object alive for existing references. The finally-deferred return capture EXCLUDES such names from deferral (`liveness._collect_nested_def_nonlocal_rebinds`) so the pure-rebind-from-finally shape keeps the CPython-correct eager copy; the residual: a closure that both MUTATES and rebinds the name, called from a finally around `return <name>`, loses the mutation in the returned object (eager copy, TPy pre-mutation vs CPython post-mutation). Fix shape: teach `scan_reassigned_vars` to count nested-def nonlocal writes as reassignments (slot model), then drop the deferral exclusion -- corpus-wide codegen change for closures that rebind. NOW ALSO REACHABLE IN RESUMABLE BODIES: since nested defs in async defs/generators compile (frame member functions), the same in-place rebind clobbers the frame FIELD -- an alias taken before the rebind sees the new object (TPy `1,999,999` vs CPython `1,1,999`); previously that shape was a loud C++ build error. Probes `/tmp/agents/finally-review/probe_closure_rebind2.py`, `/tmp/agents/nested_probe/p2_alias_rebind.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + cpython-parity) of the structural-deferral widening; resumable reachability by the nested-def frame-member review. The alias-gated slot model (2026-09-14) leaves a `nonlocal` rebind FOREIGN by construction: the storage is the enclosing function's, and a slot of the closure's own would die with the lambda, so the lowering keeps rejecting an rvalue rebind of an enclosing POINTER-local (`nested_def.rebind_slot_hoist`) and a plain-storage outer local still takes the in-place write above. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid) The closure-del guard for finally-deferred returns fires without reachability analysis: a nested def deling the returned name is rejected even when the closure is only invoked from a handler or the normal path, never from a finally.** `_check_closure_del_of_deferred_returns` pairs any deferred `return x` with any nested-def `nonlocal x; del x` in the function; under structural candidacy this rejects programs that previously compiled (probe: return in try, closure-del called only from an except handler, finally empty). Sound but over-broad by design (documented in the helper). Fix shape: narrow to closures reachable from a finally body's call expressions, or accept and document. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A pre-try alias bind of a local read later in a finally consumes it eagerly: `a = b; try: return a; finally: b.n += 1` moves `b` into `a` at the bind, so the finally's mutation of `b` is lost.** The backward last-use walker's `TpyReturn` handling clears the live set, discarding the finally's `b`-is-read fact for code positioned BEFORE the try -- `a = b` compiles as `std::move(b)` although `b` is read afterwards on the return path (TPy prints the pre-mutation value, CPython the post-mutation one). Independent of the finally-deferred return capture (reproduces at its merge-base; `return a` is not a deferral candidate since `a` is a reference bind, not an owned var). Fix shape: the return-statement arm of the backward walk must seed liveness from the enclosing finally frames before clearing. Probes `/tmp/agents/finally-parity/probe_alias_reverse.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + safety-model). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A union-typed local returned as `Own[A | B]` from inside ANY try/finally emits invalid C++ (ptr-variant to value-variant conversion).** `v: A | B = A(); try: return v; finally: ...` -- `_make_return`'s finally capture binds `std::variant<A, B> __tpy_ret = v;` where `v` is the borrow-form `std::variant<A*, B*>` local, with none of the ptr-to-value-variant conversion the no-finally return path applies; the C++ build fails loudly. Independent of whether the finally reads `v` (probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_union_noread.py`); pre-existing, surfaced while gating union locals out of the finally-deferred return capture (whose recipe also does not cover variants -- fixing this shape should add a deferred recipe too, so a finally mutating the returned union local matches CPython aliasing like the scalar fix). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Initializing a pointer-repr Optional local with a ternary whose arm is a fresh constructor call emits address-of-rvalue C++.** `b: Box | None = Box() if flag else None` -> `Box* b = flag ? &(Box()) : nullptr;` -- the slot-model materialization (`__slot_N`) is not applied to ternary-arm rvalues, so the C++ build fails loudly (`taking address of rvalue`). The plain form `b: Box | None = Box()` materializes correctly. Surfaced while writing `finally_mutates_returned_local`; workaround: assign in an `if`/`else`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `finally` body that terminates on every path but doesn't END in a literal `raise`/`return` emits an unreachable `throw;` after its catch-path copy.** `_lower_try` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:14853`) computes `finally_terminates` as a SHALLOW `isinstance(last, (TpyRaise, TpyReturn))` on the finally's last statement (`:14990`), while the normal-path elision asks the DEEP `stmts_terminate` / `try_terminates_ignoring_finally` question (`tpyc/liveness.py:227`/`:277`). So `finally: if c: raise A else: raise B` gets `finally_terminates=False`, and the catch-path copy -- which already always throws -- is followed by a dead `throw;` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2789`). The flag also rides `THIRTry.finally_terminates` into the finally-chain emit, driving the `[[maybe_unused]]` tagging and the trailing `return`/`throw` suppression at EVERY return/break/continue site inside the try body -- so the dead code appears at each exit site, not just once. Harmless: the shallow check can only err in the SAFE direction (a literal `raise`/`return` last statement always terminates, so the flag is a possible false negative only, never a false positive), and a false negative merely emits unreachable code the C++ compiler drops. Behavior is correct (verified against CPython). Fix shape: compute `finally_terminates` with `stmts_terminate(stmt.finally_body)` so both questions use one predicate. Surfaced by /tpy-ready of the finally-fall-through-elision fix.
- **[MED small] An except clause naming a class AND a subclass of it emits an unreachable C++ catch arm -- fails a strict-warning build (`-Werror=exceptions`).** `except Base:` followed by `except Sub:` (Sub derives from Base), or the single-clause tuple spelling `except (Base, Sub):`, emits `catch (const Base&)` before `catch (const Sub&)`; g++-14 rejects the second under the test harness's `strict_warn_flags`: "exception of type 'Sub' will be caught by earlier handler [-Werror=exceptions]". Valid Python that CPython accepts (the later arm is simply dead), and TPy issues no diagnostic of its own, so a user hits it as a raw C++ build error. **Pre-existing** -- the hand-written sibling form reproduces identically and predates the tuple form -- but the tuple form raises exposure sharply, because the natural Python spelling of an errno/OS group puts a base and its subclass in one clause (`except (OSError, PermissionError):`; PermissionError derives from OSError). NB `uv run tpy` does NOT reproduce it: the CLI leaves `warn_flags` empty, so only the test harness (and any user passing strict flags) sees it. The spelling-based dedup in `_except_clause_types` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`) collapses only a literally repeated name, never a subclass relationship, which the parser cannot know. Fix shape is a **design decision**, not a patch: drop an arm whose type derives from an earlier arm's (semantics-preserving -- the earlier arm already catches it) in sema where the hierarchy is known, and/or warn on an unreachable except clause (a genuine Python-level lint CPython does not give). Both faces (tuple + hand-written siblings) should be decided together. Reproducer: a `tests/cases/` case with `except (Base, Sub) as e:` -- fails the exec phase; the same case with two sibling clauses fails identically. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity flagged the shape; the coverage test the review asked for immediately failed the build). Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (the diagnostic/collapse design), not `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A QUALIFIED `asyncio.run(...)` call resolves to a USER function of the same bare name, emitting an undeclared-namespace C++ error.** A module-level `async def run(x: int) -> int` alongside `asyncio.run(main())` emits `::tpyapp::__main__::run<std::monostate>(::tpy::make_adapter<...>(main()))` -- the qualified `asyncio.run` bound to the user's `run` -- and g++ rejects it ("'tpyapp::__main__' has not been declared"). CPython runs the same source fine (the qualified name can only mean the module's). Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid; the wrong-namespace spelling suggests the call is resolved by BARE name with the qualifier dropped, so a user function shadowing any qualified stdlib call is the general shape -- same family as the qualified-`except mod.X` builtin-shadow entry below, and worth root-causing together. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mx/shadow.py` (10 lines). Workaround: rename the user function. Surfaced while probing `await` inside an `except (A, B)` body (the async probe used a helper named `run`); unrelated to that feature. Independently re-surfaced authoring the Phase-D3 `await_in_for_else` test (a local `async def run` shadowed `asyncio.run`; a duplicate LOW entry from that surfacing was folded into this one) and again writing `tests/cases/async/async_view_local_owned_frame` (its coroutine renamed to dodge it). A third duplicate was folded in from a `MED` filing that added: `run` is a likely collision in exactly the async programs that need `asyncio.run`; the g++ face varies with the user function's shape (a zero-arg `async def run()` under `asyncio.run(run())` reports `expected primary-expression before '>' token` on the stray template argument list rather than the undeclared namespace); and this is distinct from the module-qualified entries below, which are about resolution FAILING rather than resolving to the WRONG target. Second reproducer `/tmp/agents/awfix/shadow.py` (12 lines). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `isinstance()` on an EXCEPTION binding takes the union/variant path and emits `std::holds_alternative` against a class reference -- ill-formed C++.** `class Sub(Base)` (Base an Exception subclass), then `try: raise Sub()` / `except Base as e: if isinstance(e, Sub): ...` emits `std::holds_alternative<Sub>(e)` and `auto& __e = std::get<Sub>(e)` where `e` is `const Base&` -> g++ "'const Base' is not derived from 'const std::variant<_Types...>'". The same isinstance-against-a-descendant on a NON-exception class correctly warns ("folds to False (static dispatch; use @dynamic for runtime type checks)") and folds -- so the exception binding is the only receiver that reaches the variant path with no union in sight. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent, but it rejects the natural disambiguation idiom for any base-typed catch. Note the correct behavior here is NOT obvious: a caught exception IS genuinely polymorphic (C++ catch does real RTTI matching), so folding to False like a plain class would be wrong; a `dynamic_cast` narrow is the honest lowering. That makes this a design question as much as a fix. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mx/iso.py`. Workaround: none for exceptions -- restructure into one `except` clause per concrete type. Surfaced by the cpython-parity review of the `except (A, B)` tuple-form design (it blocks the join-typed-binding ergonomics). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A non-fixed-int ctor wrapper (`int(...)`) around a >int32 literal DEFAULT on a BigInt field still renders bare, and the parser mis-renders `int(x)` as a truncating C++ cast.** `big: int = int(90000000000)` as a record-field default: `records.py`'s field member-init uses `fixed_int_literal_value_from_expr`, which peels only FIXED-int ctor wrappers (`int64(...)`) -- `int` is not in `_FIXED_INT_NAMES`, so it falls through to the parser's pre-rendered string. Separately, `_get_default_value` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`) renders a non-fixed-int 1-arg ctor call as `f"{func}({args})"` -> `int(90000000000)`, which in C++ is a truncating `int` cast, not a BigInt. So the field emits `::tpy::BigInt big = int(90000000000);` -- both the macOS `long -> BigInt` ambiguity (via the inner bare token) AND a value truncation. `default_to_cpp` (function/ctor params) avoids this because it recurses through ANY 1-arg `TpyCall`. Pathological spelling (`int(...)` wrapping a literal whose field is already `int`); no realistic user impact. Fix shape: either broaden the field member-init to recurse like `default_to_cpp`, or fix `_get_default_value`'s non-fixed-int-ctor arm to not emit a C++ truncating cast. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/ctorwrap.py` (swap `int64` for `int`). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the int-literal-default fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An empty (`pass`-body) subclass used as a struct FIELD emits an incomplete-type C++ error.** `class Sub(Base): pass` then `class Holder: _s: Sub` (or ctor `def __init__(self, s: Own[Sub])`) fails to compile: `error: field '_s' has incomplete type 'Sub'` -- codegen forward-declares `Sub` but emits `Holder` (which needs `Sub` complete for the inline field) before `Sub`'s full definition. Reproduces with NO iteration / readonly / generics -- just an empty subclass as a field (`/tmp/agents/gap2/emptysub.py`). A non-empty subclass (adds its own field) is unaffected. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Emit-ordering bug: an empty subclass isn't ordered before a record that holds it by value. Fix shape: include empty subclasses in the same complete-before-use topological emit ordering non-empty records get. Surfaced writing an inherited-`__iter__` test for the for-loop const-receiver fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` fix doesn't cover a self-METHOD-CALL iterable (`for v in self.get_container():`).** `_record_iter_receiver_mutation` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) bails when `_root_name_of_expr(iterable_expr)` is None (a call has no name root), so a for-loop iterating the result of a self-method call whose `__iter__` mutates the returned receiver won't demote the enclosing method -> the same const-receiver compile error the fix eliminates for name/field iterables. `methods.py`'s explicit-call path has a None-root chain-to-self fallback (methods.py ~923) this helper omits. Exotic (a self-returning-mutating-iterable call) and loud (compile error), so filed rather than handled in the fix. Fix shape: add the chain-traces-to-self fallback (mark self mutated) for a None-root iterable, mirroring methods.py. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the const-receiver `__iter__` fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A bound cross-module coroutine handle whose callee name collides with a local coro is read as a self-edge, so valid code is rejected as `recursive coroutine embedding`.** `_bound_coro_frame_targets` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` ~888) keys the emit-ordering edge on the bare `(coro_func_name, owner_record)` pair and never consults `ConcreteCoroType.coro_module_qual` (`tpyc/typesys.py:4100`), so a handle whose struct is `helper::__coro_step` -- already complete via that module's header -- matches a same-named LOCAL unit instead. Trigger is narrow: `from helper import step as hstep` then `h = hstep()` inside a local `async def step()` DOES reproduce, while the attribute form `helper.step()` does NOT (it resolves the qualifier elsewhere), so the shape needs a bare-or-aliased import plus a name collision. Loud, no miscompile. The four owner-bearing edge sources route through `same_module_dep_unit` (`resumable_cfg.py`) for exactly this reason; this fifth source predates that helper and was left out. Fix shape: skip when `coro_module_qual` names another module, or route the owner-bearing form through the helper. Probes `/tmp/agents/iterfix/bound/main2.py` (fails) and `control.py` (compiles). Confirmed pre-existing by A/B (neutering that collector alone makes the probe compile). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A generator METHOD's frame const verdict is looked up in the FREE-function table, so a name collision hands it another function's answer.** `_frame_deep_const_verdict` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py:363`) branches on its `record_name` argument, but every generator path reaches it with `None` -- the eligibility gate (`generator.py` ~885, and the fwd-decl pass) builds and MEMOIZES the CFG before `gen_coro_struct` can pass the real record name, and the docstring sanctions that ("Generators never await, so the gate path may pass None"). So a method takes the `registry.get_function(func.name)` leg: normally that misses and yields None (benign), but a method whose name matches a module-level function picks up the FREE function's `deep_const_borrow_params`. That verdict drives the const spelling of pointer-repr tuple/union frame captures and the CFG-window const seeding, so a wrong answer is a wrong field const-ness, not just a missing one. No constructed repro (needs a generator method sharing a name with a free function that has deep-const params). Pre-existing. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, raw C++ error) Iterating a `readonly[T]`-annotated user iterable whose `__iter__` yields mutable borrows emits raw `no matching function for call to __iter__(const T&)` from `generator.hpp` instead of a clean diagnostic.** `def read_all(bag: readonly[Bag]) -> Iterator[int32]: for p in bag: yield p.x` where `Bag.__iter__` yields `Point` borrows: the generator method is deliberately emitted non-const (it exposes mutable access), so a const receiver genuinely cannot iterate it -- the REJECTION is correct, the diagnostic is not. Three runtime-header errors plus `has no member named '__next__'` surface, naming no user line. Independent of the frame-vs-peephole split (reproduces identically with a single-yield `__iter__`) and distinct from the readonly-demotion entries in this family: an explicit `readonly[T]` param cannot be demoted, so the fix is a sema check reporting "cannot iterate `readonly[Bag]`; `__iter__` yields mutable borrows" and naming the escape (drop `readonly`, or give the type a `@readonly` `__iter__` yielding readonly elements). Surfaced probing the readonly path of the frame `__iter__` emit-ordering fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An unannotated list mixing a small int literal with a >int32 one infers an `int32` element type, truncating the wide literal (C++ `-Wnarrowing` build error).** `a = [0, 1234567890123456789]` emits `std::array<int32_t, 2> a = {0, 1234567890123456789}`, which g++ rejects (narrowing `long` -> `int` inside brace-init). A list with ONLY the wide literal (`[1234567890123456789]`) infers `BigInt` correctly (`std::array<::tpy::BigInt, 1>`); the bug is the element-type JOIN over mixed int literals -- the small literal pins the common type to `int32` without checking that a sibling literal overflows it. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid; an explicit `list[int]` annotation avoids it (gets `BigInt`, and the >int32 element now renders ambiguity-safe -- the target-less int-literal render in `int_literals.py`). Fix shape: the int-literal list-element join must widen to a type holding EVERY member (BigInt when any element exceeds the fixed width), not collapse to the narrowest present. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/inf.py`. Surfaced fixing the macOS BigInt list-literal ambiguity. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `@error_return` is not rejected on `__del__` -- a `try`/`except <ReturnException>` (or any @error_return propagation) in a destructor lowers to a `return ::tpy::make_unexpected(...)` / `return {};` inside the C++ destructor body, which is invalid C++ ("returning a value from a destructor").** A destructor has no return slot, but the @error_return lowering emits its goto-based `return <expected>` unconditionally. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid-looking code; exotic (no reason to use @error_return machinery in a `__del__`). Reproduces on master (pre-existing, unrelated to the fail-fast wrap). Fix shape: reject `@error_return` / return-exception propagation in a `__del__` body at registration (alongside the other `__del__` shape checks in `tpyc/sema/registration.py`). Surfaced by the codegen-correctness review of the `__del__` fail-fast change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `async def __del__` is accepted and silently mishandled -- it emits a synchronous destructor running the body (dropping the `async`) PLUS a dead coroutine struct.** A class with `async def __del__(self)` compiles: codegen emits a real `~T()` whose body runs the method statements synchronously (ignoring that the method is a coroutine -- there is no way to `await` during C++ destruction) AND a separate, never-instantiated `__coro_T___del__` resumable-frame struct. So the async-ness is silently discarded and dead code is generated. A destructor cannot be async (destruction is synchronous), so this should be a clean sema rejection (like `self: Own[Self]` on `__del__`, already rejected). Exotic -- no user writes an async destructor -- so no current impact; loud only in that the dead struct is emitted. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/deldrop/asyncdel.py`. Fix shape: reject `async` on `__del__` at registration (alongside the existing `__del__` shape checks). Surfaced by the codegen-correctness re-review of the conditional `__del__`-wrap change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An @error_return call nested in the ARG subtree of another @error_return call is a hard compile error.** `x = f(g(3))` and `return f(g(3))` (both @error_return) fail codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:error_return.nested_call)` / `(stmt.return:error_return.nested_call)`, raised by `_reject_nested_error_return_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3233`, called from the var-decl arm at :3271 and the return arm at :10243). The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed C++: the statement handler unwraps the OUTER call, but arguments render first, so the inner fallible call consumed the handled-call flag and the inner `g` emitted as a raw `std::expected` where its success value was needed. Everyday shape -- composing two fallible calls is the ordinary way to write them in an @error_return body -- so worth queueing. Fix shape: give the inner call its own unwrap temp before the outer call composes, keying the handled-call state to the specific node instead of a single boolean, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_400_nested_er_arg.py` and `02_400b_return_form.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) The expression-level @error_return propagate unwrap skips active finally bodies; the statement-level one runs them -- an inconsistent early return that silently drops cleanup.** Inside an @error_return function a fallible call in EXPRESSION position (`return f(a) + f(b)`, an argument, a condition) unwraps through `_er_check_inline` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2513`), whose propagate arm emits a bare `if (!__er_1.has_value()) return ::tpy::make_unexpected(__er_1.error());` with no walk of `state.finally_frames` -- while its statement-level sibling `_er_check_stmt` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2532`) routes the same propagate through `_emit_finally_return`, so the finally body runs. Confirmed: `@error_return(E) def expr_pos(a, b): try: return f(a) + f(b) finally: print("cleanup")` with a failing `f` prints nothing under TPy and `cleanup` under CPython. Silent -- the output diverges only when the error path fires under an active finally. Fix shape: route the expression unwrap's propagate arm through the same finally-frame walk `_er_check_stmt` uses (the statement expression can hold multi-statement checks), or hoist expression-level fallible calls to statement temps under an active finally. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_401_er_expr_finally.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The system-lib version guard only fires when pkg-config can report a version; a too-old system lib installed without a `.pc` file still fails deep in the C compiler.** `system_version_too_old` (`tpyc/build/third_party.py`) probes `pkg-config --modversion` and is deliberately permissive when the version is undeterminable (no pkg-config, no `.pc`) so a valid from-source install is not blocked -- but that means a too-old from-source install (e.g. mbedTLS 2.27 headers in a non-standard prefix, no `.pc`) bypasses the guard and hits the cryptic API-mismatch compile error the guard exists to prevent. Acceptable today (from-source installs of a managed dep are rare and usually ship a `.pc`), but the guard is best-effort, not complete. Fix shape: fall back to a `MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER`/equivalent compile-probe against the resolved headers when pkg-config yields nothing. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the version-guard work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] The CMake-emit path (`tpyc -o`) never compiles TPy-owned third-party glue, so a `sources.cmake`-based build of any `ssl`/`datetime` program is missing the FFI shim in EVERY mode.** `resolve_build_plan` puts the glue (`mbedtls_shim.c`/`cacert_data.c`, `date_shim.cpp`) in `ThirdPartyBuildPlan.c_sources`, which only the direct-compile path (`tpyc -b` -> `BuildLayout.build_cpp_commands`) consumes. `Compiler.generate_cmake` (`tpyc/compiler.py`) and `emit_cmake_snippet` (`tpyc/build/third_party.py`) receive `third_party_plan.libs` but NOT `c_sources`, so the generated CMake project never builds the shim -- `tpystd::ssl` would link with undefined `tpy_tls_*` (and datetime with the missing date facade). Pre-existing (the shim was in `bundled_source_files`, also c_sources-only, before the system-mode work), and untested (the harness + nightly use the direct-compile path). Fix shape: thread `plan.c_sources` (source + per-file flags) through `generate_cmake`/`emit_cmake_snippet` into the emitted `sources.cmake`, mirroring how the direct path adds them. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the system-mode glue fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `@overload`-dispatched methods still emit inline-in-struct -- the residual member-body kind that needs complete sibling types at struct scope.** The ctor/special-member fix moved `__init__` ctors, `__del__` dtor/move ops, and `__copy__` copy ops to namespace scope (`records.py` `_gen_ctor_def` / mode-aware `_gen_move_and_destructor` / `_gen_copy_ops`), and plain methods already default out-of-line -- but `@overload`-specialized methods stay inline regardless of size (the emitters take a `mode` param that is always "inline" there). A body that references a mutually-recursive sibling record (or any record defined later in the module) odr-uses an incomplete type at struct scope -- clang rejects, gcc happens to accept (same mechanism as the fixed ctor case, `tests/cases/records/recursive_record_mutual`). Exotic combos, loud (toolchain-caught). Fix shape: partition-aware overload dispatch (thread the decl/def mode through the specialized-method emitters); for simple generators either fall off the peephole for cycle members or emit the factory after the structs. Surfaced by the recursive-record ctor fix survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (acknowledged divergence, no longer a nightly blocker) TPy `asyncio.Future()` is constructible without a running loop; CPython >= 3.14 raises `RuntimeError` there.** CPython 3.14 turned the "no current event loop" deprecation into an error: `asyncio.Future()` outside a running loop now raises `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop` (from `events.get_event_loop`). TPy's `lib/tpy/asyncio` still allows loop-less construction (matching pre-3.14 permissiveness) -- a silent parity divergence, but with no diagnostic/escape-hatch today. `tests/cases/async/future_basic` was restructured to construct the Future inside `asyncio.run`'s loop (so it no longer trips the divergence and the 2604 row passes), but the divergence itself is unfixed. To close it: bind Future construction to a running loop like modern CPython (raise when none), or accept it explicitly with a documented note. Surfaced by the nightly CI 26.04 rows (Python 3.14.4).
- **[LOW small] (silent misbinding, not unsound) A genuinely-new method type param whose NAME collides with an intermediate generic subclass's class param is misclassified as class-bound -- explicit type args silently discarded, mismatched args wrongly rejected.** `class Base[T]: def pick[U](self, other: U) -> U`; `class Mid[U](Base[U])`; `class Leaf(Mid[int32])`: through `Leaf`, the composed class subst carries `U -> int32` (Mid's param), so `_analyze_generic_method_call`'s classification (receiver params UNION subst keys, `tpyc/sema/methods.py`) treats the genuinely-fresh `U` on `pick` as constrained: `l.pick[StrView](5)` compiles silently dropping the type arg (interim: the hoisted arity check now rejects it loudly, though the "expects 0 type argument(s)" message is misleading -- there IS a genuine new param), and `l.pick("hello")` is wrongly rejected "expected int32". Type-consistent end-to-end (not unsound); exotic shape. Pre-existing family: before the subclass-receiver fix this shape errored "Cannot infer" (the by-name pre-substitution in `substitute_method_type_params` erased `U` regardless -- that name-capture is the true enabler). Fix shape: return the DECLARING RecordInfo from `lookup_record_method_overloads` (3-tuple), classify against the declaring class's params, and filter the subst to those params before pre-substitution (alpha-scoping the by-name capture). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model + architecture-fit) of the subclass-receiver bound fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The super() and unbound-self `Base.m(self, ...)` dispatch paths never compose the class subst down to the DECLARING base -- a shadowed-bound method inherited from a generic base above the named/direct parent still fails "Cannot infer type arguments".** Both paths (`tpyc/sema/methods.py` ~1208 `resolve_ancestor_instantiation` and ~2247 `get_parent_type_subst`) build the subst from the direct/named parent only, unlike `_analyze_instance_method`, which gets the level-by-level composition from `lookup_record_method_overloads` -- so the exact bug fixed for instance calls on this branch persists there whenever the declaring generic base sits one level above. Loud failure (wrong rejection), same family. Fix shape: route both paths through (or share the composition of) `lookup_record_method_overloads` instead of the two parallel one-level lookups. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the subclass-receiver bound fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality, not unsound) The class-shadowed method-bound check on OPERATOR dispatch sites silently short-circuits for a subclass receiver -- a violation surfaces as a cryptic C++ `requires` error instead of the clean sema diagnostic.** The method-CALL path resolves shadowed bounds through subclass receivers (fixed on `fix-method-bound-subclass-receiver`: classification uses the composed class subst), but the operator sites still derive the class-param set and subst from the RECEIVER's record: `operators.py` (`_check_operator_method_bound`) does `if record is None or not record.type_params: return` -- empty for a subclass, so the check is skipped; `expressions.py` `__contains__`/binop-dunder sites pass `record.type_params` + `build_type_substitution(receiver)`, both empty for a subclass (and the binop site's `record.get_method` doesn't walk bases at all, so an inherited dunder may miss this path entirely); `protocols.py:790` (protocol-conformance / `hash()` path) likewise passes receiver-own `record_info.type_params`, so `find_method_class_param_bound_violation` bails at its `not class_type_params` gate for a subclass. Not unsound -- codegen's `requires` clause still rejects at C++ build -- but the user sees a template error instead of `Method '...' requires type parameter 'T' to satisfy '...'`. Repro shape: `class NEBag(Bag[NotEq, 4])` + `x in b` where `__contains__[T: Equatable]`. Fix shape: derive (declaring-class params + composed subst) for operator sites the way `_analyze_instance_method` does -- likely by threading `lookup_record_method_overloads`'s composed subst into the operator bound check instead of the receiver-record fields. Surfaced by the subclass-receiver bound-inference fix's sibling survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A borrow/reference local reused across sibling/outer scopes is declared in the inner C++ scope, not hoisted -- the later use is an undeclared identifier (C++ build error).** A local bound from a reference-returning accessor (`s = arc.get()`) or a `with ... as g` guard, first assigned inside a nested block (a loop body or a `with` body) and then read/reassigned in an enclosing or sibling scope, is emitted with its C++ declaration INSIDE the inner block; the later use emits `s = &(...)` / `g = &(...)` against a variable no longer in scope -> `'s' was not declared in this scope`. Two `with m.lock() as g:` blocks in one function reusing `g`, and `s = shared.get()` inside a `while` loop then reused after the loop, both reproduce. A third face: two SIBLING `except` handler bodies reusing one name (`except X as e: v = e.code.get(...)` / `except Y as e: v = e.code.get(...)`) -- the decl lands in the first handler's scope and the second emits `'v' was not declared in this scope`; reachable from hand-written sibling clauses, so it predates (and is independent of) the `except (A, B)` tuple form, whose arms are ordinary sibling handlers. Value-typed locals hoist to function scope correctly; only borrow/reference locals mis-scope. Loud (toolchain-caught), workaround = distinct names / restructure so a borrow local lives in one scope. Fix shape: hoist borrow/reference locals to their common enclosing scope like value locals (or declare-at-first-dominating-assignment). Surfaced building the Condvar ping-pong test (tpy.sync). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects reasonable code; CPython-parity trap) A generic METHOD cannot infer its type parameter from an argument whose type is a generic-class instantiation matching a `Generic[T]`-shaped parameter.** `def wait[T](self, mutex: Mutex[T])` called as `cv.wait(m)` with `m: Mutex[PingState]` errors `Cannot infer type arguments for method 'wait'. Specify explicitly: .wait[T](...)` -- the unification `Mutex[T]` <- `Mutex[PingState]` (and its `readonly[...]`-wrapped form) is not solved for a method-level type param. The suggested explicit spelling `cv.wait[PingState](m)` compiles in TPy but is INVALID Python (`method[X]` raises `TypeError: 'method' object is not subscriptable`), so any stdlib API that needs it breaks CPython parity. Workaround: give the method a non-generic param instead of the generic handle -- e.g. a non-`@dynamic` structural protocol the handle conforms to (monomorphized, so still a static call), which is what `Condvar.wait(lock: _CondvarLock)` does to take a `MutexGuard[T]` without a method type-param. Fix shape: extend method type-param inference to unify into a generic-class-typed (and readonly-wrapped) parameter, so `wait[T](guard: MutexGuard[T])` could be written directly. Surfaced designing `Condvar.wait` (tpy.sync). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED] A comprehension over a user-defined `__iter__` emits C++ range-for (`obj.begin()/end()`) instead of the `__iter__`/`__next__` protocol -- fails to compile.** `[v for v in src]` (list/dict/set comprehension) where `src` is a user record with a generator (or any user) `__iter__` emits `auto __beg = __obj.begin(); auto __end = __obj.end();` -- but the record has no `begin`/`end`, so g++ rejects it. Reproduces with a plain non-readonly local (`/tmp/agents/gap2/comp_local.py`), so it is independent of const/readonly: the comprehension codegen path simply doesn't support user iterators (the for-loop path uses `::tpy::__iter__` correctly). Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Workaround: use an explicit `for` loop building the container. Fix shape: route comprehension iterable codegen through the same `__iter__`/`__next__` lowering the for-loop uses (not C++ range-for) for user-iterator element sources. **Also carries a latent readonly-inference gap** (masked by this): a comprehension over a mutating `__iter__` field in a read-only-inferred method won't be demoted -- `_resolve_comp_iterable` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) never records the iteration as a receiver mutation, unlike the for-loop (`_record_iter_receiver_mutation`); fix both together. Surfaced fixing the for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` bug (the iteration-family sibling). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Readonly-inference gaps for `async for` and `in`/`__contains__` (iteration-family siblings, both latent behind bigger gaps).** The for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` fix (`_record_iter_receiver_mutation`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) marks a mutating `__iter__`'s receiver mutated so the enclosing method isn't wrongly inferred readonly; the same implicit-dunder-doesn't-record-mutation gap remains in (a) `async for` over a field (`_analyze_async_for`, marks only `TpyName` iterables, not field access -- but currently unreachable because a user `async def __aiter__` + `yield` hits "async generators are not yet supported"), and (b) `x in self._src` via `__contains__` (`_analyze_comparison`, `resolved_contains` set but no mutation edge -- near-dead since `__contains__` is conventionally readonly, and this call site also carries the separate const-dict `in` bug below, so fix them together). Fix shape: route each site's implicit dunder through `_record_iter_receiver_mutation` (or the shared edge helper). Surfaced fixing the for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` bug. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NARROWED value-repr `char | None` operand compared to a str literal (`if o is not None: ... o == "a"`) is a hard compile error.** Codegen fails with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (binop.narrowed_char_eq_literal)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:4231`. The char-literal coercion keys on the RESOLVED operand type, which for a narrowed operand is `Optional[char]`, so the target-typed char render (`_lower_char_targeted`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:15149`) misses and the only render left was `((*o) == "a")` -- `char` against `const char*`, invalid C++. Reproduces for narrowed NAME and narrowed FIELD subjects. Exotic (`char | None` locals are rare) but valid Python. Fix shape: unwrap the narrowed Optional before the char-literal coercion decides, then lift the reject. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_413_narrowed_char_eq.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `char` frame local of a generator/async function initialized with a char literal (`c: char = 'a'`) emits `c = "a";` (`const char*` -> `char`, invalid C++).** A local live across a `yield`/`await` is captured as a frame field and written by `_lower_frame_field_assign` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:6682`, reached from the resumable leaf decl arm at `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py:1929`), whose init render is deliberately POSITION-BLIND -- it lowers the init against no target, so the char-literal SOURCE (`'a'`, a str literal in the AST) renders as the string `"a"`. The SYNC path is fine: a plain `c: char = 'a'` local goes through `_lower_char_targeted` and renders `char c = 'a';`. Position-blindness is correct for the other value scalars (an int/BigInt literal stays `0`, bool/float neutral); only `char` needs the target type to turn the str-literal source into a char literal. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid; confirmed for both generators and `async def` (g++: `invalid conversion from 'const char*' to 'char'`). Fix shape: the frame-field init render for a `char` slot must apply the same target-typed char render the sync decl arm uses. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_414_char_frame_local.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Truthiness of a value-repr `Optional[bytes]` (`if b:` / `not b` / `while b:` on a `bytes | None`) emits `::tpy::is_truthy(std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>)`, which the generic `is_truthy(optional<T>)` compiles to an invalid `static_cast<bool>(span)`.** The runtime has `is_truthy(optional<std::string>)` and `is_truthy(optional<std::string_view>)` overloads (str-optional truthiness works) but NO `is_truthy(optional<::tpy::BytesView>)` overload, so a bytes-optional falls to the generic template (`opt.has_value() && static_cast<bool>(*opt)`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/core.hpp:561`) and g++ rejects `static_cast<bool>` of a span. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. `b is None` (`has_value()`) and passing the optional whole are fine; only truthiness of the bare optional trips it. THIR mirrors the render byte-identically (the shape can never appear in a green corpus/exec case, so it stays routed per the AST-miscompile mirror criterion). Fix shape: add an `is_truthy(const std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>&)` overload (empty span / nullopt -> false) alongside the string ones -- or, more generally, a span/BytesView `is_truthy` so bare `bytes`/`BytesView` truthiness is covered too. Same root cause for a value-repr `Optional[user record]` with `__bool__`/`__len__` (e.g. `Own[Flag] | None`): the generic template's `static_cast<bool>(record)` fails to compile instead of dispatching to the dunder -- a record-dunder-aware overload (or per-inner dispatch) should land with the same fix. Surfaced routing value-repr Optional[bytes] params through THIR. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `Own[list[T]]` at an `@export` parameter passes the boundary validator and fails the C++ build.** [`export-own-container-param-uncompilable`] `def take(xs: Own[list[int32]]) -> int32` in an `ext_module` is admitted (the container admission strips Own like every wrapper), but the glue binds the marshalled copy to an lvalue local and passes it to the callee's `std::vector<int32_t>&&` parameter -- a hard C++ error with no TPy location; `Own[Optional[list[int32]]]` fails the same way. Pre-existing (the plain form fails identically without any Optional), surfaced by the 2026-09-22 Optional-boundary review. Fix shape: either reject `Own[container]` at a boundary param with the located Own[Cls]-style message (the host keeps its reference, but a container IS a fresh copy, so the honest alternative is) to `std::move` the owned local into the `&&` param, the way the property setter path already moves its marshalled local. Probe: an `@export` fn with `xs: Own[list[int32]]`, `uv run tpyc -b`.
- **[LOW small] Returning a view-form `str`/`StrView` value whole into an `Optional[str]` (`-> str | None`) return slot emits an un-convertible bare `return <string_view>;` (invalid C++).** [`optional-str-return-view-source`] A function `def f() -> str | None: x = "y"; return x` (or any `return <StrView local/param>` where the WHOLE view value, not a param passed through the `Optional[str]`->`Optional[str]` shim, feeds an `std::optional<std::string>` return) emits `return x;` -- but `std::string_view` does not convert to `std::optional<std::string>` (the `optional<string>` converting ctor is explicit), so g++ rejects it ("could not convert 'x' ... to 'std::optional<std::string>'"). The AST omits the `std::string(...)` wrap it emits at a plain `-> str` owned return. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. A str LITERAL (`return "y"`) compiles (bare `const char*` -> `optional<string>` is implicit), and an `Optional[str]` param returned whole takes the correct `s ? std::make_optional(std::string(*s)) : std::nullopt` shim; only a view-form value SOURCE is wrong. Workaround: wrap explicitly (`return str(x)` is not spellable; bind through the optional). Fix shape: at an `Optional[str]` return, a view-form source must take the same `std::string(view)` wrap the owned `-> str` return applies (then materialize into the optional). This is why THIR gate-rejects the shape (`return.opt_view_source`) rather than mirroring it, and a boundary pin now holds it there deliberately. **Confirmed end to end through `uv run tpy`, not inferred**: `def f(k: str) -> str | None: return k` fails the build with `error: could not convert 'k' from 'std::string_view' ... to 'std::optional<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char> >'`, which also confirms the toolchain-caught characterization above. Surfaced routing value-repr Optional[str] returns through THIR. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A NARROWED `int | None` NAME under a scalar-cast coerce at an `Own[int32]` call slot emits `(v).to_fixed_check<int32_t>()` -- the narrowing deref is dropped (invalid C++, `std::optional<BigInt>` has no `to_fixed_check`).** `def f(v: int | None): if v is not None: take(v)` (take taking `Own[int32]`) emits the coerce wrap over the BARE name where the narrowed read needs `(*v)`. Same narrowing-unwrap-dropped family as the `str | None` field-at-view-return entry below; here the coerce render path loses the deref. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. THIR gate-rejects the shape (`_own_coerce_cast_arg` requires the DECLARED type be the scalar itself) rather than mirroring the broken render -- lift that guard when fixing. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/adv_ptrlocal_coerce.py`; g++-confirmed. Surfaced by review round 12's meta-review probe of the own-coerce-cast leg. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A NARROWED `str | None` FIELD returned at a view (`StrView`) return slot emits a bare `return this->field;` -- invalid C++ (`std::optional<std::string>` does not convert to `std::string_view`).** `class Box: opt: str | None` with `def f(self) -> StrView: if self.opt is not None: return self.opt` emits `return this->opt;`; the narrowed read needs the unwrap (`return (*this->opt);`). Sibling shapes at the same slot are correct -- a plain owned `str` field emits the bare member read, which IS right there -- so it is the narrowing unwrap that is dropped, not the member render. Mirror image of the view-into-`Optional[str]` return entry above. THIR deliberately keeps this shape unrouted (it would emit the correct `(*this->opt)` and diverge from the broken oracle): the view-target coerce arm types its str-field admission on the DECLARED field type. Surfaced routing str-family field reads at the view-return sink through THIR (adversarial dual-path smoke; g++-confirmed). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A non-copyable `Own` local assigned inside a `try:` block cannot be MOVED afterwards -- it is stored optional-form and any later use silently copies (a hard error for a non-copyable type).** A `resp` bound by `resp = getresponse()` inside a `try` (getresponse returns `Own[HTTPResponse]`) is emitted as `std::optional<HTTPResponse>` (the possibly-unassigned-on-exception representation), so a later `Response(..., resp)` that should MOVE it instead attempts a copy -- rejected for the non-copyable `HTTPResponse` ("cannot be copied ... Only the original owner can be moved at its last use"), and for a COPYABLE type it silently copies (warned) + then miscompiles the move-into-`Own|None`-field via `ptr_to_optional_move(std::optional<T>&)` (expects `T*`). Reproduced whether the move is in the same try-scope, in a sibling branch, or after the try. The fix in `tplib.requests` was to bind the value from a HELPER-function return (`_send_recv`) instead of a try-scoped local -- a normal local from a call return moves cleanly. Toolchain-caught for non-copyable types (loud); SILENT extra copy for copyable ones. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/optmove{3,5}.py` (miscompile), `optmove4.py` (silent copy+warn), `optmove{6,7}.py` (helper-return workaround compiles). Surfaced building `tplib.requests` streaming (moving the `Own[HTTPResponse]` into `Response._raw`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A QUALIFIED `except mod.X:` clause whose bare name `X` shadows a builtin exception wrongly matches the BUILTIN of that name (and its subclasses), not the user's `mod.X`.** `import tplib.requests as requests` then `except requests.ConnectionError:` also catches a raw builtin `ConnectionResetError` (a subclass of builtin `ConnectionError`), even though `requests.ConnectionError` and builtin `ConnectionError` are unrelated sibling classes (both merely descend from `OSError`) -- real Python `isinstance` would never match. Root-caused to the qualified/dotted spelling specifically: the UNQUALIFIED `from tplib.requests import ConnectionError; except ConnectionError:` resolves correctly to the user class. Confirmed with a synthetic `class MyErr(OSError)` reached via `except mymod.ConnectionError` wrongly matching builtin `ConnectionResetError`, so it is a general builtin-name-shadow in qualified-except type resolution, not requests-specific. SILENT wrong control flow (reroutes to the wrong handler on a plausible real failure). Workaround: use the unqualified `from mod import X` spelling in the except clause. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_exc_module_shadow.py`, `probe_exc_unqualified.py`. Surfaced by the cpython-parity review of `requests` streaming (newly reachable: `iter_content` is the first public API that lets a raw unwrapped OS exception escape). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Forwarding a borrow-form `bytes | None` (Optional[bytes]) parameter into another call materializes a fresh owned copy instead of a zero-cost pass-through.** A function `f(body: bytes | None)` that calls `g(body)` where `g` also takes `bytes | None` emits `body ? std::make_optional(::tpy::bytes_copy(*body)) : std::nullopt` -- copying the whole payload -- even though source and destination are the same `std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>` borrow form. Not a miscompile, a perf gap; bites `tplib.requests`'s hot send path (extracting `_send_recv(body: bytes | None)` now copies the entire request body once per POST/PUT/PATCH, including large multipart uploads, where the pre-extraction code passed the owned body straight to `conn.request` with no copy). Same body-copy family as the requests `_encode_body`/`bytesview_to_bytes` perf residuals already tracked in TODO.md. Fix shape: forward a borrow-form Optional param by pass-through (no `bytes_copy`) when the destination param is the same borrow form. Workaround (lib side): keep `conn.request(body)` in the caller rather than behind a `bytes|None`-param helper. Surfaced by the codegen-correctness review of `requests` streaming. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Storing a generator's yielded REFERENCE-type value into an outer variable is neither copied nor rejected -- it aliases the generator frame and dangles once the loop ends (silent UAF).** `for chunk in gen(): first = chunk` then reading `first` after the loop (or after a `break`) prints garbage: the yielded `bytes` (a reference type) binds as a borrow into the frame's current-yield slot, and the plain outer-store copies the borrow, not the payload; the frame dies at loop end so `first` dangles. Using the loop var INSIDE the loop body, accumulating (`acc += chunk`), or copying explicitly (`first = bytes(chunk)`) are all safe -- only persisting the raw yielded value past the iteration step is wrong. Same generator-yield-borrow ABI family as the Safety-section resumable-frame borrow entries: the consumer-escape check is documented to reject re-yield/nested-capture and copy *value* stores, but a *reference-type* outer-store is neither rejected nor copied. No diagnostic; silent wrong bytes. Workaround: `x = bytes(chunk)` / `x = copy(chunk)`. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/breakcap2.py`. Surfaced adding `requests` streaming (`iter_content` chunks captured outward). The reachable surface now also covers the PRODUCER side of a relay: a resumable-frame borrow-tuple loop var rebound whole (`q0 = p` inside `for p in gen():`) and read after a later pull is accepted with no diagnostic and no copy, so the second frame field aliases the same inner element (probe `/tmp/agents/c1/p5.py`; it agrees with CPython only because the inner generator is materialized in the relay frame and outlives every read). Fix shape: the consumer-escape check must either reject or deep-copy a yielded reference-type value stored to a variable that outlives the iteration step. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `with EXPR as v:` whose EXPR is a call materializing a UNION-typed default argument emits the default's temp in a scope invisible to the with-header -- undeclared-variable C++ error.** `with obj.m("x", flag=True) as c:` where `m(self, a=None, verify: bool | str = True, flag: bool = False)` leaves `verify` to its default: codegen materializes the `bool | str` default as a `__tmp_N` variant temp but declares it in a block/statement-expression scope the with-header's `auto __ctx = obj.m(..., __tmp_N, ...)` cannot see -> g++ "'__tmp_N' was not declared in this scope". A SCALAR default (`int32 = 1`) needs no temp so does not trip it; a single union default in a FREE-function call in the with-header also compiled in isolation -- the trigger is the union-default temp landing in the with-context lowering (reproduced with a method call carrying a union default plus a later explicitly-passed arg). Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Workaround: bind the call result to a local first (`r = obj.m(...)`) then `with r:` -- the pre-bound form compiles. Fix shape: hoist union-typed default-arg temps for a with-header call into the enclosing scope (the same scope the `__ctx` temp is declared in), not the with-body block. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/withmethod.py`. Surfaced adding `requests` streaming (`with s.get(url, stream=True) as r:`, where `verify: bool | str = True` defaults). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A non-`None` constant default on a POINTER-repr union parameter is rendered bare against the variant, so the declaration does not compile.** [`pointer-union-nonnull-default-renders-bare`] `def free(r: Rec | int32 = 1)` emits `int32_t free(const std::variant<int32_t*, Rec*> r = 1);` and g++ reports `could not convert '1' from 'int' to 'const std::variant<int*, Rec*>'`; `r: Rec | str = "x"` fails the same way. Only `None` has a valid spelling at such a slot (`none_default_cpp_spelling` gives `nullptr`), which is why the sibling `r: Rec | None = None` compiles and this stayed hidden. Pre-existing on plain FREE functions, but it now reaches more C++ entities: on a resumable generator/async METHOD the same bad text is emitted three times -- the in-class factory declaration, the frame constructor, and every call that omits the argument -- because those declarations gained defaults with the resumable-factory default fix. Sites: `default_emittable` / `default_to_cpp` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) over the rule in `default_emittable_at` (`tpyc/typesys.py`). The call-site-fill regime that already handles record-typed `Optional`/union defaults is `default_needs_call_site_fill` (`tpyc/typesys.py`), and this shape misses it by the pointer-form escape (`inner.uses_pointer_repr() and not own` returns False): that escape was written for the INCOMPLETE-TYPE reason -- a `Rec*` alternative is complete where a free function is declared, unlike a value-form `std::variant<..., Rec, ...>` -- and it implicitly assumed the only default reaching a pointer-repr union slot is `None`. A non-`None` constant needs the address of an object, which no C++ default argument can name. Fix shape: route non-Optional union defaults with a non-`None` value through the call-site-fill regime like their record-typed value-form siblings (the fill already materializes a variant temp -- see the with-header entry above, which is that temp landing in the wrong scope), or render the default as a variant construction over a temp where one can be named. Repro `/tmp/agents/uniondef/main.py` (free + resumable method) and `/tmp/agents/uniondef/shapes.py` (shape matrix: `Rec | int32 = 1` and `Rec | str = "x"` fail, `Rec | None = None` compiles). Surfaced by the review round on the resumable-factory default fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A generator method that narrows an Optional reference-type `self` field is mis-inferred as `const`, const-poisoning the narrowed local.** A `def gen(self, n: int32 = 1) -> Iterator[T]` whose body does `x = self._field` (field `X | None`, `X` a reference type) then uses `x` gets emitted `const` (`__gen_C_gen C::gen(int32_t) const`), so if the method called on the narrowed local is `@readonly` (non-mutating) the local is `const X*` and a later non-const use is rejected ("invalid conversion from const X*"). Isolated triggers: yield-type is irrelevant (`int32` and `bytes` both hit it); the trigger is *narrowing an Optional reference-type self field inside the generator*. A generator that reads a non-Optional scalar field (`self._n`), or one where the narrowed field's method *mutates* self (so the generator is correctly inferred non-const), avoids it. Same "resumable generator method over a self field" family the async/generator TODO warns about. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Workaround: ensure the narrowed field's method mutates self, or copy the field's needed data into a scalar local before the generator. Fix shape: a generator method's self-const inference must account for the resumable-frame's mutation of captured `self` state. The default-drop half this entry also carried is FIXED (2026-09-09): the in-class declaration and the frame ctor now both carry the default whatever the const verdict, verified on this entry's own shape. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/gen_c.py`. Surfaced building `tplib.requests` streaming (`Response.iter_content` over `_raw: HTTPResponse | None`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] (CPython interop) A boundary-crossed user exception's `self.message = ...` attribute is unreadable on the `.so` (`e.message` -> AttributeError) though CPython-native carries it.** In TPy `self.message = msg` assigns the inherited `BaseException::message` field (the `what()`/`str()` source), NOT a data field -- so `info.fields` excludes it and the data-field setter does not set a `message` attribute; the reconstructed instance (`pytype(e.what())`) has no `.message` either. Under plain CPython (and `uv run tpy`), `self.message = msg` creates a readable instance attribute, so driver-side code reading `e.message` works there but raises `AttributeError` against the compiled `.so`. **Pre-existing** (already true for message-only excs before the data-field rung; just untested -- no driver read `e.message`), surfaced by the `interop-exc-data-fields` cpython-parity pass. **Genuinely unresolvable without modeling `super().__init__`:** TPy conflates `self.message = msg` (would expose `e.message` in CPython) with `super().__init__(msg)` (would NOT), so unconditionally setting a `message` attribute would diverge for the super-init idiom instead. Outside tpyc's diagnostic reach (the reader is plain-Python driver code). Low practical impact (data fields cross via their own attrs; `str(e)`/`e.what()` carry the message). Revisit only if it bites; a fix needs sema to record whether the user explicitly assigned `self.message`.
- **[MED small] `k in <dict>` on a const/readonly dict whose VALUE type is not `Equatable` is wrongly rejected -- the membership falls to a generic element-scan instead of `dict.contains`.** `k in d` where `d` is a const/readonly `dict[str, V]` (an inferred-const `self._store` in a readonly method, or a `readonly[dict[str, V]]` param) and `V` has no `__eq__` is a hard sema error: "'in' requires element type 'V' to conform to 'Equatable' (no '__eq__' method)". Two wrongs: (1) `in` on a dict tests KEYS, so it should never require the VALUE type Equatable; (2) even the fallback scans keys (when `V` IS Equatable, e.g. `dict[str, str]`, it compiles and returns correct key-membership), so `dict.contains` should have been used -- it's O(n), not O(1). A MUTABLE dict[str, V] with non-Equatable V uses `dict.contains` and compiles fine; only the const/readonly receiver drops to the buggy path. So the trigger is receiver const-ness, not the `__contains__` method name (an earlier read misattributed it). Same const-receiver-drops-the-right-lowering family as the borrow-local const-drop fixes already landed (and the storage-tuple/borrow-tuple residual entry below). Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: give `V` an `__eq__` (makes `in` compile and scan keys), test membership on a mutable binding, or use `.get(k) is not None`. Fix shape: `k in d` must resolve `dict.__contains__(readonly[K])` on a const/readonly dict receiver too (the const path is dropping the builtin container-membership lowering and demanding the value Equatable). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/cookieprobe` (`name in self._store` in a readonly method over `dict[str, Cookie]`). Surfaced building `tplib.requests` CookieJar. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code) A class that explicitly defines `__hash__` + `__eq__` is still rejected as a `set` element / dict key -- "missing __hash__".** `class Counter: def __eq__(self, other): ...; def __hash__(self) -> int64: return self.value` then `s: set[Counter]` errors `Type 'Counter' cannot be used as a set element (missing __hash__; use @dataclass(frozen=True) or define it explicitly)` -- even though `__hash__` IS defined explicitly. Reproduces on a PLAIN (non-`@export`) class, so it is a general Hashable-conformance gap, not interop-specific. Likely either the hand-written `__hash__` isn't detected by the Hashable-conformance check, or the `-> int64` return type isn't accepted where a plain `int`/`Py_hash_t` is expected (unverified which). Rejects-valid: a user cannot put a hand-hashable class in a `set`/`dict` key at all; the only path is `@dataclass(frozen=True)`. Consequence for interop: an exposed class can never be a `set` element / dict key even in principle, which is *why* the container-element rung (`interop-container-element-exposed-types`) defers those positions rather than admitting them. Fix shape: make the set/dict-key Hashable check recognize an explicit `__hash__`+`__eq__` pair (and confirm the accepted `__hash__` return type). **When fixing, ALSO add + test a principled interop reject (`_unsupported_exposed_element` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py::_exposed_form_error`): an `@export` class cannot be a `set`-element / dict KEY at the CPython boundary regardless of its `__hash__` -- a class copies per element at the boundary (copy-on-cross), so it has no stable hash identity for a hash table. Today the over-broad Hashable check incidentally rejects it, so that interop reject would be un-observable dead code now; fixing THIS bug removes the shadow and would silently open the copy-vs-hash-identity footgun without the interop guard (see TODO container-boundary item 1-iv).** Reproducer `/tmp/agents/plain_hash.py`. Surfaced probing set-element admission during the container-element rung. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A view-form str source inside a NESTED list literal emits ill-formed C++ -- `m: list[list[str]] = [[sv]]` (StrView `sv`) renders `{{sv}}` with no `std::string` wrap.** The inner literal gets no element target at un-threaded nested positions (list elements do not thread, unlike Array elements and dict values), so the view->owned copy chokepoint never fires and the brace-init tries to seat a `std::string_view` in a `std::string` slot -- g++ rejects it. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid. Workaround: bind the inner list first (`row = [sv]; m = [row]`) or wrap explicitly (`[[str(sv)]]`). Fix shape: thread the element target through nested list-literal positions (the same threading Array/dict already get) so `_view_source_to_owned` fires. THIR gate-rejects the shape (`container_lit.nested_view`). Surfaced by the THIR container-literal cell's probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Related to the async-frame template-loss entries but a distinct sync generic-call site. - **[LOW medium] A generic call that fails inference because an argument doesn't satisfy a generic-protocol bound reports the vague "Cannot infer type arguments" instead of the precise "does not satisfy bound".** `unwrap(NoGet(1))` where `def unwrap[R, T: Container[R]](x: T) -> R` and `NoGet` lacks `get()` errors `Cannot infer type arguments for 'unwrap'. Specify explicitly: unwrap[R, T](...)` -- the real problem is that `NoGet` doesn't conform to `Container[R]` (so the associated-type pass can't solve `R`, and it's rejected at the reject-unresolved loop `tpyc/sema/type_ops.py:1468` before ever reaching the bound-conformance check at :1477). The EXPLICIT-args spelling already gives the good message (`Type argument 'NoGet' does not satisfy bound 'Container[int]' for type parameter 'T'`, via `validate_type_param_bounds`); only the inferred path is vague. Root: `infer_type_params_for_function` returns a bare `None` for BOTH "genuinely uninferrable" and "bound violated", collapsing them so the caller can't tell which message to emit -- the `None` is deliberately silent so overload resolution can fall through to the next candidate (`type_ops.py:1481`). Rejects-invalid-code (correct rejection, misleading message), not a miscompile. Discriminator for the right message: when a sibling param stays unresolved, check whether the carrier conforms to the bound with the sibling left free -- non-conforming -> "does not satisfy bound"; conforming-but-sibling-unrecoverable -> "cannot infer" is correct. Fix shape (do NOT band-aid with a one-off out-param): the proper fix is a structured inference-failure result (reason + offending param/bound) returned by `infer_type_params_for_function`, routed so overload resolution stays silent (it discards the reason and tries the next candidate). SCOPE -- consolidate ONLY the tier that funnels through that primitive's `None` return: the free-function generic calls (`calls.py:3837/4353/5101/5128`), generic methods (`methods.py:2061`), and its record sibling `infer_type_params_for_record` (`calls.py:5484/5682`); the shared silent caller is `overloads.py:655`. Do NOT fold in two adjacent-but-separate mechanisms: the empty-container factory messages (`_raise_empty_container_from_arg` calls.py:761, and :1207/:1264) are `list()`/`dict()`/`set()` element inference keyed on `get_element_type`/`PendingListType`, a distinct path that may adopt the same failure vocabulary later but should not be force-merged here; and `_unsafe_cast_diagnostics` (:4727) is a bespoke per-function diagnostic with its own TODO to become a `@compiler_check` decorator. - **[LOW small] A None-typed generic result captured in a local cannot be used -- `std::monostate` vs `nullptr_t` hard C++ error.** `r: None = f()` where `f`'s type param inferred to `None` (e.g. `identity[R](x: R) -> R` called with `None`) emits a `std::monostate` local, and a later `r is None` renders `operator==` against `nullptr` -- no such overload, hard C++ error, no TPy diagnostic. - **[LOW small] (parity) A temp-hoisted call argument evaluates BEFORE a side-effecting receiver, reversing CPython's receiver-first order.** `make("R").eat(Box(mk("A")))` where `make()` (the receiver) and `mk()` (nested in a value-union-param arg) both print: the arg is hoisted to a `std::variant __tmp = ...;` statement emitted BEFORE the `make("R").eat(__tmp)` call expression, so the arg's side effect ("arg A") runs before the receiver's ("recv R") -- TPy prints `arg A / recv R`, CPython `recv R / arg A`. Only observable when BOTH the receiver expression and a temp-hoisted arg have side effects (a plain inline arg keeps correct order; a plain-name receiver has no side effect). Silent (no diagnostic, wrong order). Independent of the value-union double-eval fix (that fixed the COUNT; this is ORDER) -- the lazy-args change moved arg emission after receiver GENERATION but the arg's hoisted temp STATEMENT still precedes the inline-receiver call expression. Fix shape: when the receiver expression is side-effecting/non-trivial and any arg hoists a temp, lift the receiver into its own temp first (emit it before the arg temps), or emit arg temps after the receiver temp. Self-contained repro: a `Box.__init__(self, tz: Fixed | Zone | None = None)` (two value-record union arms force the arg hoist) plus `make(tag: str) -> Own[Box]` and `mk(tag: str) -> Fixed` that each `print(tag)`, then `make("R").eat(Box(mk("A")))` -- prints `A` then `R` (CPython `R` then `A`).
