Surfaced adding a side-effecting-receiver arm to the double-eval regression test; pre-existing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (parity) Rebinding `self` inside a method silently reads the ORIGINAL receiver afterwards -- CPython reads the rebound object.** `def peek(self, other: "Chain") -> int: self = other; return self.n` -- codegen emits a fresh shadowing decl for the rebind (`const Chain& self = other;`) but every subsequent `self` read still renders against the receiver (`this->n` / `return (*this);`), so TPy returns the original object's state where CPython returns `other`'s. Silent (compiles clean, wrong value). Workaround: rename the local (don't rebind `self`). Root: codegen never seeds the receiver as a scope NAME, so the rebind creates a shadow local, but the `self`-read special-casing (the `this` render) doesn't know about the shadow. Fix shape: either reject `self` rebinds with a clear diagnostic (Rust-flavored; simplest and arguably better than the confusing CPython pattern) or route post-rebind reads through the shadow local. NB the THIR path GATE-REJECTS bodies with `self` rebinds (they fall back to this AST render), so fixing this fixes both paths. Self-contained repro: /tmp/agents/self_reassign_probe shape. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the THIR return-slot-tail branch; pre-existing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Reading an Optional-REFERENCE element out of a tuple param drops const -- ill-formed C++.** `def read(pair: tuple[Box | None, int]): first = pair[0]` where `Box` is a reference type: the tuple param lowers to `const std::tuple<const Box*, ...>&` (element 0 is `const Box*`), but the extracted local is typed `Box* first = std::get<0>(pair)` -> "invalid conversion from `const Box*` to `Box*`" (g++, -fpermissive). The const of the borrowed tuple isn't propagated to the pointer-repr Optional element local. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. A plain (non-Optional) reference tuple element and a value-type Optional element are unaffected; the bug is specific to the pointer-repr-Optional element read. Fix shape: the tuple-element-extraction local for a pointer-repr Optional slot must inherit the source tuple's const-ness (`const Box*`), mirroring how plain reference elements already const-propagate. Self-contained repro: `class Box: def __init__(self, v: int) -> None: self.v = v` + `def read(pair: tuple[Box | None, int]) -> int: first = pair[0]; return first.v if first is not None else -1`, called `read((Box(5), 9))`. Surfaced adding an Optional-borrow-slot arm to the tuple double-eval regression test (union/tuple_arg_union_eval_once); pre-existing, unrelated to that fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A value of a SUB-union type does not coerce to a param/slot of a wider union (`timezone | None` arg to a `timezone | ZoneInfo | None` param is a type error) -- rejects-valid.** Sema reports "Type mismatch in argument 'tzinfo': expected None | ZoneInfo | timezone, got timezone | None"; CPython/typing accept member-subset unions. Workaround: annotate the local as the full target union upfront (datetime.py strptime/fromisoformat do this, with a comment pointing here). Fix shape: union-to-union coercion when every source member coerces to some target member (the C++ side needs a variant-widening conversion helper, mirroring to_value_variant). Surfaced by datetime v4's tz-slot widening. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An Optional or union parameter on a nested def is a hard compile error.** [`nested-def-optional-param`] `def get(r: Rec | None)` or `def pick(x: int32 | None)` nested inside a function fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.nested_def:nesteddef.param_type)`, from the nested-def param classifier at `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:4861`. The shape never worked: a nested def lowers to a C++ lambda whose params never receive the pointer/optional classification top-level params get, so the body read (`r.v`, field access on a never-classified name) and the call-site conversion (`get(a)` / `get(std::nullopt)`) disagreed and g++ rejected the combination -- the reject replaces that ill-formed render. Everyday shape (an Optional param on a helper closure is ordinary Python), so worth queueing. Container params (`list`/`dict`/`set`/`bytearray`, `readonly[...]` included) were admitted on 2026-09-03 (`tests/cases/nested_def/container_params`); Optional and union parameter forms remain rejected by the lambda parameter gate. Fix shape: seed the lambda's params with the same classification top-level params get, plus the optional-ptr call-arg conversion at closure call sites, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_452_nesteddef_opt_param.py` and `02_452b_scalar.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
  An ordinary union parameter `y: str | int32` also rejects at `stmt.nested_def:nesteddef.param_type` before the nested body lowers. The gate admits scalar, char, enum, str/bytes and supported reference types but excludes UnionType, independently of match indexing or narrowed-union capture. It is unchanged from pre-merge `987d04c5`. The repair must align lambda signature/body parameter classification and closure-call conversions; nested helpers emitted as resumable frame members use a separate path without this gate.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A nested def shadowing a BUILTIN name is a hard compile error at the call site.** [`nested-def-shadowing-builtin-call-rejected`] `def abs(x)` inside a function, then `abs(-3)`, fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.call:call.closure_import_shadow)`, from the callee classifier at `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:3747`. Previously this was SILENT wrong behavior -- the call reached `::std::abs`, not the closure, where CPython calls the closure -- so the loud reject is a strict improvement, but the valid program still does not compile. A closure shadowing a builtin is exotic, so low priority to queue. Fix shape: resolve the callee against the enclosing function's nested-def locals BEFORE the imported/builtin arm (sema's resolution already points at the closure), then widen the admission. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_453_nesteddef_shadow_builtin.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The IMPORTED-name twin rejects the same way: `from tpy import dispatch` / `def outer(): def dispatch() -> int32: ...; return dispatch()` stops at `call.closure_import_shadow` (surfaced 2026-09-12 by `int/scalar_type_names`, whose nested-def section therefore defines the shadowing def without calling it).
- **[MED small] A package __init__ that calls submodule functions from record-method bodies emits circular C++ includes -- the build fails whenever a submodule TU is compiled first.** Package-import semantics emit `child.hpp #include parent.hpp` (importing `pkg._sub` imports `pkg` first), and the parent includes the child it uses -- a cycle. Harmless when the parent's uses are in free functions (defined out-of-line in .cpp; `os/` works this way), but record METHODS emit inline in the parent header, so a TU that includes `child.hpp` first sees the parent's inline bodies before the child's declarations (`#pragma once` skips the in-flight re-include) -> `'pkg::_sub' has not been declared`. Hit by the attempted `lib/tpy/datetime/` package split (class-heavy __init__ calling `_fmt`/`_parse` helpers from datetime methods); worked around by flat `_datetime_*` sibling modules (no parent edge, acyclic). Fix shape: emit forward declarations for the parent's cross-submodule uses, or drop the child->parent include when the child does not reference parent symbols, or emit record method bodies out-of-line in the .cpp when they reference submodules. Validation case once fixed: restructure datetime as a package with a pure re-export `__init__.py` + `_types.py` submodule holding the classes (the preferred target layout; a re-export-only parent does NOT dodge the bug today -- the parent must include the types module, so a sibling TU still enters it with its own header in-flight). Surfaced by the datetime v3 module split. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Tuple-unpack targets assigned in SIBLING branches are not hoisted -- the second branch emits an assignment to an undeclared name (invalid C++).** `if flag: a, b = pair(1) ... else: a, b = pair(2)` -- the first branch emits a block-scoped declaration (`::tpy::BigInt a = std::get<0>(...)`), the second emits plain `a = std::get<0>(...)` where `a` no longer exists -> g++ "'a' was not declared in this scope". Plain (non-tuple) assignments in sibling branches hoist correctly; the pre-scan hoisting misses tuple-unpack targets. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent; any multi-branch parser/dispatcher shape hits it. Workaround: unique per-branch names (datetime v3's `_apply_directive` ships with this workaround baked in -- revert to shared names when fixed). Fix shape: teach the pre-scan hoisting pass to treat tuple-assign targets like plain assign targets. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/dt_v3/repro_unpack_hoist.py`. Surfaced by datetime v3's strptime engine. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A format spec on a user-record f-string placeholder is misapplied to the `__str__` result instead of dispatching (or being rejected) -- silent divergence for `std::format`-legal specs.** `f"{rec:>30}"` compiles to `std::format("{:>30}", ::tpy::__str__(rec))` and prints a 30-column right-padded `rec`; CPython calls `rec.__format__(">30")`, which for a plain record (`object.__format__`) raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to Rec.__format__`, and for spec-aware types (datetime delegates to strftime) produces entirely different output. Specs that are NOT string-legal (`f"{dt:%Y}"`) fail as a raw g++ `std::format` error (leaky diagnostic, no TPy sema error). Sema rejects specs only on BigInt/IntLiteral (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py:4082`); the f-string emitter (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:1451-1455`) splices the spec around whatever the placeholder rendered, the `__str__` call included. Fix shape: sema rejects non-empty format specs on user types without `__format__` (loud, CPython-faithful for plain records) until a `__format__` protocol lands (TODO.md); datetime's strftime delegation rides on that feature. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_456_record_fstring_spec.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ternary mixing a str slice with a str param is rejected: "Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'StrView' and 'str'".** `timestr = tstr[:i] if i > 0 else tstr` (with `tstr: str` a param) fails sema although both arms are the same runtime type (str IS StrView); spelled as an if/else assignment it compiles fine. Rejects-valid annoyance in parser-style code. Fix shape: unify str/StrView in the ternary join like assignment contexts already do. Surfaced by datetime v3's fromisoformat port. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A frozen dataclass with an `Optional[record]` field cannot synthesize `__hash__`: "No matching overload for hash(R | None)".** `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with `inner: R | None` fails at the synthesized `__hash__` because the `hash()` builtin overload set has no Optional arm (eq synthesis handles the field fine). Workaround: hand-write `__hash__` (datetime's aware `datetime` needed one anyway). Fix shape: an `Optional[T]`-accepting `hash` overload (hash the inner or a None sentinel, matching CPython's `hash(None)` stability) or field-wise None handling in the dataclass hash builder. Surfaced by the datetime v3 tzinfo-field probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) BigInt-default module: a LITERAL str/bytes slice bound is a hard compile error.** Under `--default-int BigInt` (or `default_int: BigInt`), `s[1:3]` fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.expr_stmt:subscript.slice_shape)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:5952`. The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed C++: the slice-bound narrow appended the runtime-BigInt conversion to ANY bound with no literal exemption, so `::tpy::BasicSlice{1.to_fixed_check<int32_t>(), 3.to_fixed_check<int32_t>()}` lexed `1.to_fixed_check` as one preprocessing-number token. Negated literal bounds (`s[-2:i]`) are the same row. Everyday shape in a BigInt-default module, so worth queueing. Scope verified: the same slice compiles under the default int, and a name-bound slice (`lo = 1; s[lo:hi]`) compiles under BigInt -- the bind-a-local workaround stands. Fix shape: exempt literal bounds in int32 range from the narrow (the BasicSlice int32 field absorbs them) or parenthesize the render before appending, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_459_bigint_slice_lit.py` and `02_459b_name_bounds.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The record-subscript BigInt-narrow width derives from `__getitem__`'s key param for ALL subscript operations -- a record whose `__delitem__`/`__setitem__` declares a different key width (or that has no single-int-key `__getitem__` at all) gets the wrong narrow on del/store.** [`record-subscript-bigint-narrow-width`] `bigint_index_narrow_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) consults `record_getitem_key_ret` only; sema's `del c[k]` requires just `__delitem__` and never validates the index against its key param (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~5166), so a record with `__delitem__(key: int)` and no `__getitem__` falls to the int32 default and `del c[2**40]` panics where CPython works -- the original BigInt-dict-key panic, alive on this rare path. A `__setitem__` key width differing from `__getitem__`'s narrows stores to the getitem width (AST and THIR share the helper, so both are consistently wrong the same way). Workaround: declare a single-int-key `__getitem__` with the intended key width. Fix shape: thread the operation's dunder into the helper (per-op key-param lookup via the same substitution-aware sema accessor, `__setitem__`/`__delitem__` falling back to `__getitem__`); the THIR mirror follows automatically (shared helper). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the BigInt-dict-key fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A structural protocol declaring `__getitem__` with a BigInt key param fails C++ concept satisfaction for conforming user records -- the shape never builds.** A `Protocol` with `def __getitem__(self, key: int) -> str` emits a concept requiring `::tpy::__getitem__(t, std::declval<::tpy::BigInt>())`, which a conforming record (methods/operator[], no free-dunder arm for the record type) does not satisfy -- g++ rejects at monomorphization. Loud, not silent. When this shape is made to work, note the subscript index render also needs the receiver's declared key width: `bigint_index_narrow_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) consults dict key types and concrete user-record `__getitem__` key params but falls to the int32 default for protocol-typed receivers, so a BigInt index would round-trip BigInt -> int32 and panic beyond int32. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bigint-dict-key/probe_proto.py`. Surfaced by the BigInt-dict-key subscript fix survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Enum members outside int32 range are accepted at sema but emit `enum class E : int32_t { A = 5000000000 }` -- ill-formed C++ (build failure).** `class BigE(Enum): A = 5000000000` compiles cleanly through sema, but the emitted enum's underlying type is unconditionally `int32_t` while the enumerator value exceeds it -- g++ rejects the narrowing. `EnumUtil<E>::from_value` similarly spells `.to_fixed_check<int32_t>()` for a BigInt arg (`einfo.underlying_type` is always int32 today), so even if the decl compiled, out-of-range lookups would panic. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Workaround: keep enum member values within int32 range. Fix shape: infer the underlying type from the member value range (int32 -> int64 widening; reject beyond int64), threading it through `EnumInfo.underlying_type` so the decl, `from_value`, and the fstring/print `static_cast<int>` arms all agree -- or reject out-of-int32 members at sema with a clear diagnostic. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probes-bigint/probe2.py` (`BigE`). Surfaced by the THIR BigInt-narrow probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) `not rec` is rejected for a user record without `__bool__`/`__len__`, although `if rec:` accepts the same operand.** `not make()` errors "Invalid operand type for 'not': Rec (expected bool, numeric, or type with __bool__/__len__)" while the bare truthiness context compiles and applies Python's always-true default. CPython accepts both (`not` is defined for every object). The asymmetry is sema-only -- codegen renders the negated always-true form fine, as the plain-enum sibling shows. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/truthy-arm/repro.py` (the removed `not make_rec()` line). Fix shape: let the `not` operand check accept any type the truthiness context accepts (the always-true default), rather than requiring a truthiness dunder. Do this together with the always-true truthiness WARNING queued in TODO.md -- both halves read the same no-truthiness-hook verdict sema already computes here, and fixing this one alone leaves `if rec:` silent about being unconditional. Surfaced fixing the folded-truthiness operand drop. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (missing diagnostic) The optional-truthiness warning does not fire for a `match` case GUARD, only for an `if`/`while` condition.** `case 1 if v:` with `v: int32 | None` compiles silently, where the equivalent `if v:` warns "Truthiness check on optional value may also exclude falsy non-None values; use 'is not None' for None-only checks". The guard is a boolean context with the same footgun (a `Some(0)` payload is falsy), so the user loses the nudge exactly where the pattern-match reads most like a None test. Codegen is correct -- only the sema diagnostic is missing; the warning is raised where `if`/`while` conditions are analysed and match guards do not route through it. Witness: `tests/cases/match/guard_truthiness` (its `# tpyc: ok` annotation pins the current no-warning behavior). Fix shape: raise the same warning from the match-guard analysis path. Surfaced fixing the resumable/guard truthiness render. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Un-narrowed truthiness of a pointer-repr `Optional[container]` (`list`/`dict`/`set`/`bytearray`) ignores inner emptiness -- `if xs:` on a `list[int] | None` emits the bare non-null pointer test, so a non-None but EMPTY container reads truthy (silent CPython divergence).** The un-narrowed form renders `if (xs)` instead of `xs != nullptr && !xs->empty()`; CPython's `bool(container)` is length-based, so an empty non-None container takes the branch in TPy but not in CPython. The *narrowed*-by-name form (`if xs is not None: if xs:`) IS correct -- it dispatches `::tpy::__len__((*xs)) != 0` via the narrowed-occurrence swap in `gen_truthy_expr`. The sibling `Optional[user-record]` case dispatches `::tpy::ptr_truthy` in both forms; containers are excluded from the un-narrowed `ptr_truthy` path by the `is_user_record` gate (`ptr_truthy` dispatches `__bool__`/`__len__` *member* calls that the container runtime types do not expose). Workaround: test `len(xs) > 0`, or narrow and bind. Fix shape: extend the un-narrowed pointer-repr Optional truthiness dispatch to route builtin-container inners through their `.empty()`/`__len__` truthiness. Sibling of the storage-form `Optional[record]` truthiness entry below (same "the source shape is excluded from the dunder dispatch" family). Surfaced during the `Optional[record]` truthiness fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Truthiness of a STORAGE-FORM `Optional[record]` source (a record FIELD or a container ELEMENT) skips the record's `__bool__`/`__len__` -- `if self.f:` / `if xs[0]:` on a `Record | None` field/element emits the bare `std::optional` non-null test, so a non-None but falsy record reads truthy (silent CPython divergence).** The pointer-repr `Optional[record]` truthiness fix dispatches the dunder only for sources that render as a raw `T*` (pointer name / call return); a field or container element is `std::optional<Record>` storage (`is_storage_form_optional_source`), which is deliberately excluded (a `ptr_truthy`/deref there would fail to compile) and falls back to the pre-existing `has_value()` render. The narrowed field form (`if self.f is None: ...; if self.f:`) is worse -- it emits `::tpy::__bool__(this->f)` against the `std::optional`, a toolchain-caught build error (pre-existing, unrelated to the un-narrowed silent case). Workaround: bind to a local first (`x = self.f; if x: ...`) so the source is a pointer name. Fix shape: unwrap the storage-form `std::optional` (`optional_to_ptr` / `(*opt)`) before dispatching the inner record's truthiness, mirroring what the pointer-name path does; the narrowed field build-error needs the same unwrap. THIR keeps these on the AST path (`truthy.optional_field_narrow`). Surfaced by the /tpy-review of the `Optional[record]` truthiness fix. **The `@property` spelling reaches the same arm since 2026-09-18** -- `if b.rec:` over an `Optional[Rec]` getter renders the bare engagement test exactly as the field read does, so the divergence is one spelling wider, not one deeper, and the fix at the shared arm (`_storage_opt_record_truthy`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) closes both; probe `/tmp/agents/r2/nt_rec.py` and its field twin. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `Any` holding a user record whose only truthiness hook is `__len__` is always truthy.** `any_to_bool_capable` in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/any.hpp` recognizes bool construction, `.empty()`, and `.__bool__()`, but not `.__len__()`. It therefore installs Any's default always-true slot even though direct implicit truthiness correctly evaluates `::tpy::__len__(record) != 0`; an empty record wrapped in `Any` diverges from CPython. Workaround: define `__bool__` as well as `__len__`, or avoid erasing the value to `Any` before the test. Fix shape: add the `__len__` capability and dispatch to the same length-based truthiness used for direct records. THIR's `::tpy::to_bool(any)` mode faithfully preserves the existing runtime behavior. Surfaced by the THIR structured-truthiness probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A walrus-bound `with` manager (`with (m := CM()):`) is a hard compile error.** Codegen fails with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.walrus)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:6890` for a walrus target the prescan hoisted. The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed: the hoisted `std::optional<CM> m;` pre-decl landed at the first statement INSIDE the `try {}`, after the `auto __ctx_N = (m = CM(...), *m);` line that reads it, so g++ rejected `'m' was not declared in this scope`, and post-with reads dangled. Scope verified: an ordinary walrus in a condition (`if (m := n + 1) > 2:`) lowers fine, so only the hoisted-target / with-manager face rejects. Exotic; workaround is to bind first (`m = CM(); with m:`). Fix shape: place the hoisted pre-decl in the enclosing scope, before the `__ctx_N` header line rather than after it, then widen the admission. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_469_walrus_with.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A global-variable write BEFORE its `global` statement compiles and runs; CPython rejects it as SyntaxError.** `def f(): g = 1; global g; g = 2` compiles in TPy (both writes hit the module global; `f()` leaves `g == 2`) where CPython raises `SyntaxError: name 'g' is assigned to before global declaration`. Root: `ast.parse` accepts the shape (CPython's check lives in the symtable stage, which TPy's parser never runs) and sema's `_analyze_global_stmt` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) has no ordering check -- `function_global_decls` is a whole-function set, so every write is treated as a global write regardless of position. Accepts-invalid parity gap, not a miscompile: TPy's behavior is self-consistent (and the AST and THIR paths emit byte-identical code for the shape). Workaround: none needed -- valid programs are unaffected. Fix shape: reject an assignment to a name that a LATER `global` statement in the same function declares (a source-order pre-pass over the function body in `_analyze_global_stmt` or the function pre-scan). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion probing the THIR global-seeding invariant (reproducer `/tmp/agents/stmt-shapes/probe_global2.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] `is_const_union_source` does not see const TUPLE-local roots -- a chain rooted at a const storage/borrow-tuple local still loses const at every const-spelling sink.** The recursive "rooted in a const source" predicate (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py:is_const_union_source`, shared by the union/optional lifts, REF_ALIAS, and `is_const_storage_source`) checks the base name only against `const_ref_params` / `const_indirect_locals`. A name bound const as a TUPLE local (`const_storage_form_tuple_locals` / `const_borrow_form_tuple_locals` / `const_optional_borrow_tuple_locals` -- e.g. a const `auto&&` storage-tuple alias) rooting a deeper chain (`q = pair[1]` where element 1 is itself a pointer-repr tuple, or a union field off such a local) is missed, so the sink declares mutable against a const lvalue (same ill-formed-C++ class as the fixed deep-source entry, one level deeper). Latent: needs nested pointer-repr tuples (or a union field off a const tuple local), not exercised in-corpus. Fix shape: widen the base-name check to all five const name sets -- but that changes `is_const_union_source` for its union/optional consumers too (value-variant lift, storage-optional lift, REF_ALIAS, `.get()` accessor, ptr-variant init), so each needs its own verification + sibling tests. Surfaced closing the deep-source `is_const_storage_source` entry. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A value printed through an Any-ISINSTANCE-narrowed binding uses C++ default formatting, not Python's.** `def show(v: Any): if isinstance(v, float): print("x", v)` with `show(2.0)` prints `x 2` (CPython `x 2.0`); the bool face prints `1`/`0` instead of `True`/`False` (probes `/tmp/agents/while-arm/probe_floatfmt.py`, `probe_boolfmt.py`). Root: the print-arg classification keys on the DECLARED type (`get_resolved_type` reads the pre-narrow `Any` binding), so the narrowed alias streams raw (`std::cout << __v`) instead of taking the `::tpy::print_float` / `print_bool` formatter -- while a direct `print(2.0)` formats correctly. Un-narrowed Any prints route `::tpy::to_string`-family dispatch and are fine; only the narrowed-alias reads mis-classify. NB THIR mirrors this byte-identically (the D15 Any-narrow arm's print RAW / truthy TO_BOOL declared-type mirrors, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` print loop + `_lower_truthy`) -- when the AST classification is fixed to use the narrowed occurrence type, update both mirrors in lockstep (the unit pins that would have flagged them went with the THIR unit suite). Fix shape: classify print args (and the truthiness arm's declared-Any `to_bool`) by the sema-retyped occurrence type when the arg is a narrowed name. Surfaced by the THIR Any-isinstance arm's byte-diff. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A `while` condition combining a WALRUS binding with a temp-materializing arg keeps single-evaluation semantics, and the temp's init may read the walrus target before its first assignment.** The per-iteration loop-head restructure (`while (true) { <temps>; if (!(cond)) break; }`) is deliberately GATED to walrus-free conditions (`contains_named_expr` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`): an in-head temp could run before the walrus assignment it reads (`while (n := head(xs)) > 0 and show([n]) >= 0:` -- `__tmp = {n}` precedes `n = ...`), and a borrow-form walrus (pointer-form, function-scope) aliasing into a per-iteration temp would DANGLE after the loop (verified UAF shape: `while (x := get_ref(Box(n))).val < 100:` + post-loop `x.val`). The gated fallback is the legacy pre-loop flush (byte-identical to the pre-fix emission): the temp evaluates ONCE -- stale across iterations -- and its init reads the walrus target's pre-assignment (default-constructed) value on first evaluation. The simple-generator peephole face instead REJECTS with a clear CodeGenError (on master it did not compile at all -- undeclared `__tmp` -- so the loud reject regresses nothing and avoids minting new silent-divergence surface). The read-before-assignment face is also live in `if`/boolop conditions today (statement-level flush precedes the condition); the conditional-position sibling entry above covers skipped-vs-run, not this value-ordering face. Underlying pre-existing safety gap: a borrow-return rooted at an rvalue-arg temp registers no loan, so nothing in sema stops such an alias outliving the temp in general. Workaround: bind the walrus in a separate statement (`while True:` + `if not ...: break`). Fix shape: hoist an optional slot pre-loop and emplace per iteration (`std::optional<T> __tmp_slot;` + `auto& __tmp_N = __tmp_slot.emplace(<init>);` in the head) -- function-scope lifetime with per-iteration re-init, matching CPython aliasing for post-loop borrows; the within-condition ordering face additionally needs the expression-order temp interleaving from the sibling entry above. Probes `/tmp/agents/while_probe/probe5.py` (ordering), `/tmp/agents/safety_check/repro3.py` (dangle). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + safety-model) of the while-condition temp fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A record rvalue or an owning CALL at a MUTATED method parameter has no hoisting row, where a container literal at the same slot hoists a named temporary.** [`record-rvalue-at-mutated-method-slot-unhoisted`] `a.absorb(A(4))` / `got = k.pick(R(3))` with `def pick(self, r: R) -> R: return r`, and `k.fill(mk())` with `def mk() -> Own[list[int32]]` or `k.fill(copy(d))` (`calls/error_own_call_at_mutable_method_slot`; the `copy()` spelling at a dict / set slot used to render bare and fail the C++ build), reject at `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`, while `k.fill([1, 2])`, `k.pick([3, 4])` and `ListTaker(copy(w.items))` hoist `__tmp_N` and bind the mutable reference (`calls/method_literal_arg_mutable_slot`, `calls/ctor_mutated_slot_field_arg`). The method family's argument table has the hoist cell for the container literal only; the free-call and constructor families hoist a record rvalue through `_record_rvalue_temp_slot`. The fix is the argument-table family collapse (TODO.md, THE NEXT ORDER item 2), which gives every family the one hoist row. Workaround: bind the rvalue to a local first.
- **[LOW small] (DOES NOT REPRODUCE 2026-09-02 -- confirm and withdraw) isinstance narrowing inside an INFERRED-readonly method drops the const spelling on a plain ptr-union param.** As filed (2026-07-03): a method whose plain (unannotated) `A | B` param is const only by inference (`deep_const_borrow_params`) and which isinstance-narrows that param in its own body lowers to non-const `std::holds_alternative<A*>` / `std::get<A*>` where the AST emits the const forms (`const A*`); the named root was that `_narrow_member_cpp` keyed the const-pointee verdict only on `lc.const_locals` (the U2 field-lift chain) and was never seeded from the method fi's `deep_const_borrow_params`. **That root is gone**: `_narrow_subject_const` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) now falls through to `_param_is_deep_const`, and the described shape emits `std::variant<const A*, const B*>` in the signature with matching `const A*` template args in the narrowing. Re-checked on the cutover branch by emitting the same source both ways (`thir_codegen` False then True) -- byte-identical, with the method in the ROUTED set, so the agreement is not a fallback artifact. The original reproducer path is gone; the re-check used the plain shape the entry describes. Withdraw once someone identifies the commit that fixed it, or supplies a shape that still diverges.
- **[MED small] `match` over a union of two same-canonical-named records is miscompiled: one covering `case` is treated as exhaustive, so the other member hits `std::unreachable()` (UB / silent wrong output).** `from m import Point as Foreign`, local `class Point`, then `def f(p: Foreign | Point): match p: case Point(y=v): return v` -- the union is correctly `std::variant<main::Point*, shapes::Point*>`, but the match is wrongly marked exhaustive, so codegen emits `switch(index())` with only `case 0` (the local `Point` arm) followed by `::std::unreachable()` and a dead `return -1`. A `Foreign` (index 1) subject falls through to `std::unreachable()` -> UB; observed silent wrong output (`f(Foreign(7))` returned `9`, the previous local value's register, instead of falling through). Root cause: union coverage is keyed by `str(member)` (bare name) -- `_match_missing_cases`'s `UnionType` arm (`str(m) not in seen_types`) and `_build_pattern_type_key` (`str(resolved) + constraint`) -- so the two same-canonical-named members both render `"Point"` and collapse to one coverage key, making a single `case Point` look like it covers both. The third and most severe site of the bare-`.name`-as-match-identity family (the concrete + union-membership identity sites were fixed on `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`). Pre-existing on `master`. Fix shape: key union coverage/missing-case tracking by qname (mirror the enum `_match_missing_cases` fix on `fix-match-aliased-enum`), so distinct same-named members stay distinct and the match is correctly non-exhaustive (fall through to the after-match code instead of `unreachable`). Sibling survey needed: same-named enum members or literal patterns collapsing in the same `str()`-keyed coverage. Surfaced by a user probe (`Point | ForeignPoint` matching) after `/tpy-review` of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`; reproducer `/tmp/agents/fp_union/`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An alias-imported record used as a `match` class-pattern against a UNION subject is wrongly rejected as "not a member".** `from m import Widget as W`, then `match u: case W(...)` where `u: W | Other` errors `'W' is not a member of union 'Widget | Other'`. `_resolve_pattern_type` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) mints the pattern's NominalType with the source spelling (`name="W"`) while the union member carries the canonical name (`name="Widget"`), so the exact-member match (`m == resolved`, `NominalType.__eq__` includes `name`) and the same-bare-name membership check both fail on the alias. Concrete (non-union) subjects work -- they compare the resolved record's qname, not the union-membership path. Pre-existing on `master` (independent of the class-pattern-identity fix; that fix preserved this branch's condition verbatim). Rejects-valid. Workaround: import the record under its own name, or match on a concrete (non-union) subject. Fix shape: resolve the pattern name to its canonical record and mint the NominalType with the canonical name (or match union members by qname), so the alias spelling doesn't defeat membership. Surfaced during `/tpy-review` of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity` while adding a union happy-path test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `match` class-pattern against a union can still bind a wrong same-named *generic* record via the base-name fuzzy fallback.** `_resolve_pattern_type` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) now rejects a wrong same-named record when all same-bare-named union members are non-parameterized, but when a same-bare-named member IS parameterized (e.g. `Box[str]`) the gate falls through to the pre-existing base-name fuzzy path, which -- for a single cross-module same-named generic member (`len(matches) == 1`) -- binds the pattern's fields against that member without a qname identity check. So `match u: case Box(...)` where `u: mod_b.Box[int32]` and the source-scope `Box` resolves to a distinct `mod_a.Box` can bind the wrong record. Narrow (needs two same-canonical-named generic records across modules, one aliased/in the union); NOT introduced by the class-pattern-identity fix -- that fix strictly added rejections and left this parameterized path unchanged from master. Fix shape: in the fuzzy fallback, require qname identity for a concrete (non-type-arg-ambiguous) pattern before binding, mirroring the non-parameterized gate. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (safety-model, architecture-fit, cpython-parity) of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `min()`/`max()` reject record operands that define the full comparison surface.** `max(date(2021, 1, 1), date(2020, 5, 5))` -> "No matching overload for max(date, date)" even though `date` (dataclass `order=True` and hand-written dunders alike) supports `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`/`==`. The min/max builtin overload set has no comparable-record arm, so every user value type is rejected. Rejects-valid, loud. Workaround: spell the comparison (`a if a >= b else b`). Affects all datetime types (date/time/datetime/timedelta). Fix shape: a protocol-bound generic overload (`min/max[T: Comparable]`) or routing through the comparable check `sorted()` uses. Surfaced by datetime v2 tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An explicit `bool(x)` call on a user value type without `__bool__` is rejected even though the implicit truthiness context works.** `t = time(14, 30); bool(t)` errors ("bool() cannot convert time") while `if t:` / `print(not not t)`-style truthiness correctly treats it as always-truthy (matching CPython's default object truthiness, e.g. time/date/datetime are always truthy since 3.5). The truthiness lowering has a default arm the `bool()` builtin overload set lacks. Rejects-valid, loud, generic (not datetime-specific). Workaround: use the value in a boolean context instead of calling `bool()`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of datetime v2. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (parity, silent wrong output) `abs()` of a BigInt EXPRESSION goes through `double`, so the result loses precision past 2^53 and prints as a float.** [`abs-bigint-expression-via-double`] `print(abs(-(2**40) - 1))` emits `::tpy::print_float(::std::fabs(static_cast<double>(...)))` and prints `1099511627777.0` where CPython prints `1099511627777` -- the value happens to survive at this magnitude, but the type does not, and past 2^53 the value does not either. A NAME-bound BigInt takes the correct arm: `n = -(2**40) - 1; print(abs(n))` emits `::tpy::BigInt::abs(n)` and prints the exact integer, so the two spellings of one expression disagree. Identical on both codegen authors, so this is not a migration artifact and the byte-diff cannot see it. The `abs` overload evidently resolves against a float arm when the argument is an unresolved arithmetic expression rather than a typed name -- the same unchecked float<->fixed-int family as the `round(huge_float)` entry below, but here the wrong arm is chosen at OVERLOAD RESOLUTION rather than inside the cast. Repro: `print(abs(-(2**40) - 1))` under plain `uv run tpy`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity) `round(huge_float)` in a bare (default-int) context silently wraps instead of overflowing.** `r = round(1751551805.5 * 1000000)` with no typed target resolves `round[T]` to the default int32, and `round_to<int32_t>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/builtins.hpp`) does an unchecked `static_cast<T>(std::nearbyint(x))` -> `-2147483648`, where CPython returns the exact int. With an `int`-typed target (`us: int = round(...)`) the BigInt arm is exact and correct. Silent wrong value in the bare case (same unchecked float->fixed-int cast family as `float(huge_int)` -> inf above, opposite direction). Fix shape: `round_to<T>` range-checks before the cast and raises `OverflowError`, or bare-context `round` defaults to BigInt. Surfaced probing datetime v2's `fromtimestamp`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED] A class-typed local alias in a resumable (suspending) `async def` follows its SOURCE variable's reassignment instead of preserving object identity -- silent CPython divergence.** `p = w; w = Counter(999)` inside an async def that suspends: TPy reads the NEW instance through `p` (prints 999) where CPython preserves identity. The alias is frame-promoted to a slot that re-reads the source's storage rather than pinning the aliased object. General to resumable frames -- NOT coroutine-handle-specific (reproduces with plain class locals; predates the bound-coroutines feature) and NOT async-specific: an ordinary two-yield generator takes the same frame path, and there the frame is worse than sync -- `p = Point(11); while i < n: alias = p; p = Point(i); yield alias.x` yields `0 1 2` where CPython yields `11 0 1`, losing even the first generation (the sync sibling gets generation 0 right). Sync bodies are NOT correct here either, contrary to what this entry previously claimed: their separate rebind slot covers exactly ONE generation, so a loop rebind clobbers from the second iteration on -- the same single-slot-reuse root cause as the sync entry above. Probes `/tmp/agents/narrow/gen_trace.py`, `plain_trace.py`. Also underlies the bound-method-coroutine receiver capture: `w = Counter(40); c = w.bump(5); w = Counter(999); await c` silently reads the reassigned receiver. Silent wrong-value divergence, the top-priority parity class. Repro: /tmp/agents/coro/general_alias_reassign_async.py (from /tpy-review of the bound-coroutines zero-alloc round, cpython-parity specialist). Fix shape: frame-promoted alias slots must pin the aliased OBJECT at bind time, not re-derive through the source slot -- align with the sync pointer-local model. DISPOSITION (bound-coroutines /tpy-ready): the feature's receiver-borrow guarantee knowingly ships with this hole (rebinding the receiver between bind and consume reads the new object through the handle); an owning MOVE of the receiver is caught (demoted to copy+warn, test async_bind_receiver_moved), reassignment is not -- a conservative rebind-while-borrowed guard symmetric with the move demotion is a design option deferred to this fix. No committed test pins the rebind divergence (it would pin wrong output); repro above. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `.cancel()` is callable on a bare coroutine value (not just Tasks) -- CPython raises AttributeError.** Every async-def call result conforms to `Cancellable[T]`, so `f().cancel()` (or `c.cancel()` on a bound handle) type-checks and compiles; CPython's coroutine objects have no `.cancel` (only Tasks do) and raise AttributeError at the same line. Pre-existing conflation (the TPy async model deliberately unifies coro/task cancellation via `Cancellable`), but bound-coroutine handles make it reachable through a named value -- and a `c.cancel()` read also clears the "never consumed" warning (see the bound-coroutines TODO exclusions entry), so the coroutine silently never runs with zero diagnostics where CPython fails loudly. Crash-direction divergence (TPy accepts a superset). Fix shape: either hide `cancel` from the user-facing surface of a *bare* coroutine value (accept it only where an owned handle is spawned/driven), or document the widened surface as a declared divergence and exclude `.cancel` reads from clearing the unconsumed warning. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the bound-coroutines feature. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An `Own[@dynamic P]` value passed to a *structural*-protocol param mis-templates -- the `unique_ptr<P>` is passed as the template arg instead of the pointee.** `poll_once(aw)` / any `Awaitable[T]`-typed structural consumer receiving an `Own[Cancellable[T]]` value emits `poll_once<T>(handle)` where the deduced param is `std::unique_ptr<Cancellable<T>>`, failing the C++20 concept check (no `__poll__` on unique_ptr). Pre-existing (repros on master via an explicit `Own[Cancellable[T]]` param forwarded to `poll_once`). For coroutine handles specifically this is now unreachable -- the bound-coroutines borrow rejection ("cannot borrow a coroutine handle into argument ...") fires first with a clean sema error -- but other `Own[@dynamic P]` sources (non-Cancellable protocols) still reach the broken emission. Fix shape: the structural-protocol arg path should deref an owned-erased source (`*handle`) like the @dynamic borrow path does, or reject with the same clean diagnostic. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the bound-coroutines feature. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The str-family respell in `gen_c_params` is dead code that reactivates silently if the C-ABI gate ever widens.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` `gen_c_params` still maps `is_any_str_type(ptype)` to `const char*`, which is the exact machinery behind the (now-closed) HIGH silent wrong-code bug: the signature respelled to `const char*` while the body rendered against `std::string_view`, so `s == "hello"` compared pointers. It is unreachable today only because sema rejects str-family types at a C-linkage signature -- and the THIR fence (`sig.linkage_c_abi`) that used to be the second line of defence was deleted as part of that same change. So the arm is untested, unreferenced, and one gate widening away from being live again with no backstop. Fix shape: delete the arm (the gate makes it unreachable, and if str ever crosses a C boundary again it will be through the marshaling-wrapper design, which owns its own conversion), or keep it and add a unit asserting the sema gate makes it unreachable. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT) A `Ptr[T]`-returning `unsafe_` primitive borrows from a TEMPORARY argument with no diagnostic, so the pointer dangles before its first use.** `Ptr[T]` carries no lifetime facts and the borrow checker has no visibility into an `unsafe_` call's return, so whenever the argument is a temporary rather than a caller-owned lvalue the returned pointer is dead on arrival. Three confirmed faces, all silent, all producing garbage at runtime: `p = unsafe_ptr(s + "x")` (the concat's `std::string` dies at the end of the statement -- PRE-EXISTING on master, independent of any `unsafe_cstr` work); `p = unsafe_cstr("literal")` and `p = unsafe_cstr(v)` for a `str`/`StrView`-typed `v` (the `str -> String` conversion materializes a temporary bound to the helper's `const std::string&`). Consuming the pointer inside the SAME full-expression is safe and is the intended spelling (`c_fn(unsafe_cstr(name))`), so the hazard is specifically binding the result to a name, returning it, or storing it in a field. A held pointer is also invalidated if the owning `String` is later mutated or reallocated -- the ordinary `std::string::c_str()` caveat. Not specific to any one primitive: it is the untracked-`Ptr`-borrow property of the family, and `unsafe_` is the documented escape-hatch namespace, so the question is diagnosis rather than prohibition. **Fix shape:** region/lifetime tracking that reaches `Ptr[T]` returns is the real answer and is IR-gated (same territory as the async borrow-escape work); the available-now narrower option is a diagnostic when a borrow-returning `unsafe_` call's argument is a temporary AND the result is bound to a name rather than consumed in place. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/cabi-str/dang1.py`, `dang4.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + cpython-parity + safety-model) of the C-ABI type gate. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A module whose name is a C++ keyword emits an unusable namespace.** `inline.py` emits `namespace tpyapp::inline { ... }` and every reference to it (`::tpyapp::inline::__tpy_init()`), which g++ rejects -- the module name is pasted into the namespace without checking it against the C++ keyword set. Any Python-legal module name that is also a C++ keyword hits this (`inline`, `template`, `typename`, `new`, `delete`, `union`, `register`, ...). Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error at the first build), not silent, and the diagnostic points at generated code rather than at the filename, so the cause is not obvious from the message. Fix shape: `module_to_cpp_namespace` should mangle a reserved identifier the way `escape_cpp_name` already does for user identifiers -- the escaping helper exists, it is simply not applied to the module-name path. Surfaced while probing `unsafe_cstr` lifetimes during the C-ABI type gate review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `@cpp_template` that splices `{N}` as a receiver emits ill-formed C++ for a literal argument, and borrows from a dying temporary for a converted one.** `@cpp_template` substitutes the argument's *rendered text*, so `{0}.data()` / `{0}.c_str()` only work when the argument happens to render as an lvalue of the expected C++ type. `unsafe_ptr("literal")` emits `"literal".data()` -- `const char[8]` has no `.data()`, g++ rejects it; the same shape on any of the four `unsafe_ptr` overloads (`str`/`Array`/`list`/`bytes`) behaves the same way. The converted-argument face is worse than a build error: when sema inserts a coercion the template lands on the temporary (`std::string(s).data()`), so the returned pointer borrows a buffer that dies with the full-expression, silently. Toolchain-caught for literals, SILENT for coercions. Fix shape: a template whose placeholder is spliced in receiver position must either materialize the argument into a named temp (the `create-lend-drop` arm in `sema/calls.py` already does this for `Own[...]` rvalues lent to borrow params) or reject a non-lvalue argument; the alternative, used for `tpy.unsafe.unsafe_cstr`, is to declare the stub `@native` against a real C++ helper so the parameter applies the standard conversion instead of a text splice. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + safety-model) of the C-ABI type gate, where `unsafe_cstr` was converted away from `@cpp_template` for exactly this reason. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Slicing a readonly(-deduced) `list` param types the result `Span[T]` (mutable) -> ill-formed C++ (`span<const T>` does not convert to `span<T>`), no TPy diagnostic.** `def mid(items: list[int32], sl: basic_slice) -> int32: s = items[sl]; return s[0]` -- a read-only body const-deduces `items` (`const std::vector<int32_t>&`), so `::tpy::list_slice(items, sl)` returns `std::span<const int32_t>`, but sema types `items[sl]` as `Span[int32]` (an explicit `s: Span[int32]` annotation is accepted too), so the local declares `std::span<int32_t>` and g++ rejects the conversion. Same root family as the readonly-deduced `Own[Span[T] | list[T]]` return entry below (deduced receiver const-ness not propagated into the sliced Span's element); this is the plain-local face. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: force the param mutable (e.g. the append/pop pair in tests/cases/operators/slice_var_index), or index elements directly. Surfaced drafting the THIR slice-ctor-call-arg corpus case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `String`-annotated binding from a view-form `str` source emits ill-formed C++ (`std::string m = s;` copy-init from a `std::string_view`).** `def f(s: str) -> None: m: String = s` -- sema inserts the `str_to_string` coercion (INIT context), whose codegen lambda is identity everywhere outside ARG, so codegen emits `std::string m = s;`; `std::string`'s `string_view` constructor is explicit, so the copy-initialization is ill-formed and g++ rejects it. The same identity arm covers ASSIGN and RETURN, so any non-ARG `str_to_string` over a VIEW source (a `str` param, a `StrView`-resolved local) miscompiles; an OWNED source (`String` value, owned str local) is fine (plain copy ctor). Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: keep the binding as `str`, or go through an explicitly-materializing source (a slice -- `strview_to_string` always wraps). Fix shape: the non-ARG identity must materialize for view-form sources; the coercion lambda cannot see the source's C++ form, so the fix belongs at the `_view_source_to_owned` chokepoint (the same one a plain `t: str = <view>` decl-init uses), not in the lambda. NB the THIR incr-42 coercion cell mirrors this emit byte-identically (`test_string_init_identity_mirrors_ast_miscompile` pins it); when the AST arm is fixed, the byte-diff + pin flag the THIR lockstep update. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_string_init.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the THIR incr 42-45 branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Reusing a `with` as-target name whose binding is a VALUE (or value-repr Optional) slot is a hard compile error -- `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.with)`.** Two faces, both refused: (1) two `with` blocks reusing a value-typed target (`with V() as x: ...` twice, `__enter__ -> int32`); (2) a value-repr Optional slot (`x: int32 | None = None`, then `with V() as x:` in a branch). A SINGLE `with V() as x:` over the same value `__enter__` compiles, so the REUSE is the trigger. `_with_target_arm` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` classifies an already-declared target and returns None for every reuse that is not a same-record pointer-local (`ASSIGN_PTR`) or a hoist-predeclared optional-record slot (`ASSIGN_OPT`); the `if arm_et is None` guard at its caller raises. The RECORD reuse family still routes (`T* g = &(enter())` then `g = &(enter())`). This supersedes the older symptom -- the ill-formed `x = &(__ctx_N.__enter__());` (value slot assigned a pointer, address-of an rvalue) -- which no longer has an emitter: the mis-render is gone and the shape is refused instead. Exotic (one as-name reused across two `with` blocks); workaround: use distinct as-names per `with`. Fix shape: add a VALUE already-declared arm (`x = enter();` for a plain value slot, the same assign for a value-repr Optional slot), or reject the value-target reuse in sema with a clear message. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Mutating a `String` param (e.g. `name += "!"` in an `__init__` body) emits the mutation against the untouched `const std::string&` param -- ill-formed C++.** Sema accepts the aug-assign and records the param in `mutated_params`, but the emitted signature stays `const std::string&` and the body writes through it (`name += "!";` / `name = ...;` on the const ref), so g++ rejects every such body. Same missing owned-copy/mutable-binding family as the str/bytes aug-assign prologue entry below, on the `String` (owned, const-ref-param) face. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: copy to a local first (`s = name + "!"`). Fix shape: a mutated `String` param must either lower `std::string&` (and callers adapt per `ctor_mutated`) or take the reassigned-param copy prologue; pick whichever matches the existing `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` model. NB the THIR ctor-arg check rejects mutated-String ctor slots (`_record_ctor_arg_supported`), so no THIR mirror exists to update. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/thir_with_tail/ctor_str5.py`. Surfaced probing the THIR str-arg ctor-slot cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ctor param needing the reassigned-copy prologue emits `T name = __param_name;` against a ctor signature that never applies the `__param_` rename -- ill-formed C++ (undeclared identifier + param shadowing).** `def __init__(self, s: str, v: int32): self.tag = s; if v > 0: s = "pos"` (any owned str/bytes/String/BigInt param reassigned in a ctor body): gen_body emits the owned-copy prologue local `std::string s = std::string(__param_s);`, but the CTOR signature path (records.py `gen_params`) passes no `reassigned_params` -- unlike gen_function -- so the param keeps its source name and `__param_s` is undeclared; g++ rejects. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: bind to a differently-named local instead of reassigning the param. Fix shape: thread `reassigned_params` into the ctor signature emit exactly like gen_function's (same missing owned-copy/mutable-binding family as the mutated-String entry above). NB the THIR ctor gate rejects the shape (`ctor.param_reassign_copy`), so no THIR mirror exists to update. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/ctor_wave/params/probe_reassign.py`, `/tmp/agents/ctor_wave/body/probe_fw6.py`. Found independently by three THIR ctor-frontier cells. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[T]` param forwarded to a base initializer emits the bare name against the base's `T&&` ctor slot -- invalid C++.** `super().__init__(q)` with `q: Own[Payload]` renders `inline Derived::Derived(Payload&& q, int32_t tag) : Base(q), tag(tag) {}` against `explicit Base(Payload&& q)` -> g++ "cannot bind rvalue reference of type 'Payload&&' to lvalue of type 'Payload'". `_lower_base_init_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py:2196`) lowers the arg through a target-less `_lower_expr` with no move arm, so the owned value is neither moved nor bindable. Filed originally as a perf-only missed move; with the base ctor spelling its `Own` param `T&&` it is a hard build error, so the kind is upgraded. Fix shape: apply the ownership-transfer move at the base-init arg sink the way the ordinary call-arg path does. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_497_own_base_init.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ctor param mutated only through a FREE-function call renders the call-site rvalue arg inline against the `A&` slot -- ill-formed C++ (prvalue bound to a non-const lvalue ref).** `class Sink: def __init__(self, a: A): mut(a); self.c = a.x` with `def mut(a: A): a.x += 1`, called `Sink(A(1))`: Phase-2 mutation propagation updates the REAL `__init__` FunctionInfo (the emitted signature is `Sink(A& a)`), but the call site's `ctor_mut` reads the SYNTHETIC constructor fi -- built by `_set_record_constructor_info` in `tpyc/sema/calls.py`, which COPIES `resolved_ctor.mutated_params` at resolution time and is never refreshed by the fixpoint -- so the mutated-slot rvalue-temp row never fires and `Sink s = Sink(A(1));` is emitted inline instead of hoisting `A __tmp = A(1);`. Direct method mutation in the ctor body (`a.bump()`) lands on the synthetic fi and works. Toolchain-caught (g++: "cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'A&' to an rvalue"), not silent. Workaround: bind the arg to a local first (`a = A(1); Sink(a)`), or mutate via a method call in `__init__`. Site: `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` -- the record-ctor arm of `_lower_expr` and `_lower_ctor_call_args` (which now serves the `raise X(args)` path too) both read `ctor_mut = fi.mutated_params` off that synthetic fi. Fix shape: refresh the synthetic ctor fi's `mutated_params` in the Phase-2 fixpoint, or have both reads go through `canonical_fi.mutated_params` (the synthetic fi already carries `canonical_fi=ctor.root`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Reassigning a pointer-repr tuple PARAM emits the assignment against the `const std::tuple<..., const T*>&` parameter -- ill-formed C++.** `def use(t: tuple[Rec, int32]) -> ...: t = (a, 5)` -- the signature renders the const borrow-tuple reference while the body emits the bare reseat (`t = ::tpy::tuple_to_storage<...>(...);`) against it; no viable `operator=`, g++ rejects. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: bind to a fresh local instead of reassigning the param. Fix shape: a reassigned borrow-tuple param needs the mutable-binding / copy-prologue family treatment (same missing-owned-copy class as the mutated-String and aug-assign param entries). NB THIR's borrow-tuple reseat dispatch EXCLUDES params (whole-body fallback, `_borrow_tuple_local_type` gate in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`), so no THIR mirror exists to update -- when the AST arm is fixed, widen that gate in lockstep. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/meta_w1/main.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + meta) of the wave-5 borrow-tuple cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `::tpy::String` FIELD written from a str LOCAL emits invalid C++ (`::tpy::String` hides `std::string::operator=(string_view)`).** `s.name = v` with `name: String` and `v` a str local (a `std::string_view`) emits `s.name = v;`, and `::tpy::String` declares only its copy/move `operator=`, so the conversion that keeps plain `str` immune is hidden. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: `s.name = String(v)`. Fix shape: route the field write through the family's view->owned bridge -- `_wrap_view_owned_sink` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), the single chokepoint for the view->owned copy, which the owned-`bytes` local reassign goes through at its name-reassign arm in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`. The `bytes` face of this entry is closed by that arm; only the `String` field write is left. Probe `/tmp/agents/bug_any/p/c_precedent.py`, found 2026-09-13.
- **[MED small] Aug-assign on a `str` param skips the owned-copy prologue and emits `+=` on the untouched `std::string_view` param -> hard C++ error; the `bytes` face of the same root is a SILENT dangling span.** `def f(a: str) -> str: a += "x"; return a` emits `a += "x";` against the `std::string_view a` parameter (no `operator+=`) -- g++ rejects it. Root: the reassigned-param owned-copy prologue (`param_needs_copy_for_reassign` -> `std::string __param_a` rename + mutable local) keys on `scan.reassigned`, but the prescan records aug-assign targets in `scan.aug_assigned` only, so the prologue never fires for a param whose ONLY mutation is `+=`. A param that is also plainly reassigned (`a = a + "x"`) gets the prologue and compiles. The str face is toolchain-caught (won't compile), but the BYTES face is silent UB: `def f(a: bytes) -> bytes: a += b; return a` emits `a = ::tpy::bytes_concat(a, b);` on the untouched `::tpy::BytesView` param -- the span's range constructor accepts the rvalue `std::vector<uint8_t>` (const element type), so it COMPILES and rebinds the span to the concat's dying temporary; every later read of `a` is use-after-free with no diagnostic. Pre-existing on `master`; reproduces without `--thir-codegen` (the THIR S3/incr-46 cells gate both faces out rather than reproducing them). Workaround: `a = a + "x"`, or copy to a local first. Fix shape: include `aug_assigned` names in the `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` prologue/signature checks (functions.py, statements.py, param_const.py read `scan.reassigned` for it) -- one fix covers both faces. Surfaced by the THIR S3 str-concat cell's param-exclusion probe; the bytes face by the incr-46 bytes-tail cell's aug-assign probe (`aug` in `/tmp/agents/probe_bytes_concat.py`). The `int` (BigInt) face is confirmed too: `def f(n: int) -> int: while n > 0: n -= 1` emits `n = (n) - ...;` against the `const ::tpy::BigInt&` param -- toolchain-caught like the str face (probe `/tmp/agents/while-temp/probe_param.py`, surfaced by the while-condition temp fix's probes). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `float(huge_int)` and BigInt-to-double conversions silently produce `inf` where CPython raises `OverflowError`.** `BigInt::to_double()` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/bigint.hpp`) returns `HUGE_VAL` via `strtod` for values beyond double range (e.g. `float(10**400)`), and every implicit int-to-float widening site (mixed `int`-with-`float` arithmetic, float ctor) inherits that, whereas CPython raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`. Silent value divergence, but only for astronomically large ints. (int/int true division no longer goes through this path -- its dedicated `truediv` overloads raise `OverflowError` correctly.) Fix shape: `to_double()` raises `OverflowError` when the magnitude exceeds double range; audit callers that intentionally want saturation, if any. Surfaced while fixing the int/int correctly-rounded-division bug. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An oversized `-> int` (BigInt) `__len__` panics UNCATCHABLY where CPython raises a catchable `OverflowError`.** `class Huge: def __len__(self) -> int: return 10 ** 30` then `len(Huge())` (or truthiness `if Huge():`) -- the BigInt `__len__` template in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp` narrows via `x.__len__().to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`, and `to_fixed_check` routes out-of-int32 magnitudes through `raise_fixedint_overflow` -> `tpy_panic` (`core.hpp:356`), an UNCATCHABLE panic ("int32 overflow: value out of range"), whereas CPython raises a catchable `OverflowError: cannot fit 'int' into an index-sized integer`. So `try: len(Huge()) except OverflowError:` never catches in TPy. Only for astronomically large `__len__` results (>= 2^31). The negative-`__len__` -> `ValueError` guard directly above the narrow is fine (fits int32, catchable); only the oversized branch diverges. Sibling of the `float(huge_int)` -> `inf` OverflowError entry above (same "should be catchable OverflowError, isn't" family). Fix shape: the `len()`/`__len__` oversized branch should raise a catchable `::tpy::raise<OverflowError>(...)` (CPython's index-size message) instead of `to_fixed_check`'s panic -- either a dedicated checked narrow in the `__len__` template or a `to_index_checked`-style extractor. Surfaced by `/tpy-next` while fixing the negative-`__len__` `ValueError` gap. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An operator inside a generic function does not dispatch through the type param's protocol bound.** `def combine[T: Addable](a: T, b: T) -> T: return a + b` errors `Invalid operand types for '+': Ref[T] and Ref[T]` even though the `Addable` bound requires `__add__`. The protocol-operand arm in `sema/expressions.py` (`is_protocol_type` -> `lookup_protocol_method_return`) handles protocol-TYPED operands but not `Ref[TypeParamRef]` operands whose bound is a protocol. Rejects-valid. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro.py`. Surfaced while fixing the self-referential-protocol recursion crash. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Operator dunders on a `@dynamic` protocol value do not dispatch.** `c // 2` where `c: Counter` (`@dynamic` protocol requiring `__floordiv__(self, other: int) -> int`) errors `Invalid operand types for '//': Counter and IntLiteral(2)`; same for other operators. The @dynamic Adapter forwards named methods but the binop resolution path never consults the protocol's dunders for a @dynamic-typed operand (the structural monomorphized path does). Rejects-valid; the `@dynamic`-protocol-with-operator-dunder surface is effectively unimplemented -- routing it likely needs `/tpy-add-feature` rather than a spot fix. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro5.py`. Needs triage.
- **[LOW small] A protocol method returning `Own[Self]` does not match a conformer returning plain `Self`-equivalent.** Protocol `__add__(self, other: Self) -> Own[Self]` vs `Meters.__add__(other: Meters) -> Meters` (a `ValueType`) -> "does not conform": `_protocol_type_matches` unwraps `Own` on the ACTUAL side only, so expected `Own[Meters]` never matches actual `Meters`, though for a value type the two describe the same by-value return. Rejects-valid. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro4.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A union-typed operand on a binary operator is accepted by sema but cannot be built in C++.** `a + u` where `u: A | B` and `A` defines a monomorphic `__add__(self, other: A) -> ...` compiles in sema (the union operand is not checked against the operator's param type) but fails the C++ build: `operator+(A, variant<A, B>)` matches no overload. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/dt_probe/mono_union.py` (also reachable via an `@overload` operator's union impl-signature, though that path's spurious operator was removed in the datetime v0 fix). Consequence: a genuine union operand on any operator is a sema-accepts / codegen-fails hole. Pre-existing, independent of `@overload`. The COMPARISON form reproduces the same class on value unions: `a == k` where `a: int32 | float64` and `k: int32` emits the bare `(a == k)` -> `variant<int32_t, double> == int32_t` matches no `operator==` (same-type union compares work -- `std::variant` compares to itself). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_union_value3.py` (the `c()` shape). Fix shape: either sema rejects a union operand on an operator (require the user to narrow first -- consistent with TPy's narrow-before-use rule), or codegen `std::visit`-dispatches the operand to the matching concrete operator. The narrow-first rejection is the cleaner static-language fit. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Surfaced during datetime v0 (`docs/DATETIME_DESIGN.md`); the comparison form by the THIR F4 U1 probes. datetime v4 raised this class's exposure: `dt.tzinfo == tz` is now a natural user spelling (`.tzinfo` returns `timezone | ZoneInfo | None`) and hits the `==` form; TPy code narrows via isinstance first (see timezone.fromutc).
- **[MED small] A storage-form union value (a `variant<A, B>` field) at a borrow position is not bridged with `to_ptr_variant` -- one live miscompile, three hard rejects, one now caught by sema.** One root cause: the union storage->borrow conversion fires at the local-decl site but is missing at the other borrow sinks. **LIVE (4) const-blind member lift**: the pointer-variant arg lift ignores the SOURCE's const verdict -- a `const A&` param, a const loop var, or a readonly method's `self` passed as a member arg into a mutable `A | B` slot emits `std::variant<A*, B*>{&(a)}` where `&(a)` is `const A*` (g++: `no matching function for call to 'std::variant<A*, B*>::variant'`). The variant spelling is fixed at lowering from the SLOT's deep-const verdict alone (`_arg_ptr_union_slot` and the `THIRUnionArgLift` construction, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:14764-14840`) and rendered source-blind by `_emit_union_arg_lift` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:838`); the narrowed-subject face (a bare `const`-extracted alias into a mutable variant slot) hits the same wall. **REJECT (1) return**: `def r(h: H) -> A | B: return h.u` fails codegen with `(stmt.return)`. **REJECT (2) call arg**: `take(h.u)` fails with `(stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.union)`. **REJECT (5) `@error_return` unwrap into a ptr-variant local**: `x: A | B = A(1)` then `x = f(...)` where `f` is `@error_return` returning `Own[A | B]` fails with `(stmt.var_decl:error_return.bind_target)` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3352`); this is also the only shape that reaches that sink's pointer-local guard, so it blocks a regression test for the guard until fixed. **RESOLVED (3) const mismatch**: a const-lifted local off a readonly receiver passed to a mutable-pointee slot is now a sema error (`Cannot pass readonly[A | B] as mutable A | B in argument 'u'`) -- the loud rejection this entry asked for, no codegen change needed. All faces are loud, none silent. Fix shape: route the return, call-arg and `@error_return`-bind borrow sinks through the same union conversion the local decl uses, and make the arg lift consult the SOURCE's const verdict (or have sema infer the param const) for face (4). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_508a_union_return.py` through `02_508e_union_er_bind.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `self.u = v` in a ctor with `v: Own[A | B]` warns "copies A | B into field; use copy()" although the emitted member-init-list MOVES (`u(std::move(v))`) -- a false-positive copy warning.** [`own-union-field-store-copy-warning`] The Own-param move is the intended zero-copy path, but the field-assign copy warning does not recognize the ctor MIL move for union-typed fields (the plain-record Own-param MIL assign does not warn). Several committed union cases carry the spurious line in their `diag.txt`. No behavioral impact; diagnostics quality only. Fix shape: suppress the copy warning when the source is an `Own[...]` param at its last use feeding the MIL move (mirror the record-field arm's verdict). Surfaced by the THIR incr-57 corpus case (`callarg_own_ctor`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] char-slot literal arguments are sema-accepted for free functions but sema-rejected for methods and constructors.** `take('a')` into `def take(c: char)` compiles (the target-typed char-literal render), but the same literal into a method (`p.set('q')`) or constructor (`P('a')`) char param is a sema type error -- the literal-into-char coercion only fires on the free-function call path. Inconsistent sema surface; reject-valid (loud), no miscompile. Workaround: bind the literal to a `char` local first. Surfaced by the THIR incr-47 char-field probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An assign-narrowed union local read at a member-typed sink renders the bare variant name (no `std::get`) -> hard C++ error, in BOTH variant forms.** [`assign-narrowed-union-read`] `def m(k: int32): x: int32 | float64 = k; v = x` -- the member-source decl narrows `x` to `int32`, so `v` infers `int32`, but codegen renders the read as the bare name: `int32_t v = x;` where `x` is `std::variant<int32_t, double>` -- no conversion exists. The extraction the narrowed read needs (`std::get<int32_t>(x)`) is never emitted at the decl-init sink (the isinstance-narrowing extraction sites in `expressions.py`/`match.py` don't cover assignment-narrowed bare-name reads). Sibling of the narrowed-union match-capture entry (BUGS.md#match-capture-union-subject) -- same root, different sink; toolchain-caught, not silent. **The POINTER-variant flavor reaches this same decl sink**, so the split between the two entries is which SINK, not which variant form: `tmp: A | B = B(3)` then `other = tmp` narrows `tmp` to `B` off its initializer and emits `B other = std::move(tmp);` against a `std::variant<A*, B*>` -- g++ `conversion from 'std::variant<A*, B*>' to non-scalar type 'B' requested`. Reading the narrowed local DIRECTLY is fine (`(*std::get<B*>(tmp)).y`) and the isinstance route is fine (it has an extraction alias `__v`), so the local-to-local bind is the whole gap. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_union_narrowlocal.py` (value variant) and `/tmp/agents/unionalias/main.py` (pointer variant). Workaround: re-annotate the local (`v: int32 | float64 = x`) or avoid the member-typed re-read. Fix shape: an assign-narrowed union name read at a member-typed sink must extract (`std::get<M>`) like the isinstance-narrowed sites do -- or sema should not narrow across a variant storage boundary it cannot render. NB the THIR F4 U1 gate rejects any narrowing-divergent union read (`_union_binding_divergent`), so THIR neither routes nor mirrors the shape -- verified for both faces (the pointer-variant repro falls back with `stmt.var_decl:name.union_binding_divergent`). Surfaced by the THIR F4 U1 probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `Send[Own[T]] | None` is not recognized as an owned (movable) param.** The `Send`/`Sync` marker distributes *inside* the Optional at construction (`Optional[Send[Own[T]]]`, not `Send[Optional[Own[T]]]`), so the owned-param peel `unwrap_optional_own(unwrap_readonly(unwrap_send_sync(ptype)))` sees `Send[Own[T]]` where it expects a bare `OwnType` and returns None -> the param is bound as a borrow instead of moved (a silent copy for a copyable T; a hard C++ error for `@nocopy`). Pre-existing (identical before the marker-peel fix; that fix covers bare `Send[Own[T]]` but not the Optional-wrapped shape). `tpy.thread.spawn`'s param is never Optional, so V1 is unaffected. Fix shape: either peel the marker per-Optional-member, or float the marker outside the Optional so the existing peel reaches it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `Send[Own[ConcreteClass]]` param annotation fails at parse time with "not Send".** `def f(x: Send[Own[Box]])` where `Box` is a user class (even a Send-able one) raises `Parse error: 'Send[Own[Box]]': 'Own[Box]' is not Send`. Only the type-param form `Send[Own[T]]` (deferred to Phase-2) and the `@dynamic`-protocol form `Send[Own[Pet]]` are accepted; a concrete class is Send-checked too early (at parse, before the class's Send-ness is known). Workaround: use a bare `Own[Box]` param, or a generic `Send[Own[T]]`. Rejection-of-valid-code. Surfaced building the `tpy.thread.spawn` regression tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A tuple-typed parameter reassignment is not rejected by sema (unlike a record-typed param), so it emits an assignment against a `const std::tuple<...>&` param -> hard C++ error.** `def f(t: tuple[int32, int32], t2: tuple[int32, int32]): t = t2` emits `t = t2;` where `t` is a `const std::tuple<...>&` parameter, which g++ rejects (assignment to a read-only reference). A record-typed param reassignment is correctly rejected at sema ("Cannot reassign parameter 'x' of type 'Inner'"), but the tuple-typed param (and, presumably, other by-const-ref value aggregates) misses that diagnostic. Toolchain-caught (won't compile), not silent. Pre-existing on `master` -- reproduces without `--thir-codegen`; a pure AST/sema gap, not a THIR issue (the THIR value-scalar tuple subscript-read cell emits byte-identical broken text to the AST path). Workaround: assign to a fresh local instead of the param. Fix shape: extend the "cannot reassign parameter" sema check to tuple-typed (and other by-const-ref) value params, not just record params. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR tuple subscript-read cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A bare `str` (view) argument doesn't auto-coerce into a `bool | str` (or other view-member union) parameter -- needs an explicit `String(...)`.** Calling `f(s)` where `f(verify: bool | str)` and `s` is a `str`/`StrView` fails the C++ build: `invalid initialization of reference of type 'const std::variant<bool, std::string>&' from expression of type 'const std::string_view'`. The view isn't wrapped to the union's owned `std::string` member at the call site. Workaround: `f(String(s))` (owned) compiles. Works once the value is already a `bool | str`-typed local (e.g. a reassignable `verify` local in curl.py), so the gap is specifically a fresh view -> union-param coercion. Same view->owned family as other union-member coercion gaps. Reproducer: `_ssl_context_for(CA_PATH)` in `tplib/requests_verify_context` (worked around with `String(CA_PATH)`). Toolchain-caught, not silent. Surfaced building the Increment 5 verify-context test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The clang-repl JIT backend (`--cxx clang-repl`, opt-in) cannot use modules needing runtime impls or managed third-party libs.** The default CompileBackend now compiles and links the session's build deps (runtime impl sources like os_impl.cpp, bundled third-party sources like PCRE2/Hinnant date, raw link flags) per eval, but the JIT backend has no link step to feed them into -- `import os` / `import re` / `from datetime import datetime` fail with unresolved symbols at JIT time. It accepts and ignores the `ReplBuildDeps` param (documented at the `execute` override). Fix shape: compile the support set to a shared object and load it into the interpreter (clang-repl `%lib`), or emit a clean "unsupported in the JIT backend, use the default backend" diagnostic when deps are non-empty. Split from the fixed CompileBackend link gap by `/tpy-fix-bug` (fix-repl-managed-libs). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED] `--mbedtls=bundled` via the CMake-emit path (`tpyc -o`) fails to link `mbedtls_shim.c` and `cacert_data.c`.** The vendored `runtime/cpp/third_party/mbedtls/CMakeLists.txt` shim (generated by `scripts/vendor_mbedtls.py`) globs only `library/*.c`, so the TPy-owned glue `runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/mbedtls_shim.c` and the CA-bundle blob `runtime/cpp/third_party/cacert/cacert_data.c` are never compiled in CMake mode -> undefined references to `tpy_tls_*` / `tpy_cacert_pem` at link. The direct-compile path (default; what `tpy file.py`, `tpyc -b`, and the test suite use) compiles both via `tpyc/build/mbedtls.py::_source_files` and works. Pre-existing for `mbedtls_shim.c` (since ssl Increment 2); the CA-bundle change adds a second file into the same untested CMake blind spot.
