- **[LOW small] A list literal does not coerce to an `Iterable[T]` (generic protocol) parameter: `f(["a", "b"])` where the param is `Iterable[T]` fails the C++ build.** `c.add_all(["a", "b"])` where `add_all(self, items: Iterable[T])` errors `no matching function ... add_all(<brace-enclosed initializer list>)`. The literal isn't materialized into a concrete `list[T]` (then matched against `Iterable[T]`) at the call boundary. Workaround: bind to a local first (`xs: list[str] = [...]; c.add_all(xs)`). Sibling of the literal-into-`Optional[list]` gap below (collection-literal contextual coercion not firing for a wrapper/protocol target). Surfaced building `collections.Counter`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A collection literal does not coerce to an `Optional` collection param: `f(["a", "b"])` where the param is `list[str] | None` fails the C++ build.** `csv.DictReader(fp, ["name", "age"])` (param `fieldnames: Own[list[str]] | None = None`) emits a brace-init `{...}` that g++ can't convert to `std::optional<std::vector<std::string>>` ("no known conversion from <brace-enclosed initializer list>"). A plain `list[str]` param takes the literal fine (`DictWriter(out, ["name","age"])` works) -- only the `| None` wrapper breaks it. Workaround: bind the literal to a local first (`fn: list[str] = [...]; DictReader(fp, fn)`). Root: the list-literal materialization targets the bare element type, not the `optional<vector>` storage, so the brace-init is ambiguous. Likely the same family as the dict/set-literal contextual-coercion gap (a plain concrete target hits the peer-unify branch); here the target is `Optional[list]`. Fix: route a collection literal whose expected type is `Optional[C]` through the same materialize-into-`C` path, then lift to the optional. Surfaced building `csv.DictReader`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An `async def` returning a tuple built from named owned (`@nocopy`/`Own`) locals COPIES the elements instead of moving them -- C++ build error.** `async def f() -> tuple[Own[A], Own[B]]: ...; a = A(...); b = B(...); return (a, b)` emits, in the coro frame, `std::tuple<A, B>{(*a), (*b)}` from the `std::optional<A>`/`std::optional<B>` frame slots (lvalues) with no `std::move`, so g++ fails `use of deleted function A(const A&)` for a `@nocopy` element. The async-return tuple-literal path does not apply last-use move to its frame-slot element locals. Workaround (used in `asyncio.open_connection`): build the tuple from fresh rvalues inline (`return (A(...), B(...))`), which C++ move-constructs. Sync-function tuple returns and the single-element / rvalue cases work; only the async-return tuple of multiple *named* owned locals is broken. Same move-out-of-named-owned-local family as the named-source whole-tuple unpack entry below, different site (async return tuple construction). Toolchain-caught, not silent. Surfaced building the asyncio streams layer (`StreamReader`/`StreamWriter` returned from `open_connection`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `KeyError` from a missing dict key carries the message `"KeyError"` instead of the key value -- `str(e)` is `"KeyError"`, CPython's is `"'absent'"`.** A missing-key read (`d["absent"]`) raises a `KeyError` whose *type* is correct (so `except KeyError` works), but `tpy::__getitem__` for `ordered_map` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp` ~167) calls `raise_key_error("KeyError")` with a fixed string rather than the formatted key. CPython reprs the key (`KeyError: 'absent'`). One-sided: catching works, message-comparing diverges. Same shape as the documented `str(KeyError(k))` gap noted for the builtins dict surface. Fix: format the key into the message (gated on the key type being printable/repr-able). Pre-existing; surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the const-container subscript-read fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (perf) A `with ... as` target whose `__enter__` returns `StrView` gets owning frame storage but its read still carries BORROW form, so a `yield` of it copies an already-owned string.** `with_owning_str_targets` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py:3291`, feeding `FrameLayoutPlan` via `_frame_layout` at `:1183`) gives the target an owning `std::string` frame field, but the yield sink `_wrap_view_owned_sink` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:478`, called from `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`) keys on the lowered value's Form fact, which still says BORROW for that read -- so `yield label` emits `return std::string(label);`, an owned->owned copy. Pinned by `tests/cases/generators/gen_yield_view_from_frame::with_view_target`, so a fix shows up as a snapshot delta. An `__enter__ -> str` target is NOT affected: view deduction promotes it and the read is storage form. The sibling instance -- a `str`/`bytes` PARAM copied into owned frame storage on the way in (`is_owned_in_coro_frame`) -- is already correct, pinned bare by `owned_param_stays_bare` in the same case. This one is really a SYMPTOM of the entry below (the target should not have been promoted to owning storage at all), so fixing that removes it. Fix shape: derive the read's Form fact from `FrameLayoutPlan`, the declared single source of truth for the frame-field form, since the instance is exactly "this field is owning". Note the plan's domain must be WIDENED first -- `_frame_layout` classifies `func.generator_locals` only, and params are classified separately (`_CoroParamKind`), so this is not a drop-in lookup. Pure perf (an owned string copied twice), no wrong output. Surfaced by the /tpy-merge-master check once `FrameLayoutPlan` landed.
- **[LOW small] (perf) A `with ... as` target whose `__enter__` returns a VIEW is promoted to owning frame storage on the strength of its type CATEGORY, not its provenance.** The with-prescan (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` ~2993) adds the target to `with_owning_str_targets` whenever `is_str_category(resolved_enter_t)`, and that category spans `str`, `String`, `StrView` and `FStr`. The rationale in the comment there is specifically the `__enter__ -> str` case, where the C++ signature returns `std::string` BY VALUE and a `string_view` field really would alias a temporary dying at the assignment's semicolon -- owning is required for that one. For `__enter__ -> StrView` the C++ return is already a `std::string_view`, so nothing owns, and whether a view field dangles depends on what it views: `with h as label:` where the frame holds `Holder& h` and `__enter__` returns a view of `self.label` is lifetime-stable, so the copy at `label = (*__with_ctx_0).__enter__();` buys nothing. That lifetime-stability argument holds only for a BORROWED manager, and only because the promotion covers the shape at all: an OWNED (rvalue) manager whose view target skips the promotion has nothing keeping the viewed object alive, which is why the manager is now frame-homed whenever the target's field points into it (`_with_field_points_into_manager`) -- so removing this promotion is safe for the owned case too, but only alongside that homing. Costs one owned-string copy per `__enter__`. It is also the CAUSE of the redundant yield-sink copy in the entry above: the field is owning while the read predicate still calls it a view, so the wrap fires on an already-owned string -- with a correctly-viewed field the wrap would be doing real work instead. Pinned as-is by `generators/gen_yield_view_from_frame::with_view_target`, so a fix surfaces as a snapshot delta. Fix shape: split the promotion by the enter type's C++ ownership -- keep it for the owning returns (`str` / `String`), and route a view return through the source-lifetime question `frame_unsafe_source` already answers for deduced view locals (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`). Same shape-vs-provenance call, and this is the last view-family frame-storage decision still keyed on shape alone. Surfaced by user review of the yield-sink branch's with-target snapshot.
- **[LOW small] `json.dumps((1, 2, 3))` (a tuple) is rejected** -- `tuple` is not a `JsonValue` member, so a tuple argument fails the union match. CPython serializes tuples as JSON arrays. Divergence: idiomatic `json.dumps((a, b))` works in CPython. Resolving it means either adding tuple handling to `JsonValue` / `json.dumps` (tuples are heterogeneous value types -- not a clean union member) or a dedicated tuple->array coercion in the json layer. Surfaced surveying json.dumps input forms. Likely `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[LOW small] `csv.writer(..., doublequote=False)` silently emits malformed CSV for a field containing the quotechar.** With `doublequote=False` and no escapechar, a field that needs quoting and contains the quotechar is wrapped in quotes without escaping the inner quote (`lib/tpy/csv.py` `_format_row`), producing unparseable output; CPython raises `csv.Error("need to escape, but no escapechar set")`. Only on the non-default `doublequote=False` path. Fix needs a small surface decision first: TPy `csv` has no `csv.Error` type -- either add one (matching CPython's hierarchy) or raise `ValueError`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of csv v1. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` for the error-surface call, then a localized fix.
- **[LOW small] Module-qualified construction of a generic class fails: `mod.GenericClass(...)` reports "Module has no function 'GenericClass'".** `csv.DictReader(fp)` (a generic `class DictReader[W]` accessed via the module attribute) is rejected, while `from csv import DictReader; DictReader(fp)` resolves and deduces `W` correctly. Module-attribute access resolves functions and non-generic classes but not generic-class construction. Workaround: direct import. Surfaced building `csv.DictReader`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `sorted(d.items(), key=...)` (and other element-type inference) on a readonly dict fails: `items()` yields `readonly[value]` for a value-typed V.** `d.items()` on a `readonly[dict[K, int]]` is typed `dict_items[K, readonly[int]]`, so iterating yields `tuple[K, readonly[int]]`; passing it to `sorted(..., key=lambda kv: -kv[1])` makes overload/type-param inference conflict (`tuple[K, readonly[int]]` vs the lambda's `tuple[K, int]`). `readonly[int]` is pointless (a value V read from a dict view is a copy), but it is materialized eagerly by `@auto_readonly` on `items()`/`values()`. The other readonly-dict reads (`.get`, `in`, for-iteration, `d[k]` with a readonly key, readonly *reference*-value reads) now work; only `.items()`/`.values()` projecting readonly onto a VALUE element is unfixed. Workaround: build the pairs list manually (`for k in d: pairs.append((k, d[k]))`) then sort that. **Fix shape:** the collapse must be POSITION-AWARE -- `readonly[value-type]` collapses to the value type only in a value position (tuple/dict-view element), NOT under `Ptr`/`Span`/`SpanIter`/`Ref` where it is the const-pointee/element (a broad `substitute_type_params` collapse breaks `Ptr[readonly[T]]` / ReadOnlyPtr -- verified). Cleanest is making `auto_readonly` value-aware at substitution (resolve `AutoReadonlyType[V]` to bare V when V is value, `readonly[V]` when reference) rather than the eager `apply_auto_readonly`. Surfaced building `collections.Counter`'s `most_common`; deferred from the readonly-dict read-access fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A yield of a CONDITIONAL rejects unless both arms are frame-resident locals.** [`yield-ternary-source-non-local-arms`] `yield a if c else b` compiles and lends when `a` / `b` are locals of the generator (the shape docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md documents), but rejects at the resumable yield sink (`res.yield_type`) when they are PARAMETERS of the same generator, and one rung earlier (`expr.ifexpr`) when they are `self` FIELDS -- although each arm on its own is a lending yield source at that slot, and CPython yields the selected object either way. Probe `/tmp/agents/genyield_impl/ternary.py`, verified 2026-09-17; it is the yield sink's ladder, not the conditional: the same arms bound to a local first (`s = a if c else b; yield s`) work. The provenance rule that picks a generic generator's slot already recurses into both arms (`is_dangling_return`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`), so only the lowering arm is missing. In a GENERIC body the local-arm spelling rejects too, one rung earlier again (`res.alias_bind` on the `s = a if c else b` bind of two subscript locals, measured 2026-09-17 while filling the position matrix of `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow`), so no conditional yield source is expressible there. Sibling of BUGS.md#subscript-elem-record, which is the same shape of gap one expression form over. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A `for` over a literal of record PARAMETERS inside a generator or `async def` spells the frame's source slot as `std::array<T&, N>`.** [`frame-for-literal-of-params-reference-array`] `def gen(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> Iterator[int32]: for x in [a, b]: x.v += 10; yield x.v` (and the non-suspending twin whose body binds a frame local) emits `::tpy::frame_loop_slot<std::array<Cell&, 2>> __for_src_0;` and `__for_src_0.emplace(std::array<Cell&, 2>{a, b});` -- *forming pointer to reference type* at the `frame_slot` constraint. The frame prescan spells the slot from the literal's resolved type, whose element type still carries the parameter's reference; the plain-function route strips it (`_owned_literal_type`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, `tests/cases/iterators/for_literal_ref_elements`), so the same literal in a plain function compiles and mutates the parameters. The frame OWNS the source it iterates, so the owned spelling is the right one here too. Fix shape: apply the owned-element spelling where the frame prescan names the `__for_src_N` slot type (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`), one spelling for both routes. Same family as the entry below and `comprehension-elem-borrow-call-array`. Surfaced 2026-09-22 merging the frame for-source rule into THIR batch 7 (identical on master alone; probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/final/merge_probe.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code) An `Array`-optimized local built from GENERIC reference values spells `std::array<T&, N>`.** [`generic-array-literal-of-references`] `def plain[T](a: T, b: T) -> int32: box = [a, b]; return len(box)` emits `std::array<::tpy::val_or_ref_t<T>, 2> box = {::tpy::param_to_storage<T>(a), ::tpy::param_to_storage<T>(b)};`, and at a reference instantiation `val_or_ref_t<T>` IS `Point&` -- an array of references, which the standard forbids (*forming pointer to reference type*, *too many initializers*). Inside a generator the same literal additionally fails the `frame_slot` constraint check. A value instantiation compiles, so the rejection depends on the type argument, not on the source. The array-literal local borrowed the ELEMENT spelling from the generic PARAMETER form (`val_or_ref_t`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/type_traits.hpp`), which is a parameter's borrow form and not a storage form -- the sibling `val_or_ptr_t` exists for exactly this reason on the tuple side. Fix shape: an owning-slot element type for a generic array local (the same question `Own[T]` storage answers), or refusing the Array optimization for an open `T` so the literal falls back to the `list` path. Probes `/tmp/agents/yield_round1/arrayref.py` (generator) and `arrayref2.py` (plain function), measured 2026-09-17; pre-existing, found while filling the yield-source position matrix of `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow` (the local container section uses a `list[T]` + `append` instead because of it). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) `itertools.cycle` lends its elements on the FIRST pass only; every later pass yields copies.** [`itertools-cycle-later-passes-copy`] `for n in cycle(f): n.v += 10` over `f = [Node(1), Node(2)]`, stopped after four steps, leaves `f` at `11 12` where CPython reads `21 22` (probe `/tmp/agents/yr_parity/p5_itertools.py`, verified 2026-09-17). `cycle` is TPy source (`lib/tpy/itertools.py`): its first loop yields the argument's element -- a lend -- but also does `saved.append(x)`, which COPIES the element into the generator's own list, and the replay loop then lends out of `saved`. So the mutation of pass 1 lands on the source and the mutation of pass 2 lands on the copy, which is why the divergence is a doubling rather than a total loss. Nothing warns, because the copy is the documented generic owning-slot contract at the append. `islice` / `takewhile` / `dropwhile` / `filterfalse` / `repeat` have no such buffer and match CPython. A TPy-source combinator that copies where CPython aliases (the C++ ones lend since 2026-09-22), and what it needs to close is an element buffer that holds BORROWS of the argument's elements rather than copies, which is the representation question TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source" is about. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) ONE ephemeral yield source demotes every other yield in the same generic generator.** [`generic-yield-mixed-source-demotes-frame`] `def mix[T](items: list[T], extra: Iterator[T]) -> Iterator[T]` that yields `items`' loop var and then `extra`'s prints `mixed 1 2 5` where CPython reads `101 102 105` (probe `/tmp/agents/yr_parity/p8_mix.py`, verified 2026-09-17); the same body without the `extra` loop mutates the source correctly. The slot is ONE type for the whole frame, so the per-generator verdict conjoins every yield source and a single unrooted one takes the value slot for all of them -- stated conservatism of the rule (`docs/ITERATOR_DESIGN.md`), not an oversight, but the result is still a silent copy at the yields that would have lent. Closing it needs a per-yield slot, i.e. a frame that can hand out a borrow at one yield and a value at another (today's `next_iter_mixin` element type forbids that), or the ephemeral source itself lending -- which is what BUGS.md#mono-iterator-relay-yield-rejects is about on the concrete side. Pinned read-only as the third inverse section of `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent) A generic generator that yields a CALLABLE's result copies the element even when the callable lends it.** [`generic-yield-fn-result-copies`] `def mapped[T, U](fn: Fn[[T], U], it: Iterable[T]) -> Iterator[U]: for x in it: yield fn(x)` consumed as `for p in mapped(lambda p: p, pts): p.x += 100` leaves `pts` at `1 2` where CPython reads `101 102` (probe `/tmp/agents/genyield_impl/fnborrow.py`, verified 2026-09-17). The per-generator provenance verdict that picks the open-`T` yield slot (`is_dangling_return` read closed-world, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) can prove a CALL lends only when the resolved signature says its return borrows from an operand; an erased `Fn` return carries no ownership at all, so the generator falls to the VALUE slot and copies the element out. A NAMED callee is unaffected -- sema infers its `U` as `Ref[Point]` and the call site substitutes `val_or_ref<Point>`, so the same generator lends (`named 101 102` in that same probe, and `iterators/gen_ref_compose` relays through one). The copy is the reason the LAMBDA `fn` section of `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow` reads instead of mutates; its `named-fn` neighbour mutates, since a named callee lends. Closing it needs the callable's declared return to carry its ownership: see `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md` and TODO.md "`Fn` return ownership visible at the definition site". Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The everyday face is `map` with a LAMBDA: `for c in map(lambda z: z, cells): c.v += 100` leaves `cells` unchanged (TPy `[11, 12]`, CPython `[111, 112]`) because the lambda's inferred return carries no borrow fact and `map`'s declared element `U` is spelled as the owned `Cell`, so the step copies -- where the named twin `map(same, cells)` with `def same(c: Cell) -> Cell` lends and mutates correctly. Silent; the one combinator spelling that still copies since the element-form unit of 2026-09-22 (the others lend off their source).
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) A generic generator that re-yields the element of an INNER generic producer hands out a copy, so mutation through the consumer's loop var never reaches the source.** [`generic-relay-inner-producer-copies`] `def eachl[T](items: list[T]) -> Iterator[T]: for it in items: yield it` and `def lend_twice[T](items: list[T]) -> Iterator[T]: for a in eachl(items): yield a`, then `for p in lend_twice(pts): p.x += 100` -- TPy prints `1 2`, CPython `101 102` (probe `/tmp/agents/relay_generic_producer.py`; identical on master 2cb3c41d3f). The loop var `a` borrows the inner frame's step slot, which the next step overwrites, so the relay takes the VALUE yield slot -- the same conservatism `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow` pins as its "inverse 2" for an `Iterator[T]` PARAMETER source, applied here to an inner producer the relay owns. Either the element must be lent from where the inner producer lends it (its own source list, which outlives both frames), or the copy needs the copy diagnostic and an escape hatch like every other owned-storage sink. Related: `generic-yield-mixed-source-demotes-frame`, `mono-iterator-relay-yield-rejects`. Found by the merge check of the generator-frame perf branch 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent copy, conservative) A generic generator whose lending callee is analyzed in a LATER module falls to the value yield slot, so it copies where its same-module twin lends.** [`generic-yield-cross-module-callee-value-slot`] `_settle_deferred_generic_yields` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) runs at the END of one module's `analyze_bodies`, over a list that the same pass cleared at its start, so a verdict can only read `return_borrows_from` of callees whose bodies that module already analyzed. Within a module that is exactly what makes the verdict order-independent; across modules it holds only in one direction. Modules are analyzed in topological order (`tpyc/compiler.py`), so an imported callee is always analyzed first -- the only way a lending callee's body can be analyzed AFTER the generic generator that yields its result is an import CYCLE, whose members are analyzed as a group. For a cycle peer the fact is still `None` at settle time, the rooting half answers conservatively, and the frame gets the value slot `T` instead of `::tpy::yield_slot_t<T>`: the consumer sees a copy and cannot mutate the element, where the byte-identical single-module spelling aliases (and CPython aliases). Conservative, so not unsafe -- the divergence is a silent CPython parity gap, not a dangle. Sibling ordering hole through the same fact, on the unsafe side: BUGS.md#cross-module-cycle-callee-borrow-unregistered. **Fix shape:** settle the deferred verdicts once per cycle GROUP (the compiler knows the SCC) or at the workspace-wide finalize, which is the same widening the sibling needs. Not reproduced end-to-end; read off the settle site and the module ordering 2026-09-17.
- **[LOW small] (missing sema diagnostic, loud THIR backstop) A generator that yields the result of a NESTED def call escapes the yield-rooting check, so an unsound borrow yield reaches codegen and is refused there under an internal construct name.** [`nested-def-callee-yield-root-unchecked`] `def g_mk(n: int32) -> Iterator[Node]` whose body defines `def mk(a: int32) -> Own[Node]: return Node(a)` and then does `yield mk(n)` passes sema: the free-call arm of `is_dangling_return` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) gates its "a function returning `Own[T]` makes a temporary" test on `self.ctx.registry.get_function(expr.func_name)`, and a nested def is absent from the module registry, so with no recorded borrow sources the open-world reading the yield-root drain uses (`assume_unknown_calls_safe=True`) falls through to "safe". THIR then refuses the body -- *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (res.yield_type)*, reported on the generator def line -- while the module-level twin (the same `mk` hoisted out of the body) gets the rule it broke: *Cannot yield local or temporary as reference ... Declare the generator `Iterator[Own[Node]]` to yield by value*, on the yield line. No miscompile, since the program is refused either way, but under an internal name and at the wrong line. Probes `/tmp/agents/fix_curfn/neg_provider.py` vs `neg_toplevel.py`, verified 2026-09-17; unaffected by the live-handle preservation in `save_function_state` (reproduces identically on both sides of it). Fix shape: resolve a nested-def callee where it lives (the enclosing body binding, `func.nested_def_nodes`) instead of gating the arm on the module registry. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `async for` over a manual async iterator COPIES the iterator source into the frame, so the loop cannot mutate the object it iterates -- and a reference-typed element additionally fails the C++ build.** Two stacked defects on the `async_for` for-strategy, both reachable from one program: `class Walker: def __aiter__(self) -> "Walker": return self` + `async def __anext__(self) -> Point` iterated as `async for p in w: p.x += 100` leaves `w.items[0].x` unchanged (CPython mutates it). (1) The iterator slot is `frame_slot<aiter_type_t<Src>>` and `aiter_type_t` is `std::decay_t<...>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp`), so a self-iterator whose `__aiter__` returns `Src&` gets *copied* into the frame at `__for_itr.emplace((it).__aiter__())` -- the loop then drives the copy. The SYNC path solved exactly this: `is_self_iterator_v` + `resumable_iter_init`/`resumable_iter_next` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/generator.hpp`) keep the slot empty for a self-iterator and re-read through `src`; the async path has no twin. Silent for a self-iterator, and a `@nocopy`/`Own` source would fail the build instead. (2) Independently, the `async_for` strategy never sets `pointer_form_loop_var`, so a concrete non-value element is emplaced into `frame_slot<T>` from the `T*` that `__anext__` returns -- ill-formed C++ (`invalid conversion from Point* to int32_t` inside `frame_slot::emplace`). Fixing (2) alone is a REGRESSION: it makes the program compile and silently produce the wrong answer via (1), so the two must land together, (1) first. The sibling `iter_next` strategy is already fixed for both. Async generators (`async def` + `yield`) are unsupported, so a manual `__aiter__`/`__anext__` class is the only route in. Repro `/tmp/agents/prereq/asyncfor.py`. Surfaced by the for-strategy borrow-form survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The for-loop result slot in a resumable frame is spelled from the ELEMENT type, so a non-value element makes it `std::expected<T&, StopIteration>` -- ill-formed C++, since a reference cannot live in `std::expected`. Two arms of `_analyze_for_strategy` do this.** (a) The `er_elem` arm: `class BagIter: @error_return(StopIteration) def __next__(self) -> Point` iterated inside a two-yield generator emits `std::expected<Point&, ::tpy::StopIteration> __for_r_0`, and libstdc++ rejects it (`non-static data member ... in a union may not have reference type` / `forming pointer to reference type`). Repro `/tmp/agents/prereq/ernext.py`. (b) The `typing.Iterator` arm for a NAMED source: same slot, same error; the temporary-source path already avoids it by spelling `decltype(std::declval<__gen_X&>().__next__())` from the stored struct rather than from the element. Arm (b) is mostly shadowed by the over-broad ephemeral-borrow rejection (a yield touching the loop var is rejected at sema first), so its reachable window is a body that mutates the element but never yields anything derived from it; arm (a) has no such shield. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid. Same borrow-form-leaked-into-an-owning-slot family as the since-fixed coro-frame `str`/view local defect, different site: there the owning slot was the yield result, here it is the `__next__` result field. Note the `er_elem` arm is also missing the borrow-form loop-var classification, but that is moot until the slot is spellable. Fix shape, covering both arms: derive the result slot from the SOURCE (its `__next__` return type, as the temporary path already does) instead of from the element type, so the borrow lands in the loop var where the storage-form classification can hold it. Was filed as two entries -- one per arm, with different prescriptions -- until the merge-master check spotted they are one defect. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `dict`/`set` literal with a coercible-but-not-equal element type rejects-valid instead of applying the runtime-checked `BigInt -> fixed-width int` coercion.** `d: dict[str, int32] = {"k": make_big()}` / `s: set[int32] = {make_big()}` (where `make_big() -> int`) is rejected at sema with `Type mismatch in variable 'd': expected int32, got int`, even though the same `int` value coerces cleanly at scalar (`x: int32 = make_big()`) and now list/tuple-element positions (the runtime-checked `to_fixed_check`). Root: the dict/set literal analyzers' per-element contextual-coercion branch only fires when the expected element type is a union/optional/Any/recursive-wrapper/covariant-generic shape; a plain concrete target (`int32`) falls to the `else` peer-unify branch, so the literal's type becomes `dict[str, BigInt]` / `set[BigInt]`, which the strict container-assignment element check then rejects. Distinct from the list/tuple gap that this sibling fix closed -- those *silently miscompiled* (ill-formed C++); dict/set instead *reject-valid* with a clean error, so it is lower severity. Fix shape: widen the contextual branch to any known concrete target and route plain-target elements through the same materialize-narrowing-coercion path `_analyze_array_literal` now uses (`_materialize_narrowing_element_coercion`), verifying the strict element check still rejects user-record slicing. Surfaced fixing the list/tuple aggregate-element coercion (`tests/cases/int/int_to_fixed_in_aggregate`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] A protocol whose method is typed with a *same-module* recursive type alias fails the C++ build -- the protocol's concept / `@dynamic` base + `Adapter`/`RefAdapter` are emitted before the recursive-alias wrapper struct is declared.** `type Tree[T] = T | list[Tree[T]]` plus `class Counter(Protocol): def count(self, t: Tree[int]) -> int32: ...` (or the `@dynamic` form) in one module emits, in the header, a virtual `count(Tree<BigInt>&)` / a `Counter` concept referencing `Tree<...>` *before* the same-module `template<...> struct Tree` (or its forward decl) appears -- g++ reports `'Tree' has not been declared` (structural: `concept 'Counter' not in namespace scope`; `@dynamic`: `RefAdapter` pure-virtual `count` not overridden due to the broken signature). Affects both structural and `@dynamic` protocols, generic recursive alias confirmed (non-generic recursive union likely same root, unverified). **Works cross-module**: importing the alias (`from treelib import Tree`) brings the wrapper in complete via the included header, so the ordering is satisfied -- this is the workaround. Toolchain-caught (C++ build error), not silent. Fix shape: in `codegen_cpp/generator.py` emit ordering, the recursive-union wrapper forward-decl/definition for a *local* alias must precede protocol (concept / `@dynamic` base / adapter) emission, mirroring the guarantee the imported-header path already provides. Surfaced by /tpy-ready coverage-hardening probes for generic recursive aliases (the `@dynamic`-protocol-method coverage gap). Covered cross-module by `tests/cases/protocols/dyn_recursive_alias_method`; the same-module case is the gap. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (parity) `open(dir, "r")` on a directory succeeds silently and `read()` returns `""` where CPython raises `IsADirectoryError` immediately.** `std::ifstream::open` does not fail for a directory in read mode (Linux `open(2)` with `O_RDONLY` succeeds on a directory; the failure only surfaces at `read(2)` as EISDIR, which iostreams swallow into failbit/empty), so `TextFile`/`BinaryFile`'s `is_open()` gate passes and the EISDIR arm of the errno-mapped open path is unreachable for read mode -- probe: `open("/tmp", "r").read()` prints `""` in TPy, raises `[Errno 21] Is a directory: '/tmp'` in CPython. Write-mode open on a directory DOES correctly raise `IsADirectoryError` (EISDIR at `open(2)` time). Silent divergence, and it defeats the read-mode half of the `IsADirectoryError` mapping the CPython-exact-OSError feature wired up; also blocks writing an EISDIR-through-`open()` test until fixed. Fix shape: after a successful read-mode open, `stat` the path (or attempt a zero-byte read and check EISDIR) and raise `IsADirectoryError` like CPython's `io.open` does at fd-wrap time. Pre-existing (the `is_open()` gate predates the errno mapping); surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the oserror-exact branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `TextFile`/`BinaryFile` reads do not surface a genuine I/O error (badbit) -- a read that fails on a device error returns "" / b"" instead of raising `OSError`.** `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/file.hpp`: the full-read path (`read()` / `read(size<0)`) drains via `ss << fs_.rdbuf()` / `istreambuf_iterator` and never checks `fs_.bad()`; the sized-read path (`read(size>=0)`) now preserves badbit across its short-read `clear()` but still doesn't *raise* on it -- a subsequent read just returns empty. CPython raises `OSError` on a real read error. Latent: badbit on a regular file is a hardware/FS fault, near-unreachable in tests; EOF (the common short-read cause) is correctly handled as empty. Fix shape: after each read, if `fs_.bad()` (not merely `eof`/`fail`), `raise_os_error(...)` -- consistently across both the full-read and sized-read paths. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the io `read(size)` change.
- **[HIGH medium, postponed: evaluation-order policy] Subexpressions evaluate in the C++ COMPILER'S order, diverging from CPython's guaranteed left-to-right -- confirmed for positional call/constructor/method arguments, both operands of a binary operator, and f-string interpolations.** [`subexpression-right-to-left-eval`] Measured against CPython with a counter function `nxt()`: `three(nxt(), nxt(), nxt())` prints `3 2 1` (CPython `1 2 3`), `print(nxt() - nxt())` prints `1` (CPython `-1`), `f"{nxt()} {nxt()}"` prints `7 6` (CPython `6 7`) -- probe `/tmp/agents/dsr/r29_evalorder.py`. Brace-initialized list/tuple literals and `print(a, b)` ARE sequenced with respect to EACH OTHER (the standard sequences a braced-init-list and a `<<` chain), while a literal that MOVES its elements -- a `@nocopy` or movable-local element, or an `Own`-returning call at a container-element slot (admitted 2026-09-15) -- renders through the `::tpy::make_vector` / `make_ordered_map` / `make_ordered_set` helpers, whose operands are call arguments like any other's (`tests/cases/list/container_elem_from_call` pins that render and cites this entry); but a print argument's own OUTPUT still interleaves wrongly: `print("x:", f())` where `f` prints emits `std::cout << "x:" << f()`, and `<<` operands evaluate left-to-right, so the prefix reaches the stream before `f()` runs -- TPy prints `x: ` then f's output then `7`, CPython evaluates every argument first and prints f's output then `x: 7`. Any print whose arguments write to stdout (or stderr on the same terminal) diverges, with no call-order bug in sight; the fix shape is the same sequencing -- materialize every side-effecting argument into temps before the first `<<`. Silent wherever the subexpressions are pure, wrong wherever they are not, and `f() - g()` needs no call syntax to trigger. Found downstream in a path tracer, where `V3(random() * 2.0 - 1.0, random() * 2.0 - 1.0, random() * 2.0 - 1.0)` drew from the random stream backwards: the result was a correctly rendered but DIFFERENT image, so nothing short of a byte comparison against CPython caught it. Raised MED -> HIGH on that evidence: the original entry was scoped to the single binary op, and the shape that actually bites -- an ordinary multi-argument call -- is both more common and equally silent. The three sub-entries below record the shapes as originally measured. **Original binary-operand measurement:** `a() + b()` (each appending to a shared list) runs `b()` then `a()` -- TPy emits the C++ expression `a() + b()` and g++ evaluates function-call arguments right-to-left (C++ leaves the order unspecified), so any observable side effect in the operands is sequenced backwards. The *result value* is correct (operator is applied to the right values); only the side-effect *order* diverges. Reproducer: `order=[]; def a(): order.append("a"); return "A"` + same for `b`; `a()+b()` gives `order==['b','a']` (CPython `['a','b']`). Notably the 3+-operand chain `a()+b()+c()` is correct (`['a','b','c']`) -- it routes through a left-to-right fold -- so the bug is specific to the single binary op. Applies to any binary operator (`+`/`-`/`*`/comparisons/etc.) whose two operands both carry side effects, not just str concat. No diagnostic; silent. Affects `<`/`==` operand order, `x[f()] = g()`-style too (unaudited). Fix shape: sequence binary-op operands left-to-right at emit (materialize the left operand into a temp before evaluating the right when either operand is non-trivial). Sequence the operands: capture the left one's VALUE before evaluating the right when either can run user code -- a reference alias is not enough, it re-reads after the write. The membership / chained-comparison sibling of this is filed above and was implemented then reverted; the two should land together so the rule is not half-applied, and the cost (a copy per affected expression) priced once for both. Probe `/tmp/agents/chain-dup/reorder.py`. Surfaced authoring the io `read(size)` tests (`fp.read(4) + "|" + fp.read()`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. **Same class, hoisted-arg shape:** an arg materialized as a named temp STATEMENT before the call (a ref-param rvalue -- container/record literal or call result -- to a free function, or any reference-type rvalue to a generator/coro method) evaluates before sibling inline args, so a multi-arg call mixing a hoisted arg with side-effecting inline args sequences wrong vs CPython's left-to-right (probe: `take(side("a"), [side("x"), side("y")], side("b"))` -> `x y b a`, CPython `a x y b`). Newly reachable via the resumable-method rvalue args that previously failed the C++ build. The fix shape generalizes: hoist ALL side-effecting args left-to-right once any arg hoists. A comprehension argument joins the hoisted shape at a CONSTRUCTOR's container slot since 2026-09-11 (`Flat(f(), [g(x) for x in h()])` runs `h`, `g`, then `f`; the free-call twin always did) -- `cases/calls/ctor_comprehension_arg` cites this entry rather than pinning the order. **Value-typed generic slots joined the scope on 2026-09-08:** an rvalue at a generic `T` parameter used to hoist a named temp, which incidentally SERIALIZED it ahead of its sibling arguments; the temp is now taken at the instantiation, so `f(side("A"), side("B"))` at a value-typed `T` renders both inline and g++ runs B then A. Not a new class and not a reason to re-add the hoist -- the monomorphic twin always had this order, so hoisting only at the generic slot would make the generic and its twin differ (the `generic-equals-monomorphic-twin` pitfall) while leaving the twin wrong; the fix is the sequencing below, which covers both. **POSTPONED 2026-09-16 -- do not fix any site of this class until the policy is decided.** The order is not "backwards", it is the C++ compiler's: g++ evaluates call arguments right-to-left and clang left-to-right in practice, and the standard guarantees neither, so a program that observes it is also toolchain-dependent (no case may pin the order in `output.txt`; pin the render). Whether TPy guarantees Python's order everywhere (a temporary per observable operand at every multi-operand site -- the sequenced stmt-expr build that was built for the moving container literal in bundle 2 and reverted for exactly this reason), only outside hot-path annotated sections, or nowhere, is one language decision (TODO.md "Evaluation-order policy"), and per-site fixes before it are inconsistent by construction. Known sites, one list: positional call / constructor / method arguments; both operands of a two-operand binary operator (the 3+-operand chain folds left to right by accident); f-string interpolations; a hoisted argument beside inline side-effecting ones; value-typed generic slots; the moving container literal (list, set, and dict, where Python also runs each key before its own value); the dict comprehension key/value pair (`dict-comp-key-value-order`, same class). One site currently REJECTS instead of diverging: `print` with a computed `sep=`/`end=` beside a call-valued positional argument (`_expr_evaluation_inert`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) -- relax it to the same declaration, or keep it, when the policy lands.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] A generator holding an `Optional[T]` local across iterations and yielding a tuple of (the narrowed previous value, the current loop var) miscompiles -- the previous-value tuple element silently reads the current loop var.** `def pairwise[T](it): prev: Optional[T] = None; for x in it: (if prev is not None: yield (prev, x)); prev = copy(x)` over `[1,2,3,4]` yields `(2,2),(3,3),(4,4)` instead of `(1,2),(2,3),(3,4)` -- the `prev` element of the yielded tuple reads `x`, not the stored `prev`. Reproduces in a plain `for a, b in pairwise(...)` loop (not a comprehension artifact), so the fault is in the generator's tuple-yield of a frame-held `Optional[T]` element alongside the loop var, not the consumer. No diagnostic; silent wrong output. The single-element `Optional[T]`-across-yield path (e.g. just `yield prev`) is untested here; the miscompile is observed for the tuple-of-(prev, x) shape. **Blocks `itertools.pairwise`** (and any windowed generator that carries a previous value). Workaround: none clean (the natural formulation miscompiles). Surfaced probing itertools v2 feasibility. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A generator with a generic `Optional[T]` accumulator written across the loop fails the C++ build (`__slot_1 is not captured` / `std::optional<int>::optional(int*&)`).** `def accumulate[T](it, func): acc: Optional[T] = None; for x in it: (acc = copy(x) if acc is None else func(acc, x)); yield acc` -> g++ errors at the resumable-frame body: the `Optional[T]` accumulator frame slot is mis-emitted (a captured-temp `__slot_1` referenced out of scope, and an `optional<int>` constructed from `int*`). The narrowed `acc` (Optional -> T) assigned back into the Optional slot across the resumable frame is the trigger. No TPy diagnostic; C++ build error only. **Blocks `itertools.accumulate`** (the generic running-fold shape). Workaround: none in the generic generator form. Surfaced probing itertools v2 feasibility. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A function/method that returns a recursive-union alias referenced *qualified* (`json.JsonValue`) fails to type-check (`expected JsonValue, got JsonValue`); the *unqualified* import (`from json import JsonValue`) compiles.** `import json; def p(s: str) -> json.JsonValue: return json.loads(s)` (and the `Own[json.JsonValue]` form, and the method form) is rejected -- the qualified alias resolves to a recursive-union form that does not match `json.loads`'s own return form, even though both print as `JsonValue`. `from json import loads, JsonValue` + `-> Own[JsonValue]` works. Almost certainly the recursive-union borrow/storage-form duality (OQ9): the cross-module qualified-alias reference produces a different form than the defining module's. Toolchain... actually a *sema* error, not silent. Workaround: import the alias by name (used by `tplib.requests.Response.json`). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/req/{m2,g1}.py`. Surfaced building `tplib.requests`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED] `isinstance`-narrowing a recursive-union element *extracted* from a container fails the C++ build unless the element is first bound to an explicitly-annotated local.** `d = json.loads(s); if isinstance(d, dict): v = d["k"]; if isinstance(v, int): ...` -> g++ `no matching function for call to holds_alternative<tpy::BigInt>(JsonValue&)` -- the extracted element is a *borrow* form (`JsonValue&`) on which `holds_alternative` is not callable. Binding `v: JsonValue = d["k"]` first (forcing a storage-form copy) makes the narrow compile and run. Shallow narrowing of the `loads` root (`isinstance(d, dict)`) is unaffected. Borrow/storage-form duality (OQ9) at the element-access boundary. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: explicit `: JsonValue` local (documented in `tplib.requests` -- affects every consumer of `Response.json()`). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/req/{g2,h2}.py`. Surfaced building `tplib.requests`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] For-iterating a narrowed `Optional[list]` accessed through an *attribute* emits a double-deref and fails the C++ build.** `if args.header is not None: for h in args.header: ...` (where `args.header: list[str] | None`, e.g. an argparse `action="append"` result) emits `auto& __obj_0 = (*(*args.header));` -- g++ `no match for operator* (operand type is std::vector<...>)`. The narrowing of the attribute does not carry to the for-loop's iterable lowering, which then derefs an already-deref'd value. *Subscripting* the same narrowed attribute works (`args.tag[0]` in `tests/cases/argparse/list_and_const_actions`), so the gap is specific to for-iteration of an Optional-list *attribute*. Binding to a local first (`hl = args.header; if hl is not None: for h in hl: ...`) narrows correctly and compiles -- used in `programs/curl/curl.py` in the `tpy-examples` repo. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Sibling of the narrowed-Optional-dict key-iter entry above. Surfaced building the curl example on `tplib.requests`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An `@overload`-ed generator METHOD is rejected at the stub: `Protocol type 'Iterator' cannot be used as a return type`.** `class C: @overload def rep[T](self, obj: T) -> Iterator[T]: ...` + a second stub + a `yield`-bodied implementation errors at the first stub's `def` line. Root: the `...`-bodied stub has `is_generator=False` (no `yield` in its body), and the method-registration return-type validation (`tpyc/sema/registration.py:1258`) rejects an `Iterator[T]` return unless `method.is_generator` -- whereas the free-function overload path (`register_overload_group`) does no protocol-return check on stubs at all, so it is lenient. Distinct from the free-function overloaded-generator crash (now fixed: the impl's `generator_yield_type` is set via `_set_generator_yield_type`); the method analog fails earlier and never reaches that path. The free-function form is the common one (itertools uses free functions), so this is lower priority. Fix shape: in the method return-type validation, treat an `Iterator[T]`-returning `@overload` stub whose group has a generator implementation as a generator (or relax the protocol-return check for overload stubs, mirroring the free-function path), then set the impl method's `generator_yield_type` (same `_set_generator_yield_type` helper). Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the free-function overloaded generator. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An annotated dict/list literal whose VALUES are container literals is rejected: `Type mismatch in variable 'g': expected list[int32], got PendingList[int32, 2]#0`.** `g: dict[str, list[int32]] = {"a": [1, 2], "b": [3]}` fails, and so does the list flavor `m: list[list[int32]] = [[1], [2, 3]]`. The annotation's element type never reaches the NESTED literal, so each inner literal stays a `PendingListType` and the outer coercion compares it against the resolved `list[int32]` slot (`_analyze_var_decl` -> `compat.coerce_expr`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py:4196`). The named-local workaround compiles (`row: list[int32] = [1, 2]; g = {"a": row}`). This is the sibling BUGS entry below already names as "the annotated dict-literal-of-list-literals case" -- it had no entry of its own. Loud reject-valid, no miscompile. Fix shape: thread the annotated container's element/value type into nested container literals during literal resolution, the same expected-type-into-nested-literal hole as the `d.get(k, [])` default. Repro `/tmp/agents/d2dbg/x/main.py`. Surfaced writing the value-position container-element exec case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `d.get(k, [])` (empty-list / collection-literal default) fails to compile: the literal default arg never resolves its element type.** `d: dict[str, list[int32]]; d.get("k", [])` -> `No matching overload for 'get' with argument types (str, PendingList[???, 0])` -- the `[]` stays a `PendingListType` (no element-type context flows from the `default: V` param to the literal), so overload resolution can't match `get(key, default: V)`. The named-local workaround (`fb: list[int32] = []; d.get(k, fb)`) compiles. Same expected-type-into-nested-literal hole as the annotated dict-literal-of-list-literals case (audit cluster 14 family); the `default` param's `V` should hint the literal. Reproducer: `/tmp/agents/getb/absent_rvalue.py`. Blocks the rvalue-default path of the dict.get(k,default) aliasing work (Stage B). Surfaced reproducing that work.
- **[LOW small] The F1 borrow-local const rule may emit `const T*` for a mutable borrow when a `@readonly` `@native` record method returns a reference type.** Now that native `-> V` reference returns alias (the native-record exclusion was removed), the readonly-method ref-return arm of `_f1_is_const` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:7772`, the `isinstance(stmt.init, TpyMethodCall)` branch keyed on `fi.is_readonly and call_returns_cpp_ref(...)`) fires and renders the bound local `const T*`; if such a method intentionally exposes a mutable `T&` and the caller wants a mutable `T*`, the borrow is silently over-constrained. No current stdlib case (the affected methods -- e.g. uninit `load` -- pick the non-const C++ overload on a non-const receiver, and `const T*` from a mutable `T&` is a safe narrowing). Latent trap for future native bindings; confirmed by reading the surviving arm, not by a reproducer. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness).
- **[LOW small] `@cpp_template` accessor methods on `@native` containers (`list`/`Span`/`Array`/`varargs.unchecked_get`) now alias for reference-type element instantiations, untested.** The native-record exclusion removal generalized aliasing to all native `-> V` reference returns, including `@cpp_template` `operator[]`-style accessors; the `unchecked_get` family is exercised only for value-type elements, so the reference-element aliasing path (`list[SomeRecord].unchecked_get(i)` bound and mutated through) has no regression test. Behavior is believed correct (operator[] returns `T&`); the gap is coverage. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness).
- **[LOW small] Free `@native` functions returning a bare reference type `-> V` value-copy the result where a `V&`-returning C++ function should alias.** `call_returns_cpp_ref` (`tpyc/value_category.py`) bails out for `is_native_import` (free native functions) before the `-> V` vs `-> Own[V]` return-shape check that now governs both user methods and `@native` *record* methods (the native-record exclusion was removed). So a free `@native` func whose hand-written C++ returns `V&` into an argument has its result copied at the call site, not aliased -- the same asymmetry the record-method fix closed, one layer up. Latent: no in-tree free native function currently returns a bare reference `-> V` (they return values, `Own`, `Optional`, or views). Fix: drop the remaining `fi.is_native_import and not fi.is_method` guard in `call_returns_cpp_ref` (the method half is already handled) so free functions also reach the return-shape check, after auditing free native bindings the way the record-method bindings were audited (confirm each bare-`-> V` free function actually returns `V&`, retype by-value ones to `-> Own[V]`). Surfaced removing the native-record return-convention exclusion.
- **[MED medium] Two-arg `dict.get(k, default)` returns a copy of the stored value where CPython returns the stored object -- warned, not yet aliased.** [`dict-get-default-copies-not-aliases`] The dict-accessor aliasing work (audit cluster 7) made `items()`/`values()`/`setdefault()` borrow, but two-arg `get` stayed by-value: its result conditionally borrows EITHER the map slot (hit) OR the default argument (miss), and an rvalue default needs a materialization slot whose lifetime is unresolved for loops (per-iteration freshness vs slot reuse) and resumable frames (suspension-crossing borrows). Loud since the same work: a call-site warning fires for reference-type values, silenced by wrapping in `copy()`; value-type results are parity-clean. Fix shape: `V& dict_get_default(m&, key, V& def)` + const overload (value-type V keeps the by-value helper, dispatched by codegen), an emit-site slot for rvalue defaults with defined loop/suspension semantics, and `return_borrows_from={-1, default}` so borrow tracking roots at both sources; typing the return as a bare `-> V` (not `Own[V]`) then makes the result alias with no extra mechanism (the precedent: setdefault is a plain `-> V` native method that aliases because native `-> V` reference returns are treated as `T&`), and the `@copy_returns_warn` decorator is dropped from the overload at the same time (the warning becomes unnecessary once the result aliases). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A pending dict/set LOCAL passed to a param with a wider value/element type is rejected instead of widening (`{"a": 1}` local into `dict[str, int64]` param -> "expected int64, got int32").** Symmetric everywhere (free functions, methods, ctors) -- `mark_container_param_context`'s dict/set arms only call `_widen_inferred_type`, which records the widening for the literal's storage but the arg-check still compares the pre-widening pending type against the param and errors. The LIST arm handles this (`coerced_element_type` makes `xs = [3]; take(xs)` into `list[int64]` compile), so the gap is dict/set parity with the list behavior. Loud reject-valid, trivial workaround (annotate the local). Reproducer: `/tmp/agents/setbug/dictwiden.py`. Surfaced authoring the pending-arg-marks tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small]** Async finally-with-await (CFG-based finally) is silently skipped when the coroutine frame is dropped mid-suspension WITHOUT cancellation (a frame abandoned outside the executor's cancel-drain path). The frame destructor runs helper-based finallies and `with.__exit__`s, but a finally body that itself suspends cannot run in a destructor. The generator sibling (yield-in-finally) gets a compile-time warning; the async shape does not, because the normal executor path runs such cleanup via cancellation (CancelledError at the suspension) and a blanket warning would flag every legitimate `finally: await ...`. Fix shape: warn only for frames that can escape executor-managed lifetime, or drain-to-completion in the owning slot before drop. CPython runs the finally at GC close.
- **[LOW small]** An `except BaseException:` (or `except GeneratorExit:`) handler around a `yield` does not observe the close when the generator is abandoned: CPython throws GeneratorExit INTO the frame, so such a handler catches it and its body runs; TPy's frame destructor runs only pending finally helpers and `with.__exit__`s (it cannot resume arbitrary handler code inside a destructor), so the handler body is skipped silently. Same can't-resume-in-a-destructor family as the warned yield-in-finally skip, but no diagnostic fires for the handler shape. Fix shape: extend the yield-in-finally warning to yields lexically inside an except-BaseException/GeneratorExit-guarded try, or accept and document. Surfaced by the GeneratorExit-on-close design pass.
- **[LOW small]** `break`/`continue` crossing a CFG-based finally (finally body contains a suspension) silently skips that finally body: `CFGBuilder._build_break/_build_continue` emit a plain Fall to the loop's break/continue BB without routing through `finally_entry_bb` (returns are parked via the pending-return slot; break/continue have no analogous path). Same hole for break inside an except handler of such a try (`ExceptRegion.parent_finally_entry_bb`). Repro in the 2026-06-10 audit (B62): async `for` + `try/finally`-with-await + `break` drops `cleanup 1`; the generator shape shares the emitter. Fix shape: park a pending-jump target the way pending returns are parked. Helper-based finallies are unaffected.
- **[LOW small] An explicitly-annotated `Array[T, N]` comprehension rejected by the stack-build gates fails with a misleading generic type mismatch.** `xs: Array[int32, 2000] = [i for i in range(2000)]` (over the `_COMP_ARRAY_MAX_SIZE` cap) and `xs: Array[int32, 4] = [g(i) for i in range(4)]` with `@error_return` `g` inside try/except both error with "expected Array[...], got list[...]" -- the gates in `_try_comp_array_size` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) suppress the PendingListType machinery entirely, so the explicit-annotation resolution rule never runs; both shapes compiled at the pre-builder base via the old loop build. Loud rejection, not a miscompile, but it rejects previously-valid code with a diagnostic that doesn't name the cause. Fix shape needs a design call: either honor the annotation with a non-lambda build for gated shapes (the loop-fill reintroduces the default-ctor side-effect divergence the builder fixed, so only sound where construction is side-effect-free) or emit a targeted error ("cannot stack-build: element calls @error_return / size exceeds cap") at the annotation-mismatch site. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective challenger.
- **[LOW small] Reading an `@error_return` property outside try/except is not rejected; the same call spelled as a method is.** The unhandled-error_return check (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:4706`) fires for direct and method calls but not for the getter hidden behind a property read: with `@property @error_return(E) def val(...)`, a bare `g.scaled(1)` outside try/except errors with "must be handled with try/except" while the adjacent `g.val` compiles and the unwrap panics at runtime on error instead. Missing safety diagnostic, not a miscompile (codegen's panic fallback is sound). Fix, RESTATED 2026-09-18: there is no `property_getter_call` any more -- a property read IS a resolved `TpyMethodCall` from sema on, so the getter reaches `analyze_call`'s unhandled check by the same route a spelled method does. What still exempts it is that the read's analysis returns before that check runs (it resolves through the record's property table, not through the call analyser), so the check has to be asked once where the read resolves, keyed on the getter's `error_return_type` like any other callee's. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the index-sequence builder (the gate-test regeneration flagged only the method line).
- **[LOW small] Repeating a mutable reference-type element has no "copies" diagnostic, asymmetric with the bulk-copy warning.** `[obj] * N` evaluates the element once and copies it into every slot where CPython aliases the same object N times -- mutating `xs[0]` updates all CPython views but only one TPy copy. The divergence is declared in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` (list repetition) but emits no compile-time signal, while the sibling bulk-copy path (`list(b)` over reference elements) warns "copies X elements" with `copy_iter()` as the acknowledgment spelling (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`). Pre-existing for the vector repeat path; the Array repeat path now shares it. Fix shape (design-gated: new warning + acknowledgment spelling need sign-off): warn on repeating a mutable reference-type element, silenced by an explicit per-slot construction or an acknowledgment spelling consistent with `copy_iter`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the repeat-pair fix.
- **[LOW small] A comprehension whose element is a reference-typed field access (`[obj.ref_field for obj in src]`) fails the C++ build with "forming pointer to reference type".** `[b.inner for b in bs]` where `Box.inner: Inner` (a reference-type field) and `bs: list[Box]` emits a `std::vector<Inner>` build that g++ rejects (`forming pointer to reference type 'Inner&'` inside `allocator`/`construct_at`). Pre-existing and independent of the source's ownership -- reproduces identically over a borrowed `list` source and an `Own[T]`-yielding generator. The comprehension element binds the field access as `Inner&` and the storage-form result vector mis-forms a pointer to it. Loud build error, not a miscompile. Workaround: bind the field to a local first (`[copy(b.inner) for b in bs]` or an explicit loop). Surfaced building a derived-sink test case for the list/set comprehension-element move fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, diagnostics] Growing an inferred fixed-`Array` sublist via the outer subscript surfaces a raw g++ error, not a TPy diagnostic.** `rows = [[i, i + 1] for i in range(3)]; rows[0].append(99)` -- the inner literal `[i, i+1]` is constant-size and unmutated, so it resolves to `std::array<int32_t, 2>` (the stack-Array optimization), and `rows[0].append(...)` then fails the C++ build with `'std::array<int, 2>' has no member named 'push_back'`. Mutation *through the outer subscript* is not tracked back to the inner literal, so the inner is never promoted to `list`. Loud failure, not a miscompile; the workaround is an explicit `rows: list[list[int]] = [...]` (forces `vector<vector<...>>`, append works -- covered by `tests/cases/list/comp_nested_vector_inner`). A leaky-C++-error class (raw g++ message instead of a TPy diagnostic). The uniform outer/middle levels of a deep-nested literal (e.g. `[[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]]`) are another way to reach it: those levels stay fixed `Array`, so `xs.append(...)` / `xs[0].append(...)` on them hits the same raw g++ error. Fix shape: either detect element-mutation through a container subscript and promote the inner pending list to `list`, or emit a TPy diagnostic at the `.append` site pointing at the `list[list[T]]` annotation. The fix's regression test (a now-rejected-with-clean-message `error_` case, or a happy case once promotion lands) goes in with the fix. Surfaced while finishing the nested-list-literal work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, diagnostics] Pending container type names leak into type-mismatch / unresolved-type diagnostics** (`PendingList[int32, 2]#0`, `PendingDict[...]#1`). User-facing errors expose the internal deferred-resolution representation instead of a resolved display name (`list[int]`, etc.); the `error_append_incompatible_nested` and `error_jagged_incompatible_elem` cases show both sides of a mismatch as raw `PendingList[...]`. Worse, the mixed-types error's *suggested fix* embeds the same repr -- `Use a type annotation like list[PendingList[int32, 2]#0 | PendingList[str, 3]#1]` -- which is unwritable (a user can't type `#0`), so the suggestion is useless until the names resolve. Pre-existing, cross-cutting all pending-type errors. Fix shape: a `PendingList`/`PendingDict`/`PendingSet` -> resolved-display-name helper (defer to the inferred element type) applied at the diagnostic-formatting boundary, *including the suggested-annotation string* (which then reads `list[list[int] | list[str]]`). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the pending-container-compat fix; suggestion face flagged reviewing the jagged-nested-list diagnostics. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, postponed: evaluation-order policy] A dict comprehension evaluates the key and value in unspecified order (CPython evaluates the key first), observable only with ordering-dependent side effects.** [`dict-comp-key-value-order`] `{f(): g() for _ in it}` emits `__result.insert_or_assign(f(), g())` -- C++ leaves the two argument evaluations unsequenced, so `g()` may run before `f()`, whereas CPython's bytecode evaluates the key expression before the value. Pure/side-effect-free key/value (the overwhelming common case) are unaffected; only a key and value with a mutual ordering dependence (e.g. both mutate a shared counter) diverge. The owned-value-move path already sequences the key into a local before the value move (`{ auto __k = key; insert_or_assign(std::move(__k), std::move(value)); }`), so it is key-before-value correct; only the non-owned/non-moving path stays unsequenced. **Fix shape:** sequence the key into a local for the non-owned path too (or whenever either side may have side effects). Pre-existing; surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the dict comprehension owned-element move. Same class as `subexpression-right-to-left-eval` and postponed with it (2026-09-16).
- **[LOW] (rejects-valid, loud) A mixed-arm ternary (`g0 if cond else C(9)`) of a reference type is a hard compile error.** When one arm is a reference lvalue and the other a fresh rvalue, sema first warns "ternary copies a reference type where CPython would alias the variable arm; use copy() to acknowledge the copy" (`tpyc/sema/statements.py:3919-3923`, keyed on `is_rvalue_source` in `tpyc/value_category.py`, which uses OR semantics over the arms so a fresh arm forces materialization), and then codegen refuses the shape outright: in a local-decl slot `error: in function 'main': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type)` (raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:9978`), and in an argument slot `(stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.record_f1)`. So the silent value-vs-reference divergence this entry was filed for is no longer reachable -- valid Python is refused loudly instead. The all-lvalue-arms ternary (`g0 if cond else g1`) still compiles and aliases correctly, so binding the fresh arm to a local first is a verified workaround. **Fix shape:** materialize both arms into a common borrow (e.g. a pointer-of-the-selected-arm) rather than a value, weighed against the cost of the extra indirection. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Annotated assignment to an attribute (`self.vals: list[int32] = [5]` in `__init__`) is rejected with `error: Invalid assignment target`.** CPython accepts annotated attribute targets (PEP 526); this is the idiomatic way to declare-and-init instance fields in `__init__`, so plain Python sources hit it immediately. The unannotated form (`self.vals = [5]`) plus a class-level annotation works, so the workaround is trivial, but the diagnostic does not say that. **Fix shape:** either accept the annotated form (treat the annotation as the field declaration, mirroring the class-level path) or reject with a targeted message pointing at the class-level-annotation convention. Surfaced writing repros for audit item #5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The "copies X into owned storage" warning renders unresolved internal type names for list-literal locals.** When the copied variable is an unannotated list literal, the warning prints the pre-resolution placeholder -- `copies PendingList[IntLiteral(1), 3]#1 into owned storage` -- because the coercion-path warning fires during body analysis, before container-literal resolution picks the final `list[T]`/`Array[T, N]` type. Cosmetic only, but the leaked `PendingList`/`IntLiteral`/`#N` internals are baked into two `auto_move` test snapshots (`borrowed_by_generator`, `value_result_keeps_move`-adjacent shapes), which will regenerate when this is fixed. **Fix shape:** defer the warning's type rendering (store the literal id, render at diagnostic-flush after resolution) or print the variable name instead of the type for pending literals. Surfaced adding the auto-move borrow-gate tests. The field-write spelling leaks the same name (`copies PendingList[IntLiteral(1), 2]#75 into field; use copy()`, 45 cells of the reference-sink sweep 2026-09-22, whose table normalises the `#N` counter because it changes with the other cells sharing the compilation).
- **[MED small] A full-Optional match capture read after narrowing inside a GENERATOR/async frame does not deref: C++ build error.** `def gen(v: int32 | None) -> Iterator[int32]: match v: case x: yield 1; ... else: yield x` (suspending match; `x` is a `std::optional<int>` frame field; the `yield x` sits under an `if x is None: ... else:` narrowing) emits `return x;` without the `*` deref -- `could not convert std::optional<int> to std::expected<int, StopIteration>`. The sync sibling derefs correctly through the same narrowing, so the gap is the resumable frame-field read path not consulting the Optional narrowing facts for value-repr fields bound by match captures. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Surfaced verifying the binds-full-optional capture semantics on the resumable sibling (audit cluster #3 fix).
- **[LOW small] An `as`-binding on an or-pattern arm that includes `None` is rejected on an Optional subject.** `case (None | 5) as v:` on `int32 | None` errors at `stmt.match`. Semantically unsettled, which is why it is the half left open: on the `None` alternative CPython binds `v = None`, which the inner-typed binding the tier draws cannot represent -- it needs the binds-full-optional treatment that plain captures got, or a clean sema rejection. Groups WITHOUT a `None` alternative (`case 1 | 2 as x:`) lower since 2026-09-14 (case `tests/cases/match/or_group_as_binding`). Filed while unifying the match guard lowering (audit cluster #4).
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) An `as`-binding on an or-pattern arm of a UNION-subject match is a hard compile error.** `case (Cat() | Dog()) as a:` on `Cat | Dog` errors `in function 'describe': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)`: `_union_arm_ok` declines the arm and `_lower_match_union` raises (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py:2938`). The older symptom was a DROPPED binding -- usually an undeclared-identifier C++ error, but SILENT when the name was pre-declared by another arm or the branch-decl hoist, leaving a stale value where CPython binds the matched object -- and the emitter that dropped it is gone, so the shape is refused up front instead. Worth queueing: CPython accepts it and the type sema gives the binding is usable. The record and Optional tiers' `as`-name half closed on 2026-09-14; this one did NOT go with them because there the group's alternatives are the subject's own type, so sema's "the `as` binds the full subject" typing is correct, while on a union it is over-wide. That is the sema-side twin BUGS.md#or-pattern-as-binding-no-join, and it asks for the set to land as one unit: the lowering side alone is small (`_union_arm_ok`'s or-branch declines any bound arm; the binding path below already spells `from_case_var=False` for `member is None`, and `_emit_match_switch_union` already emits whole bindings), but the typing decision is not. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) PER-ALTERNATIVE captures on a RECORD-subject or-pattern are a hard compile error.** `case Point(x=a, y=0) | Point(x=0, y=a):` on a concrete record subject errors `in function 'on_axis': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)`: sema binds the names fine, then `_record_arm_ok` declines the arm (a sub-pattern that is neither a wildcard nor a literal) and `_lower_match_record` raises. The name binds a DIFFERENT field per alternative, so the fix is the per-alternative block the union tier already builds for the same shape (`match.union_or_bind`), not one shared block. The `as`-NAME half of this entry closed on 2026-09-14 -- an or-group binds the whole subject, which is one thing however many alternatives there are (case `tests/cases/match/or_group_as_binding`). CPython accepts both spellings. Sibling of the union-subject entry in this group. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An exhaustive or-pattern arm with field sub-captures on a UNION subject is rejected when the arm body does not terminate.** [`or-arm-subcapture-nonterminating`] `match a:` over `Cat | Dog` with the single arm `case Cat(tags=ts) | Dog(tags=ts): ts.append("x")` errors `in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)`. So the trigger is the conjunction -- an or-group covering the whole union, binding names, whose body falls out of the arm -- not or-patterns or sub-captures on their own, and `tests/cases/match/or_nested_union` carries the same shape with a `return` and passes. CPython accepts it. Distinct from the or-pattern-bindings group directly above: those reject the BINDINGS, this one binds them fine and rejects on the fall-through. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A capture name REUSED by a nested match whose subject is `T | None` is rejected at `stmt.match`.** [`nested-optional-capture-name-reuse`] `match h:` over a `Counter` param with `case q:`, containing `match g:` over `Counter | None` with `case None: pass` / `case q: q.n += 9`, errors `in function 'reseated_optional2': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)`. Binding the inner arm to a DIFFERENT name lowers and runs, and so does the same nested pair when both subjects are records, so the trigger is the name reuse across a record tier and an Optional tier -- one hoisted slot that the two binds want in different forms. CPython accepts it (`match` is not its own scope, so the inner bind just rebinds the local). Sibling of the or-pattern/hoist group; distinct from the generator narrowed-subject entry above, which needs a resumable frame. Pre-existing: identical on master. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_optional_reseat2.py` (rejects) and `/tmp/agents/probe_opt_distinct.py` (same shape, distinct names, lowers). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A mutating METHOD CALL on a capture re-seated between `self.<field>` and a param credits only self, so the param keeps its const borrow.** [`multi-root-receiver-drops-param`] `def touch(self, other: Bag)` whose body matches `self.mine` and then `other`, binding `q` in both arms and calling `q.bump()`, emits `void touch(const Bag& other)` and then `q->bump()` against a `const Counter*` -- g++ reports `passing 'const Counter' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers`. The receiver's self-rooted loan sets `receiver_is_self` on the call edge and the self-call deferral then suppresses the direct mark, so the receiver's OTHER roots get no attribution at all. A field WRITE through the same re-seated capture (`q.n += 4`) credits both and is covered by `tests/cases/match/match_capture_mutation_credited`'s `self_and_param_reseat` section; only the method-call receiver is affected, and only when one of its roots is self. Fixing it needs a way to say "the callee's self-mutation reaches caller param N", which `MutationCallEdge` cannot express today (it carries `receiver_is_self` as a bare flag beside a callee-param-to-caller-param map), so it is a design question, not a lowering arm. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_selfmulti.py`; the single-root twin `/tmp/agents/probe_methodrecv.py` builds and runs. Surfaced writing the multi-root section for the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` for the edge shape, then the fix.
