Currently unreachable (the sema rejection blocks any such slot), so THIR stays byte-identical; when the rejection is lifted, `_union_storage_val_cpp` must read `union_alias_names` (or fall back to AST) and both must be re-verified together. Fix shape: bind the renamed local name to the resolved alias so a local-decl annotation resolves it the way the param-signature path already does. Surfaced by /tpy-review (wave5+6) building the display-vs-alias guard case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (missing diagnostic, loud) A COMPREHENSION or an owning builtin-container-method result returned directly from a borrow-returning function (`-> list[T]`) passes sema and dies as a raw g++ error instead of the located "Cannot return local or temporary as reference".** `def f(xs: list[float]) -> list[float]: return [x * 2.0 for x in xs]` (and `return xs.copy()`) reach the C++ compiler as `cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'std::vector<double>&' to an rvalue`, with no source location and no mention of `Own`. The check is present and fires correctly on every neighbouring shape: `return []`, `return list(xs)`, `return g()` (a user fn returning `Own[list[float]]`), `y = [x * 2.0 for x in xs]; return y` (bound to a local first) and `return R(1)` for a record all get the clean located error, and the `Own[list[float]]`-declared inverse (`return xs` where the return is `Own`) gets its own clean "Cannot return borrowed value ... without explicit copy()". Two independent holes in `is_dangling_return` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py:2656`), which enumerates AST node kinds: (1) it has arms for `TpyArrayLiteral`/`TpyDictLiteral`/`TpySetLiteral` but NONE for `TpyListComprehension`/`TpyDictComprehension`/`TpySetComprehension`, so a comprehension falls through to the `Default: assume safe` tail -- the fail-closed net just above it only catches expressions whose type `is_borrowing_view_type`, and `list[float]` is not one, so the guard does not cover a comprehension of a reference type; (2) the `TpyMethodCall` arm's builtin-container exemption (`~2846`, "Builtin container methods (list.pop, ...) also return Own[T] but are exempt") was written to keep the Optional pointer-repr `&(obj.method())` path from tripping, but it sits in the shared predicate, so it also suppresses the plain reference-return check for `xs.copy()`. Loud (toolchain-caught), never silent -- no wrong runtime behavior, only a confusing error with no location. Workaround: declare `-> Own[list[T]]`. Fix shape: add the comprehension arms, and move the builtin-`Own` method exemption to the pointer-repr call site rather than the shared predicate; a node-kind enumeration that decides "safe by default" wants a reflection guard (assert every rvalue-producing expression node has an arm) or the next new node kind reopens the same hole silently. Surfaced probing the CPython-interop boundary (`@export def normalize(xs: list[float]) -> list[float]`); reproduces identically in a plain non-ext module, so it is unrelated to interop. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) Boxing a bare coroutine call (`b = Box(f())`, `f` async) in a module that never imports `Cancellable` emits the @dynamic protocol type arg bare in the decl but qualified in the adapter -- uncompilable C++.** The inferred type arg is the @dynamic `Cancellable[T]`; both `TpyType.to_cpp()` and `TypeResolver.type_to_cpp` spell the DECL's arg bare (`Box<Cancellable<::tpy::BigInt>>`) because `protocol_info_of` resolves to None in the importing module and `native_cpp_names` has no entry (the protocol was never imported), while the same statement's `make_adapter` spells the qualified `::tpyapp::tpy::coro::Cancellable<...>` via `dynamic_base_name` -- g++ fails with a template-argument parse error, no front-end diagnostic. Exotic shape (boxing a coroutine handle's dynamic wrapper), toolchain-caught, never silent. Distinct from the coro-handle entries elsewhere in this file, which cover different shapes (single-use rejection, frame types); this one is purely a type-ARG spelling hole. Also the reason THIR's `_f1_dyn_protocol_type_arg` fence must stay closed for un-imported dynamic protocols until this is fixed (routing would mirror uncompilable output). Repro was at `/tmp/agents/f1fence/ccase/` (scratch; 10 lines -- `async def f() -> int` + `Box(f())` with `from tplib import Box` only). Fix shape: qualify the dynamic-protocol arg the way `dynamic_base_name` does wherever it appears in type-arg position, or register never-imported-but-inferred protocols into the name map like inferred-return records already are (generator's dep-module walk). Surfaced by the F1 type-arg fence measurement (2026-08-01). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW latent] (silent CPython divergence, hypothetical shape) A reference-type field read off an RVALUE call receiver (`x = make().field`) copies where CPython would alias IF the callee stashed the same field object into a surviving structure.** `def make() -> Own[Resp]` that stores `self.jar` (or its argument) into some surviving registry before returning: CPython's `x = make().jar` binds the SAME jar object the registry holds, so later mutation through either is visible through both; TPy copies the field out of the dying temporary (the C++ move ctor on the xvalue member), so the two diverge silently. When no surviving alias exists the copy is unobservable (fields are stored inline, the temporary is the only owner) -- verified for the `tplib/requests` cookies case, where every jar is freshly built and `CookieJar.update` deep-copies. No measured divergence exists yet; this files the CLASS. Both codegen paths emit the copy identically (the 2026-08-01 THIR alias-decl wave mirrored the pre-existing AST decl byte-for-byte, so this is NOT a THIR issue). Fix shape, if a real witness appears: warn at the sink (the implicit-copy family) or give the shape an alias-preserving lowering; needs `/tpy-fix-bug` then. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the alias-decl wave.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) An UNANNOTATED list literal can infer a fixed-size `Array[T, N]`, and then no dynamically-sized value is ever assignable to it.** `xs = [1, 2, 3]` with no mutating use infers `std::array<int, 3>`, so a later `xs = ys` for a vector-valued `ys` fails with `cannot convert 'std::vector<int>*' to 'std::array<int,3>*'` -- including through a temporary (`tmp = [...]; xs = tmp`). The inference is USE-driven: adding an `xs.append(4)` anywhere makes the same literal a `list` and everything compiles (verified both ways), so whether a reassignment several lines away is legal depends on whether some unrelated line mutates the binding. The annotated spelling (`xs: list[int32] = [...]`) is unaffected, and the diagnostic is raw g++ output naming C++ types the user never wrote. Fix is a DESIGN call, not a patch -- either a bare list literal always seeds `list` (and `Array` requires the annotation), or the array inference is pinned at the binding instead of re-derived from downstream uses -- so this needs `/tpy-add-feature`. - **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `+` over a list of a MOVE-ONLY element demands copy-construction, so it does not work on `Rc[T]`.** (`reversed()` over the same list lends its element since 2026-09-22 and compiles.) `a + b` over `xs: list[Rc[P]]` reaches `tpy::list_concat` (`container_ops.hpp:368`), whose `result.insert(result.end(), a.begin(), a.end())` static-asserts `result type must be constructible from input type`. The rest of the same downstream report's list resolves differently and is excluded from this entry: `dict` KEYS of `Rc[T]` are rejected DELIBERATELY and with a clear located diagnostic (`Type 'Rc[P]' is non-copyable and cannot be used as a dict key; dict keys must be copy-constructible`), so that one is a design item in `TODO.md`, not a bug; `dict` with `Rc[T]` VALUES works; and `heapq.heappush` fails earlier and differently (`Cannot infer type arguments for 'heappush'`). - **[HIGH small] (warned wrong output, presents as a hang -- and the remediation the warning names does not compile) Assigning a loop-body-declared list to an OUTER variable binds the outer name to the inner one's single hoisted slot, so the next iteration's `nxt: list[C] = []` empties both.** The level-order BFS shape -- `for level in ...: nxt: list[C] = []; for s in states: nxt.append(s.child(k)); states = nxt` -- prints `2 0 0` under TPy where CPython prints `2 4 8`: the frontier is wiped before it is ever expanded. TPy DOES warn (`'states' will not keep the object it was given -- 'nxt' is rebound on each iteration and both names share its storage; use copy(nxt) for an independent value`), which normally caps this family at MED, but **`copy(nxt)` does not build**: the copy makes `states` a slot that the following `for s in states:` emits as `::tpy::own_iter(std::move(states))` over a `std::vector<C>*`, and g++ reports `no matching function for call to own_iter(...)`. The other natural spelling, `states = [x for x in nxt]`, hits the self-assigning-comprehension bug above. So there is no working path. In a real solver (rubik2) the BFS finds nothing past level 1, the goal is never reached, and `while not phase_ok:` spins at 100% CPU on an empty frontier with flat memory -- a hang, not a wrong answer, where CPython finishes the same phase in 0.158s. Same single-hoisted-slot root as the loop-body-local entries above, but the sink is an ordinary outward assignment of a CONTAINER: the fix must copy or move rather than bind. Repros `/tmp/agents/dsr/r08_bfs.py` (wrong output), `r08b_copy.py` (the `copy()` build failure). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (internal error, compiler invariant violation) `Internal error: PendingStrType should be resolved before codegen (var_id=0)`, triggered by two `str`-returning method calls in a loop plus a `set([...])` literal built from one of them.** All three ingredients are required -- removing the loop, the second call, or the set literal each compiles cleanly (verified). An assertion failure rather than bad codegen, and `set()` followed by `.add()` works around it, hence MED. Filed separately from the codegen bugs because it is the compiler failing its own invariant; related to the `get_resolved_type` / `var_types` short-circuit entry above, which is where the `PendingStrType` resolution chokepoint now lives. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r09_ice.py` (14 lines). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid + unactionable diagnostic) A repeated-literal list infers a LITERAL element type, and a literal type prints identically to its base -- `Type mismatch in assignment: expected float, got float`.** `ys = [0.0] * n` types the element as the literal `0.0` rather than `float`, so an ordinary later store of a `float` variable (`ys[0] = v`) is rejected; `[-1] * 4` is the same shape (`list[IntLiteral(-1)]`). The rejection is a real defect on its own -- a `* n` repeat is a dynamically-sized list of the BASE type, not of the seed value -- but what makes it unactionable is the rendering: expected and got print the same string, so the user cannot act without reading generated C++. Two independent fixes, both worth doing: widen a repeat-literal's element to its base type, AND print literal types distinctly (`float(0.0)` or similar). The printing half is not literal-specific -- the `TextIO` field entry below fails the identical way -- so it is worth fixing as its own diagnostic-rendering change. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r15b_litmul.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `TextIO` cannot be stored in a class FIELD: `self.f = open(path, "w")` reports `Type mismatch in assignment: expected TextIO, got TextIO`.** With the field annotated `f: TextIO` the assign is rejected against a type that renders identically to the declared one -- so `open()`'s result and the annotation resolve to two distinct types both spelled `TextIO`, most likely a borrow/storage-form split that the message hides. WITHOUT the annotation the same `__init__` reports `Record 'W' has no field 'f'`. "Open a file and keep it" is a basic shape and neither message points at a fix. Shares the identical-display-name rendering problem with the repeated-literal entry above: whatever the underlying distinction is, the diagnostic must spell it. Repros `/tmp/agents/dsr/r26c_textio_field.py` (annotated), `r26_textio_field.py` (unannotated). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `TextIO` PARAMETER is unusable -- the method the API reference lists is not callable on it.** `def emit(f: TextIO, s: str) -> None: f.write(s)` is rejected with `Cannot call method 'write' on type TextIO`, though `write` is `TextIO`'s documented surface (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_io.py`) and works on the `with open(...) as w` binding in the same program. The downstream report adds that the param (arriving as `Ref[TextIO]`) is also rejected by `print(file=...)` as not satisfying `Writable`. So a file handle can be opened and used locally but not passed to a helper, which rules out the ordinary "one function opens, another writes" decomposition. Same family as the field entry above -- both look like the borrow form of `TextIO` losing the type's method surface, so they likely share a fix. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r27b_textio_param.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence) `sum()` over floats accumulates naively where CPython 3.12+ uses Neumaier compensated summation, so the two disagree by an ULP on ordinary data.** CPython's `builtin_sum` has taken the compensated fast path for float sequences since 3.12; TPy adds in a plain loop. Verified: `sum([0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1e16, -1e16])` is `0.6` under CPython and `0.0` under TPy, bit-identical to a hand-written naive loop in the same program (TPy `0.0 0.0 True` vs CPython `0.6 0.0 False`). The downstream report has the realistic form -- summing the 20 edge weights of a TSP tour gives `178.84921988630578` under CPython and `...575` here -- and shows why that is not cosmetic: their `ant` solver keeps a tour when `pathLen > bestLen`, so a one-ULP difference flips the comparison, a different tour is retained, and the divergence compounds across iterations (124 of 400 output lines differed, including entirely different tours, not just trailing digits). No error, no warning, plausible-looking output, visible only against a reference implementation -- the worst failure class this project has. Every float-summing program is exposed and numerical code is squarely in the target audience. Fix: compensate in `sum()` for float element types, matching CPython's fast path; `math.fsum` (already pure-TPy Neumaier) stays the distinct fully-exact variant. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r28_sum.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (missing diagnostic; silently breaks the dual-target promise) A module-level variable annotation that FORWARD-REFERENCES a name compiles under TPy and raises `NameError` under CPython.** `PROTEINS: list[Protein] = []` placed above `class Protein` builds and runs fine under tpyc, which resolves annotations statically -- but CPython evaluates module-level annotations at runtime, so the same file dies at import with `NameError: name 'Protein' is not defined` (both verified). An annotation added to satisfy TPy therefore breaks the CPython half of the dual-target promise, and only running under CPython reveals it -- goal #3 (source stays valid Python, existing tooling works) is exactly what this violates. Fix shape: warn when a module-level annotation references a name defined later in the file; the parser already has definition order, and it converts a run-it-to-find-out failure into a compile-time note. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r17_annot.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) `char` does not satisfy `Comparable`, so `sorted()` over characters is rejected.** `sorted([c for c in "cab"])` errors with `Type 'char' does not satisfy 'Comparable' required by 'sorted'`, though `char` is a `char` and its ordering is well-defined; the workaround is converting each to `str`. Sorting characters is an ordinary idiom (anagram keys, alphabet work). The sibling claim in the same downstream report -- that TUPLES do not satisfy `Comparable` -- is filed as its own entry below; the two are unrelated roots. Repro `/tmp/agents/dsr/r14b_char.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (rejects valid; CPython compares tuples LAZILY and TPy demands total comparability up front) A tuple satisfies `Comparable` only when EVERY element does, so `sorted(d.items())` -- the standard sort-a-dict idiom -- is rejected for any dict whose VALUE type is not itself comparable.** `sorted(d.items())` over `dict[str, list[int32]]` gives `Type 'tuple[str, list[int32]]' does not satisfy 'Comparable' required by 'sorted'`, and `dict[str, P]` for a plain record gives the same. CPython's tuple comparison is short-circuiting -- it compares element 0 and only reaches element 1 on a TIE -- so with unique dict keys the values are never compared and the sort succeeds regardless of their type. TPy's conformance check is total and static, so it rejects a program CPython runs happily; the divergence is not that TPy is stricter about a real hazard, it is that the hazard only exists on a key collision, which for `dict.items()` cannot happen. Note the shape matters and a narrow probe MISSES it: `dict[str, int32]` (both elements comparable) and `sorted([(2, "b"), (1, "a")])` both compile and sort correctly, which is why this was initially mis-triaged here as not reproducing. Fix is a design fork, so this needs `/tpy-add-feature` rather than a patch: either conformance requires only the leading element(s) with a runtime/`static_assert` story for tie-breaks, or `sorted` grows a lexicographic path that only instantiates the comparisons it needs, or the diagnostic at minimum names the offending ELEMENT and suggests `key=`. Repros `/tmp/agents/dsr/r14d_items_noncmp.py` (dict of lists), `r14e_items_record.py` (dict of records).
- **[LOW small] (cosmetic wrong output, every macro-generated body) `emit_source_comments` resolves a macro-synthesized body's line numbers against the ENTRY module's source, so `--dump-code` / `-vv` prints unrelated lines as that body's "source".** [`macro-body-source-echo-wrong-file`] A `quote_fun` / `add_method_from_source` fragment is parsed standalone, so its nodes carry FRAGMENT-local line numbers; `CodeGenContext.emit_source_comment`, `emit_definition_echo` and `source_line_text` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) index `self.source_lines` -- the entry module's lines -- by `loc.line` / `loc.end_line`, with no check that the location belongs to this file. Since the body echo became one block per implementation, the symptom is a wrong RANGE rather than wrong single lines: `Point::field_count()` (fragment `def field_count() -> int32: return 2`) carries `main.py`'s first lines as its signature and body echo (witness `tests/cases/records/macro_quote/expected/include/main.hpp`, the `field_count` definition), and a fragment whose range falls outside the entry module echoes nothing. Cosmetic only -- the emitted code is correct -- but it is live wrong output for every macro-generated body, in exactly the mode a user reads to understand what a macro produced. Fix shape: carry the fragment's own source text on the synthesized function (or on its SourceLocation's `file`) and have the echo helpers read lines from the location's file, not the entry module.
- **[HIGH medium] (rejects valid; most of the stdlib is un-importable) At `--default-int int64` or `BigInt`, 17 stdlib modules fail sema -- at BOTH widths `os`, `os.path`, `os._environ`, `os._native`, `os._types`, `io`, `socket`, `ssl`, `http.client`, `urllib.request`, `asyncio`, `asyncio._executor`, `tplib.requests` (13), plus at int64 only `datetime`, `zoneinfo`, `_datetime_fmt`, `_datetime_parse` (4 more).** Every name is listed, private submodules included, so the list and the count agree. Measured 2026-08-30 by compiling each non-macro `lib/tpy` module as its own entry at each of the three widths: 0 failures at int32, 17 at int64, 13 at BigInt -- 30 module/option pairs. `default_int` is compilation-wide, so a user who picks a non-default width loses those modules and everything importing them; the diagnostics point INTO the stdlib, giving no hint the flag caused it. Two independent root causes, and the stdlib is only the messenger -- both reject the same shapes in user code. (1) **`str`/`bytes` repeat accepts ONLY `int32`**: the stub overload is `def __mul__(self, n: int32) -> str` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_types.py:477`, `lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_types.py:1522`, and the `bytes`/`bytearray` pair in `lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_bytes.py:91,273`), so `"/" * n` for any other width errors `Invalid operand types for '*': str and int64`. This fails at the DEFAULT width too -- `"x" * v` with `v: int64` is rejected under plain int32 -- and it is inconsistent with `list`, where `[1] * v` at `int64` compiles (list repeat goes through `_analyze_list_repeat`, not an overload set). Witness `lib/tpy/os/path.py:105`, `path = "/" * initial_slashes + path`, where `initial_slashes` is an untyped local that takes the compilation's default width. (2) **`str`/`BytesView` search methods return a hard `int32`** (`find`/`rfind`, `lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_types.py:1691,1696,1937,1942`, `_bytes_view.py:73,78`) while an untyped integer local takes the default width, so the two cannot be mixed once the default is not int32: `Invalid operand types for '+': int64 and int32`. Witness `lib/tpy/_datetime_fmt.py:33`, `j = i + rel` with `i = 0` and `rel = fmt[i:].find("%")`. Fix shapes differ: (1) is mechanical -- widen the repeat overloads to the fixed-int family (plus a BigInt arm or an explicit rejection with a narrowing hint), matching what `list` already accepts. (2) is a DESIGN FORK and needs `/tpy-add-feature`, not a patch: either the search methods return the compilation's default int width (consistent with untyped locals, changes a published signature), or fixed-width mixing gets an implicit-widening rule, or the stdlib annotates every such local -- the last keeps the language as-is but leaves the same trap for every user. Reproducers: `"x" * v` with `v: int64` at default options; `i = 0; j = i + s.find("x")` at `--default-int int64`. Surfaced re-measuring the committed stdlib render's option-independence (it is int32-only; the claim that the three widths emit byte-identical C++ was withdrawn at the same time). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` for (1).
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `ValueType` record inside an `Optional` field cannot be member-initialised, though the reference-type sibling can.** [`valuetype-optional-ctor-member-init`] `class Pt(ValueType)` plus `class Holder: p: Pt | None` with `def __init__(self, p: Pt | None): self.p = p` dies with `error: in the constructor of 'Holder': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (ctor.mil_field.optional.name)`. The control is decisive: dropping `(ValueType)` from `Pt` and changing nothing else compiles clean, so this is the value-typed arm of the ctor member-init list specifically, not Optional fields in general. A value type in an `Optional` field is the shape TPy's own `std::optional<T>` storage form is best suited to, which is what makes the gap surprising. Repro `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d2_valuetype_opt_field.py`; control `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d2_control_ref.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A record holding a RECURSIVE-union field is unconstructible -- every constructor spelling rejects.** [`recursive-union-field-unconstructible`] `type Tree = int32 | list[Tree]` plus `class Holder: t: Tree` with `def __init__(self, t: Own[Tree])` refuses `Holder(int32(7))` at `expr.call:call.ctor_arg.own_union` and `Holder([int32(1), int32(2)])` at the same tag; declaring the parameter bare (`t: Tree`) moves the reject to `expr.call:call.ctor_arg.union` but does not admit it. Both union arms and both parameter forms were tried, so the type can be declared and its field spelled, and then no instance of it can be built -- the record is inert. Recursive aliases otherwise work (`tests/cases/union/generic_recursive_return` passes them as params and returns them), so this is the constructor-argument ladder missing the recursive-alias member rather than the alias machinery. Repros `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d3_recursive_field.py`, `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d3b.py` (list arm), `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d3c.py` (bare param). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A redundant `assert isinstance(x, A)` inside a `while isinstance(x, A):` body is a hard compile error.** [`redundant-assert-isinstance-in-while`] The assert rejects at `stmt.assert` when its subject is the name the enclosing loop condition already narrowed. Isolated by four controls, all of which compile: `assert isinstance(x, A)` with no loop; a plain non-isinstance assert inside a `while`; `assert isinstance(x, A)` inside `while True:`; and an UNRELATED assert (`assert t == 0`) inside the same `while isinstance(x, A):` loop. Only the pairing rejects, so the trigger is the assert re-asserting a fact the loop condition established, not asserts in loops and not isinstance asserts. Restating a narrowing inside a loop is a common defensive idiom (and a common way to satisfy an external type checker across an iteration boundary), and it costs a compile error rather than being folded away. Repros `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d4_assert_while.py` and `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p3/d4x.py` (`w1` rejects, `w2` compiles). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) An `Own[<static protocol>]` argument at a MONOMORPHIC callee is refused while the generic twin compiles and runs.** [`generic-equals-monomorphic-twin-own-static-protocol`] `def count(items: Own[Iterable[int32]]) -> int32` -- a plain, non-resumable function -- cannot be CALLED: `count(nums)` rejects with `stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.own_protocol.static` (`expr.call:...` in an expression position), while the identical generic `def count[T](items: Own[Iterable[T]])` compiles, emits `count<int32_t>(std::move(nums))` and runs. A live `generic-equals-monomorphic-twin` drift in the rejects-valid direction: the same source shape is accepted or refused purely on whether the element type is spelled. The `.dyn` sibling of this call-arg gate is tracked separately (the `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` entry); the `.static` face was untracked. Independent of the resumable frame-param gate, which admits both bodies (verified 2026-09-09 -- the mono body is exercised uncalled by `tests/cases/iterators/gen_own_protocol_frame_param`). Loud, not silent. Repro `/tmp/agents/ownproto/p10_plain_own_iterable_mono.py`; borrowed control (`Iterable[int32]`, works) `p2b_borrow_iterable_mono.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) Every `Own[<static protocol>]` argument at a METHOD callee is refused, generic or not.** [`method-arg-own-static-protocol`] `h.indexed(nums)` with `def indexed[T](self, items: Own[Iterable[T]]) -> Iterator[int32]` rejects with `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`, while the borrowed twin (`items: Iterable[T]`) compiles and runs -- so an owned protocol conformer can be passed to a free function but never to a method. Sibling of the monomorphic-callee entry above at the METHOD arg gate, and it does not need the monomorphic spelling to fire. Independent of the resumable frame-param gate (the method BODY admits; only the call face refuses). Loud. Repro `/tmp/agents/ownproto/p7c_method_own_iterable.py`, control `p23_method_borrow_iterable.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) A `@dynamic` protocol param on an `async def` body rejects on the frame; the generator half is fixed.** [`res-param-dyn-protocol-frame`] `async def body(s: Src)` with `@dynamic class Src(Protocol)` rejects with `res.param_type:protocol.dyn.async` (`tests/cases/async/error_async_dyn_protocol_param`), while the generator sibling `def gen(s: Src) -> Iterator[int32]` now compiles on the resumable frame (`Src&` / `const Src&` field -- `tests/cases/generators/dyn_protocol_param_frame`, fixed 2026-09-09). The async half stays rejected because the frame field borrows a call-site adapter, not the argument, and two paths break once the gate is opened -- both probed under a scratch gate patch, neither reachable on stock: (a) `asyncio.create_task(body(im))` BUILDS and SEGFAULTS -- the driver's `__poll__` materializes `::tpy::RefAdapter<Src, Impl> __tmp_1{(*im)};` as a case-block local and the task's frame holds `Src& s` bound to it, so the block exit at the first suspension dangles the reference; reproduced with a module-GLOBAL argument too, so it is a sub-class of `BUGS.md#create-task-ref-param-escape` that its "borrow only module globals" workaround does not cover, and no argument the user can choose makes it safe. (b) `await body(im)` inline is a hard C++ build error -- the sub-coro emplace-arg leaf emits `__sub_0.emplace((*im));`, passing `Impl&` into a ctor taking `Src&`, because that path never applies the `Adapter`/`RefAdapter` wrap every ordinary call site applies (an rvalue conformer additionally loses the wrap through `_hoist_borrowed_args`' lift to `__coro_arg_0`). The static-protocol sibling is unaffected (its frame is templated on the deduced `Impl&`, which points at the driver's own frame field). What keeps the GENERATOR half safe is scope, not an escape check: the adapter is a named local of the block that holds the handle, emitted immediately before it, so it outlives every handle there (a copy into a sibling local included -- that copy copies the frame, `BUGS.md#generator-object-binds-copy-the-frame`, and shares the block). Returning the handle is refused outright (`Iterator` is not a legal return type), and the two shapes that would carry it out of the block -- a container literal holding it (`expr.container_literal`) and a re-seat into an outer binding, the loop-body-creates / outer-pulls form (`stmt.var_decl:reseat.opt_storage_source`) -- are unlowered CODEGEN GAPS. ASAN is green on every shape that IS reachable; a lowering arm for either gap must re-examine the admission in `_res_param_ok`. Repros `/tmp/agents/dynres/esc_task.py`, `esc_task_global.py`, `await_lvalue.py`, `await_rvalue.py`; static control `esc_task_static.py`; inheritance-conformer control `esc_task_inh.py` (no adapter temp, so it would be safe -- not worth a per-argument-kind gate). Fix shape: make the adapter live as long as the frame -- hoist it into the caller's frame (extending `_lift_borrowed_rvalue_args` from "TPy-level rvalue arg" to "codegen-synthesized adapter temp") or capture a `unique_ptr<Src>` holding a `RefAdapter` (the shape the `Own[@dynamic P]` arm already renders) -- plus an adapter wrap on the sub-coro emplace-arg leaf. That is a new frame-capture form and a hidden-allocation decision, so it needs `/tpy-add-feature`, not `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) `Optional[@dynamic P]` is refused at every RECORD-METHOD parameter, though it is the one position the type is meant for.** [`opt-dyn-protocol-method-param`] `def plain(self, s: Src | None) -> int32` with `@dynamic class Src(Protocol)` errors with "Optional[Src] is only supported at a parameter position (where it lowers to a `const Src*` borrow)" -- at a parameter position, so the diagnostic contradicts itself. The free-function twin compiles and runs. `validate_type`'s `allow_pointer_repr_dynamic=True` is passed only from `registration.py:3307` (`register_function`) and `:3634` (stub registration); the record-method registration path never sets it, so a method param is validated as if it were a field. Not resumable-specific (a plain method rejects; the generator/async method rejects at the same place, before the frame gate). `docs/DYNAMIC_PROTOCOL_DESIGN.md` is wrong in the same direction: Phase 7 lists "@dynamic protocol params in record methods/constructors" as Done and Phase 8 says the `Optional` form is allowed "at a parameter position". Constructors reject the same way (`/tmp/agents/dynimpl/opt_ctor.py`). Repro `/tmp/agents/dynres/opt_meth.py` (method, rejects); control `/tmp/agents/dynres/free1_opt.py` (free function, compiles). Fix shape: thread the flag from the record-method (and constructor) registration path, and check whether the message should name the actual blocked position rather than a class of positions. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) A copy warning names the PRIVATE stdlib type behind a public module variable.** [`copy-warning-names-private-stdlib-type`] `outs = [sys.stdout, sys.stderr]` warns twice with "copies _StdStream into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit" -- but `_StdStream` is `lib/tpy/sys.py`'s internal `@native("tpy::StdStream")` class, a name the user never wrote and cannot write (the leading underscore makes it unimportable in spirit), and the suggested remedy `copy(sys.stdout)` is spelled in terms of the value, not the type. Instance of the PITFALLS class "C++ or internal names in diagnostics", one level in: the name is TPy-level but private. The same warning is correct and useful for a user record. Pinned live by `tests/cases/kwargs/kwargs_print_file_elem`, whose `diag.txt` carries the text. Fix shape: when the copied type's qualified name is a private (leading-underscore) library symbol, name the EXPRESSION (`copies `sys.stdout` into owned storage`) or the public alias instead. Surfaced closing the THIR print-file-element row (2026-09-14). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid; the diagnostic names neither the cause nor the remedy) `self.count = 0` in `__init__` -- a field created from anything but a bare parameter -- fails with "Record 'X' has no field 'count'", pointing at the line that creates it.** [`init-field-from-non-param-diagnostic`] `class Box:` / `def __init__(self) -> None: self.n = 7` errors at the assignment itself; the same class with `def __init__(self, n: int32) -> None: self.n = n` compiles. `auto_declare_fields_from_init` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`) infers a field only when the RHS is a TpyName naming an `__init__` parameter, which `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` documents ("computed expressions (`self.f = 0`, `self.f = g()`) still require an explicit class-level annotation") -- so the LIMITATION is by design, but the error text is the generic field-lookup miss from `sema/expressions.py` and reads as if the user misspelled a name. `self.count = 0` is one of the most common shapes in Python, and CLAUDE.md's own style table writes it. Fix shape: at the field-write analysis, when the receiver is `self` inside `__init__` and the name is undeclared, say that the field must be annotated at class level (or assigned from a parameter) and name the annotation to add; widening the inference to literal RHS is a separate design call (the literal's width is the open question). Repro: the two-method `Box` above, compiled as an entry module. Found closing the `nesteddef.name_collision` reject row.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid; internal type name in a user diagnostic) A loop variable bound over an un-annotated int-literal list keeps the LITERAL type, so a later tuple unpack onto that name errors with "expected IntLiteral(7)".** [`literal-loop-var-blocks-unpack-rebind`] `for i in [7, 8]:` / `for i, j in pairs:` (pairs `list[tuple[int32, int32]]`) fails sema with `error: Type mismatch in tuple unpacking: expected IntLiteral(7), got int32`, and the message has no line. Two things are wrong: the loop var over a literal-seeded container is typed `IntLiteralType(7)` rather than the resolved default-int width (a scalar rebind `i = 3` inside the same loop compiles, so only the unpack path notices), and `IntLiteral(7)` is an internal type spelling in a user-facing diagnostic -- the `docs/PITFALLS.md` "no internal names in diagnostics" class. Annotating the outer iterable (`outer: list[int32] = [7, 8]`) compiles. Fix shape: resolve the loop var's literal element type at the binding (`resolve_int_literals` with the compilation's default-int, as the range route already does for its counter), and render literal types by their resolved width in diagnostics. Repro: an unannotated `outer = [7, 8]` with `for i in outer:` wrapped around `for i, j in pairs:`. Pre-existing.

- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence on the VALUE face, pre-existing) `x in xs` over value-typed elements compares with `==` alone, so a NaN needle reports absent although the container holds it.** [`membership-skips-identity-shortcut`] CPython's containment tests `x is e or x == e` per element. The REFERENCE face is closed: a record needle renders `::tpy::seq_contains` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/container_ops.hpp`), which tests address identity before `==`, pinned by `tests/cases/operators/membership_record_needle` and by the runtime self-check `runtime/cpp/tests/test_seq_contains_identity.cpp`. What remains is the VALUE face: `nan = float64("nan"); nan in [nan, 1.0]` is False under TPy and True under CPython. It cannot be closed the same way -- a `float64` element is a bare `double`, not an object, so there is no identity to test; CPython's answer comes from the list holding a boxed float whose `is` succeeds. LANGUAGE NOTE: membership over VALUE elements is `==`-only, and NaN is the one value that makes the difference observable (`docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, Membership). The same `==`-only rule holds for the sibling sequence QUERIES -- `list.index` / `.count` / `.remove` go through `key_eq` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/lookup_key.hpp`) -- and for hashed lookup in `dict` / `set`, where CPython also tries `is` first; those are the same divergence at other operations, and for a reference element they are closable by the same helper. Every reference-typed spelling over a CONTAINER haystack is closed: that haystack has ONE render, `::tpy::seq_contains`, at every needle kind (an open-`T` needle included), so the identity leg is picked per instantiation. The TUPLE-LITERAL haystack is not that render -- `x in (a, b, c)` expands to an `==` OR-chain -- and a record needle against one is rejected at `binop.shape.in.record` rather than answered `==`-only, so the value face above is the only place the `==`-only answer is reached silently. A prior version of this entry priced the whole-corpus swap of `std::ranges::contains` at "about 1500 expected files"; the measured figure is 18 expected files / 46 occurrences, so that option is cheaper than it was recorded to be.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A `char` reprs UNQUOTED, so `list[char]` prints `[a, b, c]` where CPython prints `['a', 'b', 'c']`.** [`char-repr-unquoted`] `s = "abc"; print(list(s))` (or `print([c for c in s])`) prints `[a, b, c]`; bare `repr(c)` prints `a` where CPython prints `'a'`. The runtime has no `char` overload of `print_element` or of `__repr__` -- `str`, `std::string_view` and `String` each have one that routes through `repr_quote_string` -- so a `char` element falls through to the formattable fallback and streams the raw byte. CPython has no char type: iterating a `str` yields one-character `str`s, which repr quoted, so every TPy program that prints a container of characters diverges. Pre-existing (the runtime is untouched by the branch that made `list(s)` compile); reachable before that through a comprehension over a `str`. Fix shape: give `char` the repr of a one-character `str` (quote + escape through `repr_quote_string`) while `str(c)` / bare `print(c)` stay unquoted, and move the `char`-keyed print paths (container element, `repr()`, f-string `!r`) together. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (spurious warning on valid code) An `is not None` test on a SUBSCRIPT does not narrow it, so the guarded read still warns and still takes a runtime null check.** [`subscript-is-not-none-not-narrowing`] `xs[0].val if xs[0] is not None else -1` over `list[Box | None]` warns "Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check" at the read, and so does the statement spelling `if xs[0] is not None: print(xs[0].val)`; the same test over a NAME (`o: Optional[Box]`) or over a FIELD (`h.b`) narrows and stays silent, in the ternary and in the `if` alike. So the subject shape is the gap -- not the ternary, not the container type. An element fact is only sound while nothing writes the container between the test and the read, so closing it means deciding which writes invalidate the fact, not just adding subscripts to the narrowable-subject set. Loud (a warning plus a runtime check), never wrong output. Same family as `comp-filter-none-test-not-narrowing`. The feature side of it is TODO.md's "Subscript-keyed narrowing (`if items[i] is not None: use(items[i])`)" entry, which states the soundness conditions any fix must meet, and the Known Limitations line "Subscript narrowing: `if items[i] is not None:` does not narrow `items[i]`"; this entry is the defect view of the same gap, filed because the warning fires on code that reads correct. Pinned as the current behaviour by `tests/cases/match/optional_subject_subscript`, whose `diag.txt` carries the three warnings. Repro `/tmp/agents/fixc/tern_narrow.py`. Found by the batch-4 review 2026-09-15.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) An ESCAPING (`Callable`) lambda cannot capture an isinstance-NARROWED subject whose member is a reference type.** [`escaping-capture-of-narrowed-subject`] Reads of a narrowed subject inside the closure render the branch's extraction alias, so `_capture_entry_cpp` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) names the alias in the capture list. By REFERENCE (the `Fn` lane) that aliases the subject and is correct. By VALUE it would snapshot the record: `def run(x: A | B)` + `if isinstance(x, A): f: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: x.a` + `x.a = 99` + `return f()` printed 1 where CPython prints 99, while the SAME lambda over the un-narrowed `x` captures the pointer variant `std::variant<A*, B*>` by value and aliases (prints 99) -- so the narrowing alone flipped alias into copy, silently. The escaping lane therefore rejects with a located `expr.lambda` (pinned by `tests/cases/nested_def/error_lambda_narrowed_escaping_capture`); a VALUE-typed member still snapshots, which is what the un-narrowed union capture does too, and stays admitted (`escaping_value` section of `tests/cases/nested_def/lambda_narrowed_capture`). Two candidate fixes, both design: capture the UN-NARROWED subject by value (the pointer variant, which aliases like the un-narrowed program) and re-narrow inside the closure body -- correct but needs the narrowing re-derived at a second site, and the escaping closure then holds pointers into the caller's storage, which is exactly what the escaping lane's by-value rule exists to avoid; or keep the by-value snapshot and WARN, joining `escaping-capture-mutation-snapshot`, which documents the same copy-vs-alias divergence for the un-narrowed reference-type capture and calls it unfixable in the zero-cost model. The second is consistent with the existing rule and is the cheaper answer; the first is the one that matches CPython. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (the choice is a language decision, not a patch). Found by the batch-4 fix round 2026-09-15, which introduced the by-value alias entry; before it the shape reached the toolchain as `'__x' is not captured`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, raw toolchain spew) `sum([x, x])` inside a body generic over a FIXED-INT bound spells the `val_or_ref` trait STRUCT where the return slot wants its `_t` alias.** [`generic-fixedint-sum-val-or-ref`] `def s_use[T: AnyFixedInt](x: T) -> T: return sum([x, x])` emits `return ::tpy::builtin_sum<::tpy::val_or_ref<T>>(std::array<::tpy::val_or_ref_t<T>, 2>{...});` into a function declared `::tpy::val_or_ref_t<T> s_use(...)`, and g++ reports `cannot convert 'tpy::val_or_ref<int>' to 'tpy::val_or_ref_t<int>' {aka 'int'} in return` plus `no matching function for call to 'tpy::val_or_ref<int>::val_or_ref(<brace-enclosed initializer list>)'` in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/builtins.hpp`. No TPy diagnostic and no TPy source line. The `{T}` substitution of the `sum` stub's `@cpp_template("::tpy::builtin_sum<{T}>({0})")` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_funcs.py`) renders an open type param as the trait struct, while the surrounding signature and the array element spelling both use the alias -- the two spellings of one type must be the same one. Repro (whole program): `from tpy import AnyFixedInt, int32` / `def s_use[T: AnyFixedInt](x: T) -> T: return sum([x, x])` / `print(s_use(int32(-3)))`; the `AnyFixedSigned` / `AnyFixedUnsigned` spellings of the bound behave identically. Pre-existing under the `AnyFixedInt` bound; newly reachable under the signed/unsigned sub-protocol bounds since those became sub-protocols of `AnyFixedInt` (before that, sema stopped the program with a located bound error, so the render was never emitted). Toolchain-caught, never silent. Fix shape: make the open-T render inside a `cpp_template` substitution spell the alias the signature spells. Found by the batch-4 fix round 2026-09-15.

- **[MED small] (diagnostic quality) The "upcast narrows" warning names the lost members but not the COPY, so the reader is not told the derived object is sliced away at the storage slot.** [`upcast-warning-omits-slicing-copy`] Admitting a subclass rvalue at a base-typed record field (`_record_slice_upcast_ok`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) leans on sema's warning (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`): "upcast narrows 'Dog' to 'Pet' -- only 'Pet' fields and methods will be accessible; keep the concrete type or make 'Pet' a @dynamic protocol". Everything it says is true and it says nothing about the mechanism: the slot holds a `Pet` and `operator=` slices, so what is stored is a base-only COPY of the source, not the `Dog`. A later `isinstance(self.pet, Dog)` is then False where CPython says True, and a write through the source no longer reaches the field -- both read as unexplained, because the warning the user did see promised only a narrower member set. The divergence is declared, so this is wording, not behaviour. Pinned by `tests/cases/inheritance/upcast_field_rvalue`, whose `diag.txt` carries the current text. Fix shape: the warning names the slicing copy at storage slots (field, container element, `Own[T]`) and keeps the members-only wording where the slot is a pointer and the upcast aliases. It churns every existing upcast snapshot (28 files carry the string), so it is its own unit. Found reviewing the field-rvalue upcast admission 2026-09-15.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A GENERIC function's reference-typed parameter is always a non-const `T&`, so it cannot be spelled const.** [`generic-ref-param-drops-const`] `def has[T: Equatable](xs: list[T], x: T) -> bool: return x in xs` emits `bool has(const std::vector<T>& xs, ::tpy::param_val_or_ref_t<T> x)`, and `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` is `T&` at every reference instantiation -- the trait has no const form and the body's mutation verdict is never consulted, so a generic body that only reads still demands a mutable borrow. Workaround: spell the parameter `readonly[T]`, which renders `::tpy::readonly_form_t<T>` (`const T&` at a reference instantiation) -- used by the generic section of `tests/cases/operators/membership_record_needle` for exactly this reason; note an ARGUMENT at a `readonly[T]` slot is itself a lowering reject today (`call.generic_arg_shape`). Fix shape: a `param_readonly_or_ref_t`-shaped trait selected by the param's own mutation verdict. The CALLER half is CLOSED (2026-09-15, `tpyc/sema/calls.py`, pinned by `tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_keeps_caller_mutable`): a caller passing its own param into an open-`T` slot now keeps that param a mutable borrow, so `for p in pts: has(pts, p)` and `def f(p: Pt): has(xs, p)` build. Consequence of the caller half, measured 2026-09-15: because the slot has no const form, the caller's own const verdict is what has to give -- `def probe(self): me = self; return idf(me)` over `def idf[T](v: T) -> int32` renders `int32_t probe() const` without the caller-half fact and then fails to build (`binding reference of type 'param_val_or_ref_t<Holder>' {aka 'Holder&'} to 'const Holder' discards qualifiers`), so the method is now correctly emitted non-const and the mutation edges carry that to its callers. Closing the CALLEE half is what gives those methods their `const` back. The fact rides `FunctionInfo.mutated_params` today (the call site marks the argument root through `mark_param_mutated`), which is the set every signature consumer already reads as "cannot be const" -- legible but overloaded; splitting "mutated" from "must bind a mutable lvalue" would need a parallel lattice through `MutationCallEdge` and a union at all ~70 `mutated_params` consumers, so it is an architecture row, not part of this fix. Same family as `BUGS.md#nested-def-container-param-drops-const` (a body position whose params never run through the const-borrow verdict), and the last site left open now the resumable frame reads the verdict: here it has nowhere to land, because the SPELLING is a trait with no const variant. Found while pinning the open-T containment needle 2026-09-15. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A protocol method taking a POINTER-VARIANT UNION parameter is unsatisfiable unless the implementation mutates through it.** [`protocol-ref-param-declval-rvalue`] The general defect this entry opened with -- the concept probing every parameter as a prvalue of the bare type, so no `T&` parameter could ever be bound -- is FIXED: `gen_concept_decl` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/protocols.py`) now spells each probe at the param form the protocol's own signature declares, and records, containers, pointer-repr `Optional`s and views conform (pinned by `tests/cases/protocols/proto_param_forms`). What survives is the one form whose const-ness lives INSIDE the type: `def use(self, u: Rec | Other) -> int32` declares `::tpy::Union<Rec*, Other*>`, while an implementation that only READS the parameter infers the deep-const twin `::tpy::Union<const Rec*, const Other*>`, and `std::variant` has no mutable-to-const converting constructor -- so the concept is false and g++ reports `no matching function for call to 'drive(Impl&, ...)'` at the first call through the protocol. A MUTATING implementation conforms (its pointees stay mutable); every other param form is fine because `T&` binds `const T&` and `T*` converts to `const T*`. Workaround: mutate through the parameter, or spell it `readonly[Rec | Other]` on BOTH the protocol and the implementation. Fix shape: the const verdict for a parameter implementing a protocol method must not deviate from the form the protocol declares (a sema/ABI decision, not a spelling one) -- or the concept must accept either pointee const-ness. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/batch7/fixproto/repro/union_param_const_pointee.py`. Sibling of the slugless BigInt-`__getitem__` protocol entry above, which is the free-dunder arm of the same requires-expression. Opened 2026-09-15; narrowed to the union form 2026-09-21 when the param-form probe landed. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (wrong const verdict on an overload set, latent) A resumable frame reads the const-borrow verdict off the LAST overload of its name, not off its own signature.** [`frame-const-verdict-last-overload`] `_frame_deep_const_verdict` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) resolves the frame's per-param verdict with `registry.get_function(func.name)[-1]` (methods: `get_method_overloads(...)[-1]`), the house pattern for a `typing.overload` set, where the last entry IS the single implementation. For a `tpy.dispatch` set every variant is its own implementation with its own params, so every generator variant of a dispatched name would take the last variant's verdict -- a const capture where the body mutates, or the reverse, both of which the C++ build catches rather than miscompiling. Not reachable today: an overloaded generator ICEs before this (the frame struct name is keyed on the bare name, so two variants collide). Fix shape: resolve the FunctionInfo by the function's own identity -- there is no back-pointer from `TpyFunction` to its `FunctionInfo` today, so it wants either that link (set where the fi is registered) or a signature match, and the same `[-1]` lookup in `functions.py` (`_get_func_mutated_params`, `_get_func_addr_escapes`, and the method twins) has the same hole and should move with it. Two more readers key the const-projection verdict on `overloads[-1]` and must move too: `_method_return_const_projected` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, which decides whether a const method's borrowed return is const) and `_own_return_const_projected` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, the lowering's reader of the same fact) -- they also disagree on the fallback when the name has no overload entry (True vs the function's own `is_readonly`), which is the cleanup TODO.md tracks as "one spelling of the const-projected borrow result". Found by the batch-5 review 2026-09-15 (W6). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud; internal name in the diagnostic) A tuple TERNARY mixing a literal arm with a bound-name arm is refused, and the message spells `IntLiteral(n)`.** [`literal-elem-tuple-ternary-mismatch`] `t = (3, "c")` then `return t if f else (4, "d")` at a `-> tuple[int32, str]` return errors *Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'tuple[int32, str]' and 'tuple[IntLiteral(4), str]'* -- the literal arm's element type is never widened against the other arm (or against the return slot, which is right there), and the un-widened spelling reaches the user, which `docs/PITFALLS.md#no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` forbids. Both-name and both-literal arms are fine, so only the MIXED pair trips it. Third instance of the same class as `intliteral-in-span-slice-arg-diag` and `literal-loop-var-blocks-unpack-rebind`: a literal element type escaping the widening that every other position performs. Fix shape: widen a tuple literal's element types against the ternary's other arm / the target slot before the compatibility check, and render literal types distinctly at the diagnostic boundary. Found 2026-09-15 covering the value-tuple ternary return (`tests/cases/tuple/return_value_tuple_ternary` records the gap in its top comment). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) A resumable `for` over a POINTER-FORM loop var on the universal-iterator path passes the raw `T*` to `resumable_iter_next`.** [`frame-ptr-loop-var-universal-iter-source`] `def als(xs: list[ArrayList[int32, 4]]) -> Iterator[int32]: for a in xs: for v in a: yield v` fails the C++ build with `no matching function for call to '__iter__(ArrayList<int, 4>*&)'`: the outer loop binds `a` as a `T*` frame field (`FrameLocalKind.PTR_ALIAS`, the alias the language requires), and the inner loop's `iter_next` advance renders `::tpy::resumable_iter_next(__for_itr_1, a)` (`GenAsyncCodegen._for_src_expr` -> `render_region_expr`), so `S` deduces to the POINTER instead of the pointee. The peephole paths do not hit it -- a `list` / `dict` source takes `begin_end`, which derefs -- so it needs a source whose iteration goes through `__iter__`/`__next__` (a user container such as `tplib.ArrayList`) nested under a pointer-form loop var. Independent of constness: the same program with a MUTATED `xs` (mutable `ArrayList<int,4>* a`) fails identically. Fix shape: the advance's source expression must deref a pointer-form binding, the way the `begin_end` arm's `__for_src` does -- the loop-var form is already known there (`GeneratorForInfo.pointer_form_loop_var` / `ctx.pointer_locals`), so the render reads it rather than re-deriving. Probes `/tmp/agents/vb5/p_items.py` (the `als` section) and `/tmp/agents/vb5b/p_almut.py` (the mutable twin). Found 2026-09-15 while extending the frame const-source verdict to borrowing-view accessors; pre-existing and unrelated to that change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (latent const over-approximation, no corpus witness) The storage-Optional loop var takes ANY method call's RECEIVER as its const source, not only a borrowing view's.** [`comp-storage-opt-const-any-method-recv`] The `foreach.storage_opt_elem` leg (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) and its comprehension twin (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`, `comp.storage_opt_elem`) hop to `stmt.iterable.obj` whenever the iterable is a `TpyMethodCall` before asking `_iteration_yields_const`, on a comment that says the predicate has no method-call arm. It HAS one -- and that arm hops only for a BORROWING VIEW return, which is the correct rule: a view aliases the receiver's storage, a method returning a FRESH container does not. So `for v in obj.make_list():` over `Own[list[P | None]]` off a const receiver registers its loop var in `const_storage_opt_locals` and its consumers spell `const P*` against a mutable temporary -- the same class of spelling/reality split as `BUGS.md#frame-ptr-loop-var-universal-iter-source`'s sibling. No corpus case witnesses it (the shape needs a `T | None` element behind a container-returning method on a const receiver), and the over-approximation is toward const, so the failure mode is a C++ build error rather than wrong output. Fix shape: delete both manual hops and let the predicate's borrowing-view arm answer -- verify no snapshot moves, since that NARROWS what is called const. Found 2026-09-15 clearing the references to the deleted `CodeGenContext.iteration_yields_const`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) A resumable `for` over `.values()` of an EXPLICIT `readonly[dict[K, V]]` parameter spells the view slot off the NON-const receiver.** [`frame-view-slot-ignores-explicit-readonly`] Repro: `from typing import Iterator` / `from tpy import int32, readonly`; `class Node:` with `n: int32` and an `__init__`; `def g_ro(m: readonly[dict[int32, Node]]) -> Iterator[int32]:` with body `for b in m.values(): yield b.n`; `def main() -> None: m: dict[int32, Node] = {3: Node(33)}` then `for v in g_ro(m): print("ro", v)`; then `main()`. The parameter and the frame capture come out `const ::tpy::ordered_map<int32_t, Node>&`, but the source slot is spelled `::tpy::frame_slot<::tpy::dict_values_view<int32_t, Node>>` while `::tpy::dict_values(m)` off a const map returns `dict_values_view<int32_t, const Node>` -- g++ reports *cannot convert 'tpy::dict_values_view<int, const Node>' to 'tpy::ordered_map<int, Node>*'* inside `frame_slot::emplace`. Not specific to a reference-typed value: `readonly[dict[int32, int32]]` fails identically (`dict_values_view<int, const int>` against `<int, int>`). The INFERRED half of the same verdict is correct on this branch -- the same body with a bare `dict[int32, Node]` param spells the slot `frame_slot<decltype(::tpy::dict_values(std::declval<const ::tpy::ordered_map<int32_t, Node>&>()))>` and runs (`tests/cases/generators/frame_const_source_slots`) -- because that deduction is driven by `rcfg.ResumableFuncState.const_frame_bindings` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py`), which is seeded from the MUTATION verdict only; an explicit `readonly[...]` param never enters it, so its slot keeps the pre-branch named-type spelling. Fix shape: an explicit `readonly[...]` parameter seeds `const_frame_bindings` alongside the inferred const-borrow captures, so every slot derived from it -- the `dict_values` / `dict_items` view, its iterators, the loop var -- deduces off the const receiver. Which shape hits which: `.values()` reaches the C++ build (a bare `for k in m:` key loop is fine either way); a `.items()` loop, unpacking or not, rejects EARLIER with `res.local_storage`, the explicit-`readonly[dict]` generator limitation `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` already records -- so the mis-spelled slot is only observable through `.values()`. Pre-existing: identical build failure on master `af4cc05f89`. Found by the round-2 review of THIR batch 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (hidden allocation per iteration, output correct) A resumable `for k, v in d.items()` over a `str` KEY copies the key TWICE per iteration where the sync twin binds a view.** [`frame-items-str-key-copies`] Repro: `def g_items(m: dict[str, list[int32]]) -> Iterator[str]:` with body `for k, vs in m.items(): yield k` then `yield str(vs[0])`, driven from a `main` that fills `m: dict[str, list[int32]]` and prints the yields. The frame declares `std::tuple<std::string, const std::vector<int32_t>*> __for_tup_0;` plus `std::string k;`, and the advance runs `__for_tup_0 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<std::string, const std::vector<int32_t>*>>(*((*__for_it_0))++);` then `k = std::get<0>(__tup_1);` -- one `std::string` copy into the holder and a second into the unpacked field, every iteration. The sync twin (`def s_items(m: dict[str, list[int32]]) -> int32:` with `for k, vs in m.items(): t += len(k) + vs[0]`) binds `auto&& __for_tup_0 = *__beg_0;` and `std::string_view k = std::get<0>(__tup_1);` -- no copy at either step. The list VALUE is already a borrow on both paths (`const std::vector<int32_t>*`); only the `str` key materializes. Frame-lifetime argument for the view: the frame holds the map itself as a reference member (`const ::tpy::ordered_map<std::string, std::vector<int32_t>>& m`) and holds the live `dict_items` view and its iterators in frame slots, all of which must survive every suspension for the loop to be valid at all -- so a `std::string_view` (or a pointer into the map's key storage) is live across the `yield` on exactly the terms the iterator already needs, and the copy buys no lifetime the loop does not already assume. Site: the element spelling of the BORROW_TUPLE frame field (`FrameLocalKind.BORROW_TUPLE`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py`; the field itself is rendered by `gen_coro_struct`) and the `OWNED_STR` form the unpacked key then takes. Fix shape: the holder spells its element forms the way the sync binding's `tuple_to_pointer` target does -- `std::string_view` for a `str` key -- and the unpacked `k` field follows it. `docs/PITFALLS.md` hidden-allocation class. Pre-existing: master `af4cc05f89` emits the same two copies (it differs only in the `const` on the value pointer). Found by the round-2 review of THIR batch 5.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught; a wrong narrow behind it) A resumable `for` over a storage-`Optional` element binds the loop var as a POINTER TO THE OPTIONAL and then reads through it as if it were the payload.** [`frame-storage-opt-loop-var-missing-deref`] Repro: `from typing import Iterator` / `from tpy import int32, Own`; `class P:` with `n: int32` and an `__init__`; `class Maker:` with `base: int32`, an `__init__`, and `def make_list(self) -> Own[list[P | None]]: out: list[P | None] = [P(self.base), None]` then `return out`; `def g(m: Maker) -> Iterator[int32]:` with body `for v in m.make_list(): yield 1 if v is None else v.n`; then a `main` that drives `g(Maker(7))`. The frame declares `std::optional<P>* v = nullptr;` over a `frame_slot<std::vector<std::optional<P>>>` source, and the body renders `v = &(*((*__for_it_0))++);` then `return (((v == nullptr)) ? (1) : (v->n));` -- g++ reports *'class std::optional<P>' has no member named 'n'*. The narrow behind it is wrong too, and would be silent if it built: `v` is the address of a live vector element, so `v == nullptr` is always false and the `None` arm could never be taken. The sync twin of the same body is the model -- `const auto& v = *__beg_0;` with `(((!v.has_value())) ? (1) : ((*v).n))` -- so the frame took the pointer-alias loop-var form while the element stayed storage-form `std::optional<P>`, and neither the `optional_to_ptr` lift nor the storage-form narrow/member spelling followed. Site: the `foreach.storage_opt_elem` leg (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) and the frame local kind it picks. Fix shape: a storage-`Optional` element either binds through `::tpy::optional_to_ptr` (making `v` a real `P*`, which is what the pointer-form narrow and `->` already assume) or stays a storage-form binding whose narrow and member access are spelled `has_value()` / `(*v).` -- the two must be chosen together. Distinct from `BUGS.md#comp-storage-opt-const-any-method-recv`, which is about the same leg's const SOURCE hop (whether the loop var is registered in `const_storage_opt_locals` off a method-call receiver): that is a qualifier question with no corpus witness, while here the qualifier is irrelevant -- the shape fails identically through a mutable receiver -- and the defect is the loop var's FORM, one level below constness. Pre-existing: identical error on master `af4cc05f89`. Found by the round-2 review of THIR batch 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (const lost on valid code, silent; a misleading reject on the `@readonly` twin) A `Ptr[readonly[T]]` destination counts as address-taking FOR WRITE, so `take_ptr(self.field)` costs the method and its callers their `const`.** [`ptr-readonly-dest-counts-as-write`] Repro: `from tpy import int32, readonly, Ptr, take_ptr`; `class Point:` with `x: int32` and an `__init__`; `class Reg:` with `p: Point`, an `__init__`, and `def ptr(self) -> Ptr[readonly[Point]]: return take_ptr(self.p)`; `class Reader:` with `reg: Reg`, an `__init__`, and `def read(self) -> int32: q = self.reg.ptr()` then `return q.x`; then a `main` printing `Reader(5).read()`. It builds and prints, but emits `const Point* ptr();` and `int32_t read();` -- both non-const, although the only pointer leaving `ptr` is a `const Point*` and `read` merely reads through it. The mark is unconditional: the `vpc_active` arm of the `@value_ptr_coercion` argument handling (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`, ~5413) demands `is_mutable_lvalue(source)` and then calls `_mark_addr_taken(source)` without asking whether the destination pointee is a `ReadonlyType`. That same unconditional mutable-lvalue demand is what makes the `@readonly` spelling of the accessor reject outright -- `@readonly def ptr(self) -> Ptr[readonly[Point]]: return take_ptr(self.p)` errors *argument 'p' must be a variable, attribute, or container element (not a temporary or expression)*, a message naming the wrong reason (`self.p` IS an attribute; what it is not is MUTABLE). Reproducing the const loss needs no return at all: `def local_only(self) -> int32: q: Ptr[readonly[Point]] = take_ptr(self.p)` then `return q.x` is non-const too, so this is the ARGUMENT site, not the return site. Same class as the readonly-return fix this branch made at the return position (`tests/cases/readonly/readonly_return_no_write_grant`) -- a const borrow out of `self` records provenance without granting a write -- one annotation away from it. Fix shape: when the resolved `Ptr[...]` param's pointee is a `ReadonlyType`, require only an lvalue rather than a mutable one and register the borrow without `_mark_addr_taken`, which closes both the const loss and the reject; the message on the remaining mutable-`Ptr` case should then say the source must be mutable. Pre-existing: master `af4cc05f89` emits the same two non-const signatures and the same reject. Found by the round-2 review of THIR batch 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (const lost on valid code, silent) An `@auto_readonly` method returning a BARE borrow grants the caller write access, so a caller that only reads loses its `const`.** [`auto-readonly-bare-return-grants-write`] Repro: `from tpy import int32, auto_readonly`; `class Point:` with `x: int32` and an `__init__`; `class Reg:` with `p: Point`, an `__init__`, and `@auto_readonly` / `def view(self) -> Point: return self.p`; `class Reader:` with `reg: Reg`, an `__init__`, and `def read(self) -> int32: v = self.reg.view()` then `return v.x`; then a `main` printing `Reader(5).read()`. `Reg` correctly gets the `@auto_readonly` pair (`Point& view();` and `const Point& view() const;`), but the caller binds the MUTABLE half -- `int32_t read();` with `Point& v = this->reg.view();` -- although `read` only reads `v.x`. The identical body with the return spelled `readonly[Point]` emits `int32_t read() const;` and `const Point& v = ...` (`tests/cases/readonly/readonly_return_no_write_grant`), so the two spellings of "hand out a borrow whose constness follows the receiver" disagree, one annotation apart. Site: the return-borrow marking in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` (~1425), where `ro_return = isinstance(expected, ReadonlyType)` decides whether the escaping roots get `mark_param_mutated(..., through_field=True)` -- an `@auto_readonly` method's expected return type is the BARE `Point` on both halves of the cloned pair, so the mutable half marks `self`, the Phase-2 receiver edge carries that to `Reader.read`, and the const half is never the one the caller's binding selects. Fix shape: the const clone of an `@auto_readonly` method takes the `ro_return` verdict (its return IS a const borrow), leaving the caller's own verdict to choose the half -- which is the point of emitting a pair. Pre-existing: master `af4cc05f89` emits the same non-const `read()`. Found by the round-2 review of THIR batch 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; would dangle) A `spawn` task whose `run()` returns a BARE reference type (a borrow, no `Own`) is accepted by sema and fails in the C++ toolchain.** [`spawn-task-borrow-result-unrejected`] `def run(self) -> list[str]: ...; return self.out` on a `@nocopy` task: sema takes it, `tpy::spawn_thread`'s `using Raw = decltype(task.run())` deduces `std::vector<std::string>&`, and g++ rejects the `tpy::JoinHandle<std::vector<std::string>&>` the factory returns against the `JoinHandle<std::vector<std::string>>` the TPy wrapper expects (*no matching function for call to `JoinHandle(tpy::JoinHandle<std::vector<std::string>&>)`*). Even if the C++ types lined up the value would be a use-after-free: the task is destroyed when `run()` completes (the documented drop-at-thread-completion contract, `docs/THREADING_DESIGN.md`), so the borrow the joiner receives points into a dead task. A thread result is always owned, so a bare reference-typed `run()` return should be a located sema rejection at the `spawn` call site (*a thread result crosses the thread boundary; declare `run() -> Own[list[str]]`*), not a toolchain error with no TPy location. Tightening the `ThreadTask[R]` protocol to `def run(self) -> Own[R]` is NOT the fix: it stops a value-typed `run() -> int32` from conforming at all, so `tests/cases/threading/spawn_inferred` fails with *Cannot infer type arguments for 'spawn'* (measured 2026-09-15). Pre-existing: reproduced on `af4cc05f89` with the stock stub and again after the `join() -> Own[R]` fix (`/tmp/agents/spawn_result/p_borrowret.py`). Found 2026-09-15 while fixing the reference-typed spawn result. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `char` needle in a `set[str]` / `dict[str, V]` membership test rejects at `binop.shape.in`.** [`char-needle-membership-rejects`] `CHARS[1] in st` over `st = {"a", "b"}` prints `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.in)`, while the same needle now lands at every other `str` slot (element, arg, field, dict key) and the `str(CHARS[1])` spelling is accepted. The membership arm keys on the needle's own shape (`_MEMBERSHIP_OPS`'s resolved-`__contains__` row admits scalar and string needles) and never sees the `char_to_str` coercion sema attaches, because the container-member form takes the needle before the coerce arm. Fix shape: let the membership needle read the same `builds_fresh_value` coercion the other `str` sinks read, so the needle renders its own `std::string(::tpy::char_to_str(c))` -- or, better for a lookup, resolve the needle against the view (`char_to_strview`) so no allocation is made for a `contains` call. Probe `/tmp/agents/char_str_slot/sinks/s19_member.py`. Found 2026-09-15 enumerating the str-typed sinks for the char-at-a-str-slot family.

- **[LOW small] (missing diagnostic) The ALL_CAPS-without-Final warning never fires on an UNANNOTATED global whose initializer is an int, float or str literal -- exactly the spelling the warning exists to catch.** [`all-caps-warning-misses-literal-globals`] `WIDTH = 800` / `RATE = 1.5` / `TAG = "hi"` at module level compile silently, while `HEIGHT: int32 = 600` and the unannotated `FLAG = True` both warn `ALL_CAPS variable 'X' without Final annotation`. The unannotated arm in `_analyze_var_decl` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`, "Unannotated top-level ALL_CAPS") passes the RAW `init_type`, which for those literals is still `IntLiteralType` / the pending float / str literal form; `is_final_allowed_inner` (the `_warn_all_caps_without_final` gate) answers False for a pending literal type, so the warning is dropped. `True` has no pending form, which is why the bool case slips through and looks like the warning works. Fix shape: resolve the literal type before the gate (`resolve_int_literals` with the module's `default_int_for_literal`, and the view/str resolution the deduction pass applies), mirroring the top-level tuple-unpack arm which already resolves before recording the global. Expect snapshot churn: the new warning lands on every existing case with an unannotated ALL_CAPS literal global. TODO.md's mandelbrot entry ("the ALL_CAPS warning steers users into it") assumes the warning DOES fire on `MAX_ITER = 1000`; it does not. Probe `/tmp/agents/module_global/caps2.py`. Found 2026-09-15 while fixing the inferred-global export path.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid at four faces) A module-level binding first made INSIDE a block body gets no module slot, so it can be neither imported nor borrowed from.** [`block-level-module-binding-has-no-slot`] `try: X = 1` / `except ImportError: X = 2` at module level -- and the `if` / `for` / `while` spellings -- is everyday Python, but such a binding is emitted as a block-local of the generated `__tpy_init`, with no namespace-scope declaration. Four faces on that one missing storage: `from gmod import LOOPY` rejects with `'LOOPY' not found in module 'gmod'`; `gmod.LOOPY` rejects with `'gmod' is not a variable`; a borrow return of the name (`def view() -> StrView: return LAST` after `for w in [...]: LAST = w`) rejects with `Undefined variable: 'LAST'`; and a plain read from a function in the SAME module (`for i in range(3): MV = i + 1` at module level, `def show(): print(MV)`) rejects with `Undefined variable: 'MV'` although the top-level `print(MV)` right after the loop compiles and prints the right value (`/tmp/agents/p7_mod.py` and `/tmp/agents/round1_apply/t_mod_toponly.py`, verified 2026-09-16). The tuple-unpack spelling (`for i in range(2): A, B = (i, i + 1)`) behaves the same. Site: `SemanticContext.is_module_slot_stmt` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) answers no for anything but a direct element of the module's statement list, which is exactly what the generator's `seen_globals` walk (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py`) emits declarations for -- so sema and codegen agree, and both agree that nothing is there. Fix shape: hoist a block-level top-level binding to a module slot, declared at namespace scope and assigned where the block assigns it, gated on a definite-assignment fact (a name only one branch binds must still be an error at the read, as CPython's `NameError` is). That fact does not exist for module code today -- `_analyze_top_level` merges branch state but nothing records "definitely bound when module init ends" -- so until it does, the located rejection above is the correct behaviour rather than a workaround. Probes `/tmp/agents/fix_module_global/{gmod.py,p2_main.py,p3_main.py,p8.py,p9.py,p15.py}`. Pinned as a rejection by `tests/cases/imports/error_import_block_level_global` (the import faces) and `tests/cases/imports/error_block_level_global_borrow_return` (the borrow-return face). **Settle it together with `top-level-loop-local-static-slot`**, the sibling defect over the same storage: that one is about a block-level top-level binding codegen DOES emit, as a function-local `static` that constructs once. The two fix shapes pull in opposite directions -- this entry wants the slot lifted OUT of the block to namespace scope (so it outlives `__tpy_init` and can be imported and borrowed), that one wants a NON-static, per-iteration slot (so each pass reconstructs). One fix has to satisfy both: a namespace-scope slot that is *assigned* where the block assigns it, not initialized there (the `GLOBAL_HOIST_RVALUE` shape the for-body entry at the top of this section already names). Surfaced by the round-1 review of the inferred-module-global fix, which had widened sema to certify these bindings while codegen still emitted none for them. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; one unlocated C++ error) The `char` a string index yields still misses five `str`-family slots.** [`char-at-str-residual-slots`] The sinks that route through `compat.coerce_expr` or the dict-key check now admit a `char` and spell it as the one-character string (`tests/cases/str/char_at_str_slots`); these five do not, all pre-existing and none char-specific in their site: (1) a `*args: str` pack emits `std::array<const std::string, N>{<char>}` and dies in g++ with no TPy location, while the `*args: int32` sibling materializes correctly at the same site (`/tmp/agents/fix_char/va.py`); (2) `acc += CHARS[i]` on a `str` local -- *Augmented assignment value must be a string type, got char* (`/tmp/agents/fix_char/augadd.py`); (3) a `str | None` FIELD write -- *not yet supported ... (assign.field_write_shape)*, where the plain `str` field now lowers (`/tmp/agents/fix_char/optfield.py`); (4) a ternary arm -- *Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'char' and 'str'* (`/tmp/agents/fix_char/tern.py`); (5) `CHARS[0] == "ab"` -- *not yet supported ... (binop.shape.==)*, though the one-char compare works through the char overload (`/tmp/agents/fix_char/cmp.py`). Rows 2-5 are sema or lowering gates that enumerate the SOURCE type/shape instead of asking whether a coercion resolves for the pair; row 1 is the varargs pack builder, whose element slot is the same aggregate-element position `Coercion.builds_fresh_value` already governs -- it just never materializes. Fix shape: one pass over these five reading the same fact the other sinks read. The sixth row -- a BORROWED `str` parameter materializing an owning `std::string(::tpy::char_to_str(c))` into a `std::string_view` slot -- is CLOSED: `char_to_borrowed_str` (`tpyc/coercions.py`) is the rule at a sink that does not own, so the param and the dict LOOKUP key both view the immortal one-char table. Siblings already filed separately: `char-needle-membership-rejects`, `char-tuple-literal-admission`. Found 2026-09-15 in the review of the char-at-a-str-slot fix.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A SYNC `with` whose `__enter__` / `__exit__` is `@error_return` is a hard compile error; the `async with` faces cannot occur.** [`with-header-error-return-dunder`] `__aenter__` / `__aexit__` must be `async def`, and `async def` + `@error_return` is refused upstream at registration (*async def + @error_return is not yet supported on '...'*, verified 2026-09-15 with `/tmp/agents/r3_fix/p10_async_er.py`), so the reject scans them only so it stays total if that restriction lifts. `with r as v:` where `Res.__enter__` carries `@error_return(Gone)` now reports *`__enter__` on 'Res' returns an error with @error_return, which a `with` statement has no way to handle*.
