Before this reject the shape MISCOMPILED: the header calls the dunder implicitly, so it never reached `_check_error_return_handled` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`), the only site that decides whether an enclosing try/except admits an error return -- the target bound the raw `std::expected` and g++ failed with no TPy location (`/tmp/agents/r2/p7_sync_notry.py`), and inside a generator's decomposed try the frame emitted `v = (*__with_ctx_0).__enter__();` with no unwrap while `TpyTry.handled_error_return` stayed False (`/tmp/agents/r2/p7_with.py`). Fix shape for the FEATURE: give the `with` header the same unwrap-and-dispatch a plain call gets -- route the dunder through `_check_error_return_handled` so an enclosing try is credited, peel the error type off `item.enter_type`, and render the unwrap in `_lower_with` (and, in a frame, in the region the return-tier try builds). The reject reads EVERY overload variant of the dunder, not the first: the header resolves nothing (a dunder has no arguments beside `self`), and an `__enter__` overloaded on `self` const-ness with the `@error_return` variant second used to slip past it into a `stmt.with` lowering reject. Pinned as a rejection by `tests/cases/control_flow/error_with_error_return_enter`, whose subject is that overloaded spelling. Found 2026-09-15 in the round-2 review of the frame-try fix.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Two spellings of a BORROW-returning context manager still reject: a FREE call, and a method call whose `with` body suspends.** [`with-borrow-call-manager-faces`] `with lend(b) as q:` over `def lend(b: B) -> Guard: return b._guard` reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.with`)*, and `with b.guard_m() as q:` with a `yield` or an `await` inside the body reports `res.with_manager` -- while the same method call around a SUSPENSION-FREE body, and the `@property` spelling of either, compile and bind the manager borrowed (2026-09-21). The two faces have different owners. The free call is held out at the sync manager gate (`_lower_with` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) because the term that keeps the method spelling honest -- the RECEIVER is not a temporary -- has no free-call counterpart: the result borrows from the ARGUMENTS, and nothing decides that today (`with lend(mk()) as q:` would bind into a dying object). The suspending face is the resumable skeleton's own manager gate (`tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`), which admits the name / field / getter rows the sync gate had before the call row was added. Workaround for both: bind the manager first (`g = lend(b)` / `g = b.guard_m()`, then `with g:`). Fix shape: an argument-provenance fact for the free call, and the call row mirrored into the resumable gate. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/w2decl/matrix_s8.py`, `probe_suspend.py`.

- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic on code CPython also rejects) Reading a function's fresh local before its bare write is reported as a not-yet-supported `name.global_read`, never as an unbound local.** [`unbound-local-read-reported-as-global-read`] `COUNT = 10` at module level plus `def f(): x = COUNT; COUNT = 5` is CPython's `UnboundLocalError` shape: the bare write binds a fresh local for the whole body, so the earlier read has no value. TPy is right to stop the compile, but says *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:name.global_read)* (`stmt.expr_stmt:name.global_read` when the read is a bare `print(COUNT)`), which points the user at codegen and at the GLOBAL rather than at the local that shadows it. Sema resolves the read against the module global (the fresh-local verdict is decided at the WRITE, `tpyc/sema/statements.py` `_analyze_var_decl` / the tuple-unpack arm via `compat.is_local_shadow`), so the read is still typed as a global and only the lowering gate `_readonly_global_type` refuses it. Fix shape: the prescan that hoists a function's local names already knows the name is written somewhere in the body, so a read that precedes the first write in that function should be a located sema error naming the local (*local variable 'COUNT' referenced before assignment*), which also removes the accidental reliance on a lowering reject. Repro `/tmp/agents/r2_docs_tests/p2.py` (expr-statement read) and `p3.py` (var-decl read); the same program under `PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy uv run python` raises `UnboundLocalError`. The ATTRIBUTE-receiver spelling of the same read is the one that does NOT stop -- [`read-before-local-shadow-resolves-global`] -- and the other rejected shadow shapes are [`global-shadow-shapes-rejected-not-diverging`]. Documented as-is in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` ("Variables & Scope"). Found 2026-09-15 probing the fresh-local rule for the docs pass. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, unlocated) An `@error_return` `__getitem__` or `__add__` makes the record's generated operator bridge return the raw `std::expected`, and the C++ build fails at the class definition.** [`error-return-operator-bridge-unlocated`] `@error_return(Gone) def __getitem__(self, i: int32) -> int32` emits `std::expected<int32_t, Gone> __getitem__(int32_t) const;` next to `int32_t operator[](int32_t i) const { return __getitem__(i); }`, and g++ says *cannot convert 'std::expected<int, Gone>' to 'int32_t' in return* against the generated header with no TPy location; `__add__` fails identically through `operator+`. Same root as [`with-header-error-return-dunder`]: an IMPLICIT caller of a dunder never reaches `_check_error_return_handled` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`), the one site that decides whether an enclosing try/except admits an error return. Unlike the `with` header this one dies before any body is lowered, so no generator/async face differs -- the sync free function, the method and the frame positions all fail at the same line. The dyn-attribute dunders (`__getattr__` and friends) already reject `@error_return` at registration (`_validate_dyn_dunder`, `tpyc/sema/registration.py`); the operator dunders do not. Fix shape: the same choice the `with` header took -- either reject `@error_return` on a dunder whose only caller is an implicit operator bridge, with a located diagnostic, or give the bridge the unwrap-and-dispatch a plain call gets. Probes `/tmp/agents/r3_fix/p_getitem.py`, `/tmp/agents/r3_fix/p_add.py`. Found 2026-09-15 narrowing `_build_try`'s comment about which implicit callers bypass the chokepoint. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A CONTAINER-typed SUBSCRIPT passed to a METHOD rejects at `method.arg_shape`, while the free-function twin lowers.** [`container-subscript-into-method-arg`] `xs: list[list[str]] = [["a", "b"], ["c"]]` then `" ".join(xs[0])` reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.expr_stmt:method.arg_shape)*, while the same source at a free function (`take(xs[0])` for `def take(ss: list[str])`) compiles and runs, and binding the element first (`t = xs[0]; " ".join(t)`) is the workaround. The subscript already yields the element in borrow form -- the fact the method-arg table needs -- so this is the arg table in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` enumerating admitted SOURCE nodes for a container-typed param slot rather than asking whether the source's form already matches the slot -- the same gate shape the container ELEMENT slot had until `_container_storage_call_rvalue` gave it one form verdict to read. Everyday shape: any `str.join` / method call over a row of a list-of-lists or a dict value. Repros `/tmp/agents/r3_polish/p2.py` (reject) and `p3.py` (the two controls), verified 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Found 2026-09-15 writing the comprehension section of `tests/cases/threading/spawn_reference_result`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) A `bytearray` argument at a borrowing `bytes` parameter loses its identity the moment the callee OWNS the value -- at a return, and at `dict.get` / `dict.pop`'s default.** [`bytearray-at-bytes-param-owned-silently`] `def take(x: bytes) -> bytes: return x` called as `take(ba)` over `ba = bytearray(b"zz")` hands back a fresh `Bytes` copy: TPy prints `got b'zz'` / `after b'zz'` where CPython prints `bytearray(b'zz')` / `bytearray(b'zzA')` once `ba.append(65)` has run (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_fix/pret.py`). The dict face is `b: dict[str, bytes]` + `b.get("z", ba)` (and `b.pop`), same divergence (`/tmp/agents/review_b4/p_bytearray_default.py`). `dict.setdefault` is NOT affected: its stub declares `default: Own[V]` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_dict.py`), so `b.setdefault("z", ba)` reaches the located rule and says *expected bytes, got bytearray -- write 'bytes(...)' around it* (verified 2026-09-15). A `bytes` PARAMETER is a `BytesView`, so the bytearray-to-bytes row is `borrow_only` and `_sink_owns_its_value` admits it at `CoercionContext.ARG` -- correct while the view does not outlive the call, and unsound as soon as the callee materializes an owned `bytes` from it, which the RETURN and the two remaining dict defaults do. The OWNING sinks the caller can see (a local, a field, a container element) do reach the located rule; the parameter never does, which is the same gap as [`bytes-at-bytearray-param-unlocated`] in the opposite direction. The `void`-returning `take(ba)` is NOT a bug and must stay admitted, so the fix cannot simply make ARG owning: it needs a decision on which callee-side sinks make a borrowed parameter's cross-buffer conversion observable, and whether the answer at the call site is a reject or a warning. **On the dict face specifically:** an earlier round measured `Own[V]` on the `get` / `pop` stubs and rejected it, but that measurement predates the runtime change that gave the three natives their own `DefArg&&` parameter (2026-09-15). After it, `setdefault`'s `Own[V]` slot demonstrably accepts every borrow-form default -- a bare literal, a `String` lvalue, a `char`, a `BytesView` (`tests/cases/dict/dict_setdefault`) -- while still catching the bytearray, so the same slot on `get` / `pop` is viable and would close the dict face without touching the parameter question. Its cost is visible in the same snapshot: an `Own[V]` default is materialized on the HIT path too (`std::string __tmp_1{lv}` before a `setdefault` whose key is present), where the `default: V` slot passes the borrow straight through. Whether to spell it that way is a user decision, still open. The dict-default face REGRESSED from an unlocated g++ deduction error to a silent copy when `dict_get_default` / `dict_pop_default` took their default through `DefArg&&`; that error was not something a user could act on, so what regressed is visibility, not correctness. `tests/cases/dict/dict_get_default` now spells the explicit `bytes(ba)` at that slot and prints the values, so the case does not depend on the undecided shape. Surfaced 2026-09-15 by the review round over that runtime change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong value; and an over-reject at the rebound-global borrow rule) A walrus inside a LAMBDA body writes the ENCLOSING scope's slot instead of the lambda's own local.** [`lambda-body-walrus-binds-enclosing-scope`] `NOTE = "hello world"` at module level, `def touch(): global NOTE; return len(apply(lambda n: (NOTE := n)))` with `def apply(g: Fn[[str], str]) -> str: return g("inner")`: TPy prints `after inner`, CPython prints `after hello world` -- in CPython the walrus binds a LOCAL of the lambda (a lambda is its own scope, and a `global` declaration in the enclosing function does not reach into it), in TPy it writes the module slot (probe `/tmp/agents/r5/walrus_lambda2.py`). The same divergence applies to an enclosing FUNCTION local, not just a global. The consequence at the borrow rule is an over-reject: `prescan.walrus_names_of` runs `_kills_in_expr`, whose generic field walk descends into `TpyLambda.body`, so `global NAME` + `lambda n: n + len(NAME := "x")` counts as the outer function's rebind and a `StrView` returned off `NAME` elsewhere in the module is refused, on a program CPython accepts (probe `/tmp/agents/archfit/lam2.py`). Counting it is deliberate for now -- it keeps the rebind facts consistent with what codegen actually EMITS -- so the over-reject must be lifted in the SAME change that fixes the scoping, not before it: the parser's `written_names` / `walrus_bindings` already stop at the lambda boundary (`TpyLambda.children()` is empty), and `walrus_names_of` becomes a call to `written_names` once the emit agrees with Python. Sibling of [`nested-local-shadows-module-global`] and [`nested-local-shadow-requires-nonlocal`]: the same failure to give an inner scope its own bindings, in the one scope that is an expression. Found 2026-09-15. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) Unwrapping an `@error_return` call that returns `str` binds a VIEW into the try temp, which dies at the end of the unwrap block.** [`error-return-str-unwrap-dangles`] `@error_return(Missing) def checked(v: float) -> str` called as `try: er1 = checked(1.0) / except Missing: er1 = "raised"` emits `std::string_view er1;` then, inside a nested block, `auto __try_tmp_2 = checked(1.0); ... er1 = ::tpy::unwrap_ref_move(*__try_tmp_2);` -- the `std::expected<std::string, Missing>` temp is destroyed at that block's closing brace, so `er1` points at freed storage. With a single try the stale bytes usually survive to the next statement and the program looks right; a SECOND try/except reuses the memory and the value prints as garbage (`error-return     raised` where CPython prints `error-return hit raised`). The plain, non-fallible twin is correct: `a = make(1)` with `def make(v: int) -> str` declares `std::string a`, an owning slot. So the defect is the unwrap destination's form, not the `str` return -- the try-unwrap path gives the local the borrowed `str` parameter form where the call RESULT is owned. Silent: no diagnostic, and it compiles clean. Same borrow-form-into-an-owning-slot family as the fixed coro-frame view local; the sibling to check is a `bytes`/`BytesView` return, not probed. Fix shape: declare the unwrap destination in the owning form for a value type that owns a buffer (`std::string` / `::tpy::Bytes`), as the plain call assignment already does -- hoisting the try temp out of the nested block would also stop the dangle but leaves the local a view into a temp that dies at the try's end. Probes `/tmp/agents/match_literal/er5.py` (no `match` involved) and `er3.py`. Found 2026-09-15 writing the `@error_return` section of `tests/cases/match/numeric_literal_kinds`, whose section therefore returns `int32`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A dict comprehension whose VALUE is an `Own[C]`-returning call infers `dict[K, Own[C]]`, and the `Own` in the value slot rejects the whole comprehension at `comp.route`.** [`dict-comp-value-keeps-own`] `def make(n: int32) -> Own[list[str]]` then `dc = {i: make(i) for i in range(2)}` reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.dict_comp)*, while the same comprehension with the slot SPELLED (`dc: dict[int32, list[str]] = {...}`) compiles and runs, and the list-comp sibling (`[make(i) for i in ...]`) compiles unannotated. The route gate (`_comp_lowering_route`, `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`) asks `_comp_elem_slot_ok(args[1], allow_container=True)` of the VALUE slot, and `_container_family_slot` does not peel `OwnType` -- correctly, since an `Own[...]` DICT VALUE is not a container slot. The defect is upstream: sema's dict-comp result inference carries the value expression's declared `Own[list[str]]` into the dict type, where the list-comp element inference peels it (measured 2026-09-15: the route sees `dict[int32, Own[list[str]]]`). `Own[T]` is an ownership-transfer marker at a call's RETURN, not a storage type, so the inferred container type should be `dict[K, C]` exactly as the list comp's is. Fix site: the comp result-type inference in sema, peeling `Own` off the value expression's type the way the list-comp element path does. Found 2026-09-15 fixing the container-element-from-call reject (closed the same day: an `Own`-returning call is admitted and moved at every container-element slot), whose element-slot face is fixed; this is what still blocks the UNANNOTATED dict-comp spelling. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud -- the warning's own remedy does not compile) `copy(<borrowing call>)` is not admitted at a CONTAINER element slot, so the escape hatch the copy warning names is unavailable there.** [`copy-marker-at-container-elem`] `def borrow_rows(n: int32) -> list[str]` then `[borrow_rows(i) for i in [1, 2]]` warns *copies list[str] into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit* and rejects (correctly -- the element is a borrow); the spelling the warning prescribes, `[copy(borrow_rows(i)) for i in [1, 2]]`, rejects too, at `expr.list_comp`. The `copy()` marker has its own render (`std::vector<std::string>(x)`, not the bare call), so it is a row of its own everywhere: the `Own[T]` ARGUMENT slot has it (`_copy_own_arg`, the `copy_own` row -- `xs.append(copy(borrow_rows(i)))` compiles), and the container-literal element's RECORD family has it (`copy_construct_source` in `_container_lit_elem_ok`'s `fam == "record"` arm). The CONTAINER family of the same arm, and `_lower_comp_container_elem`, do not. Fix shape: the container arm reads `copy_construct_source` the way the record arm does, with the matching `_lower_copy_record`-style element render for a container payload. Probe `/tmp/agents/container_elem/p14.py`. Found 2026-09-15 fixing the container-element-from-call reject (closed the same day). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught for a NON-empty element; rejects valid, loud for an empty one) A nested container LITERAL element cannot share a literal with an element that forces the reserve+emplace helpers.** [`container-lit-empty-elem-under-emplace`] `lv: list[list[str]] = [make_rows(1), []]` (with `def make_rows(n: int32) -> Own[list[str]]`) rejects at `expr.container_literal` (detail `containerlit.make_empty_elem`), although each element compiles on its own. Any element that forces the reserve+emplace helpers over the brace-init -- a movable local at its last use, a `@nocopy` slot, or a call whose prvalue IS the slot's storage container -- takes the whole literal off the brace-init, and an empty nested literal has no type to deduce from once each element deduces from its own argument (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`, the `containerlit.make_empty_elem` guard). Fix shape: under `make_container` the empty nested element spells its type (`std::vector<std::string>{}`) instead of rendering a bare `{}` -- a prvalue binds the helper's forwarding reference and `emplace_back` still MOVES it, so the spelling costs no copy; the guard's claim that spelling would lose the move is wrong. The empty element's `bare_empty` is decided in `_lower_container_elem_impl` from `elem_storage`, which presumes a brace-init parent, so the parent's `make` verdict has to reach it. Probe `/tmp/agents/container_elem_fix/p7.py`. Surfaced 2026-09-15 while routing the owned-call container element off the brace-init. AMENDED 2026-09-16 (batch-6 master-merge hunt): the NON-empty sibling is worse -- it passes the compiler and fails the C++ build. `ml: list[list[float]] = [[1.0], loc]` with `loc: list[float]` a movable local at its last use, and `mixed: list[list[float]] = [[1.0], make_row(2)]` (the call-rvalue trigger), both emit `::tpy::make_vector<std::vector<double>>({1.0}, std::move(loc))`, and `make_vector(Args&&... args)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/ranges.hpp` ~112) cannot deduce `Args&&` from a braced-init-list: g++ *too many arguments to function ... [with Args = {}]*. Pre-existing at the base for the movable-local trigger; the call-rvalue element verdict added a second trigger. Same fix: under `make_container` every nested literal element spells its type. Probes under the batch-6 scratch dir `mergehunt/d.py`, `e.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) `list(gen)` over a generator that yields REFERENCE elements builds the list by COPYING each element, where the comprehension twin warns.** [`list-over-generator-copies-ref-elems-silently`] `got = list(each(pts)); got[0].x += 100` leaves `pts[0].x` at `1` under TPy where CPython reads `101` (`/tmp/agents/review_b2/p9.py`); `[p for p in each(pts)]` on the same generator emits *copies Point into owned storage; use copy()* (`p10.py`), so the two spellings of one store disagree, and the `list()` one is the silent one. Pre-existing on a MONOMORPHIC generator (`p11.py`), so it is the `list()` conversion, not the generic yield slot. Fix shape: the `list()` / `set()` / `dict()` constructor over an iterator of borrow-form elements must read the same owning-slot verdict the comprehension element reads (warn and copy, or reject for `@nocopy`), decided where that verdict lives rather than in the constructor lowering. Found 2026-09-15 by the bundle-2 parity review.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NEGATIVE numeric literal pattern (`case -1:`) is refused by the parser for every subject kind.** [`negative-literal-pattern-unsupported`] `match n: case -1: ...` reports *Unsupported match value pattern* (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`, the value-pattern arm sees a `UnaryOp` instead of a `Constant`); PEP 634's `literal_pattern` admits signed numbers, and CPython matches `-1`. Same for `-1.0` and for a negative literal inside a record-field or or-pattern. Fix shape: the parser folds a unary minus over a numeric constant into the literal at the one place it builds literal patterns, so the numeric-family validator (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) and the switch-tier label rule see an ordinary literal; the lowering already spells a negative label. Probes `/tmp/agents/review_b2/p14.py`, `p15.py`. Nearest neighbour of the cross-kind numeric literal fix of 2026-09-15, which did not touch the parser.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; `generic-equals-monomorphic-twin`) A container literal or comprehension of `Own`-returning calls REJECTS inside a GENERIC body where the monomorphic twin lowers.** [`generic-container-elem-from-call-rejected`] `def build[T](xs: list[T]) -> Own[list[list[T]]]: return [make(x) for x in xs]` (with `make(x: T) -> Own[list[T]]`) reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.container_literal)* / `(expr.list_comp)`, while the same body over `Point` compiles and moves. The element-slot admission `_container_storage_call_rvalue` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) reads `_storage_call_ret`, which does not see through an open `T` element, so the storage-form verdict is `None` at definition time. Fix shape: the verdict is about the CALL's return form (`Own[container]` is owning whatever `T` is), so `_storage_call_ret` should answer from the declared return's ownership rather than from the resolved element type. Probe `/tmp/agents/review_b2/r2/gen_twin.py`. Found 2026-09-16 by the bundle-2 safety review.

A field or subscript subject (`match p.i:`) on the guarded chain is a located `stmt.match` reject for exactly this reason -- an admission attempted 2026-09-16 was reverted the same day after the review probed the mutation: beyond the wrong answer, a SUBSCRIPT subject whose guard grows the container (`match xs[0]: case 1.0 if grow(xs):`) reallocates under the alias and the later arms read freed memory (`/tmp/agents/review_b2/r3/m4.py`) -- so only the name face diverges silently. Landing it also closes [`read-before-local-shadow-resolves-global`] and the wording halves of [`unbound-local-read-reported-as-global-read`] and [`global-shadow-shapes-rejected-not-diverging`]. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `bytes` value in an f-string is rejected by sema, where CPython interpolates its repr.** [`bytes-in-fstring-rejected`] `print(f"v={b}")` for any `bytes` expression -- a literal, a local, a field read -- fails with *bytes cannot be used in f-string (no `__str__` or `__repr__` method)*, while CPython prints `v=b'tt'`. `print(b)` on its own is fine (the print sink has `::tpy::BytesPrinter`), so the gap is only the interpolation: the f-string arg site asks the type for a `__str__`/`__repr__` and the `bytes` stub declares neither, though the runtime already renders the same text through `BytesPrinter`. - **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A branch-FIRST `Optional[T]` local whose source is an optional FIELD read off an rvalue receiver rejects, where the straight-line decl and every rebind of it compile.** [`branch-first-opt-field-rvalue-source-rejected`] `if x > 1: p: Point | None = make_holder(x).value` / `else: p = None` with a read after the `if` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.var_decl:reseat.branch_rvalue_source`)*. The VALUE-position field read is the only sink with the hole: measured against the same un-narrowed param, the aug-assign (`stmt.aug_assign`), method call (`method.recv.field_chain`), `len` (`call.native_arg.container`), `print` (`print.arg.container_field_access`), element bind (`decl.slot_type`), field write (`assign.field_write_shape`), nested setitem (`setitem.recv.field_chain`), nested element-field read `d[0].rows[0]` (`subscript.recv.field_chain`), nested read `d[0][0]` (`subscript.recv.subscript`) and for-each over `d[0].rows` (`foreach.field_parent`) all reject, located. The two NESTED reads briefly admitted -- and emitted the unchecked `__getitem__((*d), 0)` nest -- while the rooted-lvalue walk had no view of the narrowing proof; the hop predicate inside `_lvalue_chain_root` now requires it (`tests/cases/optional/error_unnarrowed_opt_elem_chain` pins the boundary, `optional/narrowed_opt_container_elem` the narrowed twins). Distinct from its two nearest siblings: `optional-list-elem-decl-drops-deref-check` is the DECL face (`r = xs[0]` binding an Optional ELEMENT, which is why its render is `optional_to_ptr(...)`), and `unnarrowed-optional-subscript` is the INDEX face (a `deref_optional_check`ed receiver whose index normalisation is dropped) -- this one normalises the index correctly and drops the RECEIVER check instead. Fix shape: the field-read arm's receiver unwrap must key on sema's proof (the same `needs_optional_runtime_check` the element-borrow shell rejects on) and render `deref_optional_check` when the proof is absent, rather than on pointer-binding membership; the three entries then share one receiver-unwrap helper. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch6_review/review/codegen/p16.py`; sink sweep `/tmp/agents/batch6_review/item1/unproven/`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of batch 6. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (front-end perf) Resolving a subscript's chained RECEIVER re-walks the chain once per hop, so the cost is quadratic in the chain's length.** [`chained-subscript-recv-quadratic`] `_chained_subscript_recv_type` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) proves the receiver is a rooted lvalue with `_lvalue_chain_root`, which asks `is_rvalue_source` per hop; that predicate's field arm recurses to the root, so an n-hop receiver costs O(n^2) node visits, and every `a.b.c[i].d[j].e[k]` read in a body pays it once per subscript. It was EXPONENTIAL before the fold (the resolver fell through to two predicates that each re-entered it one hop shorter, T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2)); the fold to one walker removed that, and what is left is the ordinary re-walk. Nothing memoizes a receiver and nothing caps the depth. Invisible on the corpus (chains are two or three hops), which is the shape CLAUDE.md's "algorithmic cliffs" note warns about: size-proportional in a place no existing benchmark grows. Fix shape unchanged: memoize the resolution on the receiver NODE for one body lowering (`tpyc/identity_map.py` is the sanctioned table keyed on an object) -- the answer is a pure function of the node plus `locals_` / `pointers`, which do not change inside one resolution. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, S4) of batch 6; re-measured after the rooted-lvalue fold.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid code, located; everyday shapes) A for-each iterable or unpack source whose chain contains a TEMPORARY-minting hop is rejected, with no way to spell the loop other than binding the hop to a local.** [`chain-temporary-hop-rejected`] Every hop of a rooted lvalue chain must name storage the root outlives, so four spellings keep a located reject: a CALL (`for x in self.get().xs` -> *(stmt.for_each:foreach.field_parent)*, pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_call_recv_foreach`, and in a resumable body by `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_unpack_chained_recv`, where the unpack off a call hop rejects at *(res.unpack)* because the frame's alias field would outlive the temporary), a SLICE (`for b in rows[i:i + 2][j]` -> *(stmt.for_each:iter.subscript_shape)*, pinned by `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_slice_recv_src`), a `@property` whose getter returns `Own[T]` (`a, b = o.made.pair` -> *(stmt.tuple_unpack)*, pinned by `tests/cases/tuple/error_own_property_recv_unpack`) and a user `__getitem__` returning `Own[T]` (`a, b = s[0].pair`, same tag, pinned by `tests/cases/tuple/error_value_getitem_recv_unpack`). Measured siblings, all admitted: the same chain with a reference-returning accessor (`-> T`, not `-> Own[T]`) at the same hop, every stored-field and reference-element hop (`hs[0].pair`, `o.h.pair`, `self.o.h.pair`, `d[1].pair`, a module-global root, a `readonly` root), and a slice as the WHOLE iterable (`for b in xs[0:2]`), where the span is the loop's own. Each rejected form is legal Python that an ordinary program writes; the workaround is one line (`inner = self.get(); for x in inner.xs`), and it is what the pinned cases document. Site: the hop walk in `_lvalue_chain_root` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), which asks `is_rvalue_source` per hop. Fix shape: materialize the temporary into a named holder that outlives the loop / the unpacked targets, and drive its lifetime from the statement rather than the expression -- a design row (where the holder is declared, and what happens when the same chain appears in a condition or a comprehension), not a predicate widening. Recorded 2026-09-16 while closing the accessor half of the chain rule.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, located) An `Own[container | None]` parameter is reachable only at a CONSTRUCTOR slot: the free-function and method slots reject the argument, and inside such a body the parameter can be neither narrowed nor returned.** [`own-optional-container-arg-slot-rejected`] With `def take(v: Own[list[int32] | None]) -> None` and a caller holding `xs: list[int32] | None = None` / `xs = [1, 2]`, `take(xs)` stops at *(expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_optional)* and the method spelling `h.put(xs)` at *(expr.method_call:method.arg_shape)*, while the constructor spelling `Holder(xs)` with the same parameter renders (copying into the field under the ordinary copy warning) -- so the `own_opt_container_ptr` argument face stays constructor-only. Two further legs sit inside the callee: narrowing the parameter (`if v is not None:`) stops at *(stmt.if:if.cond_binop.is not.optional_other_nonetype:binop.shape.is not)* and `return v` at *(stmt.return:name.own_optional_read)*, so admitting the argument alone would not make the parameter usable. The RECORD twin (`Own[Pic | None]`) is admitted at every one of those positions, which is what makes the container gap a family enumeration rather than a shape the language forbids. Supersedes the reach-gap claim of the deleted `optional-container-local-literal-reseat` entry, which blamed the literal reseat: that reseat compiles now (`tests/cases/optional/opt_slot_literal_reseat`) and the gate turned out to be one level in, at the argument face. Measured 2026-09-16 on the batch-6 tip while auditing that deleted claim.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located; everyday shape) A record ARGUMENT spelled as a field chain of TWO or more stored-field hops is rejected, where the one-hop spelling compiles.** [`deep-field-chain-at-record-arg`] `zap(o.mid.inner)` against `def zap(i: Inner)` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`expr.call:call.arg_shape.record_f1`)*; every hop is a plain stored field, so the chain names storage the root outlives and nothing about it is a temporary. Sibling table (measured 2026-09-16 at `42750f0ef4`): the one-hop `zap(o.inner)` is OK, and so are `zap(rows[0])`, `zap(d["k"])`, a `readonly` parameter at one hop (`peek_ro(o.inner)`), and the two-line workaround `m = o.mid; zap(m.inner)`; the two-hop chain rejects at a mutable AND at a `readonly` parameter alike, so it is the argument's chain depth, not the parameter's constness. Pre-existing -- the reject fires with no str/bytes anywhere in the program, so it does not involve the view machinery. Distinct from `BUGS.md#chain-temporary-hop-rejected`, which rejects a chain because one HOP mints a temporary; here no hop does and the reject is purely depth at the argument sink. Fix shape: the record argument's source admission should ask the rooted-lvalue chain walk (`_lvalue_chain_root`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) the way the field-read and for-each sinks do, instead of carrying its own one-hop receiver test. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch6_fix2/sib2.py`. Found 2026-09-16 while pinning the field-view escape rule: the intended `zap(o.mid.inner)` section of `tests/cases/records/bytes_field_read_receivers` had to be re-spelled at one hop.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid / silent wrong output) A class-qualified read or write of an INSTANCE field inside a subclass method resolves to `self`'s field, where CPython sees a class attribute that does not exist.** [`unbound-self-field-read-binds-self`] With `class Base: n: int32` (annotation only, set in `__init__`) and `class Derived(Base)`, `return Base.n` inside a `Derived` method renders `return this->Base::n;` and `Base.n = 9` renders `this->Base::n = 9;` -- the unbound-self spelling names THIS object's storage. CPython has no `Base.n` at all: the read raises *AttributeError: type object 'Base' has no attribute 'n'*, and the write creates a CLASS attribute that leaves the instance one untouched, so `Derived().bump(); print(d.n)` prints 7 under CPython and 9 under TPy. The reach is narrow: the resolution is gated on the qualifier being an ANCESTOR of the enclosing record, so `Base.n` inside `Base`'s own method is *'Base' is not an ancestor of 'Base'* and outside any method it is *'Base' is not a variable* -- only the subclass position diverges, and both its faces (read and write) do. Fix shape: an ancestor-qualified access whose target is an instance FIELD (rather than a class constant, a static method or a nested type) should be a located error naming the `self.` spelling, since no Python program means it; the existing ancestor gate is the place the field-vs-class-member split belongs. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/unbound-self-field-read/p2_scalar.py` (read), `p6_derived_write.py` (write) and `p3_own.py` / `p4_outside.py` / `p5_write.py` (the rejecting siblings). Noted in `tests/cases/inheritance/error_inheritance_base_field_iter_mutation`'s header, which reaches it through a `list` field. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity S3) of batch 6.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A user `__aiter__` that returns `self` -- the canonical CPython async-iterator idiom -- copies the iterable into the coroutine frame, so everything the iteration advances is lost to the caller.** [`aiter-self-copied-into-frame`] `class Countdown` with `def __aiter__(self) -> "Countdown": return self` and an `__anext__` that decrements `self.n`: `c = Countdown(3)`, `async for v in c: print("v", v)`, `print(c.n)` prints `3` under TPy and `0` under CPython (probe `/tmp/agents/batch6/aiter-self-copied-into-frame/aiter_self2.py`; the yielded values match, only the shared object's state diverges). The frame's iterator slot is `::tpy::aiter_type_t<S>` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`, the async-for slot) and `aiter_type_t` is `std::decay_t<decltype(std::declval<S&>().__aiter__())>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp:809`), so a BORROW-form return decays to an owned copy: the loop advances the copy's cursor and the caller's object is never touched. `tests/cases/async/async_for_method_awaiter_order` has exactly this shape but iterates a TEMPORARY (`async for v in Countdown(3)`), so its cpy phase is blind to the divergence. Fix shape: the frame slot takes the same borrow-vs-storage verdict every other frame slot takes -- a pointer/reference when `__aiter__` returns a borrow form (`self`, a field), the owned copy only when it mints a fresh iterator object. Context found with it (not a separate entry): the missing async-for invalidation warnings this entry was filed alongside are CLOSED -- since 2026-09-17 an `async for` files the same iteration borrow the sync for-each does, through the same registration, so `async for x in rows[0]` warns for an element method and for `rows.append` exactly as its sync twin does (`tests/cases/async/async_for_warn_iter_mutation`). Those warnings are what will keep the body honest once the slot below holds a borrow instead of a copy; the copy is still what makes the ITERABLE's own state diverge. Found 2026-09-16 in batch 6's round-4 parity review; pre-existing on master.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A container-of-container SLICE bound to a local rejects at the declaration, where the same slice over a scalar or record element compiles.** [`rebound-element-borrow-local-rejects`] `sl = rows[i:i + 2]` over a `list[list[Box]]` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`)* on the DECL line, annotated `Span[list[Box]]` or not, while the identical slice over `list[int32]` or over `list[Box]` compiles -- the `Span` slot needs the container pointee (measured 2026-09-17, probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/p_slice1.py`, `p_slice2.py`, `p_slice4.py`; re-confirmed 2026-09-21). That is why `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_slice_recv_src` does not offer "bind the slice to a local" as the workaround for `BUGS.md#chain-temporary-hop-rejected`: it does not compile either. The REBOUND-ELEMENT half this entry was opened for is FIXED (2026-09-21): `mid = outer[0]` / `mid = outer[1]` and every sibling the entry listed -- rebind from a literal, from a call, in an `if` arm, in a `for` body, in a method off `self.rows`, in a closure, and with a `dict` root -- now bind the reseatable `std::vector<int32_t>* mid = &(::tpy::__getitem__(outer, 0));` and match CPython; pinned by `tests/cases/list/reassigned_container_alias` and `tests/cases/list/elem_loan_merge_rebind`. Fix shape for what is left: the Span slot's pointee admission, the same widening the borrow-local decl rungs took in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity C2, test-coverage S3) of batch 6.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A borrow-returning user `__getitem__` whose result is a CONTAINER cannot be bound to a local at all, while the same getitem returning a RECORD binds the `T&` alias.** [`record-getitem-container-result-alias-rejects`] With `class Bag: def __getitem__(self, i: int32) -> list[int32]: return self.rows[i]`, both `x = g[0]` and the reassigned `x = g[0]; x = g[1]` error *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`)* on the DECL line, while the record-returning twin compiles (`Node& x = g[0];`). The gate is `_record_getitem_borrow_subscript` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), which keys the subscript's RESULT on `_f1_record`; the decl rung beside it (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) already spells both families for the name / field / element sources. Sibling: the REASSIGNED flavour of the RECORD result is refused one rung deeper, at `subscript.record_getitem`, so widening the result family alone leaves that half rejecting. Workaround: read the element through the container the getitem forwards to (`x = g.rows[0]`), which takes the element rung. Measured 2026-09-21 (probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/w2decl/probe_getitem.py`) while widening the reassigned-alias decl rungs to the container pointee.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An unannotated `list(<call>)` local that is rebound later rejects at `expr.call` on the FIRST binding.** [`list-call-decl-rebind-rejects`] `r = list(g(2))` then `r = list(g(3))` (or `r = [5]`) with `def g(n: int32) -> Iterator[int32]` dies at `main.py:<first line>: ... (expr.call)`; the same local without the rebind compiles, `r: list[int32] = list(g(2))` compiles with the rebind, and `r = sorted(g(2))` / `r = sorted(g(3))` compiles, so it is the `list(...)` call at a rebound slot, not the generator source. The literal-first twin (`r = [0]; r = list(g(3))`) is the separate Array-inference entry above (the literal infers `std::array<int, 1>`). Repros `/tmp/agents/frame_perf/rb_a.py`, `rb_c.py` (reject), `rb_e.py` (`sorted`, compiles).
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A generator call passed straight as an argument is hoisted into a function-scope temp, so its abandonment cleanup (`finally` / `__exit__`) runs when the ENCLOSING function returns, not when the call does.** [`generator-arg-temp-late-cleanup`] `t = drain(nested([1, 2, 3]), 1)` where `drain` breaks out of its `for` after one element and `nested` wraps its loop in `try/finally: print("gen finally")`: TPy prints `after drain 1`, `end of main`, `gen finally`; CPython drops the generator when `drain` returns and prints `gen finally` first. The call site emits `auto __tmp_2 = nested(__tmp_1); int32_t t = drain(__tmp_2, 1);`, so the frame (and its destructor's cleanup) lives to the end of `main`. Observable only for a generator with pending cleanup that the callee abandons. Repro `/tmp/agents/frame_perf/late_generator_arg.py`. Found by the cpython-parity probes of the generator-frame perf review, 2026-09-17.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) The shared non-value hoist classifier has no UNION arm, so a union-typed local first bound in a loop or branch body of a PLAIN function and read after it is rejected at lowering.** [`union-local-hoist-unclassified`] `for i in range(2): u: Pic | Flat = Pic(i)` with `u = Flat(i)` under an `if` in the same body, then reading `u` after the loop behind an `isinstance`, dies with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.hoist_type)`; the binding loop in an `if` arm gives the same reject under `if.hoist_type`. The ternary spelling (`u: Pic | Flat = Pic(i) if flag else Flat(i)`) never reaches the hoist -- sema stops it first with *Incompatible types in ternary expression* -- so the two-statement spelling above is the repro (`/tmp/agents/r3_parity/b/union4.py`, verified 2026-09-17). `_nonvalue_hoist_flavor` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) classifies plain non-value, pointer-repr Optional, readonly and resumable shapes and falls through on a union, and every ladder ends in that one classifier, so all six positions reject together. Pre-existing and position-independent: the plain non-sibling, non-nested spelling rejects identically (verified 2026-09-16), so it is not an anchor-placement artifact. The union of two VALUE types is unaffected (it takes the plain-value hoist). **Scope: a plain (sync) body only.** In a generator or `async def` the name is a frame member, whose declaration is the frame layout's, so the hoist never reaches the classifier and the shape compiles -- verified 2026-09-20 with `/tmp/agents/review_hoist/docs/u_gen_union.py` and `meta/q3d_union_gen_plain.py` against the sync twin `u_sync_union.py` (rejects `foreach.hoist_type`). **Fix shape:** add the union arm to `_nonvalue_hoist_flavor` -- the borrow form at a local is `::tpy::Union<A*, B*>`, which is the POINTER flavor the classifier already renders, so the arm is a classification row rather than a new render. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Reassigned non-value locals and some pattern captures hoisted out of `match` still reject in a plain function.** [`match-nonvalue-hoist-unadmitted`] Ordinary single-binding moves and copies now use the shared non-value storage flavors, independent of the subject strategy. Remaining scalar-match witnesses include a record constructed in BOTH arms (directly or inside a nested `for`), a mutable record parameter aliased in both arms, and tuple-unpacked record bindings read after the match. They still reject `stmt.match`: repeated owning writes need the match rebind-slot adapter, while capture/borrow hoists retain separate strategy and constness gates. In a record-subject match, a field capture sharing its name with an ordinary last-use assignment also rejects at `match.field_bind_ptr_hoist`; `match/error_capture_and_move_hoist` pins that separate capture-write boundary. The old blanket `nonvalue_ok` restriction no longer explains ordinary assignment failures. The value-typed two-arm loop twin remains pinned by `blk_match` in `control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`. Generator/async frame-member hoists have their separate decl-less route. Verified 2026-09-22 by `/tmp/agents/local_binding_match_docs_probe.py`, including the original tuple-unpack witness `m_sync_record_match.py`. Extend the shared slot verdict and preserve capture write modes rather than dropping every match gate. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A name a loop body binds in one `try` or `match` arm and a plain assignment binds in another is rejected after the block, where the same shape in an `if` compiles.** [`try-match-mixed-loop-arm-bind-rejected`] `try:` / `for a in range(3): v = a` / `except ValueError:` / `v = 9` then `print(v)` rejects with `variable 'v' may not be assigned at this point`; the `if`/`else` spelling compiles with one declaration in front of the `if`. Both readings assume the loop head provably runs (`range(3)` here) -- an unprovable head leaves the arm's binding maybe-unassigned on its own and the `if` spelling rejects too, which is the loop-clause rule, not this defect. The definite-assignment half is shared (the `if`, `try` and `match` merges all intersect assigned-or-loop-bound across arms, `FlowFacts.merge`), but the arm's direct binding is taken back out of the scope only at the `if` merge (`_unbind_branch_pending`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`), so at `try` and `match` the pending entry never becomes the sole authority and the read is the conservative reject. Workaround: assign the name once before the block. **Fix shape:** the unbind belongs where the arms already MEET -- the shared branch merge that the flow-facts lattice runs for every multi-arm construct -- not repeated per construct: replicating `_unbind_branch_pending` at the three `try` tiers and the `match` merge would be a third copy of a rule the merge is the single home for, and the next construct would need a fourth. Feed the merge the per-arm "new in scope" / "new pending" sets each construct already keeps for `record_branch_decls` and let it decide. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent uninitialized read) A walrus in an EXPRESSION position grants its target unconditionally, so a read after a short circuit that skipped it is never diagnosed.** [`expr-position-walrus-grants-unconditionally`] The per-path rule -- a walrus target in a condition counts as assigned on a branch only when EVERY way of reaching that branch evaluated it (`condition_walrus_assigned`, `tpyc/sema/flow_facts.py`) -- is consumed at the `if` and `while` heads only (`_analyze_condition_walrus`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`). Outside a head the same shapes leave the target plainly assigned by the walk that analyzed them. `k = -1` / `v = 0 < k < (m := g(k))` then `return m` emits `int32_t m;` with no initializer and `return m;` reads it: TPy prints `False` then `0`, CPython raises `UnboundLocalError` (the chain stops at `0 < k`, so the walrus never runs). `v = 1 if flag else (b := g(2))` then `return b` is the same shape through the ternary arm: TPy `1` then `0`, CPython `UnboundLocalError`. Probes `/tmp/agents/verify5_zt/p1_chain.py` and `p2_ternary.py`, verified 2026-09-18; pre-existing, not specific to any loop shape. The `and`/`or` spelling is the one expression position that is already correct -- `x = a and (b := f())` then `return b` is rejected with *variable 'b' may not be assigned at this point* (`p3_and.py`), because `_analyze_binop` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~911) saves `definitely_assigned` before the short-circuit operand and restores it after -- so one rule answers by OPERATOR today, and its correct answer comes from a blanket rollback rather than from the rule. **Fix shape:** grant `T & F` of the analyzed expression from the one function, so `_analyze_binop`'s arm and the ternary / chained-compare expression analysis all read `condition_walrus_assigned` instead of rolling back or granting outright; every position then inherits the rule and the head helper's subtraction step (`condition_walrus_targets` minus `if_true & if_false`) disappears with it. The same change folds `_walrus_paths` and `condition_walrus_targets` into one walk, and takes the `loop_bound_assigned` half of the rollback with it (the second spelling of the assignment lattice is not saved beside `definitely_assigned` there -- see the loop-anchor hygiene item in TODO.md). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud, two faces) A head whose truth the walrus path rule cannot relate to the branch taken loses the grant, although every path into the body ran the walrus.** [`cond-walrus-true-set-ignores-truth-facts`] `_walrus_paths` (`tpyc/sema/flow_facts.py`) computes the head's true-set structurally, with no access to the truth facts `NarrowingTracker` already holds, so two everyday heads under-approximate it. (a) An OPAQUE CALL over a short circuit: `while bool(flag and (z := g()) > 0): t += z` rejects the body read with *variable 'z' may not be assigned at this point*, and the `if` twin rejects identically; CPython runs both and prints `0 0` for `flag=False` (probes `/tmp/agents/verify2_zt/arch/d5_nested.py` and `d5_if_only.py`, verified 2026-09-18). Reaching the body implies the call returned true, but nothing relates an arbitrary call's result to which operand ran, so the walk falls to `_walrus_certain` of the call's arguments and gets the empty set; `bool(e)` specifically is the identity on truth and could be seen through. Remedy for users: drop the `bool(...)`. (b) A TERNARY head with an arm that is never true: `if (b := f()) > 0 if a else a:` and `if h((b := f()) > 0) if a else False:` both reject `print(b)` in the then-body; CPython prints `7` for each (probes `/tmp/agents/verify4_zt/safety/gen9/z4_tern_plain.py` and `z4_tern_cond_runtime.py`, verified 2026-09-18). The ternary rule intersects both arms' true-sets (`cond | (t_then & t_else)`) and has no way to drop an arm that cannot be true: the literal `False` arm is what `condition_provably_true` / the `_range_truth` fold (`tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`) already decides, and the bare `a` arm is false on the path that reaches it because the ternary's own condition is `a`. **Fix shape:** let the path walk consult the truth fold -- an arm the fold answers False for drops out of the intersection, and a truth-preserving wrapper (`bool`) is transparent to it. `_range_truth` has no `TpyIfExpr` arm today, so the ternary face needs one there as well. Both faces are loud and over-reject only; nothing miscompiles. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A REFERENCE-typed for-loop VARIABLE read after the loop is hoisted into a value slot, so the name holds a COPY of the last element where CPython holds the element itself.** [`ref-loop-var-read-after-loop-copies`] `pics = [Pic(1), Pic(2)]` / `for p in pics: pass` / `p.n += 10` then `print(p.n, pics[1].n)` prints `lv 12 2` where CPython prints `lv 12 12`: the hoist emits `std::optional<Pic> p;` before the loop and `p = *__beg_0;` inside it, copying each element into the slot, so the post-loop mutation lands in the copy and the source list never sees it. Probe `/tmp/agents/review_parity_loop/p_loopvar_plain.py`, verified 2026-09-16. Four positions witness the same emit and the same divergence: the plain shape above; across an unrelated sibling loop (`p_loopvar_sib_list.py`, `lv4 13 3` against CPython's `13 13`, and the mutable-list twin `/tmp/agents/p31_mut.py`, `mut_iter 7 6` against `7 7`); out of an enclosing `with` (`p_loopvar_with.py`, `lvw 7 3` against `7 7`; re-verified 2026-09-17 with `/tmp/agents/r3_parity/lv3.py`, `lv_with 12 2` against CPython's `lv_with 12 12`); and at module level (`p_module_loopvar.py`, `mod 13 3` against `13 13`). The body-LOCAL twin is CORRECT and shows the shape the fix wants: `for p in pics: last = p` then `last.n += 10` emits `Pic* last;` with `last = &(p);` in the body and prints `bt 13 13`, matching CPython (`/tmp/agents/round1_apply/t_bodylocal_twin.py`). What separates them is the borrow-decl fact: a statement-level binding records one (`stmt_borrow_decls`, `tpyc/sema/context.py`) and the hoist ladder then picks the pointer flavour, while the loop VARIABLE is bound by the loop machinery, records none, and the `hoist_loop_var` predecl (`_promote_pending_loop_var` in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, rendered from `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) falls through to the owning optional-storage slot. A VALUE-typed loop var copying is correct and unaffected. **Fix shape:** give the promoted loop variable the pointer form its body-local alias already gets -- the loop var borrows the element by the language model, so the predecl is `T*` and the per-iteration reseat takes the element's address, which is exactly what the alias arm renders. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, raw toolchain error) A for-loop VARIABLE promoted out of a READONLY container source gets a const-pointer predecl and a VALUE reseat.** [`readonly-loop-var-reseat-const-ptr`] `def ro_plain(xs: readonly[list[Pic]]): for p in xs: pass` followed by `print(p.n)` emits `const Pic* p;` before the loop and `p = *__beg_0;` inside it; g++ stops with *cannot convert 'const Pic' to 'const Pic\*' in assignment*. Probe `/tmp/agents/p12_roplain.py`, verified 2026-09-16. The two halves of one hoist disagree: the predecl takes the borrow form the readonly source implies, the reseat renders the storage form. Sibling of [`ref-loop-var-read-after-loop-copies`], the same disagreement settled the other way (both halves storage, hence a silent copy) over a mutable source -- one fix making the promoted loop var a borrow at BOTH halves closes both. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, raw toolchain error) A TUPLE-of-reference-type local first bound in a loop body and read after the loop predeclares the borrow form and assigns the storage form.** [`tuple-of-reference-hoist-storage-mismatch`] `for i in range(2): x = (Pic(i),)` then `print(x[0].n)` emits `std::tuple<Pic*> x;` before the loop and `x = std::tuple<Pic>(Pic(i));` inside it; the build dies in libstdc++'s `<tuple>` on `__const_assignable<Pic*>`. Probe `/tmp/agents/p16_t1.py`, verified 2026-09-16. The predecl asks for the tuple's borrow form (the local/param spelling) while the literal renders its storage form, and nothing converts between them at the reseat, although `tuple_to_pointer` / `tuple_to_storage` are that conversion at every other boundary. A tuple of VALUE elements at the same position compiles. **Fix shape:** either predeclare the storage form (the slot owns the fresh tuple, and the read after the loop is an ordinary storage read) or insert the storage-to-borrow conversion at the reseat -- the same borrow-vs-storage decision the branch-first-hoist design entry in TODO.md settles once for every hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A MODULE-level `str`/`bytes` local whose later binding owns keeps the view slot, so the global points into a freed temporary.** [`module-level-view-slot-ignores-owned-binding`] `p = "abcdef"` / `s = p[1:]` / `s = p + "d"` at module level emits a global `std::string_view s` and assigns `str_concat(p, "d")` into it -- a view over a temporary destroyed at end-of-statement; the program happens to print `abcdefd`. The sibling-loop spelling (`for i in ...: ms = long[i:]` then `for k in ...: ms = ms + "tail"`) prints garbage, which is the same slot with the same missing decision. In a FUNCTION the two bindings join and the local owns (the one-type-one-storage rule); at module level `_infer_new_local_type` returns before the view family is consulted (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`, `if self.ctx.is_top_level`), so no storage decision is ever made and the first binding's view spelling stands. Fix shape: a module slot needs the same join -- either the deduction runs for module-init locals too (the slot is a global, so its storage must be chosen once for every binding), or a module-level view slot rebound from an owning source is rejected. Probes `/tmp/agents/one_rule/fam/a_mod.py` (flat) and `/tmp/agents/one_rule_impl/probes2/sections.py` (loop form, the `module_str` section, which is why that shape is NOT in `control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`). Pre-existing; re-verified 2026-09-17 while landing the in-function join. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) An unannotated local bound to a SLICE of a temporary is not lowered.** [`unannotated-slice-of-temporary-unlowered`] `def f(p: str) -> None: t = (p + "x")[1:]` reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:subscript.slice_shape)*, while the same slice over a NAME (`t = p[1:]`) lowers. The local is correct sema-side -- its source is a temporary, so the storage deduction gives it an owned copy -- and it is the slice-of-a-non-name RECEIVER that the decl arm does not spell. CPython runs the program. Probe `/tmp/agents/one_rule/tmp2.py`. Pre-existing (the annotated spelling `t: StrView = (p + "x")[1:]` is a deliberate reject, not this). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (an extra copy per call in stdlib hot paths, never unsafe) The str/bytes storage join judges a binding after the first more strictly, so the two ORDERS of one pair of bindings can differ in whether the local copies.** [`view-storage-join-stricter-after-first-binding`] A local's FIRST binding is judged by source durability (`view_source_is_temporary`: a name, field or slice of either is a live borrow), a later binding by `is_view_compatible_source`, which fails closed on every shape its arms do not recognise -- a str SLICE among them. So `s = p[1:]` then `s = sv` (a view local) keeps the view, while `s = sv` then `s = p[1:]` makes `s` own a copy: same bindings, same type, different storage. The join itself is sound -- it takes the strictest demand, and the strict side is the copy -- but the rule the language states is that the POSITION of a binding never changes the answer, and here it changes this one. Unifying on durability alone was tried on 2026-09-17 and reverted: `is_view_compatible_source` asks the stronger question (it follows what a NAME's own binding borrows, which the durability walk does not), and answering the weaker one at the rebind site put `urllib.parse` / `tplib.requests` locals into views over dead storage -- 6 cases failed the exec phase with garbage output, a panic, and a `UnicodeDecodeError` on the captured output. Fix shape: one predicate that keeps the name-provenance arms of `is_view_compatible_source` and adds the durability answer for the shapes it fails closed on (a slice whose root is a live local), used by both the declaration seed and the rebind check. Four stdlib locals pay a per-call heap allocation for it, all of them a slice rebound into a name whose live root outlives them: `dirname`'s `head` and `expandvars`'s `name` (`os/path.cpp`), `urlsplit`'s `body` (`urllib/parse.cpp`), and `CookieJar._ingest`'s `domain_attr` / `d` (`tplib/requests.cpp`) -- each renders `std::string x = std::string(::tpy::str_slice(..))` where the same slice taken as the local's FIRST binding renders a `std::string_view`; `tests/cases/control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop` pins the same render in its `two_loop_str_views` section. Found 2026-09-17 landing the one-type-one-storage join, raised to MED 2026-09-17 on those witnesses. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (a heap allocation per iteration, never unsafe) A list-LITERAL local hoisted out of a loop loses the `std::array` slot its flat twin gets.** [`loop-hoisted-list-literal-loses-array-slot`] `for i in range(2): xs = [i, i]` with a later `xs = [9, 9]` renders `std::optional<std::vector<int32_t>> __slot_1;` per bind site and `xs = &*(__slot_1 = {i, i});` in the body -- a heap allocation on every iteration -- while the same two bindings with no loop render `std::array<int32_t, 2> __slot_1 = {1, 1};` (probes `/tmp/agents/r3_codegen/list_join.py` and `list_flat.py`, verified 2026-09-17). Neither literal is mutated or passed to a `list` param, so the Array resolution the flat shape reaches is available to the hoisted one too; the hoist's optional-storage slot is what forces the vector. Pinned (as the vector render) by `tests/cases/control_flow/block_local_reassign_after`'s `list_local` section and `tests/cases/control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`'s `two_loop_list_sibling`. **Fix shape:** give the hoisted bind site the same Array slot when the resolution says Array -- the slot is value storage either way, so this is a slot-type question, not a new flavor. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A `String` local is not recognised as the owning root of a yielded view, while the `str` and `bytes` twins are.** [`string-local-not-view-root-for-yield`] `def g(s: str) -> Iterator[StrView]: v = String(s); yield v` is rejected with *Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary; use str or String to return an owned copy* -- the spelling the diagnostic recommends is the one that fails. The `str` twin (`v = s.strip()`) and the `bytes` twin (`v = b + b"xy"`) both compile and print the CPython answer, and a `String` local is the same owning frame field they are: the frame owns the buffer for the frame's whole lifetime, so a view of it is as valid a yield root. `_local_has_borrowable_storage` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) admits a VALUE-typed local as a view root only when `view_family_for_type` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) names its family, and that lookup ends in `_VIEW_OWNED_QNAME_TO_FAMILY`, keyed on the family's owned qname alone (`builtins.str`, `builtins.bytes`) -- so `String`, a value type in neither key, falls out. Probe `/tmp/agents/r6_verify/m6_string.py`, verified 2026-09-17. Fix shape: ask the family's own membership predicate (`ViewTypeFamily.is_any_member` / `promote_param_match`, which already recognise `String` and `ByteArray`) at this site instead of the owned-qname table. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (hidden copy, no diagnostic; contradicts the language model) A generator / `async def` frame stores a bare `str`/`bytes` PARAMETER as OWNED storage, so the argument is copied into the frame although the caller already keeps it alive for the frame's whole lifetime.** [`generator-frame-copies-str-param`] `def gen_str(s: str) -> Iterator[int32]` takes the view the language model prescribes at the factory (`__gen_gen_str gen_str(std::string_view s)`) and then copies it into an owned frame field, while the record parameter of its sibling `def gen_cell(c: Cell) -> Iterator[int32]` is held by reference:
  ```cpp
  struct __gen_gen_str : public ::tpy::next_iter_mixin<__gen_gen_str, int32_t> {
      int32_t __state;
      std::string s;                        // OWNED: a copy of the caller's view
      int32_t i;
      __gen_gen_str(std::string_view s_)
          : __state(S_INITIAL), s(std::string(s_)) {}
      ...
  };

  struct __gen_gen_cell : public ::tpy::next_iter_mixin<__gen_gen_cell, int32_t> {
      int32_t __state;
      const Cell& c;                        // BORROWED: no copy
      int32_t i;
      __gen_gen_cell(const Cell& c)
          : __state(S_INITIAL), c(c) {}
      ...
  };
  ```
  The caller already materializes a TEMPORARY argument into its own block for the loop's duration in BOTH cases, so the owned capture buys nothing and the `str` argument is copied twice:
  ```cpp
  {
      Cell __tmp_1 = Cell(5);
      auto __src_0 = ::tpyapp::q::gen_cell(__tmp_1);
      ...
  }
  {
      ::tpy::String __tmp_2 = (::tpy::str_concat("ab", "cdef"));
      auto __src_2 = ::tpyapp::q::gen_str(__tmp_2);
      ...
  }
  ```
  The language model says a `str` parameter IS a view -- `String` and `Own[str]` are the spellings that ask for owned storage -- so a frame must hold the parameter the way the sync signature receives it; the copy is a deviation from the declared type, not an implementation detail. The same shape covers the whole family: `bytes` renders `::tpy::Bytes b;` ctor-copied from `::tpy::BytesView b_`, `async def` renders `std::string s;` from `std::string_view s_`, and a `str | None` / `bytes | None` param copies into `std::optional<std::string>` from `std::optional<std::string_view>`.
  A frame cannot outlive the scope that materialized its arguments today: a generator cannot be RETURNED (`Protocol type 'Iterator' cannot be used as a return type. Only @dynamic protocols can be used as return types`) and cannot be stored in a FIELD (`Protocol type 'Iterator[int32]' cannot be used as a field type in 'Holder'. Protocols are only valid as function and method parameters`) -- both probed 2026-09-17. If a frame COULD escape, that is the borrow checker's job to warn or reject AT THE ESCAPE, exactly as it must for the `const Cell&` field above, which carries the identical exposure and is not copied -- never a reason to copy.
  Fix shape: hold `std::string_view` / `::tpy::BytesView` (and `std::optional<` those `>`) in the frame for a bare `str`/`bytes` param, which retires the owned-param-capture rule recorded in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` (the "String Type Semantics" paragraph and the bytes view-deduction bullet). Then revisit the resumable-body rule stated in that same paragraph, which shrinks the "safe view" set for LOCALS sourced from those params: a view local sourced from a param is as safe in a frame as in a sync body once the param is itself a view. Release-blocking by its HIGH tag. Related: `BUGS.md#frame-view-arg-nonmaterializing-source`, the caller-side gap in that materialization (a slice or ternary source is not hoisted). Found 2026-09-17; witness `/tmp/agents/frame_param/q.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, no diagnostic) A `def` inside an `if` is emitted as a lambda INSIDE that C++ block, so a call after the block is out of scope.** [`conditional-def-lambda-block-scoped`] A module-level `if True:` holding `def helper(t: str) -> StrView: ...`, then `helper("  padded  ")` after the block, emits into `__tpy_init`:
  ```cpp
  if (true) {
      auto helper = [](std::string_view t) -> std::string_view { ... };
  }
  ...
  std::cout << "p5:" << " " << helper("  padded value here  ") << ...
  ```
  and the C++ build fails with `'helper' was not declared in this scope`; the front end emits nothing. MODULE LEVEL is the only face left: the function-BODY spelling (`def main(): flag = True; if flag: def helper(x): ...` then `helper(1)` after the `if`) is now a located error naming the block, whether or not an outer binding of the name exists, so it can neither reach the C++ build nor silently call the outer function. That leaves this entry and `BUGS.md#module-level-block-scoped-def-not-declared` describing ONE defect from two sides -- a module-level `def` is a module function rather than a `TpyNestedDef`, so the block rule never sees it -- and they should be closed together. Same root cause (a branch-local `def` binds its name only from that statement on) and the same decided fix: reject the read at compile time as an error naming the block, rather than emitting a call to a block-scoped lambda. The C++ mis-scoping is also the `def` face of the borrow/reference-local hoisting gap filed above ("A borrow/reference local reused across sibling/outer scopes is declared in the inner C++ scope"): value locals hoist, these do not. Probed 2026-09-17 (`/tmp/agents/lready/p5_toplevel_nested.py`); the function-body face re-probed after the merge (`/tmp/agents/merge6/fnbody.py`, `modlevel.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A nested `def` returning a view of a CAPTURED enclosing name is rejected, while the enclosing body's own return of the same view is accepted.** [`nested-def-captured-view-return-rejected`] `def outer(p: str): o = p[1:]` then `def inner() -> StrView: return o` fails with `Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary; use str or String to return an owned copy`, although `o` views `p`, which outlives both calls -- and the same `return o` written in `outer` itself (declared `-> StrView`) compiles and is sound. A captured PARAMETER is rejected the same way (`def inner_param() -> StrView: return p`); the nested def's OWN parameter is accepted, so the rule is "captured name", not "any name". Mechanism: `_name_is_param_or_global` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) asks `ctx.func.current_function`, which during a nested-def body is the NESTED def -- a captured enclosing name is neither its parameter nor a module global, so `is_dangling_return`'s `TpyName` arm falls through to its fail-closed `return True`. The position of the binding changes the answer here because the check's notion of a durable root is scoped to one function, unrelated to the one-type-one-storage rule for locals. Fix shape: let the durability question walk the enclosing-function chain for a captured name (an enclosing param, and an enclosing view local whose own root is durable, are both durable for a NON-escaping closure), keeping the reject for an escaping one. Probed 2026-09-17 (`/tmp/agents/lready/p1_alias.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (does not compile, no diagnostic) An operator dunder that returns a BORROW is emitted const-only, so nothing can be written through its result.** [`borrow-returning-operator-dunder-render`] `def __add__(self, o: Acc) -> Acc: return self if self.n >= o.n else o` then `c = a + b` / `c.n = 9` is accepted by the front end and fails the C++ build with *assignment of member 'Acc::n' in read-only object*; CPython makes `c` the operand itself, so the write reaches `a`. The same body under a plain method name emits `Acc& rec_m(...)` and works. The hoisted-holder spelling (`holder = Rec(0)` / `holder = b + 1` against `friend const Rec& operator+(const B& lhs, int32_t k)`) fails with *invalid conversion from 'const Rec*' to 'Rec*'* for the same reason. Cause: `IMPLICIT_READONLY_METHODS` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) stamps `is_readonly` by NAME at registration (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`), before any body fact exists, so the const projection `infer_method_const` avoids for a borrow-returning method is applied anyway. Three dunders were fixed for exactly this -- `__getitem__`, `__deref__`, `__span__` get a mutable + const overload pair -- but through a SECOND name-keyed set, `IMPLICIT_AUTO_READONLY_METHODS`, rather than by the return shape (`_apply_implicit_auto_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/method_expansion.py`, already keys on `rtype.is_value_type()`); the arithmetic, reflected and unary dunders and `__copy__` (~20 names) never joined it. Broken the same way, measured 2026-09-20: `-> Optional[Rec]` (`const Rec*`), `-> list[Rec]` (`const std::vector<Rec>&`), unary `__neg__`. **Fix shape:** drop the second set and give the overload pair to every implicitly-readonly dunder whose return is a reference type; the `operator+` friend shims (`_gen_binary_operators` / `_gen_unary_operators`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py`) need the clone-pair split `_gen_deref_operators` already does, with the receiver-constness axis on the shim's first parameter, or the two clones emit one signature twice. Four cases carry the const-only shim and change shape (`operators/op_borrow_return_alias`, `op_borrow_branch_hoist`, `op_readonly_borrow_return`, `returns/warn_return_record_borrow_dunder`); `op_borrow_return_alias`'s header states the const result as intended, but every leg of all four only READS through the result, so none exercises the write. An explicit `readonly[Acc]` return (`error_op_readonly_result_mutate`) must keep rejecting. A rule change to how dunder constness is decided, so its own unit, not a reject-queue row (user decision 2026-09-21). Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/defects/t1_mutate.py`, `t1_sibs.py`. Found 2026-09-20. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, located; everyday shape) A container literal or comprehension whose ELEMENT slot is a view type admits no source at all.** [`view-element-slot-admits-no-source`] `def take(s: StrView): xs: list[StrView] = [s]` rejects `expr.container_literal`; so does the unannotated `xs = [b.name]` where `name` is a view getter (it infers `list[StrView]`), a dict value or set element of the same type, and `ys = [b.name for _ in range(2)]` (`expr.list_comp`, raised at the comprehension route for the same slot). A name, a parameter, a slice and a call are all refused: the `view` family of `_container_lit_elem_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) has no rows. 19 cells of the property sweep (15 literal, 4 comprehension). WORKAROUND: annotate the owning element type -- `xs: list[str] = [b.name]` renders `{std::string(b.name())}`. Deliberately NOT a lowering row: a view is a pointer into another buffer and the list can outlive it (returned, stored in a field, appended to after the source dies), and the blanket reject is what currently closes the AST-era hole the sibling entry below records (a temporary's view stored at exactly this slot). Admission is a lifetime question for the MIR; the alternative -- an unannotated `[view]` inferring the OWNING `list[str]` -- is a type-inference rule change with its own TODO design entry ("Should an unannotated container literal of views infer the owning element type?"). User decision 2026-09-21: not a batch row. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/ret_lit/`. Found 2026-09-20.
- **[HIGH small] (accepts invalid, C++ error) A MODULE-LEVEL `match` on a pointer-repr `Optional[record]` global emits null tests against the POINTEE, so the program never builds.** [`module-level-optional-chain-derefs-subject`] `o: Optional[Cat] = mk()` at module level, then `match o:` / `case Cat(lives=1):` / `case None:` / `case Cat():` passes the front end and g++ reports *no match for 'operator!=' (operand types are 'Cat' and 'std::nullptr_t')*: a pointer-slot global reads as `(*o)`, so the subject alias binds `Cat&` while the `if_elif_optional` tier spells its arms `__match_subject_1 != nullptr` / `(*__match_subject_1)` for the pointer repr. No capture is involved -- the three-arm program above has none. The function-parameter, method, constructor and field-source (`match h.pet:`) spellings of the same match all build and run. Site: `_lower_match_optional_chain` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) derives its null/has-value pieces from `subj_type.uses_pointer_repr()`, which answers for the TYPE, while the subject's spelling comes from the name lowering's global-slot deref (`lc.prescan.global_slots`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`). Workaround: bind the global to a local (`v = o`) and match that, or move the match into a function. The whole-subject capture arm is fenced off this shape explicitly (the `subject_derefs` gate added 2026-09-20 with the pointer-repr capture), so only the non-capture arms reach the bad render. **Fix shape:** the tier's condition pieces belong to the lowered SUBJECT's form, not to the declared type -- take them from the same place the subject spelling comes from, so a global-slot subject either derefs consistently or is rejected with a located message. Found 2026-09-20 measuring the pointer-repr capture row.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; everyday shape) A whole-subject capture of a VALUE-repr non-scalar `Optional` (`Optional[str]`, `Optional[bytes]`) rejects, where the pointer-repr record twin binds.** [`match-optional-value-repr-full-capture`] `def pick(s: Optional[str]) -> str:` / `match s:` / `case "a": ...` / `case v:` with `if v is None:` in the arm errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)*. The capture is sema's `binds_full_optional`, so the name is the whole `str | None`, and `_lower_match_optional_chain` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) has a local render for exactly two families: the SCALAR value-opt (`_value_opt_scalar`, which covers `Optional[int32]` and friends) and -- since 2026-09-20 -- the pointer-repr one, which binds the raw `T*`. A value-repr non-scalar has neither: its storage form is `std::optional<std::string>` and the arm would have to declare that slot and keep the body's reads on the value-opt renders. The sibling table: `Optional[int32]` compiles, `Optional[Cat]` compiles, `Optional[list[int32]]` never reaches the arm (its class pattern is refused by sema first), `Optional[str]` rejects at every position (function, method, ctor, generator, async, module). Workaround: split the arm -- `case None: ...` then `case str() as v:` -- which binds the inner value and compiles today. Pinned by `tests/cases/match/error_optional_full_capture_value_repr`. **Fix shape:** the value-opt binding registry (`lc.value_opt_bindings` / `ValueOptKind`) gains the owning-slot kind the str/bytes family needs, so the arm declares `std::optional<std::string> v = <subject>;` and the body reads ride that kind rather than the scalar one; the admission then reads the kind instead of asking `_value_opt_scalar`. Found 2026-09-20 admitting the pointer-repr twin.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; everyday shape) A `match` on a pointer-repr `Optional[record]` inside a generator or `async def` rejects as soon as an ARM SUSPENDS, whatever the subject is bound to.** [`match-optional-subject-in-suspending-arm`] `def gen(x: Optional[Cat]) -> Iterator[int32]:` / `match x:` / `case Cat(lives=1): yield 1` / `case None: yield 0` / `case Cat(): yield 2` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)* at the `match`. Measured sibling table (2026-09-20, probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/matchimpl/bugprobe/m9_*.py`): the same body in a plain function compiles (`m9_sync.py`); the generator whose arms do NOT suspend -- assign in the arms, one `yield` after the `match` -- compiles (`m9_gen_nosusp.py`); an `async def` that awaits BEFORE the match compiles (`m9_async.py`); and an `async def` whose ARM awaits rejects (`m9_async_susp.py`). A LOCAL subject is no better than a parameter (`m9_local.py` rejects), which corrects the note this was filed from. Site: `_match_route` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py` ~1256) rejects any subject NAME that is in `pointers`, and a pointer-repr Optional joins that set when the body lowers under the resumable admission (`admission_pointers`, `tpyc/thir/lower/context.py`); the subject would have to read through the frame field. The union-subject twin with suspending arms rejects too, one gate later and under a different tag (`res.match_strategy`, the hook-mode route gate -- `m9_gen_plain.py`), so this is the Optional face of one limitation on suspending match arms. Workaround: compute the answer in a non-suspending `match` and suspend after it. **Fix shape:** the subject read is the frame's own pointer field, so the route's `pointers` reject should become a read of the frame binding the resumable admission already recorded, not a blanket refusal. Found 2026-09-20.
