- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Three `match` capture shapes on the RECORD tier reject: an rvalue subject under a pointer hoist, its re-seating sibling, and an `opt_storage` hoist with an lvalue subject.** [`match-capture-shape-rvalue-and-opt-storage`] All three are `stmt.match:match.capture_shape` from `_lower_match_record` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`), and all three are legal Python the deleted AST emitter rendered. (1) The hoist kind is FUNCTION-wide -- sema's borrow fact comes from a LATER lvalue match on the same name -- while this match's subject is an `Own`-returning call, so the pointer hoist meets an rvalue subject (`scripts/thir_migration/review/probes/match/r1873_ptr_hoist_rvalue_first.py`). (2) A sibling match on an `Own`-returning call re-seats a capture an earlier match pointer-hoisted: `match c: case Cat() as q:` then `match mk(): case Cat() as q:` (`q1881_reuse_rvalue_own.py`). (3) An `opt_storage` hoist with an LVALUE subject -- `match c: case Cat() as q:` where `q` is later assigned `q = mk()`, making it ever-owned (`r1889_opt_storage_lvalue.py`). Workaround: bind the call's result to a local and match that, or keep the capture name distinct per match. **Fix shape:** the three legs are the same missing verdict -- what STORAGE a capture needs given the subject's value category and the name's function-wide ownership -- which is the `LocalSlot` design entry in TODO.md; patching one leg at the raise site would leave the other two. Found 2026-09-20 while working the match reject queue.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) A borrow-returning CONTAINER call result is refused at an ARGUMENT slot, where the same result read transiently is admitted.** [`borrow-container-ret-arg-rejects`] `def items_m(self) -> list[int32]: return self.items` then `sink_l(b.items_m())` / `t.sink(b.items_m())` is a located reject (`call.arg_shape.container` / `method.arg_shape`), while `if b.items_m():` and `1 in b.items_m()` compile -- an argument is a transient position too, and the `const std::vector<T>&` slot binds the returned reference directly. The transient verdict is `SinkForm.BORROW_RET_PASSTHROUGH` on the sink's `_POS_FORMS` row, and the argument registry (`_ArgSink` / `_ArgRow` in `tpyc/thir/lower/arg_table.py`) decides against the slot type and per-call context only -- it is handed no `_ExprUse`, so the fact would have to be spelled a second time as an `_ArgReq` field plus a row per callee family. Workaround: bind the result to a local first (`xs = b.items_m()` then `sink_l(xs)`), which already compiles. Pinned by `tests/cases/calls/error_borrow_container_ret_arg`. Found 2026-09-20 while admitting the transient result positions.
- **[MED small] (does not compile, no diagnostic) A local bound to a FIELD off a READONLY method-call receiver loses the const bit and the C++ build fails.** [`const-borrow-call-field-lift-loses-const`] `@readonly def peek_ro(self) -> Mid: return self.mid` then `j = h.peek_ro().o` (an `Optional[Jar]` field) emits `Jar* j = ::tpy::optional_to_ptr(h.peek_ro().o);` and g++ reports *invalid conversion from 'const Jar*' to 'Jar*'*; the same holds when the RECEIVER is `readonly[H]`. The DIRECT alias `m = h.peek_ro()` is right (`const Mid& m = ...`), so the fact is available -- it just does not travel through the field hop: `_f1_const_rooted_source` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) stops at a call node, and `_expr_is_const_source`'s method-call arm is only consulted when the call IS the init, not when it is the init's receiver. The REF_ALIAS twin (`j = h.peek_ro().jar`) would emit `Jar& j = h.peek_ro().jar;` and fail the same way, which is why it is held out of the borrow-alias rung that admits the mutable flavour. Workaround: bind the receiver first (`m = h.peek_ro()` then `j = m.o`). Fix shape: give the field-off-a-call lift the receiver call's own const verdict rather than rooting through it. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/checks/r3/roprobe.py`. Found 2026-09-20 while admitting the mutable borrow-alias.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) A container LITERAL at a `readonly[container]` CONSTRUCTOR parameter is refused, where the same literal at the same-shaped method parameter binds inline.** [`readonly-container-literal-ctor-arg`] `class Numbers: def __init__(self, xs: readonly[list[int32]]) -> None: ...` called as `Numbers([1, 2, 3])` is a located reject, `call.ctor_arg.container`, while `t.ro_list([1, 2, 3])` emits the const-ref bind (the free-function twin rejects too: `BUGS.md#readonly-container-literal-arg-rejected`). The constructor argument is a separate admission gate that has no readonly row; the empty literal (`Numbers([])`) is refused there too. Workaround: bind the list to a local first and pass the name, or drop `readonly` from the ctor parameter. Pinned by `tests/cases/readonly/error_readonly_container_literal_ctor_arg`. Found 2026-09-20 while widening the call-argument row.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located; everyday shape) A NON-EMPTY container literal at a FREE function's `readonly[list/dict/set]` parameter is refused.** [`readonly-container-literal-arg-rejected`] `def total(xs: readonly[list[int32]]) -> int32` called as `total([1, 2, 3])` rejects `call.arg_shape.container`; the EMPTY literal binds inline (`total(std::vector<int32_t>{})`) and the record-method twin binds the non-empty brace. Workaround: bind the literal to a local first. The admission was built and withdrawn in THIR batch 7 (2026-09-22): binding the brace inline is only sound when the callee does not LEND the parameter back (`def head(xs: readonly[list[Rec]]) -> readonly[Rec]: return xs[0]` + `r = head([Rec(1), Rec(2)])` emitted `const Rec& r = head({...});`, a dangling reference that printed garbage where CPython printed 1), and the fact that decides it -- the callee's recorded `return_borrows_from` -- is missing for a NESTED def (never stamped) and for a callee analyzed later (`BUGS.md#return-borrow-of-pending-callee-unrecorded`), so a guard reading it either admits the dangle or refuses `inner([])`, which master compiles. The method family keeps such a guard (`_x_inline_container_literal`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) because its callees always have their facts. Fix shape: record the return-borrow fact for nested defs and propagate it for pending callees (the designed Phase-2 propagation), then re-admit the row under the guard; or hoist the literal to a named temporary whose lifetime the planned MIR can check. Pinned by `tests/cases/readonly/error_readonly_container_literal_arg`. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/review/safety/p7_ro_lit.py`, `/tmp/agents/batch7/closing/args/i_nested_min.py`.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, located; everyday shapes) Argument and receiver shapes THIR batch 7 stopped on and pinned as `error_` cases.** [`batch7-everyday-arg-rejects`] Each row of the batch admitted the temp-free half of a slot and left the half below rejecting; every one names its construct and line, none miscompiles, and the workaround is the same throughout -- bind the argument to a local first. (1) A container-returning CALL at a qualified (static / class) callee's container slot, `Holder.take_list(mk())` -> `method.qualcall.arg.call_rvalue`; the comprehension at the same slot compiles (`calls/error_qualcall_container_call_arg`). (2) A narrowed `Optional` FIELD at a pointee slot, `if b.items is not None: take(b.items)` -> `call.arg_shape.container`; the narrowed LOCAL compiles in all eight callee families -- the narrowing fact the row reads is recorded for names only (`calls/error_arg_narrowed_opt_field`). (3) A container LITERAL at a MUTATED slot of a NESTED constructor, `Rc.new(Box(KMut([1, 2])))` -> `call.ctor_arg.container` (`calls/error_ctor_nested_mutated_literal`); the direct constructor's temporaries -- `ListTaker(copy(w.items))`, `ListTaker(mk())` -- hoist a named temp since the rvalue-call hoist row became record-or-container (`calls/ctor_mutated_slot_field_arg`). (4) A non-empty literal at a `readonly[container]` CONSTRUCTOR parameter, `Numbers([1, 2, 3])` -> `call.ctor_arg.container`; the free-function twin is `BUGS.md#readonly-container-literal-arg-rejected`, the method twin compiles (`readonly/error_readonly_container_literal_ctor_arg`). (5) A dict or set LITERAL at a generic callee's mutated container slot, `take_dict(1, {"b": 2})` -> `call.generic_arg_shape`; the list literal has a hoisting cell there (`calls/error_generic_call_dict_literal_arg`). (6) FIXED: the borrow declaration is a flush point like every other statement, so `got = k.pick([3, 4])` hoists the literal (`calls/method_literal_arg_mutable_slot`); its record twin `got = k.pick(R(3))` still rejects at `method.arg_shape` -- the record ctor rvalue has no hoisting cell at a mutable METHOD slot where the container literal has one. (7) A member-typed name at a protocol method's value-union slot, `pp.take_union(n)` -> `method.protocol.arg_shape`; the protocol family has no flush position, so only temp-free sources bind (`protocols/error_proto_arg_union_temp`). (8) A unary dunder on a record ELEMENT, `-items[0]` -> `subscript.elem.record`; the binary operator rejects the same operand, a named local compiles (`operators/error_unary_dunder_elem_operand`). (9) `with mk().guard() as g:` -> `stmt.with`: a borrow-returning method binds the manager borrowed, so a TEMPORARY receiver would not outlive the block; the `@property` twin rejects the same way and a named receiver compiles (`records/error_method_off_temporary_receiver_with`). Fix shape for 1, 3, 5, 6, 7: one flush position threaded to the arg gate of every callee family, so the hoisting row the free family has is reachable everywhere (the arg family sweep, `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.py`, measures the 213 rows that still disagree across families); 2 needs the field-narrowing fact on the THIR read; 9 needs the receiver temp hoisted over the block. Listed 2026-09-22 at the batch's readiness gate.
- **[LOW small] (latent; no reproducer yet) A nested `def` emitted as a FRAME MEMBER inherits the frame's per-function emit state.** [`frame-member-nested-def-inherits-emit-state`] The lambda form of a nested def resets `return_cpp`, `finally_frames`, `loop_depth`, `rebind_slots` and `inline_rvalue_slots` for its body; `ResumableLeafEmitter.emit_nested_def_body` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`) does not, so a member's `try`/`finally` return temporary is spelled with the FRAME's return type and a member body emitted inside a frame loop starts at the frame's loop depth. A member `try`/`finally` with a return and a member loop with `break` both build and match CPython today (their return types coincide with the host's in every probe), so this is a latent mismatch, not an observed miscompile: the probe to write is a member whose return type DIFFERS from the generator's element type and returns through a `finally`. Found 2026-09-21 while giving the member body its own hoist drain point.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located; everyday shape) A `@staticmethod` that returns a BORROW rejects at the call.** [`static-method-borrow-return-rejected`] `@staticmethod def pick(other: B) -> Rec: return other.m` then `r = K.pick(b)` stops at `expr.method_call:method.qualcall.ret.record_f1` (`.ret.optional` for an `Optional[Rec]` return); a `str` or `int32` return compiles, and the instance-method and free-function spellings of the same body compile and run. All five borrow shapes reject (record, `Optional[record]`, `list[Rec]`, `list[int32]`, the parameter itself). Workaround: a module-level function. Measured 2026-09-21 on the return-const matrix (`method_static` row).
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) A FREE function returning a `list[Rec]` borrowed from its parameter cannot be bound to a local, where the method spelling can.** [`free-fn-record-list-borrow-local-rejected`] `def pick(other: B) -> list[Rec]: return other.rs` then `r = pick(b)` rejects `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`; `k.pick(b)` with the identical body binds `std::vector<Rec>& r`, and the free function's `list[int32]` twin binds too. One more place where the callee KIND decides an answer the value form should (the argument-side twin is the family sweep, `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.py`). Measured 2026-09-21.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) `return self.inner.m` -- a record reached through a NESTED field of `self` -- rejects at a borrow return, where `return other.m` off a parameter and `return self.inner` compile.** [`nested-self-field-borrow-return-rejected`] `stmt.return:return.record_source.field.borrow` for the record, `Optional[record]`, `list[Rec]` and `list[int32]` shapes. Workaround: bind the inner record to a local first. Measured 2026-09-21.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) An INFERRED-const method cannot be called on a `readonly[...]` receiver in the same module.** [`inferred-const-invisible-to-readonly-receiver`] `def use(k: readonly[K]): r = k.pick(b)` reports *Cannot call non-readonly method 'pick' on readonly reference* although `pick` never mutates `self` and is emitted `const`: the receiver check runs while bodies are analyzed, the inference after them (`infer_method_const`, Phase 2). So inference helps the C++ side only; the user must write `@readonly`. Fix shape: defer the receiver check the way the deferred borrow checks are, and resolve it after inference. Measured 2026-09-21 (every `readonly_recv` cell of the return-const matrix except the declared twin).
- **[HIGH small] (silent uninitialized read, no diagnostic; identical on master) A name first bound in ONE loop body and then reused as a later `for` loop VARIABLE is redeclared by the head, so a zero-trip loop reads garbage.** [`single-body-local-then-loop-var-uninitialized`] `for a in range(1, 3): n = a * 10` followed by `for n in xs:` and a read of `n` after that loop emits a FRESH `int32_t n;` at the head, uninitialized, where CPython keeps the value the first loop left: over an empty `xs` TPy printed `zero_trip 631691416` against CPython's `zero_trip 20`, with no warning (probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/review/parity/loopvar.py`, measured 2026-09-21; master and the batch-7 branch emit the same C++). The TWO-SIBLING-BODIES spelling is correct and stays correct: a name bound in two loop bodies is promoted to a function-level declaration that the head then binds (`_pending_local_is_declared`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`), and the same program with a second `for b in ...: n = b * 100` body matches CPython on the zero-trip call (`loopvar2.py`). What is left is the SINGLE-binding shape, whose one declaration sits INSIDE the loop body rather than at its anchor, so `_pending_local_is_declared` answers False and `_check_loop_var_rebind` lets the head declare its own local. Fix shape: the promotion the sibling shape already takes -- a loop-body-first binding of a name a later head reuses is one declaration of one Python local, so it belongs at the anchor the head can bind. Listed as residual (e) of the "for-loop rebind residuals" entry. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity S) of THIR batch 7. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ under the project's warning flags, toolchain-caught) Binding a borrow-returning call whose argument is a CONTAINER temporary trips g++ `-Wdangling-reference`, although the returned reference aims at another argument.** [`borrow-call-container-temp-dangling-warning`] `def ro_other(ys: readonly[list[Rec]], xs: readonly[list[int32]]) -> readonly[Rec]: return ys[0]` called as `got = ro_other(src, [9, 9, 9])` emits the correct `const Rec& got = ro_other(src, {9, 9, 9});` -- `got` aliases `src[0]`, which outlives the statement -- and g++ 14 reports *possibly dangling reference to a temporary*, which the build promotes to an error. The trigger is the temporary's non-trivial destructor: the same call with a record temporary (`pick(src[0], Rec(9))`) and the all-lvalue spelling both compile clean, and a METHOD whose return borrows the RECEIVER (`t.ro_self([9, 9, 9])`) does too. The argument gate is right to admit the shape -- it reads the callee's recorded return-borrow sources per POSITION, so it knows the literal is not what is lent back (`_x_arg_not_lent`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) -- and g++'s heuristic cannot see that. Workaround: bind the literal to a local first. Fix shape: either hoist the literal to a named temporary at a borrow-returning callee (which also answers the lifetime question the gate currently declines, `tests/cases/readonly/error_readonly_container_literal_lend_back`), or spell the bind so the warning cannot fire. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/fixargs/probe/m9_dangling.py`. Found 2026-09-21 writing the lend-back case.

## Safety / borrow checker

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught, no TPy diagnostic) A local bound to the result of a BORROW-returning operator dunder is bound `const`, so a write through it does not compile.** [`binop-borrow-result-alias-bound-const`] `xs = p + q` with `def __add__(self, other: Pool) -> list[int32]: return self.xs` emits `const std::vector<int32_t>& xs = ((p) + (q));`, and `xs.append(9)` fails in the C++ compiler where CPython appends to `p.xs`; the record payload (`x = p + q; x.n = 5` with `__add__ -> R`) emits `const R& x` and fails the same way. The const is the dunder's: sema infers `__add__` readonly (its body reads only) and const-projects its borrow return (`const std::vector<int32_t>& __add__(..) const`), and the caller's write through the bound alias never reaches that inference -- for the METHOD spelling it does (`v = h.view(); v.append(5)` turns `view` non-readonly and binds `std::vector<int32_t>& v`), so the gap is mutation propagation through an OPERATOR dunder's borrow return. The container face is a located reject (`binop.shape.+.record`): the binop result gate keeps the record slice so that it stays one; the record face has always compiled into the C++ error. The fix is sema's, one edge for both families, not a per-family fence. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic; resumable frames only) A `for` loop in a GENERATOR or `async def` that unpacks a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` element out of a tuple binds the pointer into the frame's COPY of the tuple, so a mutation through it never reaches the container.** [`frame-tuple-unpack-optional-element-aliases-copy`] `def gen(pairs: list[tuple[Optional[R], int32]]) -> Iterator[int32]: for r, n in pairs: if r is not None: r.n += n; yield r.n` -- iterating `gen(pairs)` twice yields `[4, ..]` both times where CPython yields `[4, ..]` then `[7, ..]`. The frame's unpack materializes the element as a value member (`__tup_1 = <elem>`) and lifts `r = ::tpy::optional_to_ptr(std::get<0>(__tup_1))` out of that copy; the same loop in a plain function takes `tuple_to_pointer` over the element lvalue and aliases correctly. A container element (`tuple[Optional[list[int32]], int32]`) takes the same frame binding and copies the same way (that spelling was a located reject, `res.local_storage`, until the Optional-ptr binding stopped being record-only). The fix is the frame unpack's: bind the tuple element by reference or lift the pointer before the copy, as the plain-function unpack does. Found by the route-merge unit.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A borrow-returning METHOD call as a tuple-literal element is stored BY VALUE, so a write through the tuple element is lost.** [`borrow-call-tuple-element-copies`] `v = (b.m(), 1)` with `def m(self) -> Rec: return self._r`, then `v[0].x += 1` (or, for a container payload, `v = (b.d_m(), 1); v[0]["y"] = 8`): the element captures VALUE, the tuple is `std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>{b.m(), 1}`, and the write lands on the copy -- TPy prints the old value where CPython prints the new one, no warning, no escape hatch. The element chokepoint already refuses the PROPERTY-getter spelling of the same read (`(b.p, 1)`, "an accessor result that lends storage has no render at an element slot") but not the method-call spelling, so the rule is written for one of its two faces. The record face is on master; the container face (dict / list results) took the same row on 2026-09-22 when the record-or-container gate admitted it, kept consistent with the record rather than fenced per family. Fix shape: one predicate for "a borrow-returning call captured by VALUE at an aggregate element" -- a call whose `call_returns_cpp_ref` -- refused at the chokepoint like the getter, for every kind (a language-rule change: a compiling silent copy becomes a located reject). Probe `/tmp/agents/unify/review/parity/p8.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A third face, at a MODULE GLOBAL: `G: tuple[Rec, int32] = (b.m(), 1)` with a borrow-returning `m` -- sema's `_tuple_global_binding_type` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) records the element `Own` because the call is not an lvalue (`is_lvalue`), so the global takes storage and the `top_level.tuple_global_owned_literal` row copies the borrowed result (`G = std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>{b->m(), 1};`), silently; it copied before that row too, through the old all-storage global. The predicate keyed on `call_returns_cpp_ref` that the fix shape names must also be what that sema freshness test asks, or the global face stays behind.
- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) A VIEW bound from a field of a loop element dangles once the loop's temporary source is gone -- in a plain function as much as in a frame.** [`loop-elem-view-outlives-temp-source`] `v: StrView = ""` then `for c in reversed(make_cells()): v = c.name` and a read of `v` after the loop prints garbage where CPython prints the string (3/3 runs). The source is a temporary the loop head builds, `c.name` lends that temporary's storage, and `v` keeps the view past the loop's own block; nothing warns. The same escape reaches a FIELD through a callee: `for c in reversed(make_cells()): k.take(c.name)`, where `take` stores its `str` parameter, leaves `k.seen` dangling with no diagnostic either -- the callee's field write is legal on its own, so the fact that has to travel is the ARGUMENT's provenance. Inside a generator or `async def` the bound-name shape over a combinator source is refused by the escape analysis (`frame-loop-elem-rebind-stale-reject` covers the shape that should now compile, since the frame can hold the combinator); the field-through-callee shape dangles everywhere, since no NAME is bound in the loop body at all. Repros `/tmp/agents/review_loopsrc/safety/p15_sync_twin.py` (plain function), `p14_fieldview.py` (generator) and `p25_sinkfield.py` (through a callee, admitted everywhere). Distinct from [`loop-body-view-unpack-target-dangles`] (a tuple-unpack target over a per-iteration temp) and from [`foreach-temp-receiver-borrow-dangles`] (a temporary RECEIVER, which at least warns): here the iterable itself is the temporary and the view is an ordinary assignment. **Fix shape:** the loop's source is a borrow SOURCE for anything read out of its elements, so a view assigned from one has to take the same escape verdict a view of a block-local does -- and an argument handed to a callee that retains it has to carry that provenance. Surfaced by the safety review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) The escape analysis refuses `r = x` inside a `for` over a temporary in a generator, although the frame now owns that temporary.** [`frame-loop-elem-rebind-stale-reject`] `r = Cell(0)` then `for x in cells(): r = x` (no `break`, no `else`) in a generator stops with *reference to 'x' may outlive its storage; use copy(x) for an independent value*. The premise is stale: this loop binds a name out of its elements, so the frame HOLDS `cells()` for the generator's whole life and `r` points into storage that outlives every read of it. The same body with a `break` and an `else: raise` compiles and runs correctly (`tests/cases/generators/frame_temp_loop_source`), so the reject is about the shape of the rebind rather than about the lifetime. A combinator over a temporary (`for i, c in enumerate(reversed(make_cells())): r = c`) takes the same reject even with the `break` / `else` shape; the frame can hold the combinator now (its slot type is the source's own `decltype`), so once this check asks the prescan the shape compiles. Verified 2026-09-21 after the frame took ownership, on `/tmp/agents/loop_src_loan/impl/round1/w10.py`. **Fix shape:** the escape check has to ask what the loop SOURCE is owned by -- the frame prescan already records that verdict per loop -- instead of treating every loop element as block-scoped storage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (use-after-free, WARNED and emitted) A `for` over a borrow-returning method called on a TEMPORARY receiver binds the loop to storage the receiver owns, and the receiver dies at the end of the loop head.** [`foreach-temp-receiver-borrow-dangles`] `for x in make_holder().get_cells():` emits `auto& __obj_1 = ::tpyapp::m::make_holder().get_cells();` -- the `Holder` temporary is destroyed at the end of that full expression, so every iteration reads its freed `cells`. The line is warned (*Iterator borrows from temporary receiver object; the temporary is destroyed before iteration begins*) and the program still builds and runs -- re-confirmed 2026-09-21 on both repros, so the diagnostic is present and the emit is the defect. Measured 2026-09-21: the generator form printed `read=11471694769` where CPython prints `read=11`, and the PLAIN-FUNCTION twin dangles identically (`read=12474396626`, `read=11556457979`, and one exit 139), so this is not about frames. The value is not reproducible run to run; the CLASS is the read of freed storage. Repros `/tmp/agents/loop_src_loan/p/s14_method_on_temp.py` and `/tmp/agents/loop_src_loan/p2/s14_sync_twin.py`. Nearest tracked neighbour is [`chain-temporary-hop-rejected`], which REJECTS a temporary-minting hop inside a chain; here the hop is at the ROOT of the chain and is admitted with a warning instead. **Fix shape:** the loop head materializes the receiver into a holder that outlives the loop (the same holder question that entry defers), or the warning becomes the reject its neighbours already are.

- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic, UB) A generator expression whose OWN body grows its source reads freed memory.** [`genexpr-body-grows-own-source`] `sum(v for v in xs if len(xs) < 5000 and grow(xs))` with `def grow(ys: list[int32]) -> bool: ys.append(7); return True` prints `87884129 6` where CPython prints `34964 5000`. Inside the frame, the source (`__src`) and the capture `xs` are two parameters naming one list; the frame's loop holds an ITER loan on `__src` only, and parameter-to-parameter aliasing is not tracked, so the growth through the capture is not seen. A `for` over the genexpr whose BODY grows the source is diagnosed (the creation's ITER loan on the source); this is the growth from inside the frame. Fix shape: at the creation, a capture that IS the source's root and that the frame body mutates structurally (the frame fi's `structural_mutated_params`) conflicts with the source's iteration -- the check the `Passing borrowed container ... to non-readonly parameter` warning makes at an ordinary call inside a loop. Found 2026-09-22 while fixing the genexpr for-head loan.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic, silent divergence / UB) A list, set or dict COMPREHENSION whose condition or element grows its own source is undiagnosed.** [`comprehension-grows-own-source`] `[v for v in xs if len(xs) < 5000 and grow(xs)]` (same `grow` as above) prints `3 6` where CPython prints `4997 5000`: the comprehension takes no iteration loan on its source, so neither `xs.append(...)` in the element/condition nor a mutating callee is reported, and the emitted loop walks a begin/end pair the growth may reallocate under. A `for` statement over the same source warns (`Mutation of 'xs' while iterating over it`). Fix shape: the comprehension's source registers the same ITER loan the for-each routes file (`_register_iter_loan` / `_register_iter_provenance_loan`) for the span of the comprehension's own analysis. Found 2026-09-22 while fixing the genexpr for-head loan.
- **[HIGH medium] (silent use-after-free, order-dependent) A function that returns the result of a callee DEFINED BELOW IT records no `return_borrows_from`, so its own callers take its result for fresh storage.** [`return-borrow-of-pending-callee-unrecorded`] `def via(b: B) -> Rec: return helper(b)` (or `t = helper(b); return t`) with `def helper(b: B) -> Rec: return b.m` declared after it, then `for i in range(3): b = B(i); holder = via(b)` and a read after the loop: no diagnostic, TPy `100`, CPython `102`. With `helper` declared first AND both of them free functions the fact is transitive and the caller warns and hoists. Source order is not the whole of it: record METHOD bodies are analyzed in an earlier pass than free-function bodies (`Analyzer.analyze_bodies`, passes 6 and 7), so a method wrapping a free function (`def via(self, b): return first(b)`) records nothing in ANY order (`/tmp/agents/rev_full_safety/a_order.py`). The return arm's transitive rule (8b rule 3, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) reads the callee's fact when the wrapper's body is analyzed, where it is still None, and records nothing; the alias spelling reaches the same place through an OPAQUE loan, which `mark_param_returned` deliberately does not follow -- recording every operand there made valid code a hard error by definition order. The caller-side escape check defers its verdict for exactly this reason (`ScopeTracker.settle_deferred_escapes`); a RECORDED fact cannot be deferred the same way, because later bodies read it. Fix shape: the designed one is `docs/ESCAPE_ANALYSIS_DESIGN.md` Future-Extension 8b-A -- record the return-call edges in Phase 1 and propagate `return_borrows_from` in the Phase-2 fixpoint beside `mutated_params`, which is order- and pass-independent and cross-module. It moves the readers that need the fact during body analysis (the scope-escape hoist decision, `pending-callee-precautionary-hoist`) behind the same deferral. A NESTED def is a third face of the missing fact, and there it is a silent COPY rather than a dangle: `def inner() -> R: return GR` (a module global, or any borrow the closure can hand back) then `r = inner(); r.x += 1` binds `R r = inner();` off an `R&`-returning lambda -- TPy leaves `GR` untouched where CPython mutates it, no diagnostic; the free-function spelling of the same body aliases correctly. Since 2026-09-22 the container twin (`return GL` from a nested def, `r.append(9)`) takes the same row and copies the same way where it used to reject. Probe `/tmp/agents/bmesc/pending_ret.py`, `/tmp/agents/unify/glob_ret.py`. Found 2026-09-20. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] (order-dependent destructor timing and copy warning; declared in docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md) A loop-local passed to a callee whose body is analyzed LATER is hoisted as a precaution, and the hoist stays when the callee turns out not to lend it.** [`pending-callee-precautionary-hoist`] `holder = self.own_q(t)` with `own_q` declared below the caller and returning `self.q`: the storage decision is taken at the bind, before the callee's `return_borrows_from` exists, so `t` goes to a function-scope slot; the diagnostic is settled after every body (`ScopeTracker.settle_deferred_escapes`) and correctly says nothing. What remains depends on definition order: `t`'s `__del__` runs when the slot is next assigned or at function exit instead of at the end of its iteration (`ctor 0 / ctor 1 / dtor 0 / ...` against `ctor 0 / dtor 0 / ctor 1 / ...` with the callee declared first -- the hoisted order is the one CPython prints), and a later `xs.append(t)` copies WITH the *copies ... into owned storage* warning where the other order moves silently -- for a `@nocopy` local that copy is a hard error (*@nocopy type 'B' cannot be copied into ...*, `/tmp/agents/rev_full_parity/p13_after.py`), so there the definition order decides whether the program compiles. Values never differ. The deferred diagnostics are also appended after every other body's, out of source order. Two latent notes on the list itself: `SemanticContext.trial_scope()` does not snapshot `deferred_escapes` (unreachable: `check_escape` runs only from a declaration or an assignment, never inside a trial), and module top-level statements are analyzed before the list's `clear()` (inert: the pending set is seeded after them, so nothing is recorded there). Fix shape: make a callee's borrow fact available before its callers are analyzed -- bodies in call-graph order with a conservative answer only inside a recursion cycle, or a return-provenance pre-pass -- which removes the pending branch here and the OPAQUE loans of `_register_call_result_borrow` with it. Probes `/tmp/agents/rev_esc_round2/e1_del_pending.py`, `e3_move_pending.py`, `d3_order.py`. Found 2026-09-19.
- **[HIGH medium] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; identical on master) Behind a CALL, a loop-local ALIAS or a for-each variable over a temporary is not escape-checked at all.** [`call-source-escape-through-alias-unchecked`] `saved = Point(0)` / `for i in range(3): items = [Cell(i)]; p = items[0]; saved = p.point()` (`def point(self) -> Point: return self.pt`) and `for q in make_bs(): holder = later(q)` compile with no diagnostic and read destroyed storage after the loop; the path spellings of the same lines (`saved = p.pt`, `holder = q`) are the located error *reference to 'p' may outlive its storage*. The hoistable tier (`b = B(i); holder = b.rec_m()`) IS checked. Judging the alias by the storage it points into is the fix, and deriving that from the name-keyed depth table was tried and was unsound four times -- the target resolved through its own loans, a forgotten depth entry read as outermost, an ended loop variable answered by a module global of the same name, a SLICE taken for an element of the sliced name -- so it waits for loans that carry the place (TODO.md, "ONE walk for which named storage"). Probes `/tmp/agents/rev_full_safety/d_values.py` (must keep compiling), `/tmp/agents/rev_closing/f1c.py`, `/tmp/agents/bmesc/dead_var_global.py`, `/tmp/agents/rev_tail/tc.py`, `td.py` (must not be admitted by a fix). Found 2026-09-20. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (accepts invalid, C++ error) A write through the result of a DECLARED `@readonly` method is not diagnosed.** [`readonly-method-result-write-undiagnosed`] `@readonly def peek(self, other: B) -> Rec: return other.m` then `r = k.peek(b)` / `r.x += 5` passes the front end and fails the C++ build with *assignment of member 'Rec::x' in read-only object*: `@readonly` makes the receiver and every parameter readonly, so the emitted return is `const Rec&` (the documented rule, `docs/READONLY_DESIGN.md`), but sema types the call's result as the declared mutable `Rec` and lets the write through. All five borrow shapes behave the same (record, `Optional[record]`, `list[Rec]`, `list[int32]`, the parameter itself). The right outcome is a located sema error at the write, which needs the call's result typed `readonly[...]` when the callee is declared `@readonly` and its return borrows -- explicit `readonly[T]` return annotations do not exist yet. The INFERRED twin is fixed: an inferred-const method proves its receiver only, and a return borrowing a parameter keeps its declared mutable type (`return_const_projected`, `tpyc/typesys.py`). - **[LOW small] (misleading warning) A borrow through a REFERENCE-returning receiver call is reported as a borrow of a temporary.** [`ref-returning-receiver-call-called-temporary`] `holder = b.mid_m().rec_m()` with `def mid_m(self) -> Mid: return self.mid` warns *Result borrows from temporary receiver object; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement*, but `b.mid_m()` is a reference into `b`, not a temporary, and the generated code is sound once `b` outlives the binding. `_borrow_storage_root` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) answers None for every call, so `_register_call_result_borrow` files no loan on `b` and takes the receiver for a dying temporary. The ARGUMENT variant is the same: `holder = wrap(first(b))` warns *Result borrows from temporary argument* on the line where the scope-escape check says `b`'s storage is shared. The scope-escape walk (`ScopeTracker.lend_roots`) does follow a nested call's own `return_borrows_from`, and the two now answer "which operands does this call's result borrow" by different rules: the registration reads the RAW fi for readiness and the walk the root, the walk applies `signature_may_return_borrow` ahead of every branch and the registration only to a pending callee, a body-less reference-returning stub lends its receiver to the walk and files no loan, and the registration has no nested-call arm. Fix shape: lift `ScopeTracker._call_lend_sources` beside `call_borrow_operands` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) as the one answer, returning `(index, operand)` pairs, and have `_register_call_result_borrow` and `_register_iter_provenance_loan` consume it, so the temporary warning fires only when the operand really has no root. It changes which loans are filed (new mutation-while-borrowed warnings), so it is its own unit. Probes `/tmp/agents/rev_esc_arch/nest.py`. Found 2026-09-19.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic remedy does not work) The escape diagnostics name `copy(<root>)` as the remedy for a FIELD or ELEMENT source, where copying the root is rejected.** [`escape-remedy-names-root-for-field-source`] `holder = b.m` off a loop-local says *use copy(b) for an independent value*; `holder = copy(b).m` is a located reject (`decl.rebind_source`) and the spelling that works is `holder = copy(b.m)`. A call source already says *use copy() on the assigned value*; the field, element and `@property` sources keep the root-naming text (24 pinned diagnostics). Found 2026-09-19.

- **[MED medium] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; the fact does not exist) Nothing records that a callee STASHES a borrowed argument, so an argument that lends a dying receiver's storage is admitted whenever the borrow leaves through a channel other than the return value.** [`native-stub-declares-no-param-retention`] `arg_lend_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) admits an argument only when the callee is known not to keep it alive past the call, and it reads the two per-parameter facts sema owns for a BODIED callee: `return_borrows_from` (stamped at registration for a generator or coro factory from `generator_borrow_param_indices`) and `addr_escapes_params`. Those cover the borrow leaving through the RESULT and through an ADDRESS taken of the parameter. They do not cover a third channel, and it has two faces. **TPy body**: a body that writes a VIEW-typed argument into storage reached through `self` or through another parameter (`def stash(dst: Box, s: StrView): dst.v = s`) copies a `std::string_view` rather than taking an address, so neither fact fires; `stash(box, mk().head)` compiles on master and on HEAD and prints garbage past the SSO buffer where CPython prints the string. **Native stub**: a body-less `@native` / `@cpp_template` stub has neither fact at all -- `return_borrows_from` stays None because no body was analyzed, and `addr_escapes_params` is an empty frozenset meaning "not measured" rather than "does not escape" -- so the stand-in is the whole-SIGNATURE `signature_may_return_borrow`, which registration already uses the same way for a body-less native METHOD's receiver borrow (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`). The stand-in gets the free-call corpus right: `len` / `sum` / `any` / `sorted` / `str()` admit, `reversed` / `enumerate` / `zip` / `map` / `filter` / `itertools.islice` reject because their `Iterator[T]` return is a lazy view of the argument. It is nevertheless WHOLE-signature (a stub taking two parameters and returning a view of one refuses the lend at both) and blind to a stub that writes its argument into a global or a member. Because it is blind there, `measured_arg_callee` confines it to the free-call path: at a MEMBER call the receiver outlives the call and is the natural stash target (`acc.append(v)`), so a stub callee is not consulted at all and the argument fails closed. Fix shape: make retention a DECLARED per-parameter fact -- a `ParamInfo` field set by a decorator (`@retains(...)` / its inverse), read by `arg_lend_ok` ahead of the signature fallback and checked against the runtime symbol the way `@native` names are -- and, for a TPy body, extend the escape analysis so a view-typed parameter written into storage reached through another parameter or through `self` lands in `addr_escapes_params`. It also settles `sorted(...)` vs `list(...)`, which today differ only because one stub declares `-> Own[list[T]]` and the other does not. Probe `/tmp/agents/t1r5c/p/stash2.py`. Surfaced by the property-read normalization review, rounds 4 (C13) and 5 (W31), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. A third face since 2026-09-22: `it = iter(mk()); next(it)` -- `iter` now carries the Iterator-stub retention fact, so the binding files a loan on the temporary, and `_temp_arg_kept_alive` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) mutes the dangling-temporary warning for every Iterator-returning stub as if it owned its rvalue argument the way the five combinators do; `iter()` has no owning flavor (`tpy::__iter__` has no rvalue overload), so the handle dangles with no warning. The `for`/comprehension spellings of the same shape are located rejects (`iter.call.plain`, `_iter_rvalue_source`); only the binding is unguarded.

- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) An escaping nested `def` and a SAME-NAMED `def` in an inner block: the escaping one is emitted as a borrow of the frame it outlives.** [`escaping-def-shadowed-by-inner-block-def`] `def esc()` at the body's own level, then a `def esc()` inside an `if` arm, then `return esc`: the outer renders `[&xs]` and the inner `[xs]`, so the returned closure holds a reference into the destroyed frame -- TPy prints `4` (and `697233920` on another run, the signature of reading freed storage) where CPython prints `14`. The escape/capture verdicts are looked up by NAME, so the inner `def` takes over the name and the outer one keeps the non-escaping default. THREE name-keyed tables carry the fact and a fix has to move all of them together: `FunctionTrackingState.nested_def_escapes` (a set of names) and `nested_def_nodes` (name -> node) in `_finalize_nested_def_escapes`, and `nd_index` in `_warn_stale_value_captures` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`, `nd_index.setdefault(stmt.func.name, idx)` -- first def per name wins, so the stale-capture warning points at the wrong position for the same reason). Related to [`escaping-closure-sibling-capture-dangles`]: both hand out a `[&local]` lambda past the frame's life, that one through a captured sibling, this one through a name collision. **Fix shape:** key all three by the def NODE, not its name -- `_names_used_after` was moved to node identity for the same reason. Probe `/tmp/agents/review2s/r3/if_arm_samename.py`; reproduces at `21dcef707b`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong value) A sibling nested `def` that rebinds a VALUE local through `nonlocal` is invisible to the stale-capture warning when it is written BEFORE the escaping closure.** [`nonlocal-rebind-before-escaping-closure-unwarned`] `def bump(): nonlocal n; n += 1` written before `def get(): return n` and called after it: TPy prints `0` where CPython prints `2`, with no diagnostic; the same `bump` written AFTER `get` warns. `_warn_stale_value_captures` builds its rebound-after set from the top-level statements' fact kills, and a `def` statement kills nothing -- the call that runs it is what rebinds, and by then the walk has passed the def. The cost warning does reach this shape (the capture copies), but it reports the copy, not the divergence. A reference local has the same hole in the other direction: in-place mutation by a sibling is only ever reported by the cost warning, since the dedicated stale-value warning covers rebinds alone. Probe `/tmp/agents/parity/r3/nonlocal_order.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (no located diagnostic; the C++ error is the only signal) An escaping nested `def` that must COPY a `@nocopy` capture says nothing, and the warning's remedy does not exist for the type.** [`escaping-closure-nocopy-capture-no-diagnostic`] `b = Box(5)` captured by an escaping `def esc()` with a sibling `def sib()` that also reads `b`: the sibling's read is a use after the closure, so the capture takes the copy path and the build dies with *use of deleted function `Box<T>::Box(const Box<T>&)`* pointing into generated C++, with no tpyc diagnostic of any kind -- not even the `copies local ... preventing move` warning, whose advice (`use copy()`) a `@nocopy` type has no answer for. The move path is no better: `std::function` requires a copy-constructible target, so a moved `@nocopy` capture fails in C++ too, which is why this is pre-existing at the C++ level rather than introduced by the copy rule. The same gap has a second trigger with no `@nocopy` in sight: an escaping `def` that MUTATES a copied capture emits `__setitem__(const std::vector<int>&, ...)` and fails to build (`/tmp/agents/parity/r3/two_escapes.py`; the bare mutating-copy failure is pre-existing -- `mut_copy.py` fails at the base commit too). The warning's `use copy()` remedy does not fix either trigger. **Fix shape:** decide the capture mode against the type's copyability AND against whether the body mutates the capture, and reject at the `def`, naming the capture, the type and the sibling use that forced the copy -- and say what IS possible (`Rc`/`Arc`, or a `def` that is the local's last use). Probe `/tmp/agents/review2s/nocopy_sib.py`. Found 2026-09-17 reviewing the escaping-capture rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) An ESCAPING nested `def` that captures a SIBLING nested def dangles transitively: the sibling still holds the enclosing frame BY REFERENCE.** [`escaping-closure-sibling-capture-dangles`] `def chain(): base = 7` then `def helper(x): return x + base` and `def esc(): return helper(1)`, `return esc`: `esc` escapes so it captures `helper` by value -- correctly -- but `helper` was never classified as escaping, so it renders `[&base]` and the copy inside `esc` carries that dead reference out of `chain`. TPy prints `24204` (garbage) where CPython prints `8`; no warning. The escape analysis marks the def it sees returned/stored and stops there: escaping is not propagated to the closures that def captures. Distinct from [`nested-lambda-no-transitive-capture`], which is a lambda inside a lambda rejected at the C++ level -- this one compiles and runs. **Fix shape:** the escape mark is transitive over captures, so a nested def captured by an escaping one escapes too (and takes the by-value/move capture path with it). Probe `/tmp/agents/chain_capture.py`; reproduces at `21dcef707b` and at the tip. Found 2026-09-17 reviewing the nested-def snapshot identity fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (use-after-free, no diagnostic) A generic relay generator that reads its loop variable AFTER the loop dangles into the step slot.** [`generic-relay-loop-var-after-loop`] `def relay[T](it: Iterator[T]) -> Iterator[T]: n = 0; for x in it: n += 1; yield x` then `if n > 0: yield x` after the loop, fed two `str` yields: TPy prints both elements and then panics `uncaught std::bad_alloc`, CPython reprints the last element (probe `/tmp/agents/relay_loop_var_after_loop.py`; identical on master 2cb3c41d3f). The loop var `x` is a `T*` into `__for_r_0`'s payload (the borrowed step result), and the loop's exhausting step re-emplaces that slot with the `StopIteration` result, so the post-loop read follows a pointer into destroyed storage; other payloads would read freed or reused memory rather than panic. Pre-binding `x = None` before the loop is rejected by the loop-rebind diagnostic, so only the unbound-before-loop shape reaches it. Related: the step slot's borrow is also why the relay copies in `generic-relay-inner-producer-copies`; the Compiler-bugs entry on a generator's yielded reference stored into an outer variable is the consumer-side sibling. Fix shape: a loop var that outlives its loop must not alias the step slot -- materialize it on the last step, or keep the last step result alive past the exhausting `__next__`. Found by /tpy-review round 2 of the generator-frame perf branch 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A generator relaying an `Iterator[T]` parameter element ONCE is rejected, although the borrow it hands on cannot go stale.** [`mono-iterator-relay-yield-rejects`] `def relay_once(src: Iterator[Node]) -> Iterator[Node]: for x in src: yield x` fails with *Cannot yield 'x': it borrows an element of a generator / iterator, valid only for the current iteration step*; CPython prints `relay 11 12` for the consumer that mutates through the relayed element (probe `/tmp/agents/genyield_fix/p9_relay.py`, verified 2026-09-17). The ephemeral-borrow escape rule (`_reject_ephemeral_escape`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) already makes the exception for a direct relay of a borrow TUPLE (`is_direct_tuple_relay`) on the argument that the inner source lives in THIS generator's frame and the outer consumer's use lasts one step of THIS generator -- which holds for a bare name just as it does for a tuple. Widening the exception to the bare relay is a safety-rule change and needs its own round. The GENERIC twin is not affected: the open-`T` slot falls to the value form for an ephemeral source, so `def relay[T](it: Iterator[T])` compiles and copies (pinned as the second inverse section of `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic_yield_borrow`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent memory unsafety, no diagnostic) A STARTED coroutine handle passed to `create_task` moves its frame into the task box while its borrowed-await pointer still points into the old storage.** [`started-coroutine-moved-into-task`] `c = leaf(); c.__poll__(w); create_task(c)` compiles: `__poll__` is a plain method call, so sema does not count it as consumption -- only `await` and `create_task` consume (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~2449) -- and `create_task(c)` then moves the frame into the `Box[Cancellable[T]]`. The frame's defaulted move copies its in-progress await pointer `__sub_N` (a `T*` into a sibling `frame_slot`) memberwise, the source payload is destroyed with the handle, and the heap frame resumes through a pointer to destroyed storage (the probe prints the right answer by luck). `docs/ASYNC_DESIGN.md` (Move/pin rules) says single-use sema enforces the no-move-after-start rule implicitly; it does not, because `__poll__` is reachable without consuming. Probe `/tmp/agents/pin_async/p3c_moved_borrowed_await.py`. Fix shape: leg (a) of the TODO.md item `Producers are movable only while unstarted` -- any non-readonly method call (`__poll__`) on a bound concrete coroutine counts as consumption, so `create_task` of a started coroutine is a sema error; the debug `!started` assert in the frame's move ctor is the backstop. The generator twin is `generator-object-binds-copy-the-frame` (a second binding copies the started frame).
- **[HIGH small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A `Span[T]` stored into an `Any` keeps the view, so the cell outlives the buffer it points at.** [`span-into-any-stores-view`] `xs: list[int32] = [1, 2, 3]` / `s = Span[int32](xs)` / `a: Any = s` / `return a` renders `::tpy::Any a = ::tpy::make_any(s);` -- the `std::span<int32_t>` is copied into the cell verbatim, `xs` is destroyed at the end of the function, and the returned `Any` aliases freed storage. No diagnostic at any position (local, return, container element, argument). Same class as the already-closed `any-str-local-stores-view`, which made the str/bytes families store their OWNING twin at the Any sink; the fix there was per-family, so everything outside `VIEW_TYPE_FAMILIES` was left in the bare `return e` tail of `_any_storage_form` (`tpyc/coercions.py`) -- records, `Span` and `Array`. `Span` is the member of that tail that is a VIEW, and so the one that dangles. Fix shape (a design call, not a mechanical patch): a view-family member at an `Any` sink is either REJECTED with a located diagnostic, or stored as its owned twin (a `list` copy) under the copy warning -- the choice is the same one the str/bytes families already settled the other way, and it decides whether `Any` is allowed to hold a borrow at all. Probe `/tmp/agents/any_fix/span_into_any.py`. Found by /tpy-ready on the `Any` equality work 2026-09-14.
- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) A `@readonly` METHOD that appends to a module global is not counted as a mutation of it, so a live borrow into that global is never invalidated.** [`readonly-method-global-write-under-live-borrow`] `pool: list[Node] = [Node(1)]` plus a `@readonly def log(self, k: int32)` whose body is `pool.append(Node(k))`; the caller does `q = pool[0]` / `lg.log(9)` / `print(q.v)` and prints `-1861617580` where CPython prints `1` -- `q` is a `Node&` into the vector's buffer, the append reallocates it, and the read is after free. **No diagnostic at all**, which is what makes the silence misleading: the SAME write spelled lexically in the borrowing body (`q = pool[0]; pool.append(Node(9)); print(q.v)`) does warn `Mutation of 'pool' while borrowed ('append' may invalidate references)`, so a reader takes silence for safety. (That control still prints garbage -- the warning is the only signal TPy has for this shape, and it is exactly the signal the call form loses.) Root cause: no per-def "writes a global" fact exists, and the edge set that would carry one is pruned for precisely this shape -- `_record_mutation_call_edges` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:3311`) returns early when `fi.is_readonly or fi.is_pure` (`:3314`), so a `@readonly` method records no `MutationCallEdge` whatever it does to module state. Fix shape: a per-def global-write fact (a place set, resolved per instantiation, not a boolean) riding an UNCONDITIONAL per-call callee list rather than `MutationCallEdge` (whose gate is about parameter flow and has nothing to do with globals), resolved inside `propagate_mutation_facts` before it clears `call_edges` (`tpyc/sema/mutation_propagation.py:84`), with an unknown callee conservatively TRUE (`:95`); that is rule 35 of `docs/CALLABLE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, which needs the same fact to invalidate a callable result rooted in a global (rule 28). Sibling: BUGS.md#noarg-helper-global-write-under-live-borrow, the same hole through the other gate; one fix closes both. Reproduced 2026-09-15 at `84f61a9b57` with `/tmp/agents/adv3_rb/k6_readonly_global_write.py` (control `/tmp/agents/fn_pass4/k8_lexical_control.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) A NO-ARGUMENT helper that appends to a module global is not counted as a mutation of it, so a live borrow into that global is never invalidated.** [`noarg-helper-global-write-under-live-borrow`] `pool: list[Node] = [Node(1)]` plus `def grow() -> None: pool.append(Node(9))`; the caller does `q = pool[0]` / `grow()` / `print(q.v)` and prints `-1218626053` where CPython prints `1`, with no diagnostic. Same class as BUGS.md#readonly-method-global-write-under-live-borrow but through the OTHER gate: the edge is appended only `if param_map or receiver_is_self` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:3410`), and a helper that takes nothing from its caller and is not a method builds neither, so Phase 2 has no edge to propagate along -- the callee's write stays a leaf fact. The plain-function shape is the more common of the two (a module-level cache, registry or pool grown by a helper), and it is unaffected by `@readonly`: an ordinary `def` reaches it too. Same fix: the unconditional per-call callee list under the per-def global-write place set, described as rule 35 of `docs/CALLABLE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENTS.md`. Reproduced 2026-09-15 at `84f61a9b57` with `/tmp/agents/adv3_rb/k7_noarg_helper_global.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (warned dangling borrow, wrong output) A `readonly[T]` borrow whose RECEIVER is a temporary binds to destroyed storage at every position.** [`readonly-borrow-of-temporary-receiver`] `def mkreg(n) -> Own[Reg]` with an `@readonly def view(self) -> readonly[Point]`: `v = mkreg(1).view()` emits `const Point& v = mkreg(1).view();` straight-line and `const Point* v; ... v = &(mkreg(1).view());` when the first binding is inside a branch -- the `Reg` temporary dies at the end of the statement in both, and `v.x` then reads freed storage (prints 0 where CPython prints 1). Both positions emit sema's warning *Result borrows from temporary receiver object; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement* (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~280), so the divergence is DECLARED, not silent -- and the two positions agree, which is why neither is a reject. What the warning does not do is stamp the fact anywhere the lowering can read: `_is_dangling_temporary_arg` is evaluated for the message and discarded, so no downstream pass can refuse or materialize the receiver. Fix shape (a language decision, not a patch): either MATERIALIZE the temporary receiver into a caller-side slot that outlives the borrow -- the same lift `_lift_borrowed_rvalue_args` performs for frame-capturing arguments, which makes both renders correct -- or promote the warning to a located error, which turns today's warning into a compile error for existing code. Whichever is chosen must land at BOTH positions at once: refusing one and warning at the other is the two-verdicts-by-position shape this class keeps producing. Probes `/tmp/agents/p_ro_straight_temp.py` (straight-line) and `/tmp/agents/p_ro_hoist_temp.py` (branch-first). Pre-existing at the straight-line position; the branch-first position reached it when the blanket `if.hoist_const` reject was replaced by the const-borrow classification (`tests/cases/readonly/branch_first_const_borrow` covers the NAMED-receiver shapes, which are correct and alias as CPython does). Found by /tpy-review of THIR batch 5. The `@property` spelling of the same read has no conceded tier and must not grow one: `p = mk().items` for a borrow-returning getter is a located reject (`local_decl.lends_from_temporary`), pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_property_off_temporary_receiver`, because the value-category rule asks both the accessor's return convention AND the receiver's category. Batch 6 briefly lost the second question and emitted `std::vector<int32_t>& p = mk().items();` (exit 139) for the monomorphic getter and its generic bare-`T` twin alike; whichever way this entry is settled has to settle that spelling with it. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. **Scope note (2026-09-18):** this entry is the METHOD spelling only. An accessor read through a `@property` off a temporary receiver is no longer warn-and-emit: it is a located reject at EVERY binding sink, because one `SinkForm` row answers for all of them and no sink that binds or holds a value past the full expression admits it. The positions and their pins, all under `tests/cases/records/`: local decl (`error_property_off_temporary_receiver`), branch-first decl (`..._hoisted_decl`), free-call argument (`..._arg`, which also carries the tag table), stub-method argument (`..._method_arg`), for-each (`..._foreach`) and comprehension (`..._comp`), field store (`error_property_view_store_temporary`), setitem value (`..._setitem`), `with` manager (`..._with`), return (`..._return`), `match` subject (`..._match`), module global slot (`..._global`), generator frame slot (`..._frame`); plus the aggregate ELEMENT slot, which is refused by a wider rule that holds off a NAMED receiver too (`error_property_elem_lends_storage`). TRANSIENT reads stay admitted -- `print(len(mk().items))`, `mk().items[0]`, `f"{mk().name}"`, `mk().items.count(1)`, a `+=` source, a dict key, a membership needle. An ARGUMENT asks the CALLEE rather than the position: admitted when the callee provably reads it during the call (`len` / `sum` / `any` / `sorted` / `str()` / `list()` / a user function taking a view), refused when it RETAINS (`reversed` / `enumerate` / `zip` / `map` / `filter` / any generator or coro factory, pinned by `..._retaining_builtin`). `async with` over a getter is unprobeable for this fact: the resumable `with`-manager lowering refuses any call-shaped manager first (`res.with_manager`), on master and here alike. Whether the spelled-method tier should follow is this entry's decision.

- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-scope, no diagnostic) A for-each over a borrow-returning METHOD read off a TEMPORARY receiver iterates a destroyed object.** [`property-off-temporary-receiver-iterated`] `def mk() -> Own[H]` with `def items_m(self) -> list[int32]: return self.xs`, then `for r in mk().items_m(): print(r)` emits `auto& __obj_0 = mk().items_m();` and builds the begin/end pair off it: the `H` temporary dies at the end of that statement, ASAN (g++-14, `-fsanitize=address`) reports `stack-use-after-scope` in `vector::begin()`, and the loop prints nothing where CPython prints every element. The read is WARNED -- *Iterator borrows from temporary receiver object; the temporary is destroyed before iteration begins* -- and miscompiled anyway, which is the remaining content of this entry: the diagnostic is there, the materialize-or-reject decision is not, and it is the same one `readonly-borrow-of-temporary-receiver` owns. **The `@property` spelling is fixed** (2026-09-18): the read is a method call from sema on, and an accessor read whose callee LENDS while its receiver dies is a distinct fact (`lends_from_dying_source`, `tpyc/value_category.py`) that ONE `SinkForm.DYING_SOURCE_LEND` row refuses at every sink that binds or holds a value past the full expression -- the decl and its branch-first twin, both argument spellings, the for-each and every comprehension route, the field store, the setitem value, the `with` manager, the return, the `match` subject, the module global slot and the generator frame slot, each a located reject tagged for its sink and pinned by a case (the full list is in the scope note under `readonly-borrow-of-temporary-receiver`; the tag table is in `tests/cases/records/error_property_off_temporary_receiver_arg`). Owning a copy there would be WRONG, not merely different: what a getter lends can OUTLIVE its receiver (a global, a longer-lived object) and CPython aliases it, so the copy loses every later mutation silently. The ptr-repr Optional flavour keeps master's render (the `std::optional<T> __slot_N` materialization plus the warning), which is sound for that shape because the whole optional is copied before the receiver dies. Verified pre-existing on master `afd815b028`. Surfaced by the batch-6 round-12 safety and codegen checks.

- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A frame-capturing view argument whose source is a SLICE of a temporary, or a TERNARY with a temporary arm, is not hoisted.** [`frame-view-arg-nonmaterializing-source`] With `def lens(t: StrView) -> Iterator[int32]` and `def make(n) -> str`, `for v in lens(make(6)[1:3])` emits `lens(::tpy::str_slice(make(6), ...))` -- the frame keeps a view into a `std::string` that dies at the statement, and no diagnostic fires (`_is_dangling_temporary_arg` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` has no `TpySubscript` arm, so the slice's temporary RECEIVER is invisible to it). The ternary form `lens("a" if c else make(2))` dangles the same way but does warn. Both sit outside the uniform frame-temp rule because neither node MATERIALIZES the storage the view aliases: the slice's is its receiver's and the ternary's is per-arm, so each needs its own hoist arm (hoist the receiver / hoist per arm) rather than a wider shape list. The list-slice sibling at a `Span[T]` param is loudly rejected instead (`tests/cases/generators/error_gen_view_temp_source_frame`), so the str/bytes family is the hole. Found filling the position x source matrix for the frame-temp rule 2026-09-11.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) The dangling-tuple-return root check never resolves an ALIAS hop under a FIELD borrow's dotted key.** [`field-borrow-root-skips-alias-hop`] `def via_alias(pbox: PBox) -> tuple[Counter, Counter]` whose body is `b1 = pbox` / `t = b1.pair` / `return t` is rejected with `Cannot return this tuple: its non-value elements are returned by reference into storage owned by the function`, while the direct spelling `t = pbox.pair` / `return t` is accepted. `t` borrows the storage KEY `b1.pair`; `_storage_root` cuts that to `b1`, and `_name_is_param_or_global('b1')` is False because `b1` is a local -- nothing asks what `b1` itself aliases, though its ALIAS loan on `pbox` is in the borrow graph. The returned pointers are rooted in parameter data and outlive the call, so the program is safe. Fix shape: resolve the dotted key's root through the borrow graph before the param-or-global test, i.e. ask for the roots of `b1` rather than accepting `b1` as one. Pre-existing: identical on master. This also MASKS a graph-level defect fixed on the capture-attribution branch -- a capture re-seated through two aliases of ONE storage used to resolve one path to an intermediate alias name; every source program that would expose it is rejected by this entry first, so the guard for it lives in `tpyc/test_borrow_roots.py`. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_alias_hop3.py` (both spellings in one file). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence) Binding a started generator or coroutine object to a second name COPIES the frame struct, where CPython aliases one object -- the two names then advance independently.** [`generator-object-binds-copy-the-frame`] `g = counter(); next(g); h = g; next(h); next(g)` prints `g 1 / h 2 / g again 2` in TPy and `g 1 / h 2 / g again 3` in CPython: `h = g` emits a copy (or a move) of the whole frame -- its state number, its locals, its iterator slots -- so `h` resumes from a snapshot of `g` instead of sharing it. Every second binding has the shape: a local alias, an append into a `list[Iterator[T]]`, an argument passed by value. No diagnostic. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probes/p_gen_copy.py` (closure-free); `/tmp/agents/probes/p_alias_step.py` shows it through a lambda in the frame -- `first 2 / second 3` vs CPython `first 2 / second 102`, where the copied closure now reads its own by-value snapshot rather than dangling into the original frame (it pointed at the original frame while the frame capture was `[this]`). Design note: a resumable frame is semantically a REFERENCE type -- CPython's generator object is one -- so a second binding should be a borrow-form alias the way a record's is, and a frame should not be copyable at all. That is a language decision, not a local patch: it changes what `h = g` means and what may be stored in a container. Decision pending with the user; needs `/tpy-fix-bug` once taken. Re-probed 2026-09-14 (`/tmp/agents/pin_async/p7_gen_move_after_start.py`): the `list[Iterator[T]]` leg is STALE -- sema rejects a protocol element type, so the append shape no longer compiles; and the `try`-body variant (`h = g` inside `try:`) hoists `Iterator<T>* h = &(g)` -- a concept as a pointee -- and fails the C++ build instead of copying. The coroutine twin that moves a STARTED frame is `started-coroutine-moved-into-task` below; the Pin-discipline item in TODO.md (`Producers are movable only while unstarted`) is the shared fix. One more thing a move carries away: a frame that owns a `for` loop's source holds a container LITERAL as a `std::array<T, N>` member of its own, so iterators and element pointers into that source name the frame's storage and do not survive the move either.

- **[LOW small] (a premise, not an observed divergence) A `ValueType` record carrying a `Ptr[T]` field takes every "this is a value, so the copy is independent" exemption while both copies keep pointing at the same pointee.** [`value-type-ptr-field-aliases-through-copy-exemption`] `PtrType.is_value_type()` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) is True unconditionally, so a `class Handle(ValueType)` with a `p: Ptr[Node]` field passes value-type field validation; a `T: ValueType`-bounded generic then copies it into an owning slot with no diagnostic and the two Handles share the Node. Probe `/tmp/agents/final/valuetype_ptr_probe.py` prints `99` after mutating through the original's pointer -- re-measured 2026-09-08. The exemption sites are the owning-slot sinks' `_is_value_type_param` guard (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, insert / `Own[T]` parameter / `Own[T]` return) and, more broadly, every reader that concludes independence from `is_value_type()`. **Not a CPython divergence**: both sides share the pointee, and TPy forbids writing a `ValueType` record's plain fields, so no probe distinguishes the two -- what is wrong is the PREMISE the silence rests on, which makes the exemption unsound for any future consumer that acts on "copies are independent" (and misleads a reader of the code today). Fix direction: a value type whose reachable fields include a mutable `Ptr` is copy-independent only in its own storage, so the copy-independence predicate needs to be distinct from `is_value_type()` rather than borrowed from it; the `Ptr` field itself already has the aliasing entries in this section as siblings. Predates the branch that documented the exemption. Found by the tail review of the unit-4 closing fix 2026-09-08. Re-rated MED -> LOW 2026-09-09: `Ptr` stays a value type (copied by value, like a view), the shape occurs once in the whole tree (`tpy.coro.Waker`, deliberately), and no consumer acts on copy-independence today; the entry stands as the design note that copy-independence needs its own predicate when one does.

- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic) The WALRUS spelling of a container-element select registers no borrow loan.** [`walrus-select-elem-no-loan`] `(p := rs[0] if c else None)` is classified an rvalue source by `is_rvalue_source` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) because of the `None` arm, so the binding lands in `owned_locals` and `register_binding_borrow` is skipped: the emitted `Rec* p = c ? &get(rs, 0) : nullptr;` followed by `rs.push_back(...)` gets no "Mutation of 'rs' while borrowed", where the declaration spelling warns since 2026-09-04 (`_select_arm_loans`). The both-lvalue walrus select still rejects at `expr.walrus`, so the loan arm is dead for every walrus select that emits today. Pre-existing on both paths. Fix shape: classify a select by its BORROWING arms, not by whether any arm is an rvalue.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic, dangling) A borrow-returning CALL arm of a select registers no loan, so the callee's receiver can be moved while the select's result is live.** [`select-call-arm-no-loan`] `r = rs[0] if c else h.get()` binds `Rec&` into `h`, and `h` is still auto-moved at its last use (`eat(std::move(h))`) with `r` read afterwards -- dangling, unwarned. The non-select declaration path covers this through `_register_call_result_borrow` / `return_borrows_from`; `_select_arm_loans` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) registers nothing for a call arm. Pre-existing on both paths; found by the batch-2 closing review.

- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic, dangling) A tuple-unpack VIEW target is not registered as a loan on its source, so any reseat of the source while the target is live is undiagnosed UB.** [`tuple-unpack-view-outlives-reseat`] `a, b = t` for a `str`/`bytes` element binds `std::string_view a = std::get<0>(__tup_N)` off a `const auto&` holder that aliases `t`'s storage: the target is a view into the source tuple's owned element and no loan on `t` is taken, so every reseat of `t` frees the buffer `a` views while CPython keeps `a` bound to the original string -- a plain name rebind `t = make(2)`, `r = None` on the Optional form, `del r`, and a rebind through a closure / `nonlocal`. Both the narrowed value-`Optional[value tuple]` unpack (`if r is not None: a, b = r; r = find(2); print(a)`) and the plain-tuple NAME unpack (`t = (...); a, b = t; t = (...)`) reach it. This is the tuple-unpack spelling of the class tracked as [`view-over-reassigned-param-not-invalidated`] (its whole-name container-rebind sibling closed with the alias-gated slot model, which gives such a rebind storage of its own) -- one missing rule: a whole-name reseat invalidates every view/element loan taken on that name. The SUBSCRIPT spelling of the same bind (`a = r[0]; r = find(2); print(a)`, and `a = t[0]` off a plain tuple local) does NOT dangle: sema demotes that binding to owned (`std::string a = std::get<0>((*r));`, `= std::get<0>(t);`) through the container-element rebind demotion (`view_source_borrows_map` in `_infer_new_local_view_type`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) and renders the view only when the source is never reseated -- the unpack target simply never reaches that decision. Fix shape: the same sema-level BINDING-FORM decision at the unpack -- a view target whose source the function reseats takes the OWNED form (copy at the bind) -- applied to every view-producing bind (subscript, slice, unpack) alike, with `del`, a closure write and `nonlocal` counted as the reseats they are. The demotion is the right default for a VALUE-typed view (`str`/`bytes`): a copy is semantically identical to CPython's alias and only costs an allocation, which is `@noalloc`'s domain to report -- a borrow-checker diagnostic belongs to REFERENCE-typed elements, where a copy would change meaning (the existing alias-rebind warning). The existing subscript demotion is body-wide (any reseat anywhere in the function forces the copy), an over-approximation `@noalloc` users may want flow-sensitive later. Not a per-site holder copy: an owned unpack holder (`auto __tup_N = t;` / `= (*r);` keyed on `prescan.reassigned`) was tried and reverted -- the holder is block-scoped, so a target declared before the `if r is not None:` block and read after it dangled off the holder instead (`/tmp/agents/review_opttuple2/probe_hoist.py`, `probe_hoist2.py`), and the prescan sees no `del`, closure or `nonlocal` reseat. Repros `/tmp/agents/probe1/reseat4.py` (plain tuple), `/tmp/agents/review_opttuple/probe2.py` and `/tmp/agents/probe1/reseat2.py` (narrowed Optional: `r = find(2)` / `r = None`), `/tmp/agents/review_opttuple2/probe1.py` (`del r`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic) Unpacking a `readonly[tuple[Own[T], int32]]` PARAM binds a MUTABLE alias of its element, so a write through the target mutates through a readonly param with no diagnostic.** [`readonly-own-tuple-param-unpack-mutable-alias`] `def f(p: readonly[tuple[Own[Box], int32]]) -> int32: x, k = p; x.n = 9; return p[0].n` renders `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<Box*, int32_t>>(p); auto&& x = ...` -- a non-const `Box*` off a readonly param -- and compiles; the write is visible in the callee (the param is the `&&` owned-tuple ABI, so the caller cannot observe it). Before the live-source unpack borrowed (2026-09-22) the element was copied out, so the write hit a copy; now it hits the param. The non-`Own` twin `readonly[tuple[Box, int32]]` is refused outright (`Cannot unpack non-tuple type`), so the readonly contract is enforced at the wrong shape and skipped at this one. **Fix shape:** the unpack target's borrow inherits the source's `readonly` (as `x = items[0]` off a readonly container does), so the lift spells `const Box*` and the write is rejected at sema. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the U1 unpack fix.

The plain alias `v = b` followed by `b = ...` has the same gap, so this is the view-lifetime tracker not treating a reassigned param's prologue local as a view source that later writes invalidate, not the select row; the select merely reaches it in one more spelling since 2026-09-03. Found by the batch-1 closing review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) Rebinding the RECEIVER of a method-derived view local frees the buffer the view points into.** [`view-local-outlives-receiver-rebind`] `a = make("first")` / `v = a.strip()` / `a = make("second")` / `print(v)` emits `std::string_view v = ::tpy::str_strip(a);` and prints garbage where CPython prints the first payload (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_verify/g1_rebind_receiver.py`, payloads long enough to defeat SSO). The `+=` twin on the same shape DOES warn (`Mutation of ... while borrowed`, from the receiver loan that statement-analysis step 8b registers for a view local -- pinned by `tests/cases/view_lifetime/warn_view_source_mutation`), but a plain rebind is handled by `_handle_pinned_view_rebind` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`, which reads only `pinned_view_aliases`, and that table is filled ONLY when the initializer is a bare NAME (`c: StrView = a`). With a method call as the source no entry exists, so neither face fires: unlike a SLICE source (`v = a[i:j]`, which falls back to `std::string` the moment the source is rebound) the method-derived pending view keeps the view slot, and no warning is emitted. The annotated spelling `c: StrView = a.strip()` has the identical hole (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_verify/g2_annot_rebind.py`). Fix shape: the rebind path should invalidate through the same BorrowTracker loan the `+=` path consults instead of the name-only `pinned_view_aliases` table; [`view-over-reassigned-param-not-invalidated`] and [`module-level-view-slot-ignores-owned-binding`] are the same tracker missing other write kinds. Found by the review round over the receiver-loan gate (2026-09-17). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent dangling views, no diagnostic) `list()` over an iterator of `StrView`/`BytesView` collects borrows rooted in the generator frame, which is destroyed once the iterator is exhausted.** [`collect-iterator-of-views-into-dead-frame`] `xs = list(g("AbCd"))` for a `def g(s: str) -> Iterator[StrView]` that yields views of its own frame locals prints `['+\x00\x00\x00', ...]` where CPython prints `['ABCD', 'abcdpadding padding ...']` (`/tmp/agents/r6_verify/m8_collect.py`); the param-derived twin, a generator yielding slices of its `str` param, prints the same kind of garbage (`m9_param_collect.py`, against CPython's `['ello there general kenobi', ...]`). Both verified 2026-09-17. The FOR-LOOP consumer of the same generator is correct -- a borrow yield is live exactly until the consumer's next step, which is the contract the loop honours and `list()` does not: the seam retains each view past the frame's death instead of materializing the owned form the collection needs. The comprehension spelling reaches no seam at all (`[x for x in g(...)]` reports *not yet supported ... (expr.list_comp)*), so `list()` is the one accepting path. Sibling of [`list-over-generator-copies-ref-elems-silently`] at the same seam -- there a REFERENCE element is silently copied where copying is wrong, here a value-typed VIEW is silently retained where copying is right -- both being the `list()` / `set()` / `dict()` constructor not reading the owning-slot verdict the element store elsewhere reads; one fix shape covers them. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
