The stopgap (`_warn_arm_subject_mutation`, gated on a non-scalar binding being present) now warns on: assignment to the subject path/owner prefix, an invalidating container method on the subject base (both synchronous), AND a non-readonly method call whose receiver prefix-aliases the subject (deferred to `finalize_borrow_checks` once readonly is settled; `resolve_pending_match_subject_checks`). Pointer-variant LOCAL subjects are safe (slot model). **Remaining SILENT residual:** mutation through an ALIAS of the subject (`p = h; p.swap()` / `p.pet = ...` -- needs alias tracking) and via an opaque method whose readonly verdict is unknown (`is_readonly is None`, e.g. some `@native`). **Sound fix:** register the surviving non-scalar arm bindings (and `__match_subject` for field/element sources) as loans of the subject root in the BorrowTracker for the arm's extent, and reject root mutation while they live -- a compile-time check, never a runtime copy (a copy would violate the performance goal for `str`/`BigInt`). Needs the MIR `Place`/`LoanInfo` model with arm-EXTENT-aware loans, which the current whole-function mutation facts cannot express (the deferred-check resolver is extent-blind) -- an IR-migration deliverable (see `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`). Dropped from [HIGH] to [MED] now that the verified silent shapes (scalar copy; non-scalar method-call) are closed; the remaining alias/opaque residual is rarer. Audit finding G2.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] readonly is not projected onto a NESTED borrow-form tuple element on subscript.** `t[i]` where `t: readonly[tuple[..., tuple[int32, Box], ...]]` returns the inner `tuple[int32, Box]` without `readonly`, so a write through `t[i][1].field` is not rejected at sema. Root cause: the four subscript readonly-projection sites in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` (tuple, container, protocol, record) all gate on `not elem.is_value_type()`, and `TupleType.is_value_type()` is unconditionally True -- so a tuple element (even one with borrow-form sub-elements) is treated as a copied value and skipped. The non-nested cases work (`readonly[tuple[Box, ...]]` projects `readonly[Box]`). Same family as the `readonly[list[tuple[...]]]` element-write entry above. **Fix shape:** unify the four gates to project readonly when the element is a borrow-form tuple (`TupleType.has_ref_elements()`), not only when `not is_value_type()`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the readonly-tuple-projection fix.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] General destructive move-out of aggregate members is unimplemented beyond the whole-rvalue-tuple-unpack slice.** Moving ownership *out* of an aggregate member is supported only for whole-tuple unpack of a fresh rvalue (`a, b = make_pair()` distributes each `Own[T]` element to a movable owned local -- shipped). Named-source whole-tuple unpack (`t = make_pair(); a, b = t`) is now supported (the source is moved into the temp at its last use). Still unsupported: partial element move-out (`take(pair[0])` leaving `pair[1]` live), record-field move-out (`take(rec.field)` for a `@nocopy` field), constant/dynamic-index move-out. These need per-place partial-move state tracking: representing `pair[0]` / `rec.field` as individually movable places with their own consumed flags, propagating "partially moved" up to the aggregate (so the whole value can't be used/moved once a part is), flow-sensitive merge of partial-move state across branches, use-after-partial-move diagnostics, and rejection of un-trackable dynamic-index moves -- the `Place(Local/Field/Index/...)` move-state model the borrow-tracker/MIR notes describe as future work. Reading members in place (borrow) is unaffected. Surfaced implementing the narrow whole-tuple-unpack slice (Send/Sync Phase 4 channel). **Fix shape:** add per-place move-state tracking to the borrow/move analyzer; until then multi-owner handoff routes through whole-tuple unpack or `Rc.clone()`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (large; architectural).
- **[LOW small]** A generator that captures a `str` parameter as a `std::string_view` and is iterated later than its source's lifetime dangles, with no diagnostic. `re.Pattern.finditer` (now a true generator) takes `subject: str` and holds the view across suspensions; `for m in p.finditer(make_temp_string()): ...` (or storing the generator and iterating after the source string is gone) reads freed storage. Instance of the unenforced view-lifetime model (the type system doesn't tie a captured view's lifetime to the generator object). Pre-existing in kind, but the generator form widens the window vs the old eager-`list` `finditer`, which consumed the view immediately. Reachable for any generator (free function or method) that captures a `str`/view param and outlives the argument. Fix shape belongs with the broader view-lifetime work (tie captured-view provenance to the returned generator's lifetime). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the finditer-as-generator change.
- **[LOW small] (precision, not unsound)** A `@native` method emitted through the frontend-IR plugin path (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py` `_route_decorators` -> `BUILTIN_LOWERING(tpy.native)`) cannot express `native_preserves_refs`. That property is set by a *separate* decorator (`@native_preserves_refs`, qname `tpy.extern.native_preserves_refs`) which is not in `CORE_DECORATORS`, so a plugin can't emit it -- `_route_decorators` rejects it as an unknown decorator. `_is_invalidating_method` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`) reads `native_preserves_refs` only for *builtin* records; plugin-emitted natives are user-defined and take the `direct_self_mutated` fallback, so the borrow checker conservatively treats every plugin-lowered native method as invalidating iterators/borrowed refs, potentially yielding spurious invalidation diagnostics. Latent: no in-tree plugin emits native methods yet. Fix shape: add a `native_preserves_refs` entry to `CORE_DECORATORS` (or a `_NativeSpec` kwarg) and thread it onto `TpyFunction.native_preserves_refs` in lowering. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (safety-model).
- **[LOW small] Temporary-rvalue-into-view-storage is rejected for `list`/`set` `append`/`add`/`insert` only; the sibling sinks are uncovered.** The view-lifetime fix (audit #10 item 5) rejects `list[StrView].append(make())` / `set.add` / `list.insert` of a temporary, but the same dangling-view store is still silently accepted for: `dict[StrView, ...]` / `dict[..., StrView]` literal keys/values and `d[k] = make()`, `list.extend([make()])`, list/set/dict LITERAL elements (`[make()]` typed `list[StrView]`), and `tuple`/comprehension element stores. (StrView FIELD stores are the separate Future field-lifetime feature, below.) Param/local-derived views stored into an ESCAPING container are also still accepted -- that needs container-lifetime (region) analysis, not just rvalue rejection. **Fix shape:** route every element-into-view-storage coercion through one chokepoint that rejects a temporary source (extend the `_view_source_is_temporary` check at the literal-element and dict/extend coercion sites); overlaps audit #11 (literal elements copy). Surfaced implementing audit #10 item 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An explicit `s: str = <view>` annotation is silently downgraded to view storage, binding owned-copy temporary into a `std::string_view` -- dangling.** `def use(sv: StrView): s: str = sv` emits `std::string_view s = std::string(sv);` -- the `str` (owned) annotation is overridden to view storage by the pending-view machinery (`is_view_compatible_source` returns view-safe for a view-typed source, so `initialized_from_owned=False`), yet the source coercion still materializes an owned `std::string(sv)` temporary; the result is a view into a destroyed temporary. Same for `s: str = make().strip()`. Root cause: the pending-view storage decision ignores an explicit OWNED annotation (it should force owned storage when the user wrote `str`/`bytes`), and the storage-vs-coercion choice is uncoordinated. Pre-existing; surfaced probing the view-lifetime cluster (audit #10). **Fix shape:** when the local has an explicit owned (`str`/`bytes`) annotation, resolve to owned storage unconditionally (no view downgrade); keep the owned-copy coercion. Distinct from the inferred-local promotion (#10 item 3), which routes `initialized_from_owned=True` to owned storage and is unaffected. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (precision, not unsound)** `await x` reads the awaitable's `__poll__` `is_readonly` at Phase-1 analysis time (`_analyze_await` -> `_extract_awaitable_inner`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`); auto-readonly is a Phase-2 fixpoint fact. A *user-defined* awaitable whose `__poll__` is only inferred `@readonly` in Phase 2 (no `@readonly` annotation, no direct mutation) reads `is_readonly=False` here, so `_mark_await_operand_mutated` over-marks the awaited operand's root -- blocking the enclosing async method's auto-readonly inference even though awaiting that awaitable doesn't actually mutate it. Over-approximation: conservative and never unsound (a method wrongly kept non-readonly, never wrongly readonly), and stdlib awaitables (`Task`/`Future`/`Event`/`SleepFuture`) all mutate in `__poll__` so they're unaffected. Fix shape: defer the await-mutation mark to Phase 2 via a call edge (mirroring `_is_self_call_deferred` for `self.method()`), or consult the Phase-2-finalized `__poll__` readonly verdict. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the await-self-mutation fix.
- **[LOW small] (by design, not a regression) Post-sema `replace_expr` injects AST that bypasses sema re-analysis.** `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.replace_expr` (inherited from `FunctionMacroContext`, `tpyc/macro_api.py`) splices nodes after pass 7, so the injected nodes get no mutation-fact collection (no `call_edges` for new calls -> Phase-2 propagation can miss a mutating call -- `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.note_param_mutated` is a manual escape hatch for the param-rooted mutating-call sub-case, but it only seeds `direct_mutated_params`, not `direct_structural_mutated_params`, so an emitted *structurally*-mutating call (append/insert/clear on a param) is still unrecorded), no borrow-check registration, no `deref_check` insertion, and no narrowing/readonly enforcement. The contract is documented (the caller must `set_expr_type` every emitted node and is responsible for safety), and this is inherent to the whole macro system (pre-sema `replace_expr`, builder-trace `emit_function`, and class macros already inject un-rechecked AST) -- a known limitation, not a defect introduced here. A macro that injects only value-type expressions (the shipped test) is safe. **Fix shape (future):** restrict the post-sema surface to value-type replacements (enforce via `type_of`/`set_expr_type`), or re-run the relevant sema checks over injected subtrees once the IR makes that cheap. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the post-sema function-macro phase.
- **[MED, latent] A view param (`Span[T]`) stored into a field passes sema with no diagnostic -- the field dangles when the caller's buffer dies (silent UAF).** `def keep(self, v: Span[int32]) -> None: self._s = v` compiles clean; the stored span outlives whatever backing the caller passed. At the `@export` CPython boundary the glue's copy-in vector dies when the wrapper returns, making the store an unconditional UAF on the next payload read for any exposed METHOD taking a `Span` param (property `Span` setters are rejected outright for exactly this reason -- a setter's purpose is storing -- so only the method surface remains exposed). The existing view-escape entries in this section cover the RETURN direction; this is the param-stored-into-field direction. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF). Fix shape: reject (or warn on) a view-typed param assigned into field storage, pending the region/lifetime model's loan-extent form. Probe: a `Span` setter body `self._s = v` compiled with zero diagnostics. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, safety-model) of the exposed-class @property rung. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` at a call argument is a hard compile error, and the param signature still renders the abstract base by rvalue-ref.** `def park(coro: Own[readonly[Cancellable[int32]]]) -> None` renders the param as `::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>&& coro` -- the abstract base by rvalue reference, not the erased `unique_ptr<P>` -- because the ReadonlyType wrapper defeats `is_dyn_protocol` in the Own-dyn slot key (`_dyn_own_coro_handle_arg`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:8899-8919`, which reads `OwnType.wrapped` RAW with no readonly peel), so the Own-dyn erasure arm never fires. The old silent-miscompile symptom is gone: a call `park(c)` is now rejected with `expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_protocol.dyn` ("this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation"), so valid code is refused loudly instead of emitting an unbindable argument. Dropping the `readonly` makes the same program work (`std::unique_ptr<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>> coro` at the signature + `::tpy::make_adapter<...>(std::move(*(c)))` at the call), so this is purely the Own+readonly composition; a signature-only program with no call still compiles, since the bogus `&&` param is never bound. Exotic shape rather than an everyday one (readonly-ness of an owned erased handle has no meaningful surface), but the message the user gets is the generic codegen-reject text, not an explanation. Related family to the readonly-protocol entries above but a distinct shape. Fix shape: either reject `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` params in sema with a real diagnostic, or peel the readonly in the slot key and the signature render together. Surfaced by the THIR Own-arg cell's adversarial probe (2026-07-17). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (latent, benign as emitted) A NARROWED `Optional[container]` field at an EQUALITY operand loses its unwrap.** `if self.lst is not None: return self.lst == self.other` (on `lst: list[int32] | None`, `other: list[int32]`) emits `(this->lst == this->other)`, where the unwrapped `((*this->lst) == this->other)` is the intended form -- no corpus case witnesses it. Root cause: the compare-operand sink threads `allow_whole_optional`, which suppresses the read's `narrowed_deref` flag, while the gate (`_container_compare_pair`) keys the NARROWED analyzed types and so admits the pair; the `field.whole_optional` arm then claims the read. C++ makes the emitted form compile and (for `==`/`!=` on a proven-non-None optional) agree at runtime via `std::optional`'s mixed comparison, which is why nothing has caught it. Fix shape: do not thread `allow_whole_optional` into a compare operand whose partner is a bare container (or exclude a declared-Optional/analyzed-container mismatch from the `field.whole_optional` arm at that sink). No corpus witness. Repro `/tmp/agents/cell-optfield/b7_cmp_only.py`. Surfaced by the boundary sweep of the THIR `Optional[container]`-field cell (2026-08-19). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `readonly` is not transitive through a value record's VIEW members: a `Span[readonly[W]]` element hands back a `W` whose `Span[int32]` member still aliases the same backing MUTABLY.** `class W(ValueType): data: Span[int32]` plus `def f(ws: Span[readonly[W]]) -> W: return ws[0]` emits `W f(std::span<const W> ws) { return ::tpy::__getitem__(ws, 0); }` -- the element is `const W&`, but the copy taken out of it carries `std::span<int32_t>` (the pointee is not const), so `out.data[0] = 99` writes through the readonly view with no diagnostic and the caller's buffer observes 99. `readonly[T]` const-qualifies the record OBJECT, not the storage its view members point at, and a value record's by-value copy drops the object's const-ness while keeping the members' aliases. PRE-EXISTING and not about the return: a plain local binding `w = ws[0]` launders identically, and so does the direct `ws[0].data[0] = 99`, so the gap is in the readonly TYPE rule, not in any one sink. Fix shape: propagate `readonly` into the view-typed members of a readonly record (the element type of a `Span`/`Ptr` field becomes `readonly[...]` under a readonly receiver), which needs the readonly system to rewrite member types rather than only qualify the receiver. Reproduced 2026-09-02 with `uv run tpy` (prints 99 where the readonly view promises no write); repro `/tmp/agents/paper2/bugs/roview.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output, dangling) A TEMPORARY argument or receiver of a delegated generator call dies before the embedded frame is first resumed.** [`resumable-delegate-temp-source-dangles`] A `for x in <gen call>:` with a yield/await in its body embeds the callee's frame in a `__for_src` field, and that frame BORROWS the call's arguments and receiver -- but a temporary among them is materialized in the enclosing `case S_RESUME_N: { ... }` block of the consumer's `__next__` switch (or not at all, for a view), so it is destroyed before the first `(*__for_src_0).__next__()` runs in the next case. Three reproducers, all same-module and all diverging from CPython (`PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`): (a) reference-typed temporary ARGUMENT -- `def make_list() -> Own[list[int32]]: return [11, 22]`, `def walk(xs: list[int32]) -> Iterator[int32]: yield xs[0]; yield xs[1]`, `def gen() -> Iterator[int32]: yield 0; (for x in walk(make_list()): yield x)` prints `0` then two garbage integers where CPython prints `0 11 22`; this one DOES warn ("Iterator borrows from temporary argument 'xs'; the temporary is destroyed before iteration begins") yet still compiles and runs. (b) a `StrView` over a temporary `str` -- same `gen`, with `def make_str() -> str: return "abcdefgh"` and `walk(make_str()[1:4])` over `def walk(s: StrView) -> Iterator[StrView]` -- prints `start` then two blank lines where CPython prints `start bcd bcd`, with NO diagnostic: no temp is hoisted at all, the emitted `__for_src_0.emplace(walk(::tpy::str_slice(make_str(), ...)));` lets the owning `std::string` die at that statement's semicolon while the frame keeps the view. (c) a temporary RECEIVER -- `class Bag` with `readings()` yielding `self.n` and `self.n + 1`, and `for v in Bag(7).readings():` inside a resumable `gen` -- emits `Bag __tmp_1 = Bag(7); __for_src_0.emplace(__tmp_1.readings());` and prints `0 0 1` where CPython prints `0 7 8`, again with NO diagnostic. Root cause is one thing in all three: the delegated source's operands are given BLOCK lifetime (or, for a view, full-expression lifetime) while the frame that borrows them has FRAME lifetime -- the `__for_src` / `__for_r` slots are frame fields precisely because they must survive across suspensions, and the temporaries feeding them were not given the same treatment. PRE-EXISTING and reachable from ordinary same-module code; the (b)/(c) legs are silent, which is what makes it HIGH. Fix shape: hoist the temporary into a frame field alive for the loop's lifetime, exactly as `__for_src`/`__for_r` already are (materialize it in a `frame_slot<T>` emplaced in the same case block, destroyed at loop exit), which covers the receiver and the owning source behind a view alike; with that in place the warned case (a) becomes correct and the warning goes -- if the hoist is not taken for some operand shape, that shape must become a hard reject rather than a warning that still emits. Probes `/tmp/agents/dangtmp/{a,b,c}.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A view returned off an IMPORTED global survives a `global` rebind in the DEFINING module.** [`imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`] `store.py` holds `S = "hello world..."` plus `def reset() -> None: global S; S = "x"`; `main.py` does `from store import S, reset` / `def view() -> StrView: return S` / `v = view(); reset(); print(v)` and prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original string. The same-module face of this is now a located compile error (`Cannot return a borrow of module variable 'S': function 'reset' rebinds 'S'`), decided from `SemanticContext.rebound_globals`, which `global_write_facts` fills from THIS module's bodies only -- a rebind in the defining module never reaches the importing module's certification. Fix shape: carry the rebound-globals set on the module's exports / `ModuleInfo` so the importing analyzer reads the defining module's verdict for an imported name, the way it already reads the imported type; the check site (`TypeCompatibility._check_rebound_global_borrow`) then needs no change. Probes `/tmp/agents/view_rebound_global/xmod/{store,main}.py`. Surfaced while closing the same-module `global`-rebind face of this hole (2026-09-15). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A view returned off a module global survives a MODULE-LEVEL rebind of that global.** [`returned-view-outlives-module-level-rebind`] `S = "hello world..."` / `def view() -> StrView: return S` / `v = view()` / `S = "x"` / `print(v)` -- all four at module level, no `global` statement anywhere -- prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original string. The `global`-statement face is now rejected at the return, but module init rebinds the slot by plain assignment, so `global_write_facts` (which pairs a `global` declaration with a write) does not see it, and the view-invalidation rule in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` does not either: it invalidates loans taken by a direct read of the name, not a view handed back by a call. Not simply foldable into the `global` rule: a module-level rebind is ordered relative to the calls around it (a rebind before every call is harmless, which the `global` case can never assume), so the sound form is the module-init replay (`decide_rebind_storage`) invalidating the loans a returned view holds, not a whole-name rejection. Probe `/tmp/agents/view_rebound_global/p14.py`. Surfaced while closing the same-module `global`-rebind face of this hole (2026-09-15). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) The `global`-rebind rule guards the RETURN sink only: a view stored into a field, or bound in the caller, still outlives the rebind.** [`rebound-global-borrow-open-sinks`] With `S = "hello world..."` plus `def reset() -> None: global S; S = "x"`, two sinks are unguarded. FIELD store: `class Holder` with `v: StrView` and `def take(self) -> None: self.v = S`, then `h.take(); reset(); print(h.v)` prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original (probe `/tmp/agents/safety4/fieldstore.py`). CALLER-side local: `v: StrView = S` in `main`, then `reset()`, prints the same divergence (`/tmp/agents/safety4/localread.py`). The rule lives on `TypeCompatibility.check_dangling_reference`, which every borrow RETURN and borrow YIELD funnels through and nothing else does -- a field store and a local binding are checked by their own paths, which certify a module global as durable storage (`is_param_derived_expr` / `_name_is_param_or_global`) and never ask whether it is rebound. Fix shape: the fact is already module-wide (`SemanticContext.rebound_globals`, filled by `global_write_facts`) and the slot predicate already exists (`_return_borrows_global_storage`); what is missing is reaching them from the binding sinks, which needs a decision on what the rule is there -- a field store is a REJECT like the return, but a caller-side local is ordered relative to the rebind, so a whole-name rejection would refuse programs where the rebind comes first, and the sound form is loan invalidation (same shape as [`returned-view-outlives-module-level-rebind`]). **Three more faces of the same rule, all live:** (1) the fact is decided in sub-phase 3, BEFORE `_expand_function_macros` (sub-phase 4), so a `global X` write a `@function_macro` introduces is invisible to it; (2) `_return_borrows_global_storage` exempts a `Ptr[T]` / `Span[T]` HANDLE global by the SLOT's own type and never asks where the handle points, so a `Span` global that views another global's buffer would be exempted wrongly -- latent only because such a return is rejected elsewhere; (3) `+=` on a reference-typed global is an in-place extend in CPython, not a reseat, but the rebind walk pairs a `global` declaration with any binding write including `TpyAugAssign`, so it would count as one -- reachable: the borrow rule fires first, so `return XS` before a `global XS; XS += [4]` is rejected as a rebind although CPython extends in place (the lowering does not admit the aug-assign on a global yet either, `stmt.aug_assign`); the message names only the function, so the over-reject is at least not given a false reason.aug_assign` (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_fix/iadd.py`), and the lowering that admits it must not inherit the over-rejection; (4) the whole rule is same-module only -- an imported global rebound in its DEFINING module reaches no certification at all, filed separately as [`imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`], which is the same rule missing its cross-module half rather than a distinct defect. Surfaced 2026-09-15 by the review round over the same-module `global`-rebind fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A fourth face: a view WRAPPED in a value aggregate escapes the return rule entirely -- `def v() -> Optional[StrView]: return S[0:11]` with a `global S` rebind compiles and reads freed storage (`check_dangling_reference`'s value-type early return skips it; the tuple arm mirrors that skip by design, so the two agree). Probe `/tmp/agents/safety6/p12_opt_dangle.py`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent miscompile, use-after-move) In an import cycle, a call-result borrow through a peer module whose bodies have not been analyzed yet is read as "borrows nothing", so the auto-move gate moves the container out from under the live reference.** [`cycle-peer-borrow-fact-read-as-stub`] Modules `a` and `b` import each other; each has `pick(xs: list[Item]) -> Item` returning `xs[0]` and `use()` doing `it = peer.pick(xs)` then `k = sink(xs)` with `sink(xs: Own[list[Item]])`, then `return it.n + k`. The first-analyzed member (`a`, alphabetical) emits `Item& it = b::pick_b(xs); int32_t k = a::sink_a(std::move(xs)); return it.n + k;` -- a use after move; the second member correctly copies (`std::vector<Item> __tmp_1 = xs;` with the owned-storage copy warning). Cause: `return_borrows_from` is a body-local fact consumed at the call-result bind (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~255-270), where `None` means BOTH "opaque stub, borrows nothing" and "body not analyzed yet"; the disambiguator `ctx.pending_borrow_fact_fis` is seeded by `_seed_pending_borrow_fact_fis` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` ~913-944) from THIS module only, so a cycle peer is missing from the set and its `None` takes the stub leg. Fix shape: seed the pending set from the whole import component (Tarjan already computes the components in `Compiler._compute_compile_order`, `tpyc/compiler.py` ~1594-1696, then flattens them away) so the peer registers the conservative OPAQUE borrow; measured zero churn over the 31 cyclic cases and 120 random ones when over-approximated to every user module. Step C of the TODO design entry "Call-graph fact propagation: make the unit the import COMPONENT". Found 2026-09-16 by the batch-6 propagation analysis.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) A for-each over a container more than one hop from a spellable storage key is REJECTED, because the borrow tracker keys a loan by a STRING (`name` / `name.field`) and cannot express the place the iteration borrows. One spelling escapes it in a plain `def` body -- a chain whose TAIL is a `@property`, whose loan comes from the getter's provenance instead; a resumable body rejects that one too, at `res.for_iter_borrow_unplaceable`, since its frame holds the iterators across every suspension.** [`iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`] `for b in self.grid.rows[i]`, `for b in self.inner.xs`, `for b in table[k].cells`, `for b in shelves[0].flat` and `for b in cube[i][j]` all stop with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.iter_borrow_unplaceable)* (the generator and `async for` twins stop at `res.for_iter_borrow_unplaceable` -- all three routes file the loan through one registration and take one verdict), while the one-hop siblings `rows[i]`, `g.rows`, `self.rows[i]`, `row.cells[i]` and `table[k]` compile and are checked. Binding the chain to a local first is the workaround. The reject is deliberate, not a codegen gap: `BorrowTracker.loans` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) is `dict[str, dict[str, LoanInfo]]`, and `_storage_key` can spell only a name or a one-hop `obj.field` path, so a deeper chain has no key a mutating receiver could be resolved to and every invalidating mutation of what is iterated would be silent -- a cached `__beg`/`__end` into a vector that reallocates. The single element hop that IS checked rides `LoanInfo.on_element` plus `LoanInfo.elem_index` (an `element_index_key`: a non-negative int or str literal, or a bare name) rather than a key, so two literals that differ are proven distinct and everything else conflicts -- worded as certain or as possible by `element_index_relation`. Fix shape: replace the string key with a `Place` (root name plus an ordered tuple of field / index hops, an index hop carrying the same `element_index_key` and matching by `element_index_relation`), file loans under it, and make the conflict test `equal or prefix or extension` -- then the whole chain family is checkable and the reject can be lifted. Every loans-dict consumer (`has_element_borrow`, `has_iter_borrow`, `effective_storage`, `borrow_source`, `retarget_storage_borrows` and the two `storage + "."` prefix walks, `all_storage_through_borrows`) moves with it, which is why this is a design row and not a patch. The Place has a SECOND consumer that must be designed in at the same time, or the codebase ends with two key vocabularies for one question: the view tracker already spells deep dotted paths (`field_chain_storage_key`, `o.inner.tag`) and answers "does this mutation clobber that view" by a raw string PREFIX match in `mark_view_borrowers_mutated` -- exactly the `equal or prefix or extension` relation above, spelled a second way. The two fix groups of batch 6 made opposite calls here (the iteration side refused a deeper string key, the view side extended one), which is the concrete cost of leaving them apart. Pinned by `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_unplaceable_chain_src`, `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_field_chain_src` (the pure-field chain), `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_foreach_unplaceable_chain`, `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_foreach_property_chain` (the property-tail chain a plain body admits) and `tests/cases/async/error_async_for_unplaceable_chain`. Surfaced by the batch-6 review (safety C1/C2). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. The field-read VIEW is the other half of this row: a one-hop read borrows and is demoted by a hand-kept list of write paths whose gaps are silent use-after-frees, while a deeper read copies for want of a key (`BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place`). Once the tracker owns escape as a Place fact, the depth restriction, the hand-maintained write-path list and the write receivers that list cannot see all go away. Its home is NOT a new sema structure: master's analysis-only MIR (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`, M2.1) already defines `MIRPlace` rooted at a body slot with dereference and field projections plus alias bind/reseat facts, and the loan-legality, referent-lifetime and call-summary halves are the later increments; the iteration loans and the view tracker are consumers of those increments, so this row and `BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place` wait for them rather than grow a second place vocabulary in `tpyc/sema/context.py`. Until then the whole borrow family stays fail-closed (located rejects with slugs), no further widening at the string-key layer (user 2026-09-17).
- **[HIGH medium] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; pre-existing on master) A one-hop `str` FIELD view outlives its buffer through four write paths the escape rule does not know: a `*args` pack argument, a nested-def closure that writes the record, a callee that writes a module GLOBAL, and a write through a SECOND name aliasing the same container element.** [`field-view-escape-needs-place`] `v = i.name` renders `std::string_view v = i.name;`, and each of `zap_pack(i)` (`def zap_pack(*os: Inner)` writing `x.name`), an inner `def bump(): i.name = ...`, `zapg()` writing a module-global record, and `for x in rows: x.n = ...` while a view taken through `p = rows[0]` is live replaces the buffer while the view is live; TPy then prints garbage where CPython prints the pre-write value. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/field-view-escape-needs-place/` (`pack_str_onehop.py`, `closure_escape_str.py`, `global_callee.py`, `v7_loopvar_str.py`), which is where every probe this entry names lives. The family is `str` only: a `bytes` field read takes an owned `::tpy::Bytes` copy at every depth, because it did not compile at all on master (a THIR reject) and binding it as a `::tpy::BytesView` would open a dangle class master does not have -- the guard is the `is_str` leg of the field arm in `is_view_compatible_source` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`). The one-hop `str` render is the same at master `334c182905` and at HEAD, and master has no argument demotion at all (`_demote_views_at_mutable_arg` is newer), so every one of these `str` spellings was already a view there. The spellings that DO demote, all in `tpyc/sema/calls.py` / `tpyc/sema/statements.py`: a positional or keyword argument at a parameter that is not `readonly` (`zap(one)`, `zap(rec=o)`), an alias bind of a prefix in either direction (`m = o.mid`), a write to that field (through a name, `self`, a nested field, or an unproven Optional name or field -- NOT through a property getter, which is why that receiver is rejected below), and a mutating method on the chain -- the view's safety is that LIST, not a fact any home owns, which is the entry. A read through two or more hops, off a temporary, or through a `@property` hop takes an owned copy instead: its source has no storage key a write could be resolved to, so no demotion could fire for it either. Further spellings would be escapes if they compiled, and do not: the view-family field WRITE through a `Ptr` parameter, through a `Ptr` held in a record FIELD, through a tuple element (as an argument or through a local), through a CONTAINER element (a list element, a dict value, or a `*args` pack subscript -- one rung, three spellings), through a borrow-returning CALL (`b.get().name = ...`), and through a `@property` GETTER (`h.val.name = ...`, and the `self.val.name` twin inside a method) -- `ptr_escape_str.py`, `e_ptrfield.py`, `e_tuplearg.py`, `e_tuplelocal.py`, `e_elem_write.py`, `esc_pack_str.py`, `r6_boxget.py`, `prop_recv.py`, `prop_recv_self.py`. The getter is the one receiver where even the coarse fallback cannot fire: `_mark_field_write_views` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) keys the receiver only when NO field path can be spelled, and `h.val.name` spells one -- just not the one the view was registered under. Batch 6's shared field-write receiver ladder admitted those writes (queue row `str-field-write-through-nested-receiver`), which turned a latent view into a dangling one in newly-compiling programs; the view-family write rows therefore take `_viewfam_field_write_receiver_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`), which subtracts those five receivers, and each stops again at `assign.field_write_shape` exactly as on master -- pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_str_field_write_ptr_receiver`, `error_str_field_write_tuple_elem`, `error_str_field_write_elem_receiver`, `error_str_field_write_call_receiver` and `error_str_field_write_property_receiver`. Those rejects restore master's verdict but buy no soundness by themselves: the same clobber is reachable through a compiling NEIGHBOUR on master, a `Ptr` passed on to a mutating helper, a tuple element bound to a local first, and the getter's own workaround when the view is held through a DIFFERENT alias (`r = h.val; r.name = ...` with `m = h.inner; v = m.name` live), which print garbage at master and at HEAD alike (`e_ptr_helper.py`, `e_tuple_bind_wa.py`, `wa_prop.py`; the same-alias form `wa_prop2.py` does demote). One further write receiver is an open escape at master too and is deliberately left alone here: a user `__getitem__` returning a record (`bag[0].name = ...`, `_field_over_record_getitem_ok`) is admitted on master and dangles there (`r7_getitem.py`) -- it stays ADMITTED and NOT demoted, because subtracting it would reject what master compiles. The receivers that stay admitted AND demote the held view were each measured to do so: a name / `self`, a nested field, an unproven Optional name and an unproven Optional over a field. So the branch's view-family WRITE set is not master's rule verbatim -- it is master's (`_field_receiver_or_unbound_self_ok` plus `_field_over_record_getitem_ok`) plus the nested field, the unproven Optional name and the unproven Optional over a field, minus the five subtracted receivers; only the READ rule is master's verbatim. The scalar rows keep the full ladder: no view borrows an `int32` field, so every receiver is safe there; the `bytes` rows ride the same gate and are safe whatever it admits, since a `bytes` field read is an owned copy. The global leg additionally needs the per-def global-write fact that `BUGS.md#noarg-helper-global-write-under-live-borrow` and `BUGS.md#readonly-method-global-write-under-live-borrow` are waiting on (rule 35 of `docs/CALLABLE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENTS.md`); one fact serves all three. **Fix shape:** escape becomes a borrow-tracker fact -- the `Place` of `BUGS.md#iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`, invalidated wherever anything that can reach the storage is handed out (a pack element, a closure capture, a `take_ptr`, a global a callee may write) -- and lands with that row, since its home is master's analysis-only MIR (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`, M2.1) rather than a second place vocabulary in `tpyc/sema/context.py`. That one fact answers all three halves: the four missing demotions above, the write receivers this list cannot see, and re-admitting the deeper `str` read and the `bytes` read as views. The probes in that directory are its acceptance tests -- a re-admitted view must keep every one of them at CPython parity. Do NOT extend the write-path list again: five rounds of batch 6 each added one path and each review found the next; the blanket copy that removed the whole class was tried on that branch and withdrawn (user decision 2026-09-17, minimal revert). Found by the round-3 review of THIR batch 6. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic overstates certainty) The element-loan warning claims a mutation certainly hits the iterated element when the index NAME was REBOUND inside the loop body.** [`elem-index-certainty-ignores-rebinds`] `rows: list[list[int32]] = [[1, 2], [3]]` / `i = 0` / `for v in rows[i]: i = 1; rows[i].append(v)` warns *Mutation of 'rows[...]' while iterating over it ('append' invalidates the iterator)* -- the certain wording -- for a write that provably lands on `rows[1]` while `rows[0]` is iterated. `element_index_key` answers a bare NAME so that two spellings of one name settle SAME (`for v in rows[i]: rows[i].append(v)`), and `element_index_relation` compares the keys with no notion of the name having changed value in between; the loan's `elem_index` was recorded at the ITER registration. The warning firing at all is right (a write through a rebound name may still hit the borrowed element); only "invalidates" instead of "may invalidate" is wrong. Fix shape: the loop body's fact kills are already computed (`collect_fact_kills`, `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`, called by the for-each analysis) -- an `elem_index` naming a variable the body kills degrades the relation to UNKNOWN, which is the wording branch that already exists. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch6/elem-index-certainty-ignores-rebinds/m_rebound_index.py`. Recorded as a caveat by the batch-6 index-relation work and filed by the round-3 safety review.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, no diagnostic) Inserting a new key into a dict while iterating THAT dict is silent and keeps iterating; CPython raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`.** [`dict-grows-during-own-iteration`] `t: dict[int32, int32] = {0: 1}` / `for k in t: if n == 0: t[18] = 2` / `n += 1` prints `n 2 len 2` in TPy -- the newly inserted key is visited -- where CPython stops the program. The for-each files an ITER loan on `t` itself, and the element-assignment check asks `element_hop_loan`, which deliberately skips a loan on the storage itself (it survives an element WRITE); the plain invalidating-method check never runs, because an assignment is not a method call and `dict.__setitem__` is annotated `@native_preserves_refs` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_dict.py`). That annotation is CORRECT for references -- `OrderedMap` holds `std::unordered_map<K, Node*>` over individually heap-allocated nodes, so a rehash moves no value -- which is why the neighbouring exemption is sound and this is a SIZE question, not a reference one: what is missing is a per-`__setitem__` "may GROW the receiver" fact, distinct from `native_preserves_refs`, so an inserting element-assign counts as a structural mutation against an ITER loan on the container. Probe `/tmp/agents/batch6/dict-grows-during-own-iteration/l_dict_self_iter.py`. The value-side sibling is safe and needs no change: `for v in t[0]: t[18] = [9]` keeps the iterated vector alive and prints the same as CPython (`/tmp/agents/batch6/dict-grows-during-own-iteration/k_dict_insert_lit.py`), and the same shape with a NAME key already warns "may hit the element being iterated". Found by the round-3 safety review; the reference-moving premise it was filed under is refuted above.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic overstates certainty) The iteration-mutation warning says a mutation "invalidates the iterator" even when the iterator is an OWNED object holding no reference into the iterable.** [`iter-invalidation-wording-assumes-borrow`] `for`/`async for` over a user type whose `__iter__` / `__aiter__` returns a fresh iterator by value (`-> Own[SrcIter]`, carrying only a cursor and a limit) warns *Mutation of 'src' while iterating over it ('push' invalidates the iterator)* on a `src.push(x)` in the body. Nothing is invalidated there: the iterator holds no pointer into `src`, and CPython runs the same program without complaint. The wording is right for a builtin container (whose iterator IS a pointer into the buffer) and for a user iterator that stores one (`tests/cases/async/async_for_warn_iter_mutation`'s `ptr_iter` section, where the `Ptr[Feed]` makes it true), and the loan itself is right in both cases -- only the CERTAINTY claimed is wrong. Pre-existing on the NAME spelling (`runner`, `nested` in the same case; the sync twins in `tests/cases/list/warn_iter_mutation` iterate builtin lists, where the wording is correct); batch 6 extended the same wording to one-hop element and field iterables under `async for`, so it now reaches more programs. Fix shape: the wording picks "invalidates" only when the iterator kind is KNOWN to borrow the iterable -- a builtin container, or a user iterator whose fields include a `Ptr`/reference rooted in the receiver -- and "may invalidate" otherwise; the fact is the iterator type's, decided where `__iter__` / `__aiter__` is resolved, and read by `loan_mutation_warning` / `element_loan_mutation_warning` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) instead of being assumed there. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity S1) of THIR batch 6.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic; pre-existing) A for-each over a `@property` getter files its iteration loan on the receiver ROOT, so a mutation of the storage the getter actually returned is unwarned.** [`property-iter-loan-misses-getter-storage`] `for x in b.items:` (the getter is `def items(self) -> list[int32]: return self.xs`) with `b.xs.append(9)` in the body compiles with NO diagnostic and diverges from CPython -- TPy prints `prop: 6 4`, CPython `prop: 57 10` (probe `/tmp/agents/batch6/property-iter-loan-misses-getter-storage/prov_sync.py`, which holds the divergence twice: the CALL spelling `for x in pick(xs):` with `xs.append(9)` does warn). The loan comes from `_register_iter_provenance_loan` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`), which reads the getter's `return_borrows_from` and files on `_borrow_storage_roots(gc.obj)` -- the receiver root `b` -- while the mutation resolves to `b.xs`, so the keys never meet. This is why the property-tail chain is admitted only OUTSIDE a resumable body: a loan that does not name what is iterated cannot be allowed to guard iterators that live across suspensions (`frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller`). The call twin works only because a free function's borrowed argument IS the mutated storage. Both legs still diverge from CPython in output (the iteration is over a snapshot, not the live container); this entry is about the SILENCE, which the call spelling does not share. Fix shape: file the loan on the storage the getter returned, not on the receiver -- `return_borrows_from` names only the parameter borrowed from, so the fact needed is the returned PLACE (root plus its field hops), decided where the getter's return is analyzed; the same missing place vocabulary as `field-view-escape-needs-place` and `iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`, and it should land with that design rather than as a third key-speller. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity S2) of THIR batch 6.
- **[HIGH medium] (silent heap-use-after-free) A generator or `async def` frame holds its `begin`/`end` iterators across every suspension, but the ITER loan that guards them is intra-procedural, so an invalidating mutation made by the CALLER between two resumes is never seen.** [`frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller`] `def gen(o: Inner) -> Iterator[int32]: for b in o.boxes: yield b.n`, then a caller that does `for v in gen(o): o.boxes.append(Box(99))`, compiles with no diagnostic and is an ASAN `heap-use-after-free` (READ inside `__gen_gen::__next__`, freed by the caller's `_M_realloc_insert`; built g++ 13.3 `-fsanitize=address`). The same program with the mutation in the LOOP BODY *is* caught -- *warning: Mutation of 'o.boxes' while iterating over it* -- which is the whole gap: `BorrowTracker` answers "is this storage mutated while borrowed" over ONE body, and a frame's borrow outlives the body it was registered in. It is not a property-specific defect: the one-hop field iterable (`o.boxes`) and the one-hop `@property` iterable (`o.items`) both reach it, as does the generic bare-`T` getter at a container instantiation (`class Cell[T]` with `-> T`, driven at `Cell[list[int32]]`) -- its convention is decided at the instantiation, so it is a reference exactly as its monomorphic twin is and dangles identically (`tests/cases/generics/inherited_accessor_subst` pins that shape as compiling), and the property flavour additionally files its loan on the receiver root rather than the returned container (`property-iter-loan-misses-getter-storage`), so even its body mutation is silent. Chains deeper than one hop are refused for an unrelated reason (`iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`, no key at all), which accidentally covers them. Repros in `/tmp/agents/batch6/frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller/`: `p_frame_field_onehop.py` (field, caller mutation, ASAN), `p_frame_onehop.py` (property, caller mutation, ASAN), `p_frame_field_body.py` (field, body mutation -- warned, the contrast), `p_frame_caller_loop.py` / `p_async_realloc.py` / `p_frame_realloc.py` (the deeper chains, now located rejects). Fix shape: what is left to decide is the CALLER-STORAGE source alone. A source that is a temporary as written the frame already OWNS in its `__for_src_N` slot; a source that names existing storage is bound by reference once at loop setup (`auto& __for_obj_N = o.boxes;`) and the frame holds `begin`/`end` into it across every suspension, which is the render above. Refusing that aliasing shape is one answer; a purely intra-procedural loan cannot be extended to answer it, since the mutating statement is in another body. A third option is open beside reject-or-own and is the only one that keeps CPython's semantics: iterate a vector-backed container by INDEX rather than by iterator pair, re-reading the container at each resume. Owning the source turns a CPython alias into a copy -- CPython's generator yields the element the caller appended between resumes, an owned snapshot never does -- while an index form keeps the alias and cannot dangle, since a reallocation moves the buffer but not the index. The frame's by-value property fence is gone (2026-09-18, see `own-property-iterable-materialize`), so every by-value getter -- `Own[...]`, `-> str`, and the VIEW-returning `-> StrView` / `Span[T]` / `BytesView` whose iterators were always safe -- is admitted in a frame on its `__for_src_N` slot, like the spelled twin. That widens the surface this entry covers rather than adding a kind: the fact still missing is the same one, whether a frame may ALIAS caller storage across a suspension at all. Surfaced by the batch-6 round-8 safety review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic) An alias of a container ELEMENT sees a later ELEMENT ASSIGNMENT to the same slot, where CPython rebinds the slot and leaves the alias alone.** [`element-alias-sees-element-assignment`] `mid = outer[1]` over `outer: list[list[int32]]`, then `outer[j] = [9, 9, 9]` with `j == 1`, then `len(mid)`: TPy prints 3, CPython 2, and nothing is warned. `mid` binds a reference INTO the slot and TPy's element assignment overwrites that storage in place; CPython points the slot at a different list and the one the alias holds stays alive and unchanged. Both spellings diverge: the SINGLE-binding one above, which is pre-existing (identical C++ on master; probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/review/parity/elemrebind3.py`), and the REASSIGNED alias `mid = outer[0]; mid = outer[1]`, newly reachable since the reseatable element-alias local landed (`elemrebind2.py`). The `append` flavour of the same alias IS diagnosed -- a `rows.append(...)` under a live element alias warns *Mutation of 'rows' while borrowed ('append' may invalidate references)* (`elemdangle.py`) -- so the gap is element ASSIGNMENT specifically, not element borrowing. Fix shape: the missing warning at an element assignment while an alias of an element of that container is live, with the `append` row as the model -- a diagnostics rule change, its own unit. Measured 2026-09-21, surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity C1) of THIR batch 7. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; the `@property` spelling is pre-existing) A `with` manager borrowed off a container ELEMENT dangles when the body grows the container.** [`with-borrowed-manager-element-receiver-dangles`] `with xs[0].guard_m() as q:` whose block runs `xs.append(...)` emits `auto& __ctx_1 = ::tpy::__getitem__(xs, 0).guard_m();` and binds into the element's storage, which the reallocation moves: `__exit__` then runs against the freed slot and its effect is lost -- TPy prints `after 6` where CPython prints `after 16`, with no warning (probe `/tmp/agents/batch7/review/safety/p3c_elem.py`, 2026-09-21). The METHOD spelling reaches this only through the `with.manager_borrowed` call row; the `@property` spelling (`with xs[0].guard as q:`) emits and diverges identically and predates that row, so the class is pre-existing and the row widened its reach. The gate asks whether the RECEIVER is a temporary, which an element read is not; what nothing asks is whether the container is mutated across the block -- the element-loan question the iteration warning already answers for `for`. Fix shape: take an element loan on the receiver's container for the extent of the `with`, so the existing "may invalidate references" rule fires on the mutation inside the body. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model W) of THIR batch 7. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
